INTRODUCTION

介绍


Welcome to the new edition of Secrets Of Action Screenwriting. You know, I never set out to write a best selling screenwriting book that would go for $510 as a rare edition on Amazon when it went out of print. All I ever wanted to do was write screenplays. After selling a script to a producer with a deal at Paramount, I quit my warehouse job and moved to Los Angeles to begin writing full time. I subscribed to every screenwriting newsletter or magazine, including the little newsletter that would eventually become Script Magazine. Almost every article was from some guru trying to sell their book or class. When I complained that no one seemed to have any actual screenwriting experience, the newsletter gave me a regular column... without pay.

欢迎来到新版《动作剧本写作秘诀》。说实话，我当初写剧本写作书的时候，从未想过会成为一本畅销书，更没想到它会在绝版后以510美元的稀有版价格出现在亚马逊上。我一直以来都只想写剧本。在把一个剧本卖给派拉蒙的一位制片人之后，我辞掉了仓库的工作，搬到洛杉矶开始全职写作。我订阅了所有剧本写作相关的简报和杂志，包括后来发展成《剧本杂志》（Script Magazine）的那份小型简报。几乎每篇文章都是一些所谓的“大师”在推销他们的书或课程。当我抱怨说似乎没有人真正有过剧本写作经验时，那份简报给了我一个固定的专栏……而且是无偿的。


As I continued to sell scripts and have them actually get produced, my friends started giving me their action and thriller scripts to read for feedback... and I found myself typing up the same notes again and again. So I created a “master list” of notes in a red booklet. Now I could say, “Read page 12, page 17, page 32 and page 49.” When the booklet expanded to 100 pages, a friend suggested I throw a cover on it and sell it. That was the first version of this book, made at a copyshop in the early 1990s; and up until *this* version, some of the chapters and sections remained completely unchanged. If you are one of the hundred people with one of those booklets, you have a real collector’s item.

随着我不断售出剧本并最终促成拍摄，朋友们开始把他们的动作片和惊悚片剧本给我，让我帮忙看看并给出反馈……我发现自己一遍又一遍地重复着同样的笔记。于是，我用一本红色的小册子做了一个“笔记总清单”。这样我就可以说：“读第12页、第17页、第32页和第49页。”当这本小册子扩展到100页时，一位朋友建议我给它加个封面然后拿出来卖。这就是这本书的第一版，是在20世纪90年代初在一家复印店印制的；直到*这个*版本，有些章节和段落的内容都完全没有改动过。如果你是拥有这本小册子的那100个人之一，那你可就拥有了一件真正的收藏品。


Another friend thought that little red booklet was the best screenwriting book he had ever read, and suggested I expand it and find a publisher. I wrote some new material, beefing the book up to 240 pages, then sent it to several publishers who specialized in film and screenwriting books. They all turned it down for the same reason - it focused on a single genre. One of the publishers suggested I rewrite the book so that it would be about general screenwriting and let them look at the new version. I thought they were all missing the point - the shelves were already flooded with general screenwriting books, but there wasn’t a single book on how to write a specific genre. And Secrets Of Action worked well as a general screenwriting book even though it *also* contained techniques used in the action genre. I believed in my book.

另一位朋友认为那本红色小册子是他读过的最好的剧本写作书籍，并建议我扩充内容，找出版社出版。我写了一些新内容，把书扩充到240页，然后寄给了几家专门出版电影和剧本写作书籍的出版社。他们都以同样的理由拒绝了——这本书只专注于单一类型。其中一家出版社建议我重写这本书，让它涵盖通用的剧本写作，然后让他们看看新版本。我觉得他们都忽略了重点——书架上已经充斥着各种通用的剧本写作书籍，但却没有一本专门讲解如何创作特定类型的剧本。《动作秘诀》作为一本通用的剧本写作书籍已经很成功了，尽管它也包含了一些动作类型片的写作技巧。我对我的书充满信心。


So I took the money from my next screenplay sale, found a printer, and became my own publisher. When that run sold out, I switched printers and did another couple of runs. I was the top selling screenwriting book in the Sam French bookstores - they couldn’t keep them on the shelves! Amazon sold hundreds every month, and the book ended up a featured selection of a film and theater bookclub. Other books that focused on a single genre began popping up on the bookstore shelves... many from the same publishers who wanted me to rewrite this book.

于是，我用下一部剧本的销售款，找了家印刷厂，成了自己的出版商。第一批书售罄后，我换了印刷厂，又印了几版。我的书成了萨姆·弗伦奇书店最畅销的剧本写作书籍——他们根本供不应求！亚马逊每月也卖出几百本，这本书最终还被一家电影戏剧读书俱乐部选为推荐读物。其他专注于单一类型的书籍也开始出现在书店货架上……其中很多都是出自之前想让我重写这本书的同一家出版社。


Those old chapters and sections from the original “master list” of script notes bothered me - they needed a page one rewrite. Plus, many of the film references were decades out of date. I decided not to do another print run until I’d done a complete rewrite on the book... which became difficult, because my real job is writing screenplays. For a few years this book remained out of print while I wrote scripts, did endless rounds of studio meetings and did “jury duty” on Film Festival juries around the world.

那些源自原剧本笔记“总清单”的旧章节和段落让我很困扰——它们需要从头到尾重写一遍。此外，许多电影参考资料都已经过时几十年了。我决定在彻底重写这本书之前不再印刷……但这变得很困难，因为我的本职工作就是写剧本。在接下来的几年里，这本书一直绝版，而我则忙于写剧本、参加无数次制片厂会议，并在世界各地的电影节上担任评委。


But now the time has come to revise the book, to add what I’ve learned over the past few years and examine the way the action film has evolved in the 21 st Century. I have not only updated the book, I've almost doubled it in length by added new techniques and tools and digging deeper into why one film is a classic and another is now forgotten. The last version of the book was 240 pages, this version is over 460 pages!

但现在是时候修订这本书了，我想加入过去几年里我学到的知识，并探讨21世纪动作电影的演变历程。我不仅更新了这本书，还通过添加新的技巧和工具，以及深入挖掘某些电影成为经典而另一些电影被遗忘的原因，使书的篇幅几乎翻了一番。上一版只有240页，而这一版超过460页！


#↩

TOOLS, NOT RULES

工具，而非规则


The purpose of this book is to give you the tools necessary to write an action or thriller screenplay, not to tell you how to write. There are places in the book where I might say "On page 25, THIS happens"... Those are guidelines, not part of some by-the-numbers formula which must be adhered to. Whether your Plot Point happens on page 24 or 26 or 32 or doesn't happen at all, depends on the individual script you are writing. Every screenplay and every story is different.

本书的目的是为你提供创作动作或惊悚剧本所需的工具，而不是告诉你如何写作。书中有些地方我可能会说“在第25页，会发生这样的事”……这些只是指导原则，并非必须遵循的固定模式。你的情节转折点究竟发生在第24页、第26页、第32页，还是根本不发生，取决于你正在创作的具体剧本。每个剧本、每个故事都是独一无二的。


Instead of rules or formula, think of this book as a tool box. Some of the tools you may never use, other tools you may end up using constantly. One of the reasons for reading a book on screenwriting or any creative endeavor is to call attention to tools and techniques you may have never noticed before. There's a certain “Rashomon Effect” where five people might watch the same movie or read the same script and each comes away with a different technique – one of the purposes of a book is to point out the techniques I have noticed after many viewing and studying the screenplay... and explaining the way the techniques work. You may have never noticed that tool before, and it may be exactly what you need for your next screenplay.

与其说这是一本规则或公式的书，不如把它看作一个工具箱。有些工具你可能永远用不上，而有些工具你最终可能会经常用到。阅读剧本写作或其他任何创意类书籍的目的之一，就是为了让你注意到一些你可能从未注意到的工具和技巧。有一种“罗生门效应”，五个人看同一部电影或读同一个剧本，每个人都会从中获得不同的技巧——这本书的目的之一，就是指出我在多次观看和研究剧本后发现的技巧……并解释这些技巧的运作方式。你可能从未注意到过这些工具，而它们或许正是你下一个剧本所需要的。


There is only one rule in screenwriting: the script has to work. No one cares what method you used to create the script or how many “rules” you followed or broke, they only care that the script is so exciting that they can’t put it down... and they can’t wait to buy it and put it on screen. Skip the rules, use the tools to write the best script possible.

剧本创作只有一条规则：剧本必须精彩。没人关心你用什么方法创作剧本，也没人关心你遵循或打破了多少“规则”，他们只关心剧本是否足够精彩，让他们爱不释手……并且迫不及待地想要买下它，把它搬上银幕。抛开规则，运用工具，写出最好的剧本。


Ready to open the toolbox and build something?

准备好打开工具箱，动手做点什么了吗？


  • William C. Martell, December 2011, Studio City, CA.

    William C. Martell，2011 年 12 月，加利福尼亚州 Studio City。



#↩

THE VILLAIN'S PLAN

反派的计划


The most important element of an action film isn't the hero, isn't the sidekick, isn't the dialogue, and isn't the plot. The most important element of an action film is *the Villain’s Plan*.

动作片最重要的元素既不是英雄，也不是配角，不是对白，也不是情节。动作片最重要的元素是*反派的计划*。


Why? Hitchcock said, "The better the villain, the better the picture". The Villain's Plan is the fuel for the story. The Villain brings the conflict, and story *is* conflict... no matter the genre. In a romantic comedy, if boy can easily get girl you don’t have a story. In a drama, nothing very dramatic can happen unless there is a conflict. Conflict is the key to story... and that is what makes the Villain (or antagonist or force of antagonism) the most important character in your screenplay. Take your average cop show on television - it always begins with a crime, and *then* the cops become involved. No crime, nothing for the cops to do! That CSI team can not begin searching for evidence unless there is a crime. The Homicide detectives can’t start questioning witnesses unless there was some crime for them to witness. The mediums and mentalists and Monks can’t do anything until the villain has committed some crime. When writing your action screenplay, remember that the villain is your most important character - they bring the conflict.

为什么？希区柯克说过：“反派越出色，电影就越精彩。”反派的计划是故事的燃料。反派带来冲突，而故事本身就是冲突……无论什么类型。在浪漫喜剧中，如果男主角轻易就能抱得美人归，那就没有故事可言。在剧情片中，如果没有冲突，就不会发生任何真正扣人心弦的情节。冲突是故事的关键……也正因如此，反派（或对手、反派势力）才成为剧本中最重要的角色。以电视上常见的警匪剧为例——剧情总是以犯罪开始，然后警察才会介入。没有犯罪，警察就无事可做！犯罪现场调查小组只有在犯罪发生后才能开始搜寻证据。凶杀案侦探只有在目睹犯罪后才能开始询问证人。灵媒、读心术师和僧侣们只有在反派犯下罪行后才能发挥作用。在编写动作剧本时，请记住反派角色是最重要的角色——他们带来冲突。


Let's use the quintessential action film "Die Hard" as an example. The Hero's desire and need is to reunite with his wife and children for Christmas. Is that an action movie? If you throw in a couple of fist fights and a car chase is it an action movie? No.

我们以经典动作片《虎胆龙威》为例。主人公的愿望和需求是与妻子和孩子团聚过圣诞节。这算是动作片吗？如果加上几场拳脚打斗和一场飙车戏，它还能算是动作片吗？不能。


But the villain's plan in "Die Hard" is to rob the Nakatomi Corporation's safe of millions of dollars on Christmas Eve. That's an action plot. There is an exciting story even without John McClane. In fact, if you were to delete all of the Bruce Willis scenes, you'd have an action film about Robbers vs. FBI agents. Maybe Agent Johnson ("no, the other one") would have been the hero. If Robert Davi's scenes were deleted, maybe Officer Powell would be the hero. But even without Reggie Vel Johnson, there would *still* be an action movie. Because the Villain brings the conflict and story is conflict. No Villain, no story!

但《虎胆龙威》中反派的计划是在圣诞夜抢劫中富集团的保险库，盗走数百万美元。这本身就是一个动作片的情节。即使没有约翰·麦克莱恩，故事依然精彩。事实上，如果删掉布鲁斯·威利斯的所有戏份，这部电影就变成了一部劫匪对抗联邦调查局特工的动作片。也许约翰逊探员（“不，是另一个”）会成为英雄。如果删掉罗伯特·戴维的戏份，也许鲍威尔警官会成为英雄。但即使没有雷吉·维尔·约翰逊，这部电影仍然会是一部动作片。因为反派带来了冲突，而故事的核心就是冲突。没有反派，就没有故事！


#↩

SIZE MATTERS

尺寸很重要


If your script is about a villain robbing the First National Bank in Omaha, it's a small movie. If the villain's plan is to rob every bank in Omaha on the same day, that's a medium sized movie. If your villain's plan is to rob Fort Knox, that's "Goldfinger". The difference between a “small movie” and a “big movie” usually comes down to scale of the Villain’s Plan or what is at stake. Don't just have the villain want to kill one person, have him want to wipe out an entire city or kill someone important. The higher the stakes, the more we want our hero to stop the villain.

如果你的剧本讲的是一个反派抢劫奥马哈第一国民银行，那它就是一部小成本电影。如果反派的计划是同一天抢劫奥马哈的所有银行，那它就是一部中等规模的电影。如果你的反派计划是抢劫诺克斯堡，那它就是《金手指》。小成本电影和大成本电影的区别通常在于反派计划的规模或事关重大。不要让反派只想杀一个人，而是让他想要毁灭一座城市或杀死某个重要人物。事关重大，我们就越希望我们的英雄阻止反派。


What are stakes? Here’s what my dictionary says:

什么是赌注？我的字典是这样解释的：

1) Something that is wagered in a game, race or contest.

1）在游戏、比赛或竞赛中下注的东西。

2) A monetary or commercial interest. Investment, share, or involvement in something.

2) 金钱或商业利益。投资、股份或参与某事。

3) A personal or emotional concern, interest or involvement.

3）个人或情感上的关心、兴趣或参与。

4) An investment.

4）一项投资。

5) A prize or reward.

5）奖品或奖励。

6) To risk (something) in the outcome of any uncertain venture.

6) 在任何不确定的冒险中承担（某事）风险。


The words “involvement” and “emotion” and “risk” are key to the definition of “stakes” and key to your Villain’s Plan. If your Hero has no stake in the outcome of the story, we won’t be emotionally involved in the story. If your Villain’s Plan doesn’t impact the Hero and the world around him in any way, the plan doesn’t matter and neither does the story. No stakes - no story. The greater the stakes, the greater the audience’s involvement in the story; so we usually want to play for the highest stakes possible.

“卷入”、“情感”和“风险”这几个词是定义“利害关系”的关键，也是反派计划的关键。如果你的英雄与故事的结局毫无利害关系，我们就不会对故事产生情感上的投入。如果你的反派计划对英雄及其周围的世界没有任何影响，那么这个计划就毫无意义，故事也同样如此。没有利害关系，就没有故事。利害关系越大，观众对故事的投入就越深；因此，我们通常都希望尽可能地设置最高的利害关系。


An action script needs *global* stakes or *personal* stakes - or both. If the Hero doesn't stop the Villain’s Plan, it will screw up the world or screw up the Hero's life forever. The Villain’s Plan is either going to be something so big it effects the world, or that big life-altering event that personally changes the Hero’s life forever. Global stakes are external, personal stakes are emotional. A great movie has both, which is why *Die Hard* works so well.

一部动作片剧本需要*全球性*的危机，或者*个人性*的危机——或者两者兼备。如果英雄不能阻止反派的计划，世界将会陷入混乱，或者英雄的人生将会彻底改变。反派的计划要么是足以影响世界的惊天阴谋，要么是足以彻底改变英雄人生的重大事件。全球性危机是外部的，个人性危机是情感上的。一部伟大的电影两者兼备，这也是《虎胆龙威》如此成功的原因。


The main difference between a “small film” and a big summer action film is what is at stake. Rob your father’s jewelry store or rob Fort Knox, kill the guy who has been sleeping with your spouse or assassinate the President, burn down your enemy’s house or set off a dirty bomb in an enemy country. When we dial the stakes down, we end up with a drama like “Before The Devil Knows You’re Dead” - nothing wrong with that at all, but it’s not really an action movie. Be aware, when you lower the global stakes you really need to raise the personal stakes as high as possible to compensate. When you are coming up with your story and your Villain’s Plan, look at the size of the stakes.

“小成本电影”和暑期档大片的主要区别在于故事的冲突程度。抢劫你父亲的珠宝店还是抢劫诺克斯堡？杀死与你配偶有染的男人还是刺杀总统？烧毁敌人的房子还是在敌国引爆脏弹？如果我们降低冲突程度，最终就会得到像《在魔鬼知道你死前》这样的剧情片——这本身没什么问题，但它并非真正的动作片。请注意，降低全球冲突程度时，你必须尽可能提高个人冲突程度来弥补。在构思故事和反派计划时，务必考虑冲突的规模。


#↩

ACTIVE VILLAINS

活跃的反派


Your Villain needs to be an active character, so his plan has to be *active*. He must want to *do something*. Rob a bank, blow up a plane, assassinate the President, take over Chicago, steal government secrets from a high security vault, make a million dollar drug deal, go back in time and kill the mother of his enemy, take over a corporation, or create an earthquake which turns Nevada into beachfront property.

你的反派必须是一个积极主动的角色，所以他的计划也必须是*积极的*。他必须想要*做点什么*。抢劫银行、炸毁飞机、刺杀总统、占领芝加哥、从高度戒备的金库窃取政府机密、进行价值百万美元的毒品交易、回到过去杀死敌人的母亲、接管一家公司，或者制造一场地震把内华达州变成海滨度假胜地。


If the Villain just wants to be left alone, you've got a dull film on your hands. Why? Because the Hero is the character who just wants to be left alone. Look at "Shane" or "The Gunfighter" or "Witness" or the last “Rambo” movie or just about any action film. The hero is trying to get through life without shooting anyone, then the Villain sets his plan into motion, and the hero must do something to stop him. The Villain is *active* - their plan is what kicks off the story, and the Hero is usually *reactive* (which is not the same as passive) and must stop the Villain’s Plan.

如果反派只想安安静静地过日子，那这部电影就太无聊了。为什么？因为英雄往往只想独善其身。看看《原野奇侠》（Shane）、《枪手》（The Gunfighter）、《证人》（Witness）、最后一部《第一滴血》（Rambo）或者几乎所有动作片。英雄原本只想平安无事地过日子，不杀人，然后反派开始实施他的计划，英雄必须阻止他。反派是*主动的*——他们的计划推动了故事的发展，而英雄通常是*被动的*（这与被动不同），他必须阻止反派的计划。


You can have the most vile, un-lovable, ugly hero in the world, and as long as the Villain's Plan makes sense and is active, we will still identify with the hero and root for him to save the day. Because the Villain's Plan is the fuel for action, not the hero's appeal. If you don't believe me, check out Lee Marvin in "Point Blank" or Mel Gibson in the remake version "Payback". These are not nice people and in any other film they would be villains! I am using the terms “Villain” and “Hero” in this book for “antagonist” and “protagonist” because there’s less typing involved... and we’re dealing with action movies. We’ll get into Bad Guy Leads - anti-heroes and anti-villain’s - in the next chapter... and why sometimes Good Guys Wear Black.

即使你塑造了一个世界上最卑鄙、最令人厌恶、最丑陋的英雄，只要反派的计划合情合理且切实可行，我们仍然会认同这个英雄，并希望他能力挽狂澜。因为推动剧情发展的动力是反派的计划，而不是英雄本身的魅力。如果你不信，可以看看李·马文在《步步惊魂》（Point Blank）中的角色，或者梅尔·吉布森在翻拍版《复仇》（Payback）中的表现。他们可不是什么好人，换作其他任何电影，他们都会是反派！本书中我用“反派”和“英雄”来指代“对手”和“主角”，是因为这样打字比较省事……而且我们讨论的是动作电影。下一章我们会深入探讨反派主角——反英雄和反派——以及为什么有时候好人也会穿黑衣。


The Villain's Plan will be to achieve a specific goal by the end of the story, and only the hero can stop him. The villain is usually the driving force in an action or thriller script. Their plan is what creates the forward momentum. One of the reasons why there was no *Daredevil 2* is because the first film had a Villain who was not *active* and the film ended up ho-hum instead of exciting. Kingpin has no plan at all, so Daredevil has nothing to stop.

反派的计划是在故事结尾达成某个特定目标，而只有英雄才能阻止他。在动作片或惊悚片中，反派通常是推动剧情发展的关键人物。他们的计划推动着故事向前发展。之所以没有《夜魔侠2》，其中一个原因是第一部电影中的反派不够积极主动，导致影片平淡无奇，缺乏刺激感。金并根本没有任何计划，所以夜魔侠也无计可施。


Kingpin wants to maintain a status quo - he wants nothing to change. That's a non-goal. It's something he *already has*, so there's nothing to pursue. Nothing active for Kingpin to do. He has already achieved his goal - which makes him *passive* instead of active. Had Daredevil been actively closing in on Kingpin - attacking Kingpin in scene after scene - then Kingpin could be *reactive*. But Daredevil isn't doing anything that threatens Kingpin. We have no direct conflict in the story!

金并只想维持现状——他不想改变任何事情。这根本算不上什么目标。他*已经*拥有了现状，所以没有什么需要追求的。金并无任何主动可言。他已经实现了目标——这使他变得*被动*而非主动。如果夜魔侠积极地逼近金并——在一幕又一幕的场景中攻击他——那么金并或许会*被动*。但夜魔侠并没有做任何威胁到金并的事情。故事中根本没有直接的冲突！


A Villains Plan needs to be active. Not just maintaining his evil empire or hiding from authorities or anything else that is not actively doing something that the Hero must stop. What is your Villain’s Plan? How are they working throughout the screenplay to achieve it? How does the Hero get in its way?

反派的计划必须是实际行动，而不仅仅是维持其邪恶帝国、躲避当局追捕，或者做其他任何英雄必须阻止的事情。你的反派计划是什么？在整个剧本中，他们是如何一步步实现计划的？英雄又是如何阻挠他们的？


#↩

MOTIVATIONALLY SPEAKING

励志演讲


The villain brings the conflict and story is conflict, so your Villain’s Plan is your story. A stupid Villain’s Plan makes for a stupid story. A flawed Villain’s Plan makes for a flawed story. An unbelievable Villain’s Plan makes for an unbelievable story. A clever Villain’s Plan gives you a clever story. The more clever the Villain’s Plan, the more clever the Hero must be to thwart it... and vice versa. If the audience can't believe the plan will work or that the villain can get away with it, or if they don’t understand why the villain would want to do it in the first place, they'll reject your story. You never want to make things easier for the hero by creating a flawed Villain’s Plan - because that ends up making your Hero look stupid.

反派制造冲突，而故事的核心就是冲突，所以反派的计划就是你的故事。一个愚蠢的反派计划造就一个愚蠢的故事。一个有缺陷的反派计划造就一个有缺陷的故事。一个匪夷所思的反派计划造就一个匪夷所思的故事。一个巧妙的反派计划造就一个巧妙的故事。反派的计划越巧妙，英雄就越需要聪明才能挫败它……反之亦然。如果观众不相信这个计划会奏效，或者不相信反派能得逞，或者不理解反派为什么要这么做，他们就会拒绝你的故事。你永远不应该为了方便英雄而设计一个有缺陷的反派计划——因为那样最终只会让你的英雄显得愚蠢。


Your Villain's Plan should be the exact thing we'd do if we were the villain, and needs to make sense given the situation. Which means your villain needs to be motivated, and their motivation needs to make sense. Be logical. Villains who are pure evil are not very believable, and not very interesting. Two dimensional characters - even if the film is in 3D - come off as cartoons. If Fred Flintstone threatened to kill you, would you be worried? Just as the Villain’s Plan has to make sense or the whole story doesn’t make sense, the *villain* needs to make sense.

你的反派计划应该正是我们作为反派会采取的行动，并且必须符合情境。这意味着你的反派需要有动机，而且这个动机必须合情合理。要讲逻辑。纯粹邪恶的反派既不可信，也不有趣。二维角色——即使是3D电影——也会显得像卡通人物。如果弗雷德·弗林特斯通威胁要杀了你，你会担心吗？正如反派计划必须合情合理，否则整个故事就说不通一样，反派本身也必须合情合理。


Your villain (and Villain’s Plan) even needs to make sense even if they are crazy... maybe especially if they are crazy. Both Dietrich (Collin Cunningham) in my “Hard Evidence” MOW and The Joker (Heath Ledger) in “The Dark Knight” may be insane and unpredictable, but they have a plan that our hero must stop. The Joker keeps saying that “It’s all part of the plan” but is obviously out of his mind... except all of his insanity adds up to a plan: anarchy. He is a true terrorist, creating crazy situations that throw day-to-day life in Gotham City into complete chaos. And we understand that as a plan. When he pits the ferryboat full on convicts against the ferryboat full of commuters just to see what happens; he is tearing down society and civility. His plan is to make us all crazy - and he gives us many different and conflicting motivations for doing this. Though he’s crazy, he has an objective that makes sense.

你的反派（以及反派的计划）即便疯狂也必须合情合理……或许正因为疯狂才更应该如此。我写的《铁证如山》里的迪特里希（科林·坎宁安饰）和《黑暗骑士》里的“小丑”（希斯·莱杰饰）或许都疯癫且难以捉摸，但他们都有一个我们的英雄必须阻止的计划。小丑不断重复“一切都在计划之中”，但他显然已经疯了……然而，他所有的疯狂最终都指向一个计划：无政府状态。他是一个真正的恐怖分子，制造各种疯狂的局面，让哥谭市的日常生活陷入彻底的混乱。而我们明白，这正是他的计划。当他故意挑拨满载囚犯的渡轮和满载通勤者的渡轮，只是为了看看会发生什么时，他就是在摧毁社会和文明。他的计划是让我们都陷入疯狂——为此，他给出了许多不同且相互矛盾的动机。尽管他疯了，但他的目标却合情合理。


Even a serial killer has some sort of motivation and some sort of plan. They don’t kill random people with random weapons for no reason - even Jigsaw from the “Saw” movies has a reason for making ex-drug addicts stick their hands into a bucket of syringes to find the key to some door that may lead to freedom. A serial killer is just like any other villain - they need a motivated plan that makes some sort of sense. Watch "Manhunter" or "Silence Of The Lambs" (better yet, read the books by Thomas Harris) for an idea of how the FBI uses psychological profiles to nab serial killers. The Crawford character in both of those movies is based on real life FBI serial killer profiler John Douglas, and his book "Mindhunter: Inside The FBI's Elite Serial Crime Unit" (written with Mark Olshaker) is a fascinating look at what motivates serial killers. There is always a pattern and always a motivation. The “because he’s crazy” excuse for an unmotivated villain just doesn’t work.

即使是连环杀手也有某种动机和计划。他们不会无缘无故地用随机的武器杀害陌生人——即使是《电锯惊魂》系列电影中的“竖锯”，也并非毫无缘由地让戒毒者把手伸进装满注射器的桶里，寻找通往自由之门的钥匙。连环杀手和其他反派一样，都需要一个合情合理的计划。观看《人魔猎手》或《沉默的羔羊》（最好是阅读托马斯·哈里斯的原著小说），就能了解FBI如何利用心理侧写来抓捕连环杀手。这两部电影中的克劳福德一角都取材于现实生活中的FBI连环杀手侧写师约翰·道格拉斯，他与马克·奥尔沙克合著的《心理猎手：FBI精英连环犯罪小组内幕》一书，深入剖析了连环杀手的作案动机。他们的作案模式和动机总是存在的。用“因为他疯了”来解释反派角色缺乏作案动机是行不通的。


#↩

UNPREDICTABLE PLANS

不可预测的计划


Though your Villain has to have a plan, it should not be predictable. The best Villain’s Plans have a twist in them. They look like one thing but are actually another... and sometimes even something else after that. In “Die Hard” at first it seems like Hans is going to hold all of the people at the Christmas Eve party as hostage for ransom... and it appears as if what he wants is for some political prisoners to be released. But underneath that is his real plan - to break into the vault at Nakatomi and steal $640 million in bearer bonds. The Police plan on cutting all of the power to the tower to force Hans to give up... but that is part of Hans’ plan! Cutting the power will allow him to open the vault. The plan seems to be one thing but is actually something else.

虽然反派必须有计划，但计划不应该是可以预料的。最精彩的反派计划往往出人意料。它们表面上看起来是一回事，实际上却是另一回事……有时甚至还有更深层次的含义。在《虎胆龙威》中，汉斯一开始似乎打算挟持圣诞夜派对上的所有人作为人质勒索赎金……而且他似乎想要释放一些政治犯。但在这背后，隐藏着他的真正计划——闯入中富大厦的金库，窃取价值6.4亿美元的无记名债券。警方计划切断大厦的所有电力，迫使汉斯投降……但这恰恰是汉斯计划的一部分！切断电力将使他能够打开金库。计划表面上是一回事，但实际上却是另一回事。


In “Goldfinger”, the Villain’s Plan seems to be to break into Fort Knox and steal the USA’s gold reserves. Bond tells Goldfinger that his plan will not work - the time it would take to load all of that gold onto a train, and the weight of the gold, makes it impossible. Goldfinger laughs and explains that his plan was never to steal the gold - he has a dirty atomic bomb and his plan is to contaminate the gold - making it worthless... and all of the other gold in the world (including his stockpile) worth more. You never want the Villain’s Plan to be predictable, you want it to be twisted and clever.

在《金手指》中，反派的计划似乎是闯入诺克斯堡，窃取美国的黄金储备。邦德告诉金手指，他的计划行不通——把所有黄金装上火车所需的时间，以及黄金的重量，都使得这个计划根本不可能实现。金手指却大笑起来，解释说他的计划从来就不是偷黄金——他拥有一枚脏原子弹，他的计划是污染黄金，使其失去价值……这样一来，世界上所有其他的黄金（包括他自己的藏品）都会变得更值钱。你永远不希望反派的计划是可以预料的，你希望它出人意料、巧妙绝伦。


#↩

WHAT IF THINGS GO RIGHT?

如果一切顺利呢？


The plan also has to make sense and work. A stupid villain’s plan makes for a stupid movie. The plan may make sense until the hero stops the villain... but what if the hero failed? Would the villain’s plan have worked? Let’s say you write a thriller about a group of bank employees who decide to rob their own bank in the two hour period one day where the security cameras are being serviced and the electronic lock on the vault is off. The employee-robbers study a photo of the same man, cut from a magazine, so that when the police question them they can all describe the same robber. But one bank employee is reluctant to break the law, and locks himself in the vault. Now the others have two hours to get him out, maybe shoot him so that it looks like the fake robber shot him, and get their money. Our hero has just changed the game, and the focus of the story is now our hero in the vault. Sounds exciting, right?

计划必须合情合理且行之有效。一个愚蠢的反派计划只会成就一部愚蠢的电影。计划或许在英雄阻止反派之前都说得通……但如果英雄失败了呢？反派的计划还能成功吗？假设你写了一个惊悚故事，讲述一群银行员工决定在某天监控摄像头维护、金库电子锁关闭的两个小时里抢劫自己的银行。这些劫匪研究了一张从杂志上剪下来的同一人的照片，这样当警察询问他们时，他们都能描述同一个劫匪。但其中一名银行员工不愿违法，把自己锁在了金库里。现在其他人有两个小时的时间把他救出来，或许还可以开枪打死他，伪装成是那个假劫匪开枪打的，然后拿到他们的钱。我们的英雄扭转了局势，故事的焦点现在转移到了被困在金库里的英雄身上。听起来很刺激，对吧？


But what if the hero had gone along with the scheme? Okay, they rob their own bank, they all describe the same suspect to the police, and the police are now on a permanent wild-goose chase looking for the menswear model on page 28 of last month’s Newsweek. Except for one problem. How did the menswear model know that they would be servicing the video cameras at that exact time? And how would he know the electronic lock on the vault would also be off at that exact time? There had to be an inside man. So the police begin investigating and questioning all of the bank employees, and looking for anything unusual in their recent past. And even if they sweat them all and miraculously no one in this group of non-criminals slips up, they will keep watching them until someone accidentally spends a penny more than they earned, and then they are all busted. This is a stupid plan, because it *requires* the hero to lock himself in the vault and ruin the original plan. You want to look all the way down the line and make sure the villain’s plan works if everything happens to go right - because the villain is *planning* on his plan working... not planning on the hero screwing it up.

但如果英雄真的参与了这个计划呢？好吧，他们抢劫了自己的银行，所有人都向警察描述了同一个嫌疑人，于是警察开始没完没了地追查上个月《新闻周刊》第28页上的男装模特。但问题是，那个男装模特怎么会知道他们会在那个时间维护监控摄像头？他又怎么会知道金库的电子锁也会在那个时间打开？肯定有内应。于是警察开始调查并讯问所有银行员工，寻找他们近期的任何异常记录。即使他们把所有人都揪出来，奇迹般地这群“非犯罪分子”中竟然没有人露出马脚，他们也会一直监视他们，直到有人不小心多花一分钱，然后所有人就都落网了。这计划太蠢了，因为它*需要*英雄把自己锁在金库里，从而破坏原计划。你要把事情想清楚，确保如果一切顺利，反派的计划能够成功——因为反派*计划*他的计划是成功的……而不是计划让英雄搞砸。


#↩

PUNISHMENT FITS THE CRIME

刑罚与罪行相称


Newton’s 3 rd Law is that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. That means that if the villain jay walks, the cop doesn't draw his gun and shoot him. If the Villain's Plan is to kill everyone in our hero's family, the reason can't be that the hero once splashed mud on the villain's clothes... unless you're writing a satire like "Slaughterhouse 5". The villain’s actions and motivations must make sense, and he has to react in a believable way. It's okay for actions to escalate (in fact it's required), but don't try skipping from loud words to machine guns. The punishments needs to fit the crime even if the villain is dishing it out.

牛顿第三定律指出，每一个作用力都有一个大小相等、方向相反的反作用力。这意味着，如果反派乱穿马路，警察不会拔枪射杀他。如果反派的计划是杀光主角一家，那么原因不可能是主角曾经把泥巴溅到反派的衣服上……除非你在写像《第五号屠宰场》那样的讽刺作品。反派的行为和动机必须合情合理，他的反应也必须令人信服。反派的行为可以升级（事实上，这是必须的），但不要试图从大声叫嚣直接跳到动用机关枪。即使是反派施暴，惩罚也必须与罪行相符。


The Villain's Plan shouldn't be so complicated that it becomes incredible. Every once in a while I see a film where the Villain's Plan is so complex that there has to be an easier way for the bad guy to make a buck! “Law Abiding Citizen” has a bunch of story problems, including an attempt to switch hero and villain in the middle of the film (which never works), but Gerard Butler’s plan in that film is just silly. He’s a normal guy whose wife and child are killed and the DA (Jamie Foxx) made a deal that sets the killer free. So Butler murders the killer, then allows himself to be arrested so that he can have a good alibi when he tries to kill Foxx. Um, getting arrested *on purpose*? That does not sound like a good plan to me. But Butler has already dug a huge tunnel - complete with several rooms - so that he can get in and out of jail whenever he wants. The tunnel goes to one of the Solitary Confinement cells, and he has to kill another prisoner so that he can get sent to solitary... and by good luck, ends up in the very solitary cell that his tunnel is under. Um, since he ends up in prison anyway - and kills a guy - why not just kill Foxx *before* he gets arrested for murdering the guy who killed his wife and kid? He may have actually gotten away with that.

反派的计划不应该复杂到匪夷所思。我偶尔会看到一些电影，反派的计划复杂到让人觉得肯定有更简单的赚钱方法！《守法公民》这部电影有很多剧情问题，包括试图在电影中途互换主角和反派（这种做法根本行不通），但杰拉德·巴特勒在片中的计划简直愚蠢至极。他饰演的是一个普通人，妻子和孩子被杀，地方检察官（杰米·福克斯饰）与凶手达成协议，释放了凶手。于是巴特勒杀了凶手，然后故意被捕，这样他就可以为自己刺杀福克斯提供不在场证明。呃，*故意*被捕？这听起来可不是什么好计划。但巴特勒已经挖了一条巨大的隧道——里面甚至还有好几个房间——这样他就可以随时进出监狱。那条隧道通往一间单独监禁的牢房，他必须杀死另一名囚犯才能被送进单独监禁室……而且运气不错，他最终被关进了隧道所在的那个单独监禁牢房。嗯，既然他最终还是进了监狱——而且还杀了人——为什么不在福克斯因谋杀杀害他妻儿的凶手而被捕之前就杀了他呢？说不定他真的能逍遥法外。


Beware of any plan where the villain plans to make the hero’s life hell by killing the people around him... um, why not just kill the hero and get it over with? Less chance of the villain being caught killing the hero’s kindergarten teacher. The closest distance between two points is a direct line - not some Rube Goldberg plan with a dozen chances to fail and even more chances for the villain to get caught. If you want revenge, just shoot the guy. Wouldn't that be easier? Quicker? Less chance of getting caught? The minute the Villain's Plan begins looking silly, you're in big trouble. If the Villain's Plan doesn't work, neither will the movie.

要警惕任何反派计划通过杀害英雄身边的人来让他生不如死的阴谋……嗯，为什么不直接杀了英雄一了百了呢？这样反派被抓的几率会小得多，毕竟他杀了英雄的幼儿园老师。两点之间直线最短——而不是什么鲁布·戈德堡式的复杂计划，那种计划失败的几率高达十几倍，被抓的几率更是高得离谱。如果你想复仇，直接毙了他。这样岂不是更简单、更快捷、更不容易被抓？反派的计划一旦显得荒谬可笑，你就麻烦大了。如果反派的计划失败了，电影也就完了。


A great villain’s revenge plot can be found in J. Lee Thompson's "Cape Fear" (1962) where Robert Mitchum's plan is simply to follow and hound Gregory Peck until the man cracks. Mitchum's plan is to never break the law, just break Peck. He stalks the family, kills the family dog (probably a misdemeanor), and the police can do nothing to stop him because he has done nothing illegal... he wants to goad Peck into crossing the line and doing something illegal, so Peck will be arrested. This is a great game of cat and mouse, where the villain is so clever we worry that he'll actually get away with it. If you haven't seen the original version of this film, add it to your Netflix queue.

J·李·汤普森执导的《恐怖角》（1962）堪称反派复仇计划的经典之作。罗伯特·米彻姆饰演的角色计划跟踪并纠缠格里高利·派克，直到他崩溃。米彻姆的计划并非触犯法律，而是要击垮派克。他跟踪派克一家，杀死了家犬（这或许只是轻罪），而警察却束手无策，因为他并未触犯任何法律……他想要激怒派克，让他越过底线，做出违法之事，从而被捕。这是一场精彩的猫鼠游戏，反派如此狡猾，以至于我们担心他真的会逍遥法外。如果你还没看过这部电影的原版，不妨把它添加到你的Netflix片单中。


#↩

IN 5 EASY LESSONS

只需5节简单课程


The other way that “the punishment fits the crime” is critical is the crime itself. Whatever the villain’s plan is, the degree of difficulty will be tied to whatever is at stake. If Goldfinger’s plan is to rob Fort Knox, and he just shows a gate guard a fake ID and he drives in and finds the big vault of gold on “day lock” and pops it open and fills up his truck and drives off, that is not believable. Stealing $200 billion in gold needs to be $200 billion worth of difficult. You need a flying circus of hot babes in crop dusters that spew poison gas that will kill all of the soldiers, you need your own army in gas masks, you need explosives to blast open gates, you need a giant industrial laser to cut open that huge steel door... none of this is going to be easy! Getting that gold will be $200 billion worth of difficult! This is true for the over-all plan, plus anything small that happens in a scene - the risk and degree of difficulty has to be equal to the reward. If the hero lost his keys and has to break into his house, it can be easy. If he is breaking into the villain’s house, it must be difficult... or we won’t believe it. The difficulty of the task must be equal to the reward. If you make it too difficult for the villain or too easy for the hero, we won’t believe it.

“罪刑相称”的另一个关键之处在于犯罪本身。无论反派的计划是什么，其难度都与所涉利益息息相关。如果金手指的计划是抢劫诺克斯堡，他只是向守卫出示了一张假身份证，然后开车进去，发现金库处于“白天上锁”状态，打开金库，装满黄金，扬长而去，这显然不可信。窃取价值2000亿美元的黄金，难度也必须达到2000亿美元。你需要一支由性感美女组成的飞行马戏团，驾驶喷洒毒气的飞机消灭所有士兵；你需要一支戴着防毒面具的军队；你需要炸药炸开大门；你需要巨型工业激光切割那扇巨大的钢门……这一切都绝非易事！获取这笔黄金的难度将达到2000亿美元！这一点适用于整体计划，也适用于场景中的任何小细节——风险和难度必须与回报相匹配。如果英雄丢了钥匙，不得不破门而入，这可能很容易。但如果他要闯入反派的房子，那就必须很困难……否则我们不会相信。任务的难度必须与回报相符。如果对反派来说太难，或者对英雄来说太容易，我们就不会相信。


#↩

SILLY VILLAINS

愚蠢的反派


Your villain has committed the perfect murder in order to take over a multi-million dollar corporation from his partner. The Detective starts nosing around, and discovers some minor evidence; not enough to convict, but enough to convince him that the villain is a suspect. More evidence mounts - but still not enough to convict. In Act 3 the Detective confronts the villain, usually in these films at a dinner party or at a country club. What does the villain do? He pulls out a machine gun and tries to kill the Detective. Why? So that the Detective won't continue his investigation.

你的反派精心策划了一场谋杀，企图从合伙人手中夺取一家价值数百万美元的公司。侦探开始四处调查，发现了一些零星证据；虽然不足以定罪，但足以让他相信反派是嫌疑人。更多证据接踵而至——但仍然不足以定罪。在第三幕中，侦探与反派对峙，通常是在晚宴或乡村俱乐部。反派会怎么做？他掏出一把机关枪，试图杀死侦探。为什么？为了阻止侦探继续调查。


Wait a minute! If the police didn't have enough evidence before, they sure do after the villain shoots up a dinner party!

等等！如果说之前警方证据不足，那么在歹徒枪击晚宴之后，他们肯定掌握了足够的证据！


In real life the villain would probably just call his attorney, and fight it out in court... where he has a good chance of winning. How many real life crooks have we seen walk after their “dream team” of lawyers found some loophole in the law or created reasonable doubt where there wasn’t any. If the villain absolutely had to kill the cop, he would find some perfect murder scenario. Maybe siphon off the brake and steering fluids from the cop's car and arrange a meeting late one night at the end of a long, winding cliff side road. He’d find some way to kill the cop that could never be traced back to him, because he isn’t a silly villain. It's important to question every single move your villain makes, and make sure it's logical and not far-fetched or too complicated or just plain silly.

现实生活中，反派很可能会直接打电话给律师，在法庭上据理力争……而且胜算很大。我们见过多少罪犯在他们的“梦之队”律师找到法律漏洞或凭空捏造出合理怀疑后逍遥法外？如果反派非要杀警察不可，他肯定会找到完美的谋杀方案。比如，偷走警车的刹车油和转向油，然后安排在某个深夜，在一条漫长蜿蜒的悬崖公路尽头见面。他会找到一种杀人方法，而且保证不留任何痕迹，因为他可不是个傻瓜。重要的是，你要仔细审视反派的每一个举动，确保它们合乎逻辑，而不是牵强附会、过于复杂或荒谬可笑。


#↩

THUNDERBALL THEORY

霹雳弹理论


The Villain's Plan should be threatening to others... even the people watching the film or reading your script, if possible. It's nice to have the hero save himself, but if he can save the rest of the city, too, even better. In “The Satan Bug” - a great thriller from 1965 - someone has stolen top secret germ warfare canisters from a government lab, and spy-guy George Maharis must find them before the terrorist leader (a great Richard Basehart) unleashes them on Los Angeles. If he doesn’t outwit the terrorist and find the canisters in time, millions will die. The Villain's Plan poses a major threat to others.

反派的计划应该对他人构成威胁……最好甚至对观看电影或阅读剧本的人也构成威胁。英雄拯救自己固然不错，但如果他还能拯救整个城市，那就更好了。在1965年的经典惊悚片《撒旦虫》中，有人从政府实验室偷走了绝密细菌战罐，间谍乔治·马哈里斯必须在恐怖分子头目（由优秀的理查德·贝斯哈特饰演）将它们释放到洛杉矶之前找到它们。如果他不能智胜恐怖分子并及时找到这些罐子，数百万人将会丧命。反派的计划对他人构成了重大威胁。


But, what would have happened to Los Angeles if Maharis fails? How can the audience know what this “satan bug” will do to people so that they can be properly frightened? If I say I can kill you with this ripe tomato, you have no idea how I could do that, or how painful death by ripe tomato might be. What we need is a demonstration. In “The Satan Bug” Los Angeles is the second target - the first is a small town in Florida where everyone is instantly killed by the bug. They show Maharis some raw footage of the town full of bodies as part of his briefing. Now that the audience has seen what this “satan bug” can do, they don’t want that to happen to the nice people in Los Angeles...

但是，如果马哈里斯失败了，洛杉矶会发生什么？观众如何才能了解这种“撒旦虫”会如何残害人类，从而真正感到恐惧？如果我说我可以用这颗熟透的西红柿杀死你，你根本无法想象我是怎么做到的，也无法想象被熟透的西红柿杀死会有多么痛苦。我们需要的是一场演示。在《撒旦虫》中，洛杉矶是第二个目标——第一个目标是佛罗里达州的一个小镇，镇上所有人都被这种虫子瞬间杀死。在向马哈里斯进行简报时，他们播放了一些小镇上尸横遍野的原始影像。现在观众已经见识过这种“撒旦虫”的威力，他们不希望洛杉矶的善良居民也遭遇同样的命运……


I call this the Thunderball Theory - in “Thunderball” Largo steals *two* nuclear weapons, so that he can test one just to prove to the authorities that he’s not kidding. The second nuke is hidden somewhere in Miami. Now James Bond must stop Largo before he kills all of the nice people in Miami. If that sounds familiar to you, it’s because it’s also the plot to “True Lies”, which also features a demonstration of the nuke on one of the Florida Keys before Ah-nuld has to save his wife and daughter and stop the villains from nuking Miami. For some reason, they always pick Miami! If your villain has some sort of high tech weapon, make sure he or she tests it so that we can see what it does. That will help us imagine what might happen to those poor people in Miami.

我称之为“霹雳弹理论”——在《霹雳弹》中，拉戈偷走了*两枚*核武器，他试爆一枚只是为了向当局证明他并非虚张声势。第二枚核弹藏在迈阿密的某个地方。现在，詹姆斯·邦德必须阻止拉戈，否则迈阿密的善良居民们将会惨遭屠戮。如果你觉得这似曾相识，那是因为《真实的谎言》的剧情也与之类似，同样在佛罗里达群岛上演了一场核弹演示，之后阿诺·施瓦辛格必须拯救他的妻子和女儿，并阻止反派用核弹轰炸迈阿密。不知为何，他们总是选择迈阿密！如果你的反派拥有某种高科技武器，那就确保他或她进行测试，让我们看看它的威力。这将有助于我们想象迈阿密那些可怜的人们将会遭遇怎样的命运。


Another aspect of this is fulfilling your promise to the audience. If Dennis Hopper in “Speed” says he’s going to blow up that bus, the audience wants to see the bus explode. We’ve been thinking about that bus exploding for almost half the film - if it goes under 55mph it’s gonna blow - so the only way we will truly be satisfied is if it explodes. We’ve been thinking about it for too long to have it *not* explode. There was a time when an action movie could get by with the hero completely preventing the Villain’s Plan, but we live in the time of big spectacle entertainment. In “Air Force One”, we want to see the plane crash into the ocean and disintegrate. You don’t want the hero to prevent all of the excitement! We want to see things blow up on screen! So, instead of cutting the red wire (no - the green one) you might have the hero thwart the Villain’s Plan by removing the bomb from a populated area to someplace where it can still blow up real good... just not hurt anyone. The threat of an explosion is kind of a promise you need to pay off - whether it’s having the villain demonstrate the bomb, or having the bus or plane or villain explode at the end. If you promise us an explosion, we want to see it.

另一个方面是兑现你对观众的承诺。如果丹尼斯·霍珀在《生死时速》里说他要炸毁那辆巴士，观众就想看到巴士爆炸。我们几乎在电影的前半段都在想着巴士爆炸——如果车速低于55英里/小时，它就会爆炸——所以只有巴士爆炸，我们才能真正感到满足。我们已经想了太久，它不可能不爆炸。过去，动作片可以靠英雄彻底阻止反派的计划来博眼球，但我们现在生活在一个追求宏大场面娱乐的时代。在《空军一号》里，我们想看到飞机坠入大海，解体。你不想让英雄阻止所有精彩的场面！我们想看到银幕上爆炸！所以，与其剪断红线（不，是绿线），不如让英雄把炸弹从人口稠密区转移到某个地方，这样炸弹仍然可以爆炸，但不会伤及任何人，从而挫败反派的计划。爆炸的威胁就像是一种需要兑现的承诺——无论是让反派展示炸弹，还是让巴士、飞机或反派在结尾爆炸。如果你承诺会有爆炸，我们就想看到它。


#↩

MULTIPLE VILLAINS?

多个反派？


The villain brings the conflict, and story is conflict; so if you have three villains you end up with three stories in one script. Difficult enough to tell one story in a 110 page screenplay, let alone three. This may explain why those Joel Schumacher “Batman” movies with a half dozen villains didn’t work. If you have four villains with four Villain’s Plans going on at the same time it’s like playing pinball with the hero - he just bounces back and forth between stories until the story turns to mush. You end up with a bunch of subplots instead of one main plot.

反派制造冲突，而故事的核心就是冲突；所以，如果剧本里有三个反派，最终就会出现三个故事。在110页的剧本里讲好一个故事都够难的了，更何况是三个。这或许可以解释为什么乔·舒马赫执导的那些有六个反派的《蝙蝠侠》电影最终失败了。如果四个反派同时进行四个反派计划，就像让英雄玩弹珠游戏一样——他会在不同的故事线之间来回弹跳，直到故事变得一团糟。最终，你会得到一堆支线剧情，而不是一个主线剧情。


The only way multiple villains work is if there is only *one* villain’s plan or if you have a “Red Harvest” situation. But wait, how can you have five villains and only one Villain’s plan? They are either partners (which doesn’t work very well) or you have a “ladder of henchmen” that leads to your main villain.

多个反派角色只有在只有一个反派的计划，或者出现类似“红色收割”那样的局面时才行得通。但是等等，五个反派怎么可能只有一个计划呢？他们要么是同伙（这不太合理），要么就是你设计了一个“喽啰阶梯”，最终通向你的主反派。


The problem with partners is that you have a two headed villain and often this cuts each villain’s power in half - making each half as threatening. Plus we have an uneasy alliance between both villains, which may mean they spend just as much time trying to kill each other as they spend trying to kill the hero. And because we have to establish each villain and then establish their alliance, we are burning through script pages before we get around to the story. In order to keep more than one villain focused on the plan and not each other, it’s a good idea to have one of the partners be in charge. In “The Dark Knight”, Salvatore Maroni (Eric Roberts) and Two Face (Aaron Eckhart) may partner with The Joker, but we know who is really in charge... it’s all part of the plan.

双头反派的问题在于，这往往会使每个反派的实力减半，从而使每个反派都同样具有威胁性。此外，两个反派之间还存在着不稳定的联盟，这意味着他们可能花费大量时间互相残杀，而不是试图杀死英雄。而且，由于我们必须先塑造每个反派，然后再建立他们的联盟，因此在真正进入故事之前，剧本就已经消耗了大量篇幅。为了让多个反派专注于计划而不是彼此，让其中一个反派担任领导是个好主意。在《黑暗骑士》中，萨尔瓦托·马罗尼（埃里克·罗伯茨饰）和双面人（艾伦·艾克哈特饰）可能与小丑结盟，但我们知道谁才是真正的幕后主使……这一切都在计划之中。


Movies like “Point Blank” and the original “Get Carter” and “The Limey” and “Columbiana” create a “ladder” of henchmen that the hero climbs to get to the main villain behind it all. Though those are all revenge movies, the “ladder” also works in other kinds of action movies where the hero may think Mr. Fairfax is the villain, but Fairfax is only working for Mr. Carter, and when Carter ends up working for Mr. Bronson... and each character we think is the villain is just a rung of the ladder - an employee of someone else. Eventually our hero gets to the top of the ladder - the actual villain who employs all of these henchmen. We have one Villain behind it all and one Villain’s Plan, but the hero doesn’t know that as he is climbing the ladder.

像《步步惊魂》（Point Blank）、原版《卡特探员》（Get Carter）、《莱姆帮》（The Limey）和《哥伦比亚》（Columbiana）这样的电影，都构建了一个由众多喽啰组成的“阶梯”，英雄需要一步步攀登，最终才能找到幕后的真正大反派。虽然这些都是复仇电影，但这种“阶梯”结构也适用于其他类型的动作片。例如，英雄可能误以为费尔法克斯先生是反派，但费尔法克斯只是卡特先生的手下；而卡特最终又为布朗森先生效力……我们认为的每一个反派角色，其实都只是阶梯上的一个台阶——是其他人的雇员。最终，我们的英雄会到达阶梯的顶端——找到真正操控所有这些喽啰的大反派。幕后只有一个大反派，只有一个大反派的计划，但英雄在攀登阶梯的过程中对此一无所知。


Both the Unequal Partners and Ladder Of Henchmen end up being *one* villain and *one* villain’s plan when all is said and done, but the “Red Harvest” Situation really has two villains and two villains' plans. Even if you haven’t read Dashiell Hammett’s novel “The Red Harvest” you have probably seen one of the movies inspired by it: “Fistful Of Dollars” or “Last Man Standing” or “Miller's Crossing” or “Sukiyaki Western Django” or any of the others. These stories have our hero stuck in the middle between two warring groups, each lead by a strong villain. Usually both villains have the same plan - take over a city or state or planet - and our hero ends up playing one villain against the other so that they cancel each other out. Of course, he has to battle *both* villains along the way. Though the “Red Harvest” Situation is usually two villains fighting over a territory, they can be fighting over *anything* - a stolen nuke, a magic sword, a kidnapped scientist. The more original and interesting your villain’s plan, the more interesting and original your screenplay.

无论是“不平等的伙伴”还是“爪牙阶梯”，最终都指向同一个反派及其计划，但“红色收割”的情况则截然不同，它涉及两个反派及其各自的计划。即便你没读过达希尔·哈米特的《红色收割》，你也可能看过根据它改编的电影，比如《荒野大镖客》、《最后的男人》、《米勒的十字路口》、《寿喜烧西部片》等等。这些故事讲述的是，我们的英雄被夹在两个敌对势力之间，每个势力都由一个强大的反派领导。通常，两个反派的计划相同——占领一座城市、一个州或一个星球——而我们的英雄最终会利用其中一个反派与另一个反派作对，使他们相互抵消。当然，在此过程中，他必须与两个反派都交战。虽然“红色收割”情境通常是指两个反派为了争夺地盘而战，但他们也可以为了任何东西而战——被盗的核弹、魔法剑、被绑架的科学家。反派的计划越新颖有趣，你的剧本也会越精彩独特。


Without a logical, well motivated, threatening villain's plan and an interesting and active villain, you don't have a story. And without a story, what's the hero going to do? Collect unemployment?

如果没有一个合乎逻辑、动机充分、具有威胁性的反派计划，以及一个有趣且活跃的反派角色，故事就无法成立。而没有故事，英雄又能做什么呢？去领失业救济金吗？



#↩

THE HERO'S JOB

英雄的职责


The hero's job is to stop the villain.

英雄的任务是阻止恶人。


Indiana Jones has to stop the Nazis from getting control of the Lost Ark and winning World War 2. Batman has to stop The Joker from creating chaos in Gotham City. Those guys in “Armageddon” have to stop that big asteroid from slamming into Earth. Dirty Harry has to stop the Scorpio Killer from killing again.

印第安纳·琼斯必须阻止纳粹夺取失落的约柜，从而赢得第二次世界大战。蝙蝠侠必须阻止小丑在哥谭市制造混乱。《世界末日》里的那些家伙必须阻止那颗巨大的小行星撞击地球。肮脏的哈里必须阻止天蝎杀手再次行凶。


Since the Villain's Plan fuels the story, the hero has to be someone who gets in the way of the plan. "The fly in the ointment, the monkey in the wrench," as John McClane says in "Die Hard". The hero can be a cop, a fireman, a private eye, a reporter, a regular guy, a pro-golfer, a lawyer, a scientist, a psychic, a sumo wrestler, or a weatherman. The more interesting the Hero’s day job is, the more interesting the character. But whatever his day job is, it has to fit in with the Villain's Plan. Your hero is connected to your villain and Villain’s Plan and the concept; so you can’t just create a protagonist character and then plug them in to the story. They have to fit.

既然反派的计划推动着故事发展，那么英雄就必须是阻碍计划实施的人。正如约翰·麦克莱恩在《虎胆龙威》中所说，“美中不足，煞风景”。英雄可以是警察、消防员、私家侦探、记者、普通人、职业高尔夫球手、律师、科学家、通灵师、相扑选手或气象员。英雄的日常工作越有趣，这个角色就越引人入胜。但无论他的日常工作是什么，都必须与反派的计划相契合。你的英雄与反派、反派的计划以及整个故事概念息息相关；所以你不能只是创造一个主角，然后把他/她硬塞进故事里。他/她必须与故事完美契合。


If the villain is smuggling weapons into the country, the odds of a weatherman being the only one who can stop him are pretty slim. That’s going to seem contrived and inorganic and silly. More likely, the hero of this story is going to be in the Coast Guard, or a Customs Agent, or maybe even a longshoreman working at the docks who sees something suspicious... or someone related to one of those people. Your Hero will be someone who would logically come between the Villain and the success of their plan. Your Hero is not some random choice - the Hero is part of the story, and the story is the Villain’s Plan. So, if you have always wanted to write a movie about a sumo wrestler, you can’t just force him into the weapons smuggling story without making people wonder what the heck he’s doing there. Your best plan there would be to *start* with the Sumo Wrestler character and find a Villain’s Plan he logically gets in the way of.

如果反派走私武器入境，一个气象员是唯一能阻止他的人的可能性微乎其微。这显得牵强附会、不合情理，甚至很荒谬。更有可能的是，故事的英雄会是海岸警卫队队员、海关人员，甚至是码头工人，他可能发现了什么可疑的事情……或者与这些人有关。你的英雄应该是能够合乎逻辑地阻止反派计划成功的人。你的英雄并非随意选择——英雄是故事的一部分，而故事本身就是反派的计划。所以，如果你一直想写一部关于相扑选手的电影，你不能硬把他塞进武器走私的故事里，否则观众会疑惑他到底在干什么。最好的办法是先从相扑选手这个角色入手，然后找到一个他能够合乎逻辑地阻碍的反派计划。


The hero's "day job", personality, and emotional conflict are facets of the Villain's Plan. This is why there are so many cop and private eye heroes in old films. Cops will naturally get in the way of any criminal activity. It's called a "franchise" in the TV world. A franchise is what places a hero in the line of fire week after week. You can have a cop show or a crime lab show or a lawyer show, and you know criminal activities will be part of the story every week.

英雄的“日常工作”、性格和情感冲突都是反派计划的组成部分。这就是为什么老电影里有那么多警察和私家侦探英雄的原因。警察自然会介入任何犯罪活动。在电视界，这被称为“系列剧”。系列剧让英雄每周都身处险境。你可以看警匪剧、犯罪实验室剧或律政剧，你知道犯罪活动每周都会是剧情的一部分。


#↩

DETECTIVE DAY JOBS

侦探日常工作


My advice on hero's day jobs is to be creative. Don't make her a cop or a private eye, if you can give her a job you've never seen on screen before. In “The Ninth Gate” Johnny Depp plays a rare book dealer hired to steal a rare first edition for a client. In “The DaVinci Code” Tom Hanks plays a college professor who is an expert on codes and symbols. In the movies based on Tom Clancy novels, hero Jack Ryan is an information analyst for the CIA who always ends up in the field (where he doesn’t belong). In my “Crash Dive!” movie for HBO, my hero was a retired Naval Engineer who knew everything about how submarines work, but nothing about fighting or shooting guns... so he must use the *submarine* against the villains who have hijacked it. If at all possible, find a franchise that hasn't been used before, instead of making your hero a cop or an FBI proflier.

关于主角的日常工作，我的建议是发挥创意。别让她当警察或私家侦探，如果可以的话，给她安排一份你在银幕上从未见过的职业。在《第九道门》中，约翰尼·德普饰演一位受雇为客户盗取一本珍贵初版书的古籍商。在《达芬奇密码》中，汤姆·汉克斯饰演一位精通密码和符号的大学教授。在根据汤姆·克兰西小说改编的电影中，主角杰克·瑞恩是中央情报局的信息分析员，总是被派往一线（尽管他并不擅长）。在我为HBO创作的电影《冲锋陷阵！》中，我的主角是一位退休的海军工程师，他精通潜艇的运作原理，但对战斗和射击却一窍不通……所以他必须利用潜艇对抗劫持它的恶棍。如果可能的话，尽量选择一个以前从未被用过的题材，而不是让你的主角成为警察或FBI探员。


When a day job is over-used it becomes a cliche, even if it’s true. Yes, police detectives solve crimes... but we’ve seen that so many times it seems old. Even television shows don’t use police detectives and private eyes any more: they have Mentalists and Crime Scene Investigators and Human Lie Detectors and Blood Spatter Experts and Psychics. Movies like “Brick” and “Winter’s Bone” take all of the elements of a standard private eye story and find unique characters and unusual worlds which make the films something we haven’t seen before. Though both of those are indie films, Shane Black’s brilliant “Kiss Kiss Bang Bang” gives us a complicated version of an actor on a “ride along” who ends up in the middle of a slam-bam action private eye-type story. In my "Undercurrents" script, the hero is a yacht captain investigating a murder on his boat while they're hundreds of miles from the nearest port.

当一种日常职业被过度使用时，即使它本身是事实，也会沦为陈词滥调。没错，警察侦探破案……但我们已经看过太多次了，感觉老套乏味。就连电视剧也不再使用警察侦探和私家侦探：取而代之的是心灵感应师、犯罪现场调查员、人体测谎仪、血迹喷溅专家和通灵者。像《追凶》（Brick）和《冬天的骨头》（Winter's Bone）这样的电影，汲取了传统私家侦探故事的所有元素，并挖掘出独特的角色和不同寻常的世界，使影片呈现出我们前所未见的风格。虽然这两部都是独立电影，但沙恩·布莱克（Shane Black）的杰作《亲亲，砰砰》（Kiss Kiss Bang Bang）为我们呈现了一个复杂的故事：一位演员在“搭车”中意外卷入了一场惊险刺激的私家侦探故事。在我的剧本《暗流涌动》（Undercurrents）中，主人公是一位游艇船长，他正在调查发生在船上的一起谋杀案，而此时他们距离最近的港口已有数百英里之遥。


#↩

SUPERMAN VS. EVERYMAN

超人VS.普通人


There are two basic types of hero characters in action films: the Superman Type and the Everyman Type. The Superman Type doesn't have to wear his underwear on the outside and probably can't fly. We idolize the Superman Type, we identify with the Everyman Type.

动作电影中的英雄角色大致可以分为两类：超人型和普通人型。超人型英雄不必把内裤穿在外面，而且可能也不会飞。我们崇拜超人型英雄，而我们认同普通人型英雄。


The Superman Type is the guy we wish we were: Tough, invulnerable, macho, action oriented. He lives in the action world, craves a good shoot out, and goes looking for trouble whenever possible. James Bond is the ultimate Superman Type. He always keeps his cool. The type of tough guys that Sylvester Stallone, Steven Seagal, Clint Eastwood and Ah-nuld always played. Jason Statham is one of the few action leads who still play this type of hero. "Rambo" fits this category, but "Rocky" doesn't. The Bourne movies give is a great schizoid hero: an Everyman who used to be a Superman Type: we can identify with him, but when trouble strikes he becomes the bad ass we wish we were. The Superman Type was most popular in the 1980s and early 1990s in films, but has since gone out of style except in B movies.

超人型角色是我们梦寐以求的那种人：强悍、刀枪不入、充满男子气概、行动力十足。他生活在动作世界里，渴望酣畅淋漓的枪战，并且总是伺机惹是生非。詹姆斯·邦德堪称超人型角色的典范。他总是保持冷静。西尔维斯特·史泰龙、史蒂文·西格尔、克林特·伊斯特伍德和阿诺德·施瓦辛格都曾扮演过这类硬汉。杰森·斯坦森是少数几位仍然扮演这类英雄的动作片男主角之一。《第一滴血》系列电影中的兰博也属于这一类型，但《洛奇》系列则不然。《谍影重重》系列电影塑造了一个极具分裂感的英雄形象：一个曾经是超人型角色的普通人：我们能够与他产生共鸣，但当危机来临时，他又会变成我们梦寐以求的硬汉。超人型角色在20世纪80年代和90年代初的电影中最为流行，但此后除了在B级片中出现外，已经逐渐过时。


The Everyman Type is the guy we are: A normal man, vulnerable, who is forced to become involved in the action. He is a reluctant hero. He doesn't go out looking for trouble, but trouble seems to find him. These are the kinds of guys Matt Damon and Will Smith and Denzel and Russell Crowe usually play. The Everyman Type hero has become more popular over the years, to the point of completely eclipsing the Superman Type. This probably began with Bruce Willis in the first "Die Hard", but now even superhero characters are played as Everyman Types. “Spider-Man” is a troubled teen who must learn that with great power comes great responsibility, Christian Bale’s Batman is a tortured soul trying to do the right thing by doing the wrong thing, and all of those X-Men and X-Women are regular folks who are cursed by super powers. Average people, just like you and me, who are thrust into danger and have to learn how to survive... while wearing tights and a cape. Lately, Superman Type superheroes like both Hulks and “Superman Returns” and “Green Lantern” haven’t seemed to do well with audiences. Everyman type superheroes like “Captain America” seem to be what audiences would rather watch... and that doesn't bode well for the new “Superman”.

“普通人”类型其实就是我们自己：一个平凡、脆弱，却被迫卷入事件的人。他是个不情愿的英雄。他并非主动惹事，但麻烦似乎总是找上门来。马特·达蒙、威尔·史密斯、丹泽尔·华盛顿和罗素·克劳通常扮演的就是这类角色。“普通人”类型的英雄近年来越来越受欢迎，甚至完全盖过了“超人”类型。这或许始于布鲁斯·威利斯在第一部《虎胆龙威》中的表演，但如今就连超级英雄角色也被塑造成了“普通人”的形象。“蜘蛛侠”是一个问题少年，他必须明白能力越大，责任越大；克里斯蒂安·贝尔饰演的蝙蝠侠是一个饱受折磨的灵魂，他试图通过做错事来做正确的事；而所有X战警和X女战士都是被超能力诅咒的普通人。他们和我们一样，都是普通人，却被卷入危险之中，不得不学习如何在身穿紧身衣和披风的情况下生存下来。最近，像绿巨人、《超人归来》和《绿灯侠》这类超人式的超级英雄似乎不太受观众欢迎。观众似乎更喜欢看像“美国队长”这样的平民英雄……这对新版“超人”来说可不是什么好兆头。


The great thing about Everyman Heroes is that the roles allow for more depth and character, and that means a non-action actor like Jake Gyllenhaal can step into the role. More casting options gives your screenplay a better chance of making it to the screen. With the exception of Jason Statham we seem to have a real shortage of tough guy actors these days. There don’t seem to be any new Lee Marvins and Jimmy Cagneys and Charles Bronsons in the pipeline right now, and audiences seem to prefer the more vulnerable and identifiable action leads. Because that might change while this book is on your shelf, let’s talk a bit about...

“平民英雄”的妙处在于，这类角色赋予了人物更深层次的内涵和个性，这意味着像杰克·吉伦哈尔这样的非动作片演员也能胜任。更多的选角选择意味着你的剧本更有可能被搬上银幕。除了杰森·斯坦森之外，如今我们似乎真的缺少硬汉演员。目前似乎没有新的李·马文、吉米·卡格尼或查尔斯·布朗森涌现，而观众似乎更喜欢那些更脆弱、更易于产生共鸣的动作片主角。因为这种情况或许会在你读完这本书之前发生改变，所以我们不妨来聊聊……


#↩

BAD ASS HEROES

超酷英雄


Though they’d probably rather die than put on a pair of tights, the Bad Ass Hero is part of the Superman Type. A fantasy character who will take on an entire gang with his bare hands and never show a trace of fear or self-doubt. You know all of those Chuck Norris jokes? Those are all about him being a Bad Ass Hero. These are super heroes in the real world - and we wish we were them.

虽然他们可能宁愿死也不愿穿上紧身衣，但这种“硬汉英雄”其实属于超人类型。他们是幻想中的人物，能赤手空拳对抗一整帮恶棍，而且从不流露出丝毫恐惧或自我怀疑。你听过所有关于查克·诺里斯的笑话吗？那些笑话都是在说他是个“硬汉英雄”。这些是现实世界中的超级英雄——而我们也希望自己能成为他们。


A Bad Ass Hero might be surrounded by a dozen bad guys and make a little speech or explain exactly how he’s going to whop all of them at once, then spring into action and kick all of their asses and stroll away. That’s what Billy Jack and Steven Seagal used to do. Other Bad Ass Heroes are men of few words - they skip the speech and just kick everyone’s ass, then grab a burger and a beer. These guys are the blue collar version of James Bond - they’re tough, they say clever things we wish we could think of (“Go ahead, make my day”), they’re ultra-confident, they are never afraid (or never show their fear), and they never show any sign of weakness or show pain. These are the kind of guys who get shot and take it like a man. Men of violence who *hurt people*. Even though Seagal swiped his character from “Billy Jack”, but did a great job with it. Seagal *breaks people’s bones* in fight scenes - he’s savage.

一个硬汉英雄可能会被十几个坏蛋包围，然后发表一番演说，或者详细解释他将如何一举击败他们，接着立刻行动，把他们全部揍趴下，扬长而去。比利·杰克和史蒂文·西格尔以前就是这么做的。另一些硬汉英雄则寡言少语——他们省略了演说，直接把所有人揍趴下，然后去吃汉堡喝啤酒。这些人就像蓝领版的詹姆斯·邦德——他们强悍，会说出我们梦寐以求的妙语（“来吧，让我高兴高兴”），他们超级自信，从不畏惧（或者从不显露恐惧），也从不示弱或表现出痛苦。他们是那种即使中枪也能像个男人一样承受伤害的硬汉。他们是暴力之人，会伤害别人。尽管西格尔的角色借鉴了“比利·杰克”，但他演绎得非常出色。西格尔在打斗场面中会打断别人的骨头——他是个狠角色。


One element of being a Bad Ass Hero is not being overly fancy - if the martial arts looks too much like ballet, they aren’t a bad ass anymore. Seagal did that Bad Ass Hero speech thing - where he gives his super confident warning about how, exactly, he will beat the crap out of the ten guys surrounding him. No fear - he has it all planned out. He doesn’t do any fancy moves, he *hurts them* in the most direct way he can. He’s a Bad Ass.

成为真正的硬汉英雄，关键在于不要过于花哨——如果武术动作看起来太像芭蕾，那就称不上硬汉了。西格尔就做过那种硬汉英雄式的演讲——他自信满满地警告说，他会如何把围在他身边的十个人揍得落花流水。他毫无畏惧，一切都在他的计划之中。他没有花哨的招式，而是用最直接的方式*痛击*他们。他才是真正的硬汉。


Liam Neeson is a Bad Ass in Luc Besson & Robert Mark Kamen’s “Taken”, Denzel is a Bad Ass in Gary Whitta’s “The Book Of Eli”, but for whatever reason Mel Gibson softened the lead character in Brian Helgeland’s “Payback” and turned him into an everyman... which went against the grain of the story. The key to a Bad Ass Hero is mystery - not knowing too much about him or her, which would make them human (and not superman). The Man With No Name drifts into town and shoots a lot of people. Where did he come from? Why is he doing this? What’s his name? The more we remove the mystery the less of a fantasy figure the Bad Ass Hero becomes. It’s okay to know that Dirty Harry’s wife was killed by a drunk driver - that is more a “character shading moment” than a motivation for Harry to stomp on the Scorpio Killer’s wounded leg. Maybe her death is what caused him to lose his last trace of humanity? A Bad Ass Hero is *not* human, they are supermen (and women) who don’t wear their emotions on their sleeves and don’t seem to feel pain or anger or kindness. Like Chuck Norris, they just kick ass.

利亚姆·尼森在吕克·贝松和罗伯特·马克·卡门的《飓风营救》中是个狠角色，丹泽尔·华盛顿在加里·惠塔的《艾利之书》中也是个狠角色，但不知为何，梅尔·吉布森在布莱恩·海尔格兰德的《复仇》中却软化了主角，把他变成了一个普通人……这与故事的基调背道而驰。一个狠角色英雄的关键在于神秘感——对他或她了解不多，这样才能让他们显得更有人情味（而不是超人）。“无名氏”来到小镇，大开杀戒。他从哪里来？他为什么要这么做？他叫什么名字？我们越是揭开谜团，狠角色英雄就越不像个虚构人物。知道“肮脏的哈里”的妻子是被酒驾司机撞死的，这没什么大不了的——这与其说是哈里踩在“天蝎杀手”受伤的腿上的动机，不如说是“人物性格刻画”。或许正是她的死让他彻底丧失了人性？真正的超级英雄*并非*人类，他们是超人（无论男女），不轻易流露情感，似乎感受不到痛苦、愤怒或善良。就像查克·诺里斯一样，他们只会横扫一切。


#↩

KRYPTONITE

氪石


One important thing to remember when creating your hero, even if he’s a Bad Ass, is that they can't be invincible. I read a script where the hero shot six armed bad guys in the opening scene. Great, but where does it go from there? In the final scene where the hero and the villain face off in town square (it was a western) I already knew the hero was the quicker draw and the writer hadn’t established any special skills or tricks for the villain. Where was the suspense? Where was the conflict? Why should I care? The script was boring and predictable, because the hero could not be beaten. He was too Bad Ass!

塑造英雄时，即便他是个狠角色，也要记住一点：他不可能无敌。我读过一个剧本，开头英雄就干掉了六个持枪歹徒。这很精彩，但接下来剧情该怎么发展呢？在最后英雄和反派在城镇广场决战的场景（这是一部西部片）中，我已经知道英雄拔枪更快，而编剧并没有给反派安排任何特殊技能或招式。悬念何在？冲突何在？我为什么要关心？剧本枯燥乏味，毫无悬念，因为英雄根本打不过。他太厉害了！


Remember, villains must always be stronger or smarter than the hero. In the good James Bond films, the villain is a father figure to Bond. He talks condescendingly to Bond. When Bond points out that flaw in Goldfinger's plan to rob Fort Knox, Goldfinger already knows you can't transport that much gold by truck in a single day... In fact, Goldfinger's plan hinges on it. Bond is no match for Goldfinger at this point.

记住，反派必须比英雄更强大或更聪明。在优秀的詹姆斯·邦德电影中，反派往往是邦德的“父亲”般的人物。他总是居高临下地和邦德说话。当邦德指出戈德芬格抢劫诺克斯堡计划中的漏洞时，戈德芬格其实早就知道一天之内不可能用卡车运送那么多黄金……事实上，戈德芬格的计划就建立在这个漏洞之上。此时的邦德根本不是戈德芬格的对手。


He's also no match for Odd Job. In the Bond films, the lead henchman is physically stronger than Bond. We'll talk more about henchmen in a later chapter, but it's important to note than in every good James Bond film, the villain is smarter than Bond and the lead henchman is stronger than Bond. Bond is clearly the underdog... even though he is a Superman Type.

他根本不是奥德乔布的对手。在邦德电影中，头号反派的体格都比邦德强壮。我们会在后面的章节详细讨论反派角色，但值得注意的是，在每一部优秀的詹姆斯·邦德电影中，反派都比邦德更聪明，头号反派的体格也比邦德更强壮。邦德显然处于劣势……即使他拥有超人般的超能力。


The Hero needs to be the underdog or the movie will be over in 5 minutes... or boring for the next 105 minutes. If every time the hero gets surrounded by badguys, he can easily kick their asses... boooring! The villain need some way to defeat the hero. Superman is stronger than anyone else in the world, but his nemesis Lex Luthor always manages to find a big chunk of Kryptonite before he embarks on one of his schemes, making Superman vulnerable. Every Bad Ass hero needs an Achilles heel or someone bigger and stronger and meaner they eventually have to fight against (like the late great Robert Tessier) or some plan by the villain that makes the outcome of the struggle unpredictable. If your Bad Ass Hero is the fastest draw in the west, there needs to be some legendary retired gunfighter who was twice as fast and shows up at the end. Our fantasy of being the ultra tough guy stops working if there are no challenges. Figure out what the “kryptonite” is and then start building its legend in your story so that the audience worries your hero might have to deal with it... and then their fears come true.

英雄必须是弱者，否则电影五分钟就结束了……或者接下来的105分钟会很无聊。如果每次英雄被坏人包围，他都能轻松把他们揍趴下……那就太无聊了！反派需要有办法打败英雄。超人比世界上任何人都强，但他的宿敌莱克斯·卢瑟总能在实施阴谋之前找到一大块氪石，让超人变得脆弱。每个酷炫的英雄都需要一个致命弱点，或者一个更强大、更凶狠的对手（比如已故的伟大演员罗伯特·泰西尔），或者反派会设计一些让战斗结果难以预料的计谋。如果你的酷炫英雄是西部拔枪最快的人，那么最后就需要出现一位速度是他两倍的传奇退休枪手。如果没有挑战，我们对超级硬汉的幻想就无法成立。找出“氪星石”是什么，然后在你的故事中开始构建它的传说，让观众担心你的英雄可能会遇到它……然后他们的担忧变成了现实。


Your Hero probably isn’t stronger than Villain, they are just more dedicated and more willing to take risks for what they believe in. If your villain isn't stronger than your hero, there's no challenge, no suspense, and no reason for the audience to buy a ticket in order to find out what happens next.

你的英雄可能并不比反派更强大，他们只是更执着，更愿意为了自己的信念承担风险。如果你的反派不如你的英雄强大，那就没有挑战性，没有悬念，观众也就没有理由买票去看接下来的剧情了。


#↩

MIRROR IMAGES/FLIP SIDES

镜像/翻转面


Heroes and Villains are frequently linked. Belloq tells Indiana Jones: "You and I are very much alike... Our methods are not different as much as you pretend. I am a shadowy reflection of you. It would take only a nudge to make you like me; to push you out of the light." and in "The Empire Strikes Back" (also written by Lawrence Kasdan) Darth gives a similar speech to Luke.

英雄与反派之间常常存在着某种联系。贝洛克对印第安纳·琼斯说：“你和我非常相似……我们的手段并没有你想象的那么不同。我是你的影子。只需轻轻一推，你就会变得像我一样；把你推离光明。”而在《星球大战：帝国反击战》（同样由劳伦斯·卡斯丹编剧）中，达斯·维达也对卢克发表了类似的言论。


Heroes and Villains linked this way are called "Flipsides". This device goes back as far as "Manhattan Melodrama" (1934) where the gangster and the District Attorney were childhood friends. Heroes and Villains often share the same destination, but are traveling separate roads. "Strangers On A Train" actually begins by showing us two sets of train tracks merging together, then shows us two sets of shoes walking from opposite directions to the lounge car. Both men share the same desire, to kill a relative; but Bruno (the villain) will act on his desire while Guy (the hero) realizes that murder is impolite.

以这种方式联系在一起的英雄和反派被称为“对立面”。这种手法可以追溯到1934年的《曼哈顿旋律》，片中的黑帮分子和地方检察官是儿时的朋友。英雄和反派往往有着相同的目标，但却走着不同的道路。《火车怪客》的开头展现了两条铁轨交汇的画面，然后镜头转向两双分别从相反方向走向餐车的鞋子。两人都渴望杀死自己的亲人；但布鲁诺（反派）会付诸行动，而盖伊（英雄）则意识到杀人是不礼貌的。


Hitchcock uses flipsides in many of his films. In "Frenzy" the hero, Richard Blaney, shares the same initials as the villain, Bob Rusk... But the initials are flipped. Like "Manhattan Melodrama", Rusk and Blaney are childhood friends... only one of them is a serial killer and the other is the police's prime suspect... And the only one who can stop the killer from striking again.

希区柯克在他的许多电影中都运用了反转手法。在《狂凶记》中，主人公理查德·布莱尼和反派鲍勃·拉斯克的首字母相同……但顺序颠倒了。和《曼哈顿旋律》一样，拉斯克和布莱尼是儿时的朋友……只不过其中一人是连环杀手，另一人是警方的头号嫌疑人……也是唯一能阻止杀手再次作案的人。


I used a similar device in my script for "The Base", about a disgraced Marine named Ronald L. Murphy given the assignment of infiltrating a secret society on a Marine Base. The secret society is run by the charismatic Sgt. Marty L. Rackin. Hero and villain share more than the same initials, both are searching for father figures, both have troubled pasts, neither is good at following orders, both have trouble with authority figures. Once undercover, Murphy becomes Rackin's best friend... practically his brother. They are flipsides. When Murphy discovers that Rackin's secret society is running drugs on base (and worse), he must turn against his own surrogate brother, betray him, in order to complete his mission. Too bad they changed all of that before filming it!

我在为电影《基地》写的剧本里也用了类似的桥段。故事讲述的是一个名叫罗纳德·L·墨菲的落魄海军陆战队员，奉命潜入一个海军陆战队基地的秘密社团。这个秘密社团由魅力十足的马蒂·L·拉金中士领导。英雄和反派不仅名字首字母相同，而且有很多共同点：他们都在寻找父亲般的角色，都有着不堪回首的过去，都不擅长服从命令，也都难以与权威人士相处。潜入后，墨菲成了拉金最好的朋友……几乎就像亲兄弟一样。他们性格截然相反。当墨菲发现拉金的秘密社团在基地贩毒（甚至更糟）时，为了完成任务，他不得不背叛自己如同亲兄弟般的拉金。可惜的是，他们在拍摄前把这些都改了！


#↩

TO DESTROY HIM

毁灭他

#↩

I MUST BECOME HIM!

我必须成为他！


Even if the hero isn't the villain's flipside, the hero often must become the villain in order to conquer him. A by-the-rules cop has to go renegade ("The Big Heat") or a meek everyman must become a warrior ("Straw Dogs"), the hero usually crosses the line into the villain territory before he can vanquish him. Often there is a physical transformation as well. In Oliver Stone's "Platoon" Charlie Sheen's face becomes scarred throughout the film, until he resembles Tom Beringer (the villain). In "Apocalypse Now" and "Predator" the heroes paint themselves to resemble the villains before they go into battle against them. In "Predator", the creature chameleons to look like the forest; and before the final battle Ah-nuld coats himself with mud and leaves, becoming almost invisible in some shots. In "Face/Off" John Travolta must not only take Nick Cage's face to vanquish him, he must also live Nick Cage's life!

即使英雄并非反派的对立面，为了战胜反派，英雄往往也必须变成反派。一个循规蹈矩的警察必须叛逆（《大热》），一个温顺的普通人必须成为战士（《稻草狗》），英雄通常在击败反派之前，都会越过界限，进入反派的领域。通常，英雄还会经历身体上的转变。在奥利弗·斯通的《野战排》中，查理·辛的脸在整部电影中逐渐伤痕累累，最终变得像反派汤姆·贝林格。在《现代启示录》和《铁血战士》中，英雄们在与反派决战前，会把自己涂成反派的样子。在《铁血战士》中，怪物会伪装成森林的模样；而在最终决战前，阿诺·施瓦辛格用泥土和树叶涂满全身，在某些镜头中几乎隐形。在《变脸》中，约翰·特拉沃尔塔不仅要夺取尼古拉斯·凯奇的脸来战胜他，还要过尼古拉斯·凯奇的生活！


Christopher Nolan’s “The Dark Knight” is a great example of a hero who must become the villain in order to conquer him. The Joker is an anarchist with no pattern and no motive except destruction. Alfred tells him a story about a bandit in Burma who threw away whatever he stole, “Some men aren’t looking for anything logical, like money. They can’t be bought, bullied, reasoned or negotiated with. Some men just want to watch the world burn.” The Joker is such a man. Batman asks how they finally caught the bandit. “We burned the forest down.” They burned his world. Both Batman and District Attorney Harvey Dent become villains in the course of the story, and do terrible things to stop The Joker. At one point, Dent says, “You either die a hero, or live long enough to see yourself become the villain.” Heroes and Villains are often very similar, and the little things that make them different are the most critical parts of their characters. What are those differences in your story?

克里斯托弗·诺兰的《黑暗骑士》就是一个很好的例子，讲述了一个英雄为了战胜反派，必须先堕落成反派的故事。小丑是一个无政府主义者，他没有任何行为模式，除了破坏之外别无动机。阿尔弗雷德给他讲了一个缅甸土匪的故事，这个土匪会把偷来的东西全部扔掉。“有些人追求的不是金钱之类的东西，而是他们无法被收买、胁迫、讲道理或谈判。有些人只想看着世界毁灭。”小丑就是这样的人。蝙蝠侠问他们最终是如何抓住那个土匪的。“我们烧毁了森林。”他们烧毁了他的世界。在故事中，蝙蝠侠和地方检察官哈维·丹特都变成了反派，为了阻止小丑，他们做了可怕的事情。丹特曾说过：“你要么英勇就义，要么苟活到亲眼目睹自己变成反派。”英雄和反派往往非常相似，而那些细微的差别恰恰是他们角色最关键的部分。在你的故事里，这些差别又是什么呢？


#↩

OPPOSITES REACT

异性相反应


Sometimes it's not the similarities between heroes and villains, but the differences that are important. In "Die Hard" Bruce Willis is a hard working blue collar every day guy, and Alan Rickman is a suave tailored over educated snob. There is an underlying theme of working class struggle in "Die Hard" which links it to the social message films Warner Brothers was famous for in the 1930s, like "Captain Blood". When Willis and Rickman tangle at the end, it's working stiffs like you and me against a profit hungry corporate raider (literally). In this case you are showing the difference in values between your characters and this will tie directly into your theme (the point of your story or aspect of the human condition you are exploring). If your protagonist is logical and level headed and your antagonist is angry and emotional, that difference is secretly what your story is about. If you have a hero who forgives and a villain who holds a grudge, that’s the aspect of the human condition you are exploring. This is why you need to consider the relationship between hero and villain carefully.

有时候，英雄和反派之间的相似之处并不重要，重要的是他们的差异。《虎胆龙威》中，布鲁斯·威利斯饰演的是一个辛勤工作的蓝领工人，而艾伦·里克曼则饰演了一个衣着考究、举止优雅的势利眼。影片中蕴含着工人阶级斗争的主题，这与华纳兄弟在20世纪30年代以《铁血船长》等影片而闻名的社会题材电影有着异曲同工之妙。当威利斯和里克曼在影片结尾展开对决时，正是像你我一样的普通劳动者对抗一个唯利是图的企业掠夺者（字面意义上的）。在这种情况下，你展现了角色之间价值观的差异，而这将直接与你的主题（故事的核心或你所探讨的人性层面）联系起来。如果你的主角逻辑清晰、冷静沉着，而你的反派愤怒易怒，那么这种差异正是你故事的真正核心所在。如果你塑造了一个宽恕他人的英雄和一个怀恨在心的反派，那么这就是你所探讨的人性层面。所以，你需要仔细考虑英雄和反派之间的关系。


Analyze the similarities and differences between your hero and villain. They are the two most important characters in your script. You should know as much as you can about them before you begin writing. If you haven't spent the time developing their relationship and characters you may end up with an unsatisfying action script... And audiences won't care about the cool fight scenes.

分析你的英雄和反派之间的异同。他们是剧本中最重要的两个角色。在动笔之前，你应该尽可能多地了解他们。如果你没有花时间去塑造他们的关系和性格，最终可能会写出一个令人失望的动作剧本……而观众也不会在意那些炫酷的打斗场面。


#↩

IT TAKES TWO TO TANGLE

纠缠不清需要两个人


One of the most common questions I get is, “Can my Hero be my Villain?” That question can be taken two ways: in some sort of weird split personality thing the hero discovers he’s the villain at the end, or can the hero be a bad person?

我最常被问到的问题之一是：“我的英雄可以成为我的反派吗？”这个问题有两种理解方式：一种是英雄在某种奇怪的人格分裂的情况下，最终发现自己是反派；另一种是英雄本身可以是坏人。


Let’s begin with the first version: aside from this being the #2 screenplay cliche (after some form of “it was all a dream” - Chuck Norris waking up next to Suzanne Pleschette or Clint Eastwood in the shower fantasizing) it’s almost impossible to pull off on screen. An action film requires physical action, and how do the hero and villain fight if they are the same person? “Fight Club” turns them into two different characters, our hero and Tyler Durden, so that they can actually fight on screen and can have big dramatic battles along the way... but when it is exposed at the end that they are the same dude, you wonder how our hero could punch himself so hard - and in places where he couldn’t actually reach on himself. And that’s the one that worked!

我们先来说说第一个版本：除了这是第二大老套的剧本桥段（仅次于某种形式的“一切都是梦”——比如查克·诺里斯醒来发现自己身边躺着苏珊娜·普莱谢特，或者克林特·伊斯特伍德在淋浴时幻想），这种情节几乎不可能在大银幕上实现。动作片需要肢体动作，如果英雄和反派是同一个人，他们该如何打斗呢？《搏击俱乐部》将他们设定为两个不同的角色，我们的英雄和泰勒·德顿，这样他们才能在银幕上真正地打斗，并一路上上演精彩的戏剧性战斗……但当最后揭晓他们是同一个人时，你会好奇我们的英雄是如何把自己打得那么狠——而且还是打到他自己根本够不到的地方。而这居然是成功的版本！


#↩

I'M THE BAD GUY?

我是坏人吗？


The problem with Hero Is Villain is that it usually out-clevers itself. In order to hide that the hero is also the villain, you have to do some sort of “cheat” to create the fight scenes and car chases and shoot outs and other physical action. This sort of thing can be done in a novel where you can trick the reader into believing that the same person is two different characters, like in William Goldman’s novel “Marathon Man” where Doc and Scylla end up being the same person in a great twist... but in Goldman’s screenplay version that twist is dropped completely. The characters are fused into one, because if we see Scylla The Assassin (played by Roy Scheider) and then see Doc The Nice Businessman (played by Roy Scheider), even the dumbest guy in the audience will figure out they are the same person. The amount of “cheats” required to make Hero Is Villain work almost guarantees that it will not work. Plus, why go through all of the trouble of having the villain pretend to be the hero? It’s kind of a cheap trick just to create a mind blower twist at the end. Oh, let me note that “Fight Club” also began as a novel, where this sort of thing works.

“英雄即反派”的问题在于它通常会弄巧成拙。为了掩盖英雄同时也是反派的事实，你必须耍一些“花招”来制造打斗、追车、枪战和其他动作场面。这种手法在小说中或许行得通，你可以让读者误以为同一个人是两个不同的角色，比如威廉·戈德曼的小说《马拉松人》，小说中“医生”和“斯库拉”最终揭晓为同一个人，剧情出现了精彩的反转……但在戈德曼的剧本版本中，这个反转被完全放弃了。两个角色被融合为一体，因为如果我们先看到“刺客斯库拉”（罗伊·施奈德饰演），然后再看到“和蔼的商人医生”（罗伊·施奈德饰演），即使是最笨的观众也能看出他们是同一个人。“英雄即反派”这种手法需要如此多的“花招”，几乎注定了它最终会失败。而且，何必费尽心思让反派假扮英雄呢？这不过是故弄玄虚，为了在结尾制造一个令人震惊的反转。哦，对了，我还要补充一点，《搏击俱乐部》最初也是一部小说，这种手法在小说里是行得通的。


Add to that, the audience does a “skin jump” into the protagonist of your script. For two hours, they “become” the hero and live the adventure of your story vicariously. Movies are the grown up version of “let’s pretend”, and we may not strap on a cap gun and plastic badge, but we still imagine that we are the hero up there on screen. If we have been the hero for 105 minutes and then you suddenly tell us we are really the villain, we are not going to like that... and probably end up hating the movie. There are a couple of movies that pull this off other than “Fight Club” - “The Verdict” (1946) and the best mystery film ever made, “The Last Of Sheila” (1973).

此外，观众会“感同身受”地进入你剧本的主角。在两个小时里，他们“变成”了英雄，间接地体验着你故事中的冒险。电影是成人版的“角色扮演”，我们或许不会戴上玩具枪和塑料徽章，但我们仍然会想象自己就是银幕上的英雄。如果我们扮演了105分钟的英雄，然后你突然告诉我们，我们其实是反派，我们肯定不会喜欢……而且很可能会讨厌这部电影。除了《搏击俱乐部》之外，还有几部电影也做到了这一点——《大审判》（1946）和史上最佳悬疑片《希拉之死》（1973）。


Both films have *two* lead characters - a Holmes and Watson - so that when one is revealed as the villain, we are still able to identify with the other... and the betrayal we feel is the same betrayal that other character feels. In both cases it’s the genius Holmes-like character who is revealed to be the killer and the Watson-like character (who is easier for us to identify with) who figures it out at the end.

两部电影都有两个主角——福尔摩斯和华生——这样，当其中一个被揭露为反派时，我们仍然能够认同另一个……我们感受到的背叛，也是另一个角色所感受到的背叛。在这两部电影中，都是天才般的福尔摩斯式人物被揭露为凶手，而华生式人物（我们更容易认同他）则在最后识破了真相。


In “The Last Of Sheila”, Richard Benjamin’s screenwriter is the Holmes-like character who figures it all out with the help of James Mason’s director... But Mason has one problem with Benjamin’s explanation and is playing around with forensic evidence... and realizes that the only other way it adds up is if Benjamin is the killer. So we have *partner* detectives for the entire film, and at the end the story passes the lead from the partners to Mason, so that we are identifying with him when it’s revealed that Benjamin is the killer.

在《希拉之死》中，理查德·本杰明的编剧就像福尔摩斯一样，在詹姆斯·梅森饰演的导演的帮助下，最终揭开了所有谜团……但梅森对本杰明的解释有所怀疑，他仔细研究了法医证据……最终意识到，如果本杰明就是凶手，那么所有证据就都说得通了。因此，整部电影中都有两位搭档侦探，而到了结尾，故事将线索从搭档转移到了梅森身上，当真相揭晓，本杰明就是凶手时，观众的视角自然而然地会与梅森产生共鸣。


Both films also have a strong antagonist who is not the killer. This gives the team someone to fight against, so that we can have physical struggle and dramatic scenes along the way. In “The Last Of Sheila”, James Coburn’s producer character is a complete jerk - and his cruelty lingers in scenes where he’s not on the screen. Because his cruel game leads to the murder, he is a great antagonist before the murder... and after. Mason can't have a conflict with the actual killer during the story, so we need an adversary to battle... and that means an antagonist who is not the killer.

两部电影都塑造了一个强大的反派角色，但他并非真正的凶手。这使得团队有了可以对抗的对象，从而得以展现肢体冲突和戏剧性的场景。在《希拉之死》中，詹姆斯·柯本饰演的制片人是个十足的混蛋——即使他不在银幕上，他的残忍也挥之不去。因为他的残酷游戏最终导致了谋杀，所以他在谋杀发生前和发生后都是一个出色的反派角色。梅森在故事中无法与真正的凶手正面交锋，所以我们需要一个对手来对抗……这意味着需要一个并非凶手的反派角色。


The three keys to “detective is the killer” plots are:

“侦探就是凶手”这类情节的三大关键要素是：


1) Partners, with the Watson character as our identification and the Holmes character as the killer.

1）搭档，以华生为我们的化身，以福尔摩斯为凶手。

2) A strong antagonist who is not the killer, but who the team can tangle with throughout the story giving us physical and dramatic conflict.

2）一个强大的反派角色，他不是凶手，但团队可以在整个故事中与他纠缠，给我们带来身体和戏剧性的冲突。

3) The killer is revealed at the very end, after the baton has been passed to the Watson character.

3）凶手在影片结尾才揭晓，此时接力棒已经交给了华生这个角色。


#↩

HISTORY OF VIOLENCE

暴力史


Another sort of Hero Is Villain deals with stories where the Hero has a dark past - they *used to be* a villain - and that past catches up with them in the story, forcing them to decide what color hat to buy. Movies like “Salt” with Angelina Jolie, “Unknown” with Liam Neeson, and “A History Of Violence” with Viggo Mortensen show us characters who used to be villains but are now heroes - and play the hero role in the story. Deciding if these characters are heroes or villains may be confusing at first, but look at what they do *in the present day story* - Evelyn Salt may be a Russian sleeper agent, but in the story she fights the spy ring she is a part of. This version of Hero Is Villain works really well, creating a flawed protagonist dealing with not only their dark past but the temptation to return to it. Probably has its roots in those retired gunfighter westerns.

另一种“英雄即反派”的设定，讲述的是英雄有着一段黑暗的过去——他们曾经是反派——而这段过去在故事中如影随形，迫使他们做出抉择。像安吉丽娜·朱莉主演的《特工绍特》、利亚姆·尼森主演的《不明身份》以及维戈·莫滕森主演的《暴力史》这样的电影，都展现了曾经是反派如今却成为英雄的角色，并在故事中扮演着英雄的角色。乍一看，这些角色究竟是英雄还是反派或许令人困惑，但看看他们在故事的当下做了什么——伊芙琳·绍特或许是一名潜伏的俄罗斯特工，但在故事中，她却与自己所属的间谍组织展开了斗争。这种“英雄即反派”的设定非常成功，塑造了一个有缺陷的主角，他不仅要面对自己黑暗的过去，还要应对重蹈覆辙的诱惑。这种设定或许源于那些以退休枪手为主角的西部片。


#↩

BAD GUY LEADS

反派主角


The other version of the question can be translated to: Can the protagonist be a criminal? The answer to that is: Hell yes! I’ve been using “Hero” and “Villain” in this book, but really we’re talking about protagonist and antagonists... and there is no moral or legal requirements involved in being a protagonist, you just have to be the lead character. There are many action films with Bad Guy Lead characters: heist movies, prison films, gangster films, Film Noir, revenge films, hit man movies, and probably a dozen other subgenres. We often have dark fantasies and wish we could do very bad things for two hours, and when the lights come up we are not wanted by the law in seven states or dead on the street in a pool of blood.

这个问题的另一种说法是：主角可以是罪犯吗？答案是：当然可以！我在这本书里一直用“英雄”和“反派”这两个词，但实际上我们讨论的是主角和反派……成为主角并没有什么道德或法律上的要求，你只需要是故事的主角就行了。有很多动作片都是以反派为主角：抢劫片、监狱片、黑帮片、黑色电影、复仇片、杀手片，以及其他十几种子类型。我们常常会有一些黑暗的幻想，希望自己能做两个小时的坏事，而当灯光亮起时，我们既不会被七个州通缉，也不会死在血泊中。


A potential issue with Bad Guy Leads and other anti-hero movies is loss of audience involvement. Even if your lead is a vicious killer, the audience needs to become involved in your story and care about the outcome. Two great tools you can use to accomplish this are *Understandable Motivations* and *Values & Moral Codes*.

以反派为主角的反英雄电影可能存在的一个问题是观众缺乏参与感。即使你的主角是个凶残的杀手，观众也需要投入到故事中，关心故事的结局。实现这一点的两个有效方法是：*合理的动机*和*价值观与道德准则*。


#↩

UNDERSTANDABLE

可以理解


We don’t have to “like” a protagonist, but we usually need to understand their motivations. Don’t assume the audience will just go along for the ride, take us inside the story so that we understand the protagonist’s motivations. This is easier with a straight ahead revenge film like “Colombiana” or “Faster” or “Get Carter” or the 70's crime film “The Outfit” where Robert Duvall gets out of prison and goes gunning for the mob boss who ordered his brother’s murder. When your brother is murdered you do something about it... something violent. But your protagonist doesn’t need something corny like a sister who needs an operation to make them “likeable”, Tony Montoya in “Scarface” (either version) is a immigrant to the United States just trying to make it to the top, just trying to live the “American Dream”, and using chainsaws and machineguns to achieve this. We may not agree with his methods, but we understand his motivations - we all want a better life for ourselves and our families. If the audience understands why the protagonist is doing these terrible things, they may not like them but they will hang out with them for a couple of hours.

我们不必“喜欢”主角，但通常需要理解他们的动机。不要想当然地认为观众会顺着剧情走，要带领我们深入故事，理解主角的动机。像《哥伦比亚人》、《速度与激情》、《卡特探员》或70年代犯罪片《黑帮老大》（罗伯特·杜瓦尔饰演）这样的直白复仇电影更容易做到这一点。在《黑帮老大》中，杜瓦尔饰演的角色出狱后，便开始追杀下令杀害他兄弟的黑帮老大。当你的兄弟被谋杀时，你会采取行动……采取暴力手段。但你的主角不需要像“需要整容才能讨人喜欢”那样老套的情节，比如《疤面煞星》（无论哪个版本）中的托尼·蒙托亚，他是一个来到美国的移民，一心只想出人头地，实现“美国梦”，为此他不惜使用电锯和机枪。我们或许不认同他的做法，但我们理解他的动机——我们都渴望为自己和家人创造更美好的生活。如果观众理解主人公为何要做出这些可怕的事情，他们或许并不喜欢这些事，但也会愿意花几个小时陪伴他们。


Professional criminal leads like Roberts DeNiro in “Heat” and Duvall in “The Outfit” are anti-heroes - protagonists on the wrong side of the law. Bad Guy Leads.
