If the museum curator was behind the theft on page 97, he was behind it on page 10... and didn’t need the childhood friend, the con man or the cat burglar babe.

虽然剧本里的所有事件发生时都合情合理，但当我们把那些“巧妙”的情节转折都一一呈现后，整个故事就变得毫无逻辑可言了。这是因为故事就像洋葱一样，层层叠叠，层层剥开，我们才能逐渐接近真相。作为编剧，我们必须了解表面之下的东西。这就是我们写大纲的原因——这样我们才能了解剧本的每个层面，而不仅仅是表面。我们将在下一章讨论大纲，但最好的方法始终是从内而外地构思剧本。如果博物馆馆长是第97页盗窃案的幕后黑手，那么他在第10页就已经是了……根本不需要什么儿时好友、骗子或者女飞贼。


Stories are about revealing information, and that means you have to know what the underlying truth is and build your story from there. In a way you’re going to plot your story several times: once when you create the core story, and once for each level where information is revealed until you come to the surface of the story. Your surface plotting has to make sense and hang together as much as every layer beneath it. Every time we pull back a layer, the story must still make sense. The plotting must still hold up. If you’re making up the story as you go along, either you end up with a story that’s all surface where nothing is revealed or you run the risk of revealing things that just don’t make any sense.

故事的本质在于揭示信息，这意味着你必须了解其背后的真相，并以此为基础构建故事。某种程度上，你需要多次构思故事：第一次是在构建核心故事时，第二次则是在揭示信息的每一层时进行构思，直到最终揭开故事的真相。你构建的表层情节必须逻辑清晰、环环相扣，与它之下的每一层都一样。每次揭开一层，故事都必须保持逻辑性，情节必须经得起推敲。如果你边写边编故事，最终要么会得到一个只有表面、没有揭示任何实质内容的故事，要么就会冒着揭示一些根本站不住脚的信息的风险。


It’s important to know every level of the story when you are writing the screenplay. In the movie "Ghost", on the surface of the story Sam (Patrick Swayze) has a girlfriend named Molly (Demi Moore) and a best friend named Carl (Tony Goldwyn). One night Sam is shot by a mugger and dies... becoming a ghost. But when we peel back layers, we discover Sam’s killer has a key to his apartment... and Sam’s killer was paid by somebody to steal something from Sam... and Sam’s killer is now coming after Molly... and the guy who paid Sam’s killer is... Carl! What’s more, Carl has been using the bank where they work to launder money. That scene a couple of minutes into the film where Carl asks Sam for his secret computer code? - part of the money-laundering scheme!

在创作剧本时，了解故事的各个层面至关重要。在电影《人鬼情未了》中，故事表面上讲述的是山姆（帕特里克·斯威兹饰）有一个名叫莫莉（黛米·摩尔饰）的女友和一个名叫卡尔（托尼·戈德温饰）的挚友。一天晚上，山姆被劫匪枪杀身亡……变成了鬼魂。但当我们层层剥开故事时，会发现杀害山姆的凶手拥有他公寓的钥匙……而且凶手受雇于人，偷走了山姆的某样东西……现在，凶手又盯上了莫莉……而雇佣凶手的人竟然是……卡尔！更令人震惊的是，卡尔一直在利用他们工作的银行洗钱。影片开头几分钟，卡尔向山姆索要电脑密码的那场戏——正是洗钱计划的一部分！


When Bruce Joel Rubin wrote that scene, he probably already knew what was lurking in all of those layers down at the core of the story. He had to create the core and then build layer after logical layer until he came to the surface. Though these things might happen in rewrite if you don't outline, the problem – just like in time travel – when you change some element in the past of your script you end up changing everything else... and that means a ton of rewriting and then more rewriting and then more rewriting – and we are talking major “everything must go” rewrites! The layers all have to make sense, and each layer is what creates the next layer. Early in the film when Sam thinks it’s just the mugger breaking in to loot his apartment, that makes sense. Later in the film when Sam discovers Carl is behind it all, that also makes perfect sense. Every layer makes sense.

当布鲁斯·乔尔·鲁宾创作那场戏时，他可能已经知道故事核心层层隐藏着什么。他必须先构建核心，然后一层层地构建逻辑，直到最终揭示真相。虽然如果不事先列提纲，重写时也可能出现这种情况，但问题在于——就像穿越时空一样——当你改变剧本过去某个情节时，最终会影响到其他所有方面……这意味着大量的重写，一遍又一遍地重写——而且是那种“全部推翻重写”的大改！每一层都必须逻辑自洽，每一层都为下一层奠定基础。影片开头，当山姆以为只是劫匪闯入他的公寓行窃时，这合情合理。影片后半段，当山姆发现卡尔才是幕后黑手时，这也完全说得通。每一层都自有其道理。


Plotting works layer by layer. You have to know what’s true at the core and build from there. Starting at the surface usually results in a script that doesn’t make any sense by the time you get to the end. That’s why outlines are a good idea.

构思剧本需要层层递进。你必须先了解故事的核心，然后以此为基础构建情节。如果从表面入手，最终写出来的剧本往往不知所云。这就是为什么列提纲是个好主意。


#↩

TENNIS PLOTTING

网球计划


Another way to make sure your plotting works is to think of your story as a game of tennis. The ball doesn’t just hop over the net on its own... somebody has to hit it - same thing with a story. Things don’t just happen on their own. They happen because someone causes them to happen. After that, another character reacts to that event, and that reaction knocks the ball back over the net so that the other player must react to it. The ball isn’t going back and forth on its own. Characters are hitting it!

确保情节顺利进行的另一个方法是把你的故事想象成一场网球比赛。球不会自己跳过球网……必须有人击球——故事也是如此。事情不会自行发生。它们之所以发生，是因为有人促成了它们的发生。之后，另一个角色会对事件做出反应，而这个反应又会把球击回球网，迫使对方做出反应。球不会自己来回弹跳。是角色在击球！


Usually, the antagonist serves. He creates the problem that the protagonist must solve. In Graham Yost’s "Speed", Howard (Dennis Hopper) rigs explosives to the cables of an elevator. He blows up the elevator cables, sending a car full of people into free fall... until the emergency brakes catch them... but Howard has explosives attached to the brakes, too; and he demands $3 million or he’ll send the elevator car full of passengers crashing to the basement. That’s his serve.

通常，反派扮演着“服务者”的角色。他制造问题，让主角去解决。在格雷厄姆·约斯特执导的《生死时速》中，霍华德（丹尼斯·霍珀饰）在电梯缆绳上安装了炸药。他引爆了电梯缆绳，让满载乘客的电梯坠落……直到紧急制动系统启动……但霍华德也在制动系统上安装了炸药；他索要300万美元，否则就让满载乘客的电梯坠入地下室。这就是他的“服务”。


Jack (Keanu Reeves) and the SWAT team show up to prevent the elevator car from falling. The ball is in their court, and they have to hit it back. Jack and Harry (Jeff Daniels) volunteer to check the explosives on the elevator. They discover it’s a very professional job - no way to disarm the bomb... but Jack has an idea. He takes the cable from a window-washer platform and attaches it to the elevator... the ball has been knocked back into Howard’s court.

杰克（基努·里维斯饰）和特警队赶到现场，阻止电梯坠落。主动权在他们手中，他们必须扭转局面。杰克和哈里（杰夫·丹尼尔斯饰）自告奋勇检查电梯里的炸药。他们发现这套装置非常专业——根本无法拆除……但杰克想到了一个办法。他从擦窗机上取下一根钢缆，连接到电梯上……现在主动权又回到了霍华德手中。


Howard hears them do this and blows the elevator brakes. The elevator falls... knocking the ball back into Jack’s court.

霍华德听到他们的动静，拉响了电梯刹车。电梯坠落……又把主动权交到了杰克手中。


But the elevator is stopped by the window-washer cable. Jack and Harry save the passengers. They realize that Howard blew the brakes in response to their attaching the window-washer cable... which means he’s in the building. Jack and Harry figure out he’s in the freight elevator and climb down to attack - knocking the ball back to Howard’s side of the net.

但电梯被擦窗机的钢索拦住了。杰克和哈里救出了乘客。他们意识到，霍华德因为他们绑上钢索而拉响了刹车……这意味着他已经进入了大楼。杰克和哈里发现他在货梯里，于是爬下去发起进攻——把球击回了霍华德的球门区域。


Howard captures Harry, reveals that he has explosives strapped on his body and a pressure-release trigger in his hand. He will explode himself, Harry and the whole building unless Jack drops his gun and allows Howard to escape - knocking the ball back to Jack.

霍华德抓住了哈利，并亮出他身上绑着炸药，手里拿着一个泄压阀。除非杰克放下枪，放霍华德逃走，否则他就会引爆炸弹，炸毁哈利和整栋大楼——这样一来，机会就又回到了杰克手中。


Jack shoots Harry in the legs making him a hostage that Howard must carry. How can Howard escape while carrying a guy? That knocks the ball back into Howard’s court. Howard lets go of Harry and escapes... only to explode in the building’s garage.

杰克开枪击中了哈利的腿，使他成为人质，霍华德必须背着他逃走。霍华德背着人质怎么可能逃脱？这下主动权又回到了霍华德手中。霍华德放开哈利逃走了……却在建筑物的车库里爆炸身亡。


You might think that Jack has won this round, but the explosion is Howard’s return volley. He has faked his own death in order to get away.

你或许以为杰克赢了这一局，但爆炸声却是霍华德的反击。他假装死亡，以此逃脱。


Now, if we were to look at the motivation for Howard’s elevator plan, we’d find out that he was a 30-year veteran of the Atlanta PD bomb squad who was injured in an explosion and has been denied his pension. He wants $3 million: $100,000 for every year he spent on the police force... every year he wasted in service of a police force that didn’t appreciate him. “I got a medal and a pink slip.” So Howard’s “serve” is motivated. That serve is in reaction to another action. We could trace back the actions and reactions behind being denied his money if we wanted - there would be a reason. Everything has a reason - there is no coincidence in this story.

如果我们探究霍华德电梯计划的动机，就会发现他曾是亚特兰大警察局拆弹小组的一名老兵，服役30年，在一次爆炸中受伤，退休金却被拒发。他想要300万美元：相当于他在警队服役的每一年10万美元……每一年他都浪费在了这支不领情的警队里。“我拿到了一枚奖章，却被解雇了。”所以，霍华德的“服役”是有动机的。这种“服役”是对另一件事的回应。如果我们愿意，可以追溯他被拒发退休金背后的种种行为和反应——总能找到原因。凡事皆有因——这个故事里没有巧合。


Howard still needs his pension, and now he’s mad at Jack for screwing up his plan. He spent two years setting up that job and wants the money due him. He sees Jack getting a medal on the news and decides to hit the ball back into Jack’s court...

霍华德仍然需要他的养老金，现在他因为杰克搞砸了他的计划而怒火中烧。他花了两年时间才安排好那份工作，他想要回属于他的钱。他看到新闻上杰克获得了一枚奖章，于是决定以牙还牙……


By planting a bomb on bus #2525 that will explode if the bus goes below 50 mph... he calls Jack to tell him about it. Again, this is a logical reaction to Jack’s foiling the elevator plan. He not only wants his money, but he also wants revenge against Jack for foiling his elevator plan. The ball is back in Jack’s court. Jack hops on the bus to save the passengers and foil Howard's new bus plan.

他计划在2525路公交车上安装炸弹，如果车速低于50英里/小时就会爆炸……他打电话告诉杰克这件事。这再次印证了杰克破坏电梯计划的合乎逻辑的反应。他不仅想要回自己的钱，还想报复杰克破坏了他的电梯计划。现在主动权又回到了杰克手里。杰克跳上公交车，去拯救乘客，并挫败霍华德的新巴士计划。


On the bus there are many times where they hit the ball back and forth to each other. Jack gets the injured driver off the bus, and a passenger tries to get off at the same time... so Howard sets off an explosive charge near the doors and kills the passenger. Howard's bomb will explode if the bus goes below 50 mph, and rush-hour traffic threatens to slow them down so Jack takes the bus off the freeway and onto the L.A. Airport runway where there is no traffic. Howard has a timer (attached to his gold watch) that will blow up the bus even if it continues circling the runway at 50 mph - ball back in Jack’s court. Howard seems to know exactly what is going on in the bus. Jack searches and discovers the hidden cameras on the bus. Jack has a video loop made of the passengers on the bus to fool Howard so that he can offload the passengers - ball back in Howard’s court. Back and forth - each one knocks the ball back to the other. Each event is in reaction to the one that comes before it. Nothing happens by coincidence. It’s all a result of cause and effect.

在巴士上，他们多次互相抛球。杰克把受伤的司机扶下车，与此同时，一名乘客也想下车……于是霍华德在车门附近引爆了炸弹，炸死了这名乘客。霍华德的炸弹会在巴士时速低于50英里时爆炸，而高峰时段的交通拥堵可能会让他们减速，所以杰克把巴士开离高速公路，驶入洛杉矶机场的跑道，那里没有车辆。霍华德有一个定时器（连接在他的金表上），即使巴士继续以50英里的时速绕着跑道行驶，定时器也会引爆炸弹——现在轮到杰克了。霍华德似乎对巴士上发生的一切了如指掌。杰克搜查并发现了巴士上的隐藏摄像头。杰克制作了一段循环播放的乘客视频，用来迷惑霍华德，以便让乘客下车——现在轮到霍华德了。他们你来我往，互相抛球。每一件事都是对前一件事的反应。世上没有偶然的事，一切都是因果关系的结果。


Here’s where plotting often breaks down in bad scripts - after the initial “serve” the protagonist or antagonist quit playing for a while, and the ball bounces back and forth on its own. That’s impossible, and we know it. Or, the ball is hit to some other player on some other court; and even if the ball is hit back to our court and our protagonist, it isn’t really part of the game, is it? When something (good or bad) happens without reason, it seems impossible. It’s that ball bouncing back on its own. Or, the protagonist swings his racquet and misses, but the ball hits a bird flying over the court and goes back to the antagonist’s side of the net. That just doesn’t seem within the rules!

糟糕的剧本往往在这里出现情节漏洞——在最初的“发球”之后，主角或反派会停止比赛一段时间，然后球会自己来回弹跳。这根本不可能，我们都知道。或者，球被打到其他球场的其他球员那里；即使球又被打回我们的球场，回到主角手中，这也不算是比赛的一部分，对吧？当某些事情（无论是好事还是坏事）毫无理由地发生时，就显得不合情理。比如，球自己弹了回来。或者，主角挥拍落空，但球却击中了一只飞过球场的鸟，然后又飞回了反派的球网一侧。这显然不符合规则！


We want the ball to bounce back and forth between the antagonist and protagonist – the Hero and Villain - each reacting to what the other has done.

我们希望故事中的反派和主角——英雄和恶棍——之间来回互动，彼此对对方的行为做出反应。


If the antagonist has a gun to the protagonist’s head and suddenly the police show up to save the day, that’s not real. Nothing has caused the police to show up. If the protagonist tells the police that the antagonist will soon put a gun to his head, that’s unreal - how can the protagonist know exactly what the antagonist will do? Everything that happens has to be logically motivated. Everything is a reaction to some action that happened previously. You need to be able to trace back the reactions to actions and those actions need to be logical... something the audience might do if they were the character. Howard may be a mad bomber, but he’s got a logical reason for everything he does. He wants the money he thinks he deserves and will blow stuff up until he gets it. There are reasons behind his actions. Nothing is a coincidence.

如果反派用枪指着主角的头，然后警察突然出现救场，这不真实。警察的出现没有任何直接原因。如果主角告诉警察反派很快就会用枪指着他的头，这也不真实——主角怎么可能准确预知反派的行动？所有发生的事情都必须有合乎逻辑的动机。一切都是对先前某个行为的反应。你需要能够追溯这些反应，而这些反应本身也必须是合乎逻辑的……是观众如果身处角色之中可能会做出的行为。霍华德或许是个疯狂的炸弹客，但他做任何事都有其合理的原因。他想要他认为自己应得的钱，所以会不惜一切代价炸毁东西直到得到为止。他的行为背后都有原因。一切都不是巧合。


#↩

MacGUFFINS

麦格芬


The MacGuffin is a physical device that drives the story - the thing that everyone is after, and screenplays using this type of plot device are some form of quest, or maybe a game of hot potato or keep away. The Maltese Falcon is probably the most famous one, but the Lost Ark is also a good example. The term comes from Alfred Hitchcock who once defined a MacGuffin as a device for capturing the indigenous lions in the Scottish Highland... but there are no lions in the Scottish Highlands... hence, no such thing as a MacGuffin! Except, there's a MacGuffin in almost every Hitchcock movie.

麦格芬（MacGuffin）是一种推动剧情发展的实体道具——是所有人都在追寻的东西。运用这种情节道具的剧本通常讲述的是某种形式的冒险故事，或者像是一场“烫手山芋”或“抢夺游戏”。《马耳他之鹰》可能是最著名的例子，但《失落的方舟》也是一个很好的例子。这个词源于阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克，他曾将麦格芬定义为一种用来捕捉苏格兰高地本土狮子的装置……但苏格兰高地根本没有狮子……因此，根本不存在麦格芬这种东西！然而，几乎每一部希区柯克的电影里都有麦格芬。


“North By Northwest” has two MacGuffins - the little pre-Columbian statue that villain Van Damm is determined to buy at the auction (because it is filled with top secret microfilm) and the CIA spy George Kaplan who everyone has confused protagonist Roger Thornhill for. So we have a double MacGuffin – Thornhill must find Kaplan, and Kaplan is chasing Van Damm to get the pre-Columbian statue and microfilm.

The MacGuffin drives the story - where would “The Maltese Falcon” be without The Maltese Falcon? It is the most important element in the story... but Hitchcock noted that even though it drives the story, what it is doesn’t matter very much. In “North By Northwest” we have that pre-Columbian statue, and inside is a roll of microfilm. Van Damm is smuggling this microfilm out of the USA - and delivering it to the Soviets. The CIA must stop him and recover that microfilm and Thornhill ends up being the guy in the middle. So the fate of the free world rests on who ends up with the statue and the microfilm that is inside it by the end of the movie. The film is all about that microfilm! It’s what Van Damm has been up to since the very first frame and why he has been trying to kill George Kaplan... the only man who can get Thornhill off the hook. So the microfilm is *really* why they are trying to kill Thornhill.

What is on the microfilm? It doesn’t really matter. What matters is that we will lose the Cold War if Van Damm delivers the microfilm to the enemy. And that’s why the MacGuffin is both the most important element in the story (it drives the story, and who ends up with it is what the story is *about*), but also unimportant (as long as we know people will kill for it, who cares what it really is?). The scene where the Professor tells Thornhill what's on the microfilm takes place on the tarmac of an airport (Northwest Airlines) and you can’t hear a thing that is said because a plane is taking off.

CIA spy George Kaplan, the MacGuffin that Thornhill is chasing? Doesn't exist. He's a decoy set up by the CIA to keep suspicion away from their real agent who is in deep cover.

《西北偏北》有两个关键道具——反派范·达姆决心在拍卖会上买下的那尊前哥伦布时期的小雕像（因为里面藏着绝密缩微胶片），以及被所有人误认为是主角罗杰·索恩希尔的中央情报局特工乔治·卡普兰。因此，影片中有两个关键道具：索恩希尔必须找到卡普兰，而卡普兰则在追捕范·达姆，试图夺取那尊前哥伦布时期的小雕像和缩微胶片。关键道具推动着故事发展——如果没有《马耳他之鹰》，《马耳他之鹰》又会是什么样子呢？它是故事中最重要的元素……但希区柯克指出，尽管关键道具推动着故事发展，但它本身是什么却并不重要。在《西北偏北》中，我们看到了那尊前哥伦布时期的小雕像，雕像里面藏着一卷缩微胶片。范·达姆正试图将这卷缩微胶片走私出美国，并交给苏联。中央情报局必须阻止他并找回那卷缩微胶片，而索恩希尔最终成了夹在中间的关键人物。因此，自由世界的命运取决于电影结尾谁能最终得到雕像和其中的缩微胶片。整部电影都围绕着那卷缩微胶片展开！从影片一开始，范·达姆就一直在做这件事，这也是他为何要刺杀乔治·卡普兰的原因……因为只有卡普兰才能让索恩希尔脱罪。所以，缩微胶片才是他们刺杀索恩希尔的真正原因。

缩微胶片里究竟有什么？其实并不重要。重要的是，如果范·达姆把缩微胶片交给敌人，我们将输掉冷战。这就是为什么麦格芬既是故事中最重要的元素（它推动剧情发展，故事的核心在于谁最终得到了它），又显得无关紧要（只要我们知道有人会为了它杀人，谁又会在乎它到底是什么呢？）。教授告诉索恩希尔缩微胶片上的内容的那场戏发生在机场（西北航空公司）的停机坪上，由于飞机正在起飞，你什么也听不清。

中情局特工乔治·卡普兰，索恩希尔追寻的麦格芬？根本不存在。他是中情局为了掩盖真正卧底特工的嫌疑而设下的诱饵。


Rare coins, rare books, murder weapons, plans to the Death Star, the letters of transit in “Casablanca”, the identity of Rosebud in ”Citizen Kane”, the ring in “Lord Of The Rings” and all kinds of things that both good guys and bad guys must posses which propels the plot forward are MacGuffins. In Hitchcock's “The Lady Vanishes” the MacGuffin is a *tune* that is really a code. In “The 39 Steps” it's a formula that Mr. Memory has memorized. The more interesting and unusual your MacGuffin the better!

I think you can still have the MacGuffin be the thing that drives the story and yet not really care what’s on the microfilm, but we live in a post CSI world where people like to know the details. Today, they would want to know what’s on that microfilm. The cool thing about a MacGuffin is that it makes a dandy high concept substitute. If the *MacGuffin* is some high concept device, then you can have a standard non-high con action movie. “Raiders Of The Lost Ark” is a non-high concept action-adventure story... but the Ark can level mountains, and whoever controls it will win the war. Is that *lightning* shooting out of the Ark?

稀有硬币、珍稀书籍、凶器、死星设计图、《卡萨布兰卡》中的过境信、《公民凯恩》中罗斯巴德的身份、《指环王》中的戒指，以及正反双方都必须拥有的各种推动剧情发展的关键物品，都是麦格芬。在希区柯克的《贵妇失踪记》中，麦格芬是一首实际上是密码的旋律。在《三十九级台阶》中，它是记忆先生记住的公式。你的麦格芬越有趣、越不寻常越好！我认为你可以让麦格芬成为推动故事发展的关键，而不必真正关心缩微胶片上的内容，但我们生活在一个后《犯罪现场调查》时代，人们喜欢了解细节。如今，他们肯定想知道缩微胶片上的内容。麦格芬的妙处在于它能完美替代高概念。如果麦格芬本身就是个高概念装置，那么你就可以拍一部普通的、不讲究高概念的动作片了。《夺宝奇兵》就是一部不讲究高概念的动作冒险片……但方舟能移山填海，谁控制了它谁就能赢得战争。那是从方舟里射出的闪电吗？


So, these days, I would make the MacGuffin something exciting and cool rather than just a plot device - because it adds production value. I have an unpublished novel from decades ago about good guy spies and bad guy spies all trying to get their hands on this lost microfilm. Could have been anything, but I decided it was the plans for the “freon bomb” that flash freezes anything in a 5 mile radius. The opening chapter had a test on a tropical island which froze chimpanzees so that they shattered when touched. That raised the stakes and made the story more interesting than “just microfilm”. One of the great things about making the MacGuffin something specific is that you can create some great high concept element that will raise the stakes and elevate the excitement of your screenplay. If everyone is after something, it's a good idea to make it valuable.

所以，现在我会把“麦格芬”（MacGuffin）设计成既刺激又酷炫的东西，而不仅仅是推动剧情发展的工具——因为它能提升作品的制作价值。我几十年前写过一部未出版的小说，讲的是正邪两派间谍都想得到一份遗失的缩微胶片。本来可以是任何东西，但我决定它是“氟利昂炸弹”的设计图，这种炸弹能瞬间冻结方圆五英里内的所有物体。开篇章节描写了在热带岛屿上进行的一项试验，试验中，黑猩猩被冻住，一碰就会碎裂。这大大提升了故事的紧张感，让它比“仅仅是缩微胶片”更有吸引力。把“麦格芬”设计成具体的东西的好处之一在于，你可以创造出一些绝妙的高概念元素，从而提升剧情的紧张感，增强剧本的刺激性。如果每个人都在争夺某样东西，那么最好让它变得价值连城。


Whether you think of your story like a game of tennis or as an onion or as a quest for some MacGuffin, you need to make sure that your plotting works. That means planning your story from the inside out, knowing every layer and every level of truth and making sure that each makes sense. The greatest characters and the most clever dialogue in the world won’t save a story that’s full of coincidence or doesn’t add up by the time the film is over. Plotting an action screenplay may be difficult, but it doesn’t have to be murder... though many action screenplays may contain a murder or two. Now that we know how structure and plot work, how do we put that all together into a story? Well, our next step is to come up with an outline that takes pacing into account.

无论你把故事想象成一场网球赛、一个洋葱，还是寻找某个关键道具，你都需要确保情节环环相扣。这意味着要从内到外地规划你的故事，了解每一个层面、每一层真相，并确保每个层面都合情合理。即使是世界上最伟大的角色和最精妙的对话，也无法拯救一个充满巧合或最终逻辑不通的故事。创作动作剧本可能很困难，但并不一定非得是谋杀……尽管许多动作剧本中确实包含一两起谋杀案。既然我们已经了解了结构和情节的运作方式，那么如何将它们融合到一个故事中呢？下一步，我们需要制定一个兼顾节奏的大纲。



#↩

TIMELINING

时间线


Action film producer Joel Silver says: "You've got to have a 'whammo' every ten minutes; an explosion, a car chase, a fight scene, to keep the audience interested." Silver believes this is the most important thing in action film, and he's probably right.

动作片制片人乔尔·西尔弗说：“你必须每隔十分钟就来个‘重头戏’；爆炸、飞车追逐、打斗场面，才能吸引观众。”西尔弗认为这是动作片最重要的部分，他的说法或许是对的。


Silver has made the most successful action films ever – from “48 Hours” to “Commando” to “Predator” to “Die Hard” to “Road House” to “Lethal Weapon” to “Executive Decision” to “The Matrix” to the new “Sherlock Holmes” movies – and I had to leave out most of his hit action films for space! Let's just say, the dude knows what he's talking about.

西尔弗执导过史上最成功的动作片——从《48小时》到《突击队》到《铁血战士》到《虎胆龙威》到《威龙杀阵》到《致命武器》到《最高危机》到《黑客帝国》再到新版《大侦探福尔摩斯》系列电影——而由于篇幅限制，我不得不省略他大部分的热门动作片！这么说吧，这家伙绝对是行家。


This may seem like some crazy Hollywood concept, but it's just basic *pacing* - a word that has been around since the 14 th century. Pacing and tempo are basic elements of music and dramatic works, and when I wrote an article on pacing for Script Magazine a few years ago I decided to use romantic comedies as examples to show that a steady pace is important in all genres. Joel Silver's “every ten pages whammo” was true for all of the popular rom-coms that I timed for the article. According to Merriam-Webster pacing is “the rate of movement; especially : an established rate of locomotion”. Pacing and Timing are critical to all genres, but especially action films. Long slow spots and an abundance of static talk scenes will sink your script before it ever gets made. Action scripts contain action scenes and you've got to keep those car chases and shoot outs coming, or the audience will get up and leave.

这听起来可能像是好莱坞的某种疯狂概念，但其实只是基本的“节奏”概念——这个词早在14世纪就出现了。节奏和韵律是音乐和戏剧作品的基本要素。几年前，我为《剧本杂志》（Script Magazine）撰写了一篇关于节奏的文章，当时我决定以浪漫喜剧为例，说明稳定的节奏在所有类型片中都至关重要。乔尔·西尔弗（Joel Silver）所说的“每十页就来个重磅炸弹”的说法，在我为这篇文章计时的所有热门浪漫喜剧中都得到了印证。根据韦氏词典的解释，“节奏”指的是“运动的速度；尤指：既定的运动速度”。节奏和韵律对所有类型片都至关重要，尤其是动作片。冗长的慢镜头和大量的静态对话场景会让你的剧本在拍摄之前就夭折。动作片剧本包含动作场景，你必须让追车和枪战不断上演，否则观众就会起身离场。


Our job as screenwriters is to rupture bladders.

我们编剧的工作就是让观众膀胱破裂。


The audience has just spent $7 on a king sized Coca-Cola with free refills, which is almost empty about halfway through the film (they started drinking it while watching all of those ads before the movie). Now they're looking for that dead spot in the story so that they can run to the bathroom. That part of the film where nothing interesting is happening and doesn't seem likely to happen for a couple of minutes. Just long enough to race to the restroom and race back. Our job is to make sure there are no dead spots, no slow spots, no time to race to the restroom... so that there is at least one messy bladder explosion at every showing of our film.

观众刚花了7美元买了一大杯可以无限续杯的可口可乐，电影放到一半的时候，这杯可乐就快喝完了（他们在电影开始前的广告时间就开始喝了）。现在他们正想着找个剧情的空档去趟洗手间。就是那种电影里没什么精彩情节，而且看起来接下来几分钟都不会有新剧情出现的段落。刚好够他们冲进洗手间，然后再冲回来。我们的任务就是确保电影里没有空档，没有拖沓，没有时间让他们冲进洗手间……这样，我们每场电影放映至少都会出现一次“膀胱爆炸”的尴尬场面。


The pacing of your script is critical. We have all seen movies that had those dull sections where nothing seemed to be happening, and we've all seen movies that just dragged along. Though a compelling story might make a slow paced film tolerable, it's still a slow paced film. Pacing is one of the most important elements of a screenplay, yet you seldom see it mentioned in screenwriting books or screenwriting classes. What *is* pacing?

剧本的节奏至关重要。我们都看过一些电影，其中不乏情节沉闷、仿佛什么都没发生的段落；我们也看过一些电影，节奏拖沓冗长。虽然引人入胜的故事或许能让一部节奏缓慢的电影变得可以忍受，但它仍然是一部节奏缓慢的电影。节奏是剧本最重要的要素之一，然而在剧本写作书籍或课程中却很少见到它的身影。那么，节奏究竟是什么呢？


Pacing is the frequency of exciting events in your screenplay (or in the movie). The more exciting events, the faster paced your screenplay. The fewer exciting events, the slower paced your screenplay. Pretty simple.

节奏指的是剧本（或电影）中激动人心的事件出现的频率。激动人心的事件越多，剧本节奏就越快；激动人心的事件越少，剧本节奏就越慢。就这么简单。


For the most part, the exciting events will be what I call the "genre juice" - those juicy genre scenes that people buy tickets to see. Those scenes that make it into the trailer. In a comedy, those are the comedy set pieces. In action they are the action scenes. In a thriller they are the suspense scenes. Though we all want great characters and a great story, the reason why we go to a comedy film is to laugh - so the funny scenes are critical. You need enough funny scenes in a comedy so that those folks who bought that $7 soft drink can't make a dash for the restroom because they don't want to miss all of those funny things that they know are coming, because the film so far has been filled with funny scenes. We pay to see a comedy film because it's funny - so the script better bring that funny and keep us laughing. If you have a comedy script with five funny scenes out of 50-60 scenes, that's not very funny. Nothing to keep you from visiting the bathroom or the candy counter or even playing that game on your cellphone.

大多数情况下，真正精彩的部分就是我所谓的“类型片精华”——那些吸引观众买票观看的类型片经典桥段，也就是预告片里出现的那些镜头。在喜剧片里，它们是喜剧桥段；在动作片里，它们是动作戏；在惊悚片里，它们是悬疑戏。虽然我们都想要精彩的角色和引人入胜的故事，但我们去看喜剧片的真正目的是为了开怀大笑——所以搞笑的桥段至关重要。一部喜剧片里需要足够多的搞笑桥段，这样那些花了7美元买了饮料的观众才不会因为不想错过那些他们知道接下来会出现的笑料而匆匆跑去洗手间，因为到目前为止，电影里已经充满了各种搞笑的场景。我们花钱去看喜剧片就是因为它好笑——所以剧本必须保证足够的笑点，让我们一直笑个不停。如果你的喜剧剧本里50到60个场景只有5个搞笑桥段，那它就称不上好笑。没有任何事能阻止你去洗手间、糖果柜台，甚至在手机上玩游戏。


#↩

TACKED ON PACING

附加节奏


There are two ways to insure that your script is well paced:

确保剧本节奏流畅有两种方法：


1) Include the pacing in your outline/plan so that it becomes part of the structure.

1）将节奏控制纳入你的大纲/计划中，使其成为结构的一部分。

2) Edit and rewrite your script once it is finished to improve pacing.

2）剧本完成后，进行编辑和重写，以改善节奏。


If you include the pacing in your outline, you have "built in pacing", if you try to create pacing after the fact you may end up with contrived pacing... plus a whole lotta rewriting! I have seen many action films where it seems like someone just threw in a gratuitous car chase because the pace was lagging. That's usually what happens when pacing is an after-thought the scenes stuck-in during rewrites stick-out like a sore thumb! That is why I prefer to build my action scenes (or whatever the "genre juice" is) into the outline, so that they are part of the story itself. The juice scenes become part of the story's skeleton, not something I stick on in a rewrite that wasn't part of the original story.

如果在大纲中就把节奏考虑进去，节奏就“内置”了；如果事后才去调整节奏，最终可能会显得生硬刻意……而且还得重写一大堆！我看过很多动作片，感觉就像是为了弥补节奏拖沓而硬塞进去一段莫名其妙的追车戏。这通常就是事后才考虑节奏的后果——重写时硬塞进去的那些场景显得格格不入！所以我更喜欢把动作戏（或者其他任何“类型元素”）融入大纲，让它们成为故事本身的一部分。这些“元素”场景会成为故事骨架的一部分，而不是在重写时硬塞进去的、原本不属于故事的东西。


It also helps to think about the “juice scenes” when you are looking for story ideas and thinking about characters. Though a car chase is an exciting scene that may be in the trailer and may get the audience to pay for the ticket and may keep them from making that mad dash to the restroom, it is also a *character scene* and a *story scene*. Your protagonist is in trouble and must make life or death situations in a car chase, so think of the “juice scenes” as character scenes as well. They aren't just something to keep the story exciting, they are also scenes of conflict that will expose character. That's another reason why those pasted on action scenes (or comedy scenes or romance scenes or suspense scenes) do not work - they are not part of the protagonist's emotional journey and not part of the story. You want to build the “juice scenes” into your story so that the hysterical comedy set piece is a required part of the character's story and can not be removed. Any scene that *can* be removed, *should* be removed... so any scene you can just tack onto your script is a scene that doesn't belong in your script. You want to make sure that all of those exciting "juice scenes" are integral to the story.

在构思故事和塑造角色时，思考“精彩片段”也很有帮助。虽然飙车戏很刺激，预告片里可能会出现，也能吸引观众买票，甚至让他们暂时忘了冲进洗手间，但它同时也是*角色塑造片段*和*故事片段*。你的主角身陷险境，必须在飙车中做出生死抉择，所以也要把这些“精彩片段”看作是角色塑造片段。它们不仅仅是为了让故事更精彩，更是展现角色性格的冲突场景。这也是为什么那些生硬地插入的动作戏（或者喜剧戏、爱情戏、悬疑戏）行不通的另一个原因——它们并非主角情感历程的一部分，也不是故事的组成部分。你应该把这些“精彩片段”巧妙地融入到故事中，让那些令人捧腹的喜剧桥段成为角色故事中不可或缺的一部分，不容有失。任何可以删掉的场景，都应该删掉……所以，任何可以随意添加到剧本里的场景，都不应该出现在你的剧本里。你要确保所有那些精彩的“刺激场景”都是故事不可或缺的一部分。


#↩

HEART BEAT

心跳


Pacing is the heart beat of your screenplay - it's what keeps your story alive and moving. Pacing has nothing to do with the depth of your characters, the amount we care about them, or the emotional resonance of your story. All of those things are important, but have nothing to do with pacing. You can have the greatest characters in the greatest story in the world, but without a regular heart beat it will die on the page. Slow paced scripts about fascinating characters are still slow paced - but we may stick around longer to see what happens to them.

节奏是剧本的心脏——它让你的故事鲜活起来，推动情节发展。节奏与人物的深度、我们对人物的关心程度，或者故事的情感共鸣都无关。所有这些固然重要，但都与节奏无关。你可以拥有世界上最精彩的故事和最棒的人物，但如果没有规律的节奏，它也会死气沉沉。节奏缓慢的剧本，即使讲述的是引人入胜的角色，节奏依然缓慢——但我们或许会更愿意留下来看下去，看看他们的命运如何。


Pacing is the frequency of exciting events (heart beats) in your story as well as the spacing of those events. You want to have enough heart beats to keep yourself alive, and you want those heart beats to come on a fairly regular basis. Irregular heart rhythms are NOT a good thing. Not enough heart beats is also NOT a good thing. You don't want all of your heart beats to come at once, then go 30 minutes without any heart beat... if one extreme didn't kill your story, the other extreme is sure to.

节奏指的是故事中激动人心的事件（心跳）出现的频率以及这些事件之间的间隔。你需要足够的心跳来维持故事的完整性，并且这些心跳要相对规律。心律不齐绝对不是好事。心跳太少也同样不好。你肯定不希望所有的心跳都同时出现，然后又连续30分钟没有任何心跳……如果一种极端情况没有毁掉你的故事，那么另一种极端情况肯定会。


Is there a rhythm to the placement of the scenes (or are there long dead spots where nothing exciting happens)? Does the action or suspense or humor snowball and intensify? If your action screenplay becomes *less* exciting as it progresses, you're in a heap-o-trouble. Pacing should intensify, not grow limp. Remember, our job is to rupture bladders. The more the audience has to go to the bathroom, the more we have to do to keep them in their seats.

场景安排是否流畅（还是存在冗长的沉闷段落，毫无精彩之处）？动作、悬念或幽默元素是否层层递进，愈发强烈？如果你的动作剧本随着剧情发展变得索然无味，那就麻烦大了。节奏应该渐入佳境，而不是拖沓冗长。记住，我们的任务是让观众欲罢不能。观众上厕所的次数越多，我们就越要竭尽全力让他们留在座位上。


#↩

TIMELINING

时间线


How can you make sure you have a “whammo” or heartbeat within every ten minutes of your film? You build the pacing into the screenplay through a technique I call "Timelining". It's basically a modified beat sheet designed to take pacing into account.

如何确保你的电影每隔十分钟就有一个“高潮”或“心跳”？你可以通过一种我称之为“时间线”的技巧，将节奏融入剧本创作中。它本质上是一种经过改良的节拍表，旨在将节奏控制纳入考量。


Some people use 3x5 cards to outline their scripts, but you have no idea how many minutes/pages each card represents. So I use a “Timeline” - a 'beat sheet', which lists critical scenes, except it's broken down into five minute/page increments. The average script is a page per minute of film, and even though that is just an estimate it is a good enough guideline for use in an outline. It may not end up perfect, but it keeps us in the right range. If you use 3x5 cards or some other form of outline, that's fine – but make pacing a consideration. If you want to try “timelines”, here is how that method works:

有些人用3x5卡片来勾勒剧本大纲，但你根本不知道每张卡片代表多少分钟/多少页。所以我用的是“时间线”——一种“节拍表”，它列出了关键场景，只不过是以五分钟/页为单位进行划分。一般来说，剧本每分钟对应一页电影内容，虽然这只是个大概的估计，但对于大纲来说已经足够用了。最终可能并不完美，但至少能保证我们把范围控制在合适的范围内。如果你用3x5卡片或其他形式的大纲，那也没问题——但一定要考虑节奏把控。如果你想尝试“时间线”，以下是它的使用方法：


Start with a standard piece of eight and a half by eleven lined paper. On the top of the page, write the title of your script. You can just write "Title:" for now. Neatly number by fives, each line on the left hand side. Start with 5, end with 110. But between 30 and 35 skip a line, and do the same between 80 and 85. In those spaces, write "end Act 1" and "end Act 2" and draw a little box around them. Now CIRCLE numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 95, 100, and 105. Those are your 'whammos'. Put a little star next to 55. That's your midpoint, and will probably be an emotional turning point for your lead character.

首先准备一张标准的8.5×11英寸的横格纸。在纸张顶部写下剧本标题。现在你可以只写“标题：”。在左侧每行整齐地编号，每行5个数字。从5开始，到110结束。但在30到35之间空一行，80到85之间也空一行。在空行处分别写上“第一幕结束”和“第二幕结束”，并用方框框起来。现在圈出10、20、30、40、50、60、70、80、90、95、100和105这几个数字。这些是你的“转折点”。在55旁边画一颗小星星。这是你的中点，很可能是主角的情感转折点。


Now you can look at the *heart beat* of your script without turning pages or trying to figure out how much time a 3x5 symbolizes. You know that each line is 5 minutes of screen time and 5 pages of script. You know that within every ten minutes something exciting is going to happen until Act 3, when your heart beat increases (as it does when you get more excited) and your screenplay has more script action. You know that this film will mean at least one messy bladder explosion in every cinema.

现在，你无需翻页或费力计算3x5代表多少时间，就能感受到剧本的“脉搏”。你知道每一行都代表5分钟的银幕时间和5页剧本。你知道每隔十分钟就会发生一件激动人心的事，直到第三幕，你的心跳会加快（就像你越兴奋，心跳就越快），剧本里的动作戏也会更多。你知道这部电影至少会让每家影院的观众都吓得尿裤子。


Now all you have to do is fill in the blanks...

现在你只需要填空即可……


#↩

BRAINSTORMING

头脑风暴


Grab a note pad and write "menu" at the top. Now number the lines from one to five on the left hand side and start brain storming scene ideas for your script. When you get five of them, keep numbering as you go. Write down character scenes, emotional scenes, plot scenes, romance scenes, and action scenes.

拿个笔记本，在顶部写上“菜单”。然后在左侧从一到五编号，开始构思剧本的场景。想出五个场景后，继续编号。分别写下人物场景、情感场景、情节场景、爱情场景和动作场景。


Don't censor yourself. If you come up with an idea, write it down. This is brainstorming – it's not about whether the idea is “good” or not, it's a volume business! If you get 27 ideas, flip to a new page and come up with some more. If you get 25 ideas, number the next line 26... You'd be surprised how that blank line will jog another idea from your mind. You want to come up with as many ideas as you can!

不要自我审查。想到什么就写下来。这是头脑风暴——重点不在于想法好不好，而在于数量！如果你想到了27个点子，就翻到新的一页，再想一些。如果你想到了25个，就在下一行写26……你会惊讶地发现，空白的一行往往能激发你新的灵感。你要尽可能多地想出点子！


Don't begin numbering up to 27, because you'll probably choke up. How can anyone come up with 27 ideas? It's impossible. But anyone can come up with one idea at a time... and they add up.

别一开始就数到27，因为你可能会卡壳。谁能想出27个点子呢？这根本不可能。但任何人都可以一次想出一个点子……然后这些点子加起来就不少了。


Remember that you'll need at least a dozen action scenes. Try to come up with more, so you can choose the best. Here's where you try to come up with those "action scenes you'd like to see". A *rooftop* car chase? Write it down! A “high noon” style shoot out in mid air between two ejected fighter pilots? Write it down! A fist fight on the roof of a speeding truck? Write it down! You'll need big action scenes and little action scenes. That way you can "build" your script to bigger and bigger climaxes. Let your imagination run wild – you want to try to find the action scenes we have never seen before. The more ideas you have, the more you can choose from. You should always end up with a numbered empty line at the end of your menu.

记住，你至少需要十二个动作场景。尽量多想一些，这样才能从中挑选出最好的。现在，你可以尽情构思那些“你希望看到的动作场景”。一场*屋顶*飞车追逐？写下来！两名弹射逃生的战斗机飞行员在空中展开一场“正午”式的枪战？写下来！在疾驰的卡车车顶上进行一场拳击？写下来！你需要一些大型动作场景，也需要一些小型动作场景。这样你才能逐步构建剧本，最终达到越来越精彩的高潮。尽情发挥你的想象力——你要努力找到那些前所未见的动作场景。你的想法越多，可供选择的就越多。最终，你的菜单末尾应该始终留出一个编号的空白行。


Once you have your “menu” of ideas, it's time to pare them down into the best scenes. Try to find the theme or nexus which ties your action scenes to your plot and character scenes. You may come up with a kick-ass motorcycle chase, but it might not fit in with the rest of the story... so it's outta there! We don't want to use some action scene just because it's “cool”, we want it to be part of the story.

一旦你有了想法的“菜单”，就该把它们精简成最佳场景了。试着找到能将动作场景与情节和人物场景联系起来的主题或核心。你或许能想出一个精彩绝伦的摩托车追逐戏，但它可能与故事的其他部分格格不入……那就把它删掉吧！我们不想仅仅因为某个动作场景“很酷”就把它用进去，我们希望它成为故事的一部分。


Once you have your best ideas, it's time to decide where to put them on your time line. It's best to start with your plot scenes, then add the character and emotion scenes, and save the action scenes for last. This way, the action serves your plot and character, not the other way around.

有了最佳创意之后，就该决定如何安排它们在时间线上的位置了。最好先写情节场景，再添加人物和情感场景，最后才写动作场景。这样，动作场景才能服务于情节和人物，而不是反过来。


The average screenplay has about 60 scenes, so your average scene is going to be around 2 pages. Hey, some may be shorter than that, some may be longer than that- it's just an average. But that means every line on your time line will probably have 2 or 3 scenes. You may end up with some extended action scenes – the car chase in “Bullitt” is *ten* minutes long! One five minute segment where the hit men chase Bullitt through San Francisco's hilly streets. Then Bullitt turns the tables on them, and chases the hit men for five minutes on country roads... Until the hit men run into a gas station. BLAAMM! The ten minute car chase ends with a bang. That scene is 7.5 pages in the screenplay, by the way. Though that scene is longer that 2 or 3 pages, it's also the big centerpiece action scene for the film, and I have never heard anyone complain that it was too long. The only real rule about scene length is that it can't overstay its welcome – if you have a 5 page *dialogue* scene and it is tense and riveting, that's all that matters. But a 5 page scene is a freak, so make sure the scene really does work at that length and can not be improved by trimming it down.

一部电影剧本平均有大约60个场景，所以平均每个场景大概两页左右。当然，有些场景可能更短，有些可能更长——这只是个平均值。这意味着你时间线上的每一行可能都对应两到三个场景。你可能会遇到一些超长的动作场景——比如《警网铁金刚》（Bullitt）里的追车戏就长达十分钟！其中五分钟，杀手们在旧金山起伏的街道上追逐布利特。然后布利特反败为胜，在乡村公路上追了五分钟……直到杀手们跑进一个加油站。砰！十分钟的追车戏以一声巨响结束。顺便一提，这个场景在剧本里占了7.5页。虽然这个场景比两三页长，但它也是整部电影的核心动作戏，而且我从没听说有人抱怨过它太长。关于场景长度，唯一真正的规则就是它不能过长——如果你写了一场五页的*对话*场景，而且紧张刺激、引人入胜，那就足够了。但五页的场景确实很少见，所以要确保场景在这个长度下确实有效，而且删减后也不会更好。


When you fill in your action scenes, remember that variety is the spice of life. Don't put two car chases or two shootouts right next to each other. In fact, car chases probably need to be separated by at least 30 minutes, unless you're doing a sequel to Walter Hill's "The Driver" or a “Transporter” sequel. You don't want to be repetitious. One exciting shoot out after another can get boring! The key to a great action script is a balanced diet. Some fight scenes, some car chases, some shoot outs, some adventure oriented scenes (mountain climbing?)... A little of everything and not too much of one thing all at once.

在构思动作场景时，记住多样性才是关键。不要把两场飙车戏或两场枪战戏紧挨着安排。事实上，除非你是在拍沃尔特·希尔的《亡命驾驶》或《玩命速递》的续集，否则飙车戏之间至少要间隔30分钟。你肯定不想让剧情重复。一场接一场的刺激枪战会让人感到乏味！一部精彩动作剧本的关键在于均衡的元素搭配。一些打斗戏、一些飙车戏、一些枪战戏、一些冒险场景（比如登山？）……各种元素都要有所涉及，不要一次性堆砌太多。


Try to *build* the action scenes from small to large. If you start with the end of the world, you have no place to go! Try to make each action scene either bigger than the one before it or more personal. Have you seen "To Live And Die In L.A."? It has this killer car chase in the middle of the film... which is followed by a bunch of smaller action scenes which seem more suited to Act One than Act Three. Be careful not to use an "Act One Action Scene" in Act Three, or an "Act Three Action Scene" in Act One. Save the best for last, if you can. You don't want the audience to be disappointed by the next action scene, and the best way to do that is to make each action scene *better* than the last. This is where last chapter's plotting lessons come into play – you want your story to grow organically from the concept, and use the outline as your first creative step. The charcoal sketch an artist makes before they break out the oils and brushes.

尝试从小规模开始构建动作场景。如果你一开始就展现世界末日，那就没有发展的空间了！尽量让每个动作场景都比前一个更大，或者更具个人色彩。你看过《生死时速》（To Live and Die in L.A.）吗？影片中段有一段精彩绝伦的飙车戏……之后是一系列规模较小的动作场景，这些场景似乎更适合放在第一幕而不是第三幕。切记不要把“第一幕的动作场景”放到第三幕，或者把“第三幕的动作场景”放到第一幕。如果可以，尽量把最好的留在最后。你肯定不希望观众对接下来的动作场景感到失望，而最好的办法就是让每个动作场景都比上一个更精彩。这就是上一章的剧情构思技巧发挥作用的地方——你希望你的故事从概念中自然而然地发展，并将大纲作为你创作的第一步。就像艺术家在拿起油彩和画笔之前先画的炭笔草图一样。


Another important element to consider in your timeline is how the action scenes relate to your protagonist. You want the action in Act Three to be *more personal* than the action in Act One. "Lethal Weapon" is a great example. In Act One, the action scenes are more plot related – deal with the death of his friend's daughter. But in Act Two the bad guys begin shooting people Danny Glover knows, and by Act Three, they have kidnapped his daughter. Each action scene should draw the protagonist *deeper* into the action until the protagonist's life is on the line.

在时间线中，另一个需要考虑的重要因素是动作场景与主角的关联。你希望第三幕的动作场面比第一幕的动作场面更具个人色彩。《致命武器》就是一个很好的例子。在第一幕中，动作场景更多地与剧情相关——比如处理他朋友女儿的死亡。但在第二幕中，坏人开始枪杀丹尼·格洛弗认识的人，到了第三幕，他们绑架了他的女儿。每个动作场景都应该让主角更深地卷入其中，直到他的生命受到威胁。


#↩

ONLY A MODEL

仅供参考


Timelines are also a valuable tool in studying existing films. It's important to study films and see how and why they work, in order to learn how to improve our scripts. So I suggest timelining some existing films to use as 'models'. Often comparing similar films to see what they have in common and what elements are different. I think studying films is an eye opener – I had no idea how many scenes were in a film and how short those scenes were until I began watching films and timing them out.

时间线也是研究现有电影的宝贵工具。研究电影，了解它们的运作方式和原因，对于改进我们的剧本至关重要。所以我建议为一些现有电影绘制时间线，作为“模型”。经常比较类似的电影，看看它们的共同点和不同之处。我认为研究电影令人大开眼界——在开始观看电影并计算时间之前，我根本不知道一部电影有多少个场景，每个场景又有多短。


Though when I first began timing films it was with a watch and flashlight in a dark cinema, the easiest method now is just dropping a DVD or BluRay into the machine and writing down the time on the monitor. I usually note the amount of time the credit sequence takes and subtract that from the times when I'm finished. I make a “beat sheet” listing all of the plot, character, and action beats in a film... but I also list the time when these events occur. I usually write when a scene ends: Car chase on street/23 (minutes into the film). Now adapt your beat sheet onto a timeline, by placing everything within 5 minute increments.

虽然我最初开始给电影计时是在黑暗的电影院里用手表和手电筒，但现在最简单的方法是直接把DVD或蓝光光盘放进播放机，然后记下屏幕上的时间。我通常会记下片尾字幕的播放时间，然后从我看完电影的时间中减去这个时间。我会制作一个“节奏表”，列出电影中所有的情节、人物和动作节点……以及这些事件发生的时间。我通常会在场景结束时写下：街头追车/23分钟（电影开始时间）。现在，把你的节奏表整理到时间轴上，以5分钟为单位进行标记。


One of the things you'll probably notice is a phenomenon I call "Chapterizing". Strangely enough, things will often actually happen within five minute blocks. For instance, in Richard Price's "Sea Of Love", 35 minutes into the film Al Pacino and John Goodman begin setting up dates with potential suspects. During the five minute segment from 35 - 40 minutes, they set up the dates, go to the restaurant and meet date #1, date #2, and date #3. Exactly 40 minutes into the film, Pacino meets date #4... Ellen Barkin. She is the lead suspect *and* Pacino's romantic interest in the film.

你可能会注意到一种我称之为“章节化”的现象。奇怪的是，很多事情实际上都发生在短短五分钟之内。例如，在理查德·普莱斯执导的《情海》中，影片进行到35分钟时，阿尔·帕西诺和约翰·古德曼开始与潜在嫌疑人约会。在35分钟到40分钟这五分钟里，他们安排好约会，前往餐厅，分别与第一位、第二位和第三位约会对象见面。影片进行到40分钟时，帕西诺遇到了第四位约会对象……艾伦·巴金。她既是主要嫌疑人，也是帕西诺在影片中的恋人。


That five minute "chapter" of "Sea Of Love" covers setting up the dates and meeting 3 suspects who we *know* are not the killer. The next five minute "chapter" gives us 2 minutes of Al and Ellen, and 3 minutes of tracking a grocery delivery boy who becomes a prime suspect.

《爱之海》这五分钟的“章节”讲述了安排约会和与三位嫌疑人见面的过程，我们*知道*他们并非凶手。接下来的五分钟“章节”则用了两分钟展现艾尔和艾伦的互动，以及三分钟追踪一位送货员的情节，而这位送货员最终成为了主要嫌疑人。


Exactly 45 minutes into the film, Al bumps into Ellen by accident, and they decide to go on a date. That 5 minute block concerns the things leading up to the date, and the date itself. 50 minutes into the film, the date 'ends' with Al and Ellen making love.

影片进行到45分钟时，艾尔偶然撞见了艾伦，两人决定约会。接下来的5分钟主要讲述了约会前后的种种准备和约会本身。影片进行到50分钟时，约会以艾尔和艾伦发生性关系而“结束”。


I don't know why films tend to "chapter out" like this into 5 minute segments. Maybe that's the way they were outlined, maybe that's the way they were edited. But it's a weird phenomena you can use to your advantage, by trying to find the "chapter title" of each five minute block. "Al and Ellen go on a date". "Al tries to propose marriage and blows it". This will help you focus on what is the central idea of each sequence. Instead of aimless scenes which don't seem to build anywhere, we know from the time they set up the dates that they will find a suspect. Each event in the five minute segment takes them CLOSER and CLOSER to finding that suspect. The sequence ends when they've found her. If it helps you to think of your story in 5 page sequences, go for it! If that gets in your way, don't do it – there are no rules! It's all about finding the methods which create the best results.

我不知道为什么电影喜欢把故事分成五分钟的片段，就像“章节”一样。也许是剧本大纲就是这样写的，也许是剪辑的缘故。但这确实是一个你可以利用的奇特现象，你可以试着找出每个五分钟片段的“章节标题”。比如“艾尔和艾伦约会”。“艾尔试图求婚，结果搞砸了”。这能帮助你聚焦每个片段的核心思想。这样一来，就不会出现漫无目的、毫无进展的场景，而是从他们安排约会的那一刻起，我们就知道他们最终会找到嫌疑人。五分钟片段中的每个事件都让他们离找到嫌疑人越来越近。当他们找到嫌疑人时，这个片段就结束了。如果你觉得用五页纸的片段来构思故事对你有帮助，那就用吧！如果这反而阻碍了你，那就别用——没有硬性规定！关键在于找到能带来最佳效果的方法。


I suggest making timeline models of your favorite action films, to give you an example of how they're paced. You may find certain patterns in these timelines. For instance, there tend to be two basic ways that buddy cop films work: "Red Heat" and "48 Hours" are almost identical when broken down. Sometimes finding patterns is a great method to discover what normally works in a subgenre, other times it's a great way to find the cliches so that you can avoid them or subvert them. Knowing how a genre or subgenre works is a great tool to have in your toolbox.

我建议你制作自己最喜欢的动作电影的时间线模型，这样可以让你更好地理解它们的节奏。你可能会在这些时间线中发现一些规律。例如，搭档警匪片通常有两种基本模式：《红场特警》和《48小时》的模式几乎完全相同。有时，寻找规律是发现某个子类型电影成功要素的绝佳方法；有时，它则是找出俗套、避免或颠覆它们的有效途径。了解某个类型或子类型的运作方式，绝对是你电影创作工具箱里的必备利器。


By timelining existing films, you will get a feel for what makes them work. Once that pacing becomes part of your subconscious, you can throw away your timelines and abstracts and write from your heart. Think of timelines as bicycle training wheels: for a while you need them just to keep balance, but soon you've learned to balance on your own and no longer need them. After a while, you'll be able to say "This needs a whammo", and write in the scene. Until then, using a timeline is a valuable tool in keeping the pacing of your action scripts tight...

通过梳理现有电影的节奏，你会逐渐领悟到它们成功的秘诀。一旦这种节奏感成为你的潜意识，你就可以抛弃时间线和抽象概念，完全凭感觉写作。把时间线想象成自行车的辅助轮：一开始你需要它们来保持平衡，但很快你就能学会独立骑行，不再需要它们。一段时间后，你就能说出“这里需要加点力度”，然后直接把场景写进去。在此之前，时间线仍然是保持动作剧本节奏紧凑的宝贵工具……


And exploding a few bladders while you're at it.

而且顺便还弄爆了几颗膀胱。



#↩

ORGANIC ACTION

有机作用


There are four ways you can write a screenplay - from the inside out, from the outside in, only the outside and only the inside. And that is the order of preference. The best method is to start with character and then find the high concept external conflict that will force the character to deal with their emotional conflict. You can also begin with your high concept and find the character with the emotional conflict that will be best explored by the physical conflict. Not good at all is a script that is only external conflict with no character and no drama. Worse is a screenplay that is only emotional conflict and no external conflict – we can't really see emotional conflict without some external conflict to dramatize it, so that ends up a dull movie that doesn't explore character at all... unless there are big steaming piles of exposition telling us what the character is feeling.

剧本创作有四种方法——由内而外、由外而内、只关注外部冲突和只关注内部冲突。这四种方法的优劣顺序也各不相同。最佳方法是从人物入手，然后找到能够迫使人物面对自身情感冲突的高概念外部冲突。你也可以从高概念入手，找到一个能够通过外部冲突更好地展现其情感冲突的人物。完全没有好的剧本是只有外部冲突而没有人物塑造和戏剧张力的。更糟糕的是只有情感冲突而没有外部冲突的剧本——没有外部冲突的戏剧化呈现，我们无法真正理解情感冲突，最终只会拍出一部乏味的电影，完全没有深入刻画人物……除非有大量冗长的旁白来告诉我们人物的感受。


Wait... did you say *emotional conflict*? Aren't we talking about action movies?

等等……你说的是“情感冲突”？我们说的不是动作电影吗？


Film is a dramatic medium, and as I've said a million times – car chases don't buy movie tickets, people do... so make sure your screenplay is about the people. Emotional conflicts are what makes our characters come alive and they help the audience identify with the protagonist. If your protagonist doesn't have emotional problems, there is no way for us to see their emotions... and they may come off like a robot. Remember, in “Terminator 2” even robot Ah-nuld has emotions. He knows why humans cry. We need both physical conflict (car chases, fist fights, explosions) *and* emotional conflict... and they need to be connected.

电影是一种戏剧媒介，正如我无数次强调的——飙车戏卖不出去票，真正吸引观众的是人……所以，务必确保你的剧本以人为本。情感冲突赋予角色生命，帮助观众与主角产生共鸣。如果你的主角没有情感问题，我们就无法感受到他们的情感……他们可能会显得像个机器人。记住，在《终结者2》中，即使是机器人阿诺德也有情感。他知道人类为什么会哭泣。我们需要动作场面（飙车、打斗、爆炸）和情感冲突……而且这两者必须紧密相连。


In my 2 day class I have a technique called “The Thematic” that shows you how to find interesting characters and scenes and dialogue and just about everything else based on the theme – the point of your story or element of the human condition that your screenplay is exploring... yes, we are still talking about action movies. My theory is that everything in your screenplay is there to explore the theme – so it is all connected. One of the ways to find your theme is through the protagonist's emotional conflict.

在我为期两天的课程中，我会介绍一种名为“主题分析法”的技巧，它能教你如何根据主题——也就是你故事的核心或剧本所探讨的人性层面——找到有趣的角色、场景、对话以及几乎所有其他元素……没错，我们仍然在讨论动作电影。我的理论是，剧本中的一切都是为了探索主题——它们之间是相互关联的。找到主题的方法之一就是通过主人公的情感冲突。


Just making a detective an alcoholic is meaningless (and cliché) unless the case sends him into bar after bar where temptation awaits. The emotional conflict needs to be connected to the physical conflict – not two separate stories. You don't want to graft some emotional problem on from the outside – if you begin with concept or external conflict you want to really dig in and find the emotional conflict that is already part of the story.

仅仅把侦探设定成酗酒者毫无意义（而且老套），除非案件让他不断出入酒吧，面临各种诱惑。情感冲突必须与现实冲突相连，而不是两个独立的故事。你不能从外部强加情感问题——如果你从概念或外部冲突入手，就应该深入挖掘，找到故事本身固有的情感冲突。


#↩

WHAT IS STORY?

什么是故事？


My definition of story: A story is when a character is forced to solve an emotional problem (why we care) in order to solve an external problem (the conflict we see - cool idea plus explosions) in order to prevent a catastrophic event from occurring (stakes)... often by a specific deadline.

我对故事的定义是：故事是指角色被迫解决一个情感问题（我们为什么关心这个问题），从而解决一个外部问题（我们看到的冲突——很酷的想法加上爆炸），以防止灾难性事件发生（风险）……通常是在特定的期限内。


Character and concept are connected, as is everything else in the screenplay – the subplots and the scenes and the locations and the dialogue. All of the pieces are part of one story, and that is what I call “organic screenwriting”. It's all grown from a story seed – where the emotional conflict and external conflict are connected. Nothing is grafted on from the outside, nothing is just some random scene or idea glued onto the story just because it sounds cool. If you have a scene that is *only* character or *only* action, it's best to find a better scene that is both character *and* action. We've all seen movies where it seems like three assistants with three different screenplays collided on the way to the copy machine, and each picked up 110 random pages and then someone filmed it. We don't want our screenplays to be like that. We want them to *make sense*.

角色和概念是相互关联的，剧本中的其他一切——支线剧情、场景、地点和对话——也都是如此。所有元素共同构成一个故事，这就是我所说的“有机剧本创作”。一切都源于一个故事种子——情感冲突和外部冲突相互交织。没有任何东西是从外部嫁接上来的，没有任何东西只是因为听起来很酷就随意地把某个场景或想法粘到故事里。如果你有一个场景*只有*角色*或*只有*动作*，最好找到一个更好的场景，既有角色*又有*动作*。我们都看过这样的电影：三个助理拿着三个不同的剧本，在去复印机的路上碰面，每人随机拿了110页，然后就有人把它们拍了下来。我们不希望我们的剧本变成那样。我们希望它们*合情合理*。


This “making sense” thing is not a new idea. About 2,400 years ago Aristotle came up with the Three Greek Unities: time, location, event (action). Though time and location we can play around with in film, the Unity Of Event (action) is still important – a story is about *one* thing happening. Not a bunch of different things that happen to a single character, but one big event that happens to your protagonist. Protagonist with a problem. Who is your protagonist and what is their problem? One of the odd issues that pops up in some screenplays is the protagonist is some sideline character who isn't really involved in the problem... and the screenplay seems blah even if there are lots of explosions. You don't want to use some peripheral character as your lead, or force some lead into a story that doesn't have anything to do with them. You need to create the right lead for the story or the right story for the lead. It all has to be part of the plan!

这种“合乎逻辑”的理念并非新概念。大约2400年前，亚里士多德提出了希腊三一律：时间、地点、事件（动作）。虽然在电影中我们可以灵活运用时间和地点，但事件（动作）的统一性仍然至关重要——一个故事讲述的是一件事情的发生。不是发生在同一个角色身上的一系列不同事件，而是发生在主角身上的一件大事。主角面临着一个问题。你的主角是谁？他的问题是什么？一些剧本中经常出现一个奇怪的问题：主角是一个无关紧要的配角，与问题本身毫无关联……即使有很多爆炸场面，剧本也显得平淡无奇。你肯定不想让一个边缘角色成为主角，或者强行把一个与他毫无关系的主角塞进一个故事里。你需要为故事创造合适的主角，或者为主角创造合适的故事。这一切都必须纳入计划之中！


#↩

ORGANIC EXAMPLE

有机示例


In Werb and Colleary's script for “Face/Off” the central conflict (where the external conflict and emotional conflict intersect) is FBI Agent Sean Archer's relentless pursuit of the man who killed his son... at the expense of the rest of his family.

在韦伯和科利里为《变脸》创作的剧本中，核心冲突（外部冲突和情感冲突的交汇点）是联邦调查局特工肖恩·阿彻不懈地追捕杀害他儿子的凶手……却牺牲了其他家庭成员的利益。


Family is at the core of the theme, and most of the action scenes have a family-based component in them, whether it's Archer rescuing his daughter from the Villain, or Archer rescuing the Villain's son in the middle of a massive shoot out, or the henchman taking a bullet so that his sister (Gina Gershon) can live. Every character and most of the scenes in the film reflect Archer's central conflict concerning family... and job vs. family specifically. *All* of the characters are defined by decisions they must make between job and family.

家庭是影片的核心主题，大多数动作场面都与家庭息息相关，例如阿彻从反派手中救出女儿，在激烈的枪战中救出反派的儿子，或是手下为了保护妹妹（吉娜·格申饰）而挺身挡子弹。影片中的每个角色和大部分场景都反映了阿彻关于家庭的核心冲突……尤其是工作与家庭之间的抉择。所有角色都因必须在工作和家庭之间做出选择而塑造自身。


The *External Conflict* is that villain Castor Troy has hidden a bomb somewhere in Los Angeles and Archer must “become” Troy (through a face transplant – sci fi when this film was made) in order to fool Troy's brother Pollux into telling him the bomb's location before it explodes. The conflict escalates when Troy escapes and “becomes” Archer and takes over his life, and the investigation. Where Archer sacrifices family for career, Troy is a family man who is devoted to his brother and only works when he's having fun. These two have opposite priorities – and through the shoot outs and speedboat chases, the film will explore issues of work vs. family. That is what the story is about underneath its skin.

外部冲突在于，反派卡斯特·特洛伊在洛杉矶某处藏匿了一枚炸弹，而阿彻必须“变成”特洛伊（通过换脸手术——在当时这还是科幻技术），才能骗过特洛伊的弟弟波勒克斯，让他说出炸弹的藏匿地点，以免炸弹爆炸。当特洛伊逃脱并“变成”阿彻，接管了他的生活和调查后，冲突进一步升级。阿彻为了事业牺牲家庭，而特洛伊则是一个顾家的男人，他全心全意爱着弟弟，只有在玩乐的时候才会工作。两人的价值观截然相反——影片将通过枪战和快艇追逐，探讨工作与家庭之间的冲突。这才是故事的真正核心所在。


The *Emotional Conflict* meets the External Conflict when Troy escapes and takes over Archer's life... and becomes a better husband and father than Archer has been since his son was killed!

当特洛伊逃脱并接管了阿彻的生活时，情感冲突与外部冲突相遇了……自从阿彻的儿子被杀后，特洛伊成为了比阿彻更好的丈夫和父亲！


Instead of going to his wife and daughter for help, Archer continues his relentless pursuit of Troy. Seeking out the terrorist's henchman (Nick Cassavettes) and girlfriend in an attempt to destroy Troy. Continuing his mistake of thinking destroying the man who killed his son will bring his family together. The more Archer ignores his Emotional Conflict through denial, the bigger the External Conflict becomes. Troy takes over his family and takes over his job and sends Archer on the run – the two men have switched places. Archer must deal with his family problems in order to regain his identity and bring down the terrorist. He must resolve his Emotional Conflict in order to resolve the External (plot) Conflict. Become himself inside before he can regain his identity outside.

阿彻没有向妻子和女儿寻求帮助，而是继续不懈地追捕特洛伊。他找到了恐怖分子的同伙（尼克·卡萨维茨饰）和女友，试图除掉特洛伊。他错误地认为，除掉杀害他儿子的凶手就能让家庭重归于好。阿彻越是否认自己的情感冲突，外部冲突就越发严重。特洛伊接管了他的家庭和工作，迫使阿彻亡命天涯——两人互换了身份。阿彻必须先解决家庭问题，才能重拾自我，最终扳倒恐怖分子。他必须先解决内心的情感冲突，才能化解外部（情节）冲突。他必须先找回自我，才能在外部世界重拾自我。


The film ends with Archer and his family back together raising Troy's son as a surrogate for the son he lost.

影片结尾，阿彻和他的家人团聚，抚养特洛伊的儿子，作为他失去儿子的替代品。


#↩

THROUGHLINES & YOU

主线与你


Some of you may have seen “Face/Off” and are wondering what the fistfight on the out of control speedboat at the end had to do with the bomb Castor Troy planted somewhere in Los Angeles... Hey, aren't these just a bunch of unrelated action scenes stuck together to make a film? I'm so glad you asked that! Whenever you come across some film that seems to have one or two plots, or maybe a protagonist who changes their goal, it's always a good thing to take a step back to see if there is a larger goal that includes both of the smaller goals.

你们当中有些人可能看过《变脸》，并且想知道结尾在失控快艇上的那场拳击赛和卡斯特·特洛伊在洛杉矶某处安放的炸弹有什么关系……嘿，这不就是一堆毫不相干的动作场景拼凑成一部电影吗？问得好！每当你遇到一部电影，感觉只有一两条情节线，或者主角的目标不断改变时，最好退后一步，看看是否存在一个更大的目标，而这个目标包含了这两个较小的目标。


In “Face/Off” the story is not about Sean Archer trying to find the bomb in Los Angeles, it is about Sean Archer trying to get revenge against Castor Troy for killing his son. The opening scene is Troy trying to kill Archer and accidentally killing his son by mistake. That sets up the central conflict – it is what makes Archer a broken man *and* hell bent on revenge. The story is not about the bomb, it's about Archer trying to avenge his son – which ends in that face off on the out of control speedboat. The other conflict elements, be they bombs or kidnapped daughters, all flow from that central conflict. They are *sub-conflicts* that are directly connected to the main conflict. Nothing grafted on from the outside, but grown from the central conflict seed.

在《变脸》中，故事的重点并非肖恩·阿彻在洛杉矶寻找炸弹，而是他如何为被卡斯特·特洛伊杀害的儿子复仇。开场便是特洛伊试图杀死阿彻，却意外误杀了自己的儿子。这便奠定了故事的核心冲突——正是这场冲突让阿彻心碎，并让他一心复仇。故事的重点不在于炸弹，而在于阿彻如何为子复仇——最终以在失控快艇上的那场对决告终。其他冲突元素，无论是炸弹还是被绑架的女儿，都源于这个核心冲突。它们是与主冲突直接相关的次要冲突，并非外生添加，而是从核心冲突的种子中自然生长而来。


A “throughline” is the spine of your story – the thing that connects all of the story elements. When you get into a development meeting on your screenplay, you will hear that word *a lot* - and the reason why are all of those movies that really are just a bunch of random events connected because they happen to the same character. Because those kinds of films tend to confuse viewers, producers try to avoid making them... while give you a list of unrelated cool scenes they want you to write into the screenplay. Hey, part of writing screenplays is to create the silk purse that they can turn into a sow's ear. But we need to *begin* with the silk purse – and that means all of our story elements need to be connected.

“贯穿线”是故事的脊梁——它将所有故事元素连接起来。当你参加剧本开发会议时，你会*频繁*听到这个词——原因在于，很多电影实际上只是一堆随机事件的集合，仅仅因为它们发生在同一个角色身上才勉强联系在一起。由于这类电影往往会让观众感到困惑，制片人会尽量避免拍摄它们……同时却会给你列出一堆看似精彩却毫不相关的场景，希望你把它们写进剧本里。嘿，剧本创作的一部分工作就是打造一个精美的“丝绸钱包”，然后让他们把它变成一个“猪耳朵”。但我们必须*从*这个“丝绸钱包”开始——这意味着我们所有的故事元素都必须相互关联。


The throughline is usually going to be connected to either the External Conflict or the Emotional Conflict – if there is a giant asteroid heading towards Earth or a giant shark eating people in Amityville, the throughline will be resolving that conflict. But when the throughline is tied to the Emotional Conflict you have to be careful that there is a visual goal and visual resolution to the Emotional Conflict as well as “steps” leading to the resolution that we can see, so that the audience knows we are making progress. If the Emotional Conflict is “invisible” (not dramatized and visual) and/or *internal*, the audience may feel like the story is spinning its wheels or just a bunch of unconnected scenes. Usually this is not a problem with an action film, but this was the issue with “The Black Dahlia” – the throughline dealt with the emotional conflict and was completely internal so it often seemed like a bunch of unrelated scenes and subplots.

故事主线通常会与外部冲突或情感冲突相连——例如，如果一颗巨型小行星正朝着地球飞来，或者阿米蒂维尔有一条巨鲨在吃人，那么主线就会着手解决这些冲突。但当主线与情感冲突相关时，必须确保情感冲突有一个视觉目标和视觉解决方案，并且通往解决方案的“步骤”清晰可见，以便观众知道故事正在推进。如果情感冲突是“隐形的”（没有戏剧化和视觉化呈现）和/或*内在的*，观众可能会觉得故事原地打转，或者只是一堆互不相关的场景。通常动作片不会出现这种情况，但《黑色大丽花》就存在这个问题——主线处理的是情感冲突，而且完全是内在的，所以经常给人一种场景和支线剧情杂乱无章的感觉。


#↩

EMOTIONAL CONFLICT?

情绪冲突？


"Wait a minute!" some of you are saying. "*Emotional* conflict? Hey, we're talking about action pictures, aren't we? We don't need no stinking emotional conflict!"

“等等！”你们有些人可能会说，“*情感*冲突？嘿，我们说的是动作片，不是吗？我们不需要什么该死的情感冲突！”


Emotions are what make our characters human and what allows the audience to identify with them, and care whether they live or die. Without an emotional conflict the hero becomes two dimensional. Cardboard. The audience will have trouble identifying with them, and find the over-all conclusion of the film less satisfying. Instead of emotional the story becomes mechanical. Sure, you might be able to get away with not having an Emotional Conflict with the 'Superman Type' lead character, but why would you want to?

情感赋予角色人性，让观众能够与他们产生共鸣，关心他们的生死。没有情感冲突，英雄就会变得扁平，如同纸片人。观众难以产生共鸣，也会觉得影片的结局不够令人满意。故事不再充满情感，反而变得机械。当然，你或许可以勉强让“超人”式的主角摆脱情感冲突，但你为什么要这么做呢？


The most common way Emotional Conflicts are explored in film is through a Character Arc – a gradual change in the protagonist which takes place during the film due to the external conflict (plot). In “Witness” John Book (Harrison Ford) begins as a violent Philadelphia cop and through his association with the Amish gradually becomes a man who would rather use reason than violence. He learns one of those Hollywood valuable lessons. Now, you probably didn't even notice the Character Arc in “Witness” because it was shown through the actions of the protagonist and there wasn't any big speech or swelling orchestral music. You never want to use a sledge hammer to slam home your point or emotional conflict, you want to be subtle... make it almost invisible. We want the audience to *experience* it, but not necessarily think about it. Feel it – we are talking about emotions, right? Feelings.

电影中最常见的展现情感冲突的方式是通过人物弧线——主人公在影片中因外部冲突（情节）而发生的渐进式转变。在《证人》中，约翰·布克（哈里森·福特饰）起初是费城一名暴力警察，但通过与阿米什人的接触，他逐渐变成了一个宁愿用理性而非暴力来解决问题的人。他领悟到了好莱坞电影中常见的宝贵教训。你可能根本没注意到《证人》中的人物弧线，因为它是通过主人公的行动展现的，没有冗长的演讲，也没有激昂的管弦乐。你永远不想用大手笔来强调你的观点或情感冲突，你想用更微妙的方式……让它几乎难以察觉。我们希望观众*体验*它，但不一定非要思考它。感受它——我们谈论的是情感，对吧？感受。


Yes, in an action film.

是的，在一部动作片里。


As a challenge, I've taken a violent existential revenge film from the 1960s, John Boorman's "Point Blank" starring Lee Marvin. Okay, this is also my favorite film, so I've seen it a million times. The lead character, Walker, has no first name, almost no dialogue and shows no emotions... But he has an Emotional Conflict!

为了挑战自己，我选择了一部六十年代的暴力复仇电影——约翰·布尔曼执导、李·马文主演的《步步惊魂》。好吧，这也是我最喜欢的电影，所以我看过无数遍了。主角沃克没有名字，几乎没有台词，也不流露任何情感……但他却有着强烈的情感冲突！


The External Conflict: Walker, a career criminal who cooks up a large scale robbery with the help of his wife and best friend. After pulling the heist, the wife and best friend kill Walker and split with the cash. But Walker rises from the dead, tracks them down, and kills them and anyone else who gets in his way. A cold hearted vengeance machine. Many people die.

外部冲突：沃克，一个职业罪犯，伙同妻子和好友策划了一场大规模抢劫。抢劫成功后，妻子和好友杀死了沃克，并瓜分了赃款。但沃克死而复生，一路追踪他们，并杀死了他们以及任何阻挡他的人。他是一个冷酷无情的复仇机器。许多人因此丧命。


The Character Arc: Before the robbery, Walker is a playful, fun, character. We see him flirting with his wife, joking with his best friend. He's alive.

人物弧光：抢劫案发生前，沃克是一个爱玩爱闹、风趣幽默的人。我们看到他跟妻子调情，跟最好的朋友开玩笑。他当时还很健康。


After he's shot, he becomes cold and brutal. Dead inside. Unfeeling and uncaring. He hooks up with his wife's sister (played by Angie Dickenson) and uses her to find both his wife and best friend. After both are dead, Angie accuses him of being dead inside. Of not caring or trusting anyone.

他中枪后变得冷酷无情，内心如同行尸走肉，麻木不仁。他与妻子的妹妹（安吉·迪肯森饰演）勾搭上，利用她寻找妻子和挚友。两人死后，安吉指责他内心早已麻木，对任何人都不信任。


The Emotional Conflict: Walker has his vengeance, but still isn't satisfied... he wants his cut of the robbery money, and drafts Angie to help him. Angie fights him, and Walker finally realizes he will have to trust her and care about her, or she isn't going to help him. He must heal himself and stop being dead inside in order to achieve his goal. They actually go on a date in the film...the scene where he isn't killing people or trying to find people to kill.

情感冲突：沃克复仇成功，却仍不满足……他想要分得抢劫所得，于是拉拢安吉帮忙。安吉与他对抗，沃克最终意识到，他必须信任她、关心她，否则她不会帮他。他必须治愈自己，摆脱内心的麻木，才能达成目标。在电影中，他们甚至还约会了一次……那场戏里，他没有杀人，也没有到处寻找目标。


Conclusion: After he rejoins the living and learns to love and trust again, he is emotionally whole and has the strength required to get his cut of the money... But realizes he can be satisfied without it. He's alive again!

结论：当他重返人间，学会再次去爱和信任之后，他的情感完整了，也拥有了争取自己那份钱财的力量……但他意识到，即使没有钱，他也能过得很满足。他又活过来了！


Walker is forced to confront his Emotional Conflict (being dead inside) in order to solve his External Conflict (getting vengeance and his stolen money back and killing a lot of people).

为了解决外部冲突（复仇、夺回被盗的钱财和杀很多人），沃克被迫面对他的情感冲突（内心已死）。


Character Arcs don't have to be “learning a valuable lesson” - often they are about honest character who become dishonest or in the case of “Straw Dogs” a reasonable non-violent person who becomes a violent bad-ass... and maybe loses a piece of his soul in the process. “Unforgiven“ opens with Clint Eastwood as a reformed gunman who has given up violence, and tracks his arc step-by-step until he ends up a violent drunken killing machine. So the “valuable lesson” in that film would be that sometimes you just have to reject morality and kill a bunch of people.

人物弧光不一定非得是“吸取宝贵教训”——很多时候，它们讲述的是正直的人变得不诚实，或者像《稻草狗》那样，一个理性的非暴力人士变成一个暴力恶棍……或许在这个过程中也失去了一部分灵魂。《不可饶恕》以克林特·伊斯特伍德饰演的改过自新的枪手开场，他放弃了暴力，影片一步步地展现了他的堕落过程，直到他最终变成一个酗酒的暴力杀人机器。所以，这部电影的“宝贵教训”应该是：有时候你必须抛弃道德，杀人如麻。


And Character Arcs aren't always about characters *changing* - no transformation is required! Usually a Character Arc is about a character *changing back* - and “Face/Off” is a great example of this. Archer is a good husband and father until his son is murdered by a bullet meant for him, and from that moment on he loses his way – he becomes all about revenge instead of family. The film doesn't show us him changing, but shows us him realizing the wrong turn he made and getting his life back on the right track. Because people seldom change in real life, it is more realistic to show your character get knocked off course and have the story force him to find his way again. The great thing about this is that you can use the event that screwed up your hero's life as a story point – either opening with it as “Face/Off” does of revealing it later.

角色弧线并非总是关于角色的*改变*——无需任何转变！通常，角色弧线讲述的是角色*回归正轨*的故事——《变脸》就是一个很好的例子。阿彻原本是一位好丈夫、好父亲，直到他的儿子被一颗原本射向他的子弹夺去了生命。从那一刻起，他迷失了方向——他一心只想复仇，而非顾家。影片并没有展现他如何改变，而是展现了他如何意识到自己走错了路，并最终重回正轨。因为现实生活中人们很少改变，所以展现角色偏离正轨，然后让故事迫使他重新找到方向，这才是更符合现实的做法。这样做的好处在于，你可以将导致主角人生崩塌的事件作为故事的关键点——既可以像《变脸》那样在故事开头就揭示出来，也可以在后面慢慢展开。


There are two basics endings to a story – protagonist solves the problem, or problem solves the protagonist. You can have a tragedy where the character arc turns the protagonist into a monster or where the protagonist loses... as long as that is the point of your screenplay. You want to make sure the things that happen in your screenplay are there for a reason.

故事的结局基本有两种——主角解决问题，或者问题反过来解决主角。你可以写一个悲剧，让主角经历角色转变，最终变成一个怪物，或者让主角失败……只要这是你剧本的主旨。你要确保剧本中发生的每件事都有其存在的理由。


#↩

NO ARC?

没有弧光？


A Character Arc is only one kind of Emotional Conflict – and not a requirement in your screenplay. But you usually do need some sort of Emotional Conflict in order to humanize your protagonist. Though Indiana Jones does have a subtle Character Arc in “Raiders Of The Lost Ark” (the most curious man in the world who puts treasure before people and plans to con Marion out of the headpiece... and by the end will shut his eyes tight and protects Marion – putting people before treasure) most of the Emotional Conflict in the script focuses on his rocky relationship with Marion. She is his ex-lover and there is a major unresolved conflict. But he is forced to work with her and deal with that conflict. The big emotional scene in the story is when Indy thinks he has killed Marion and gets drunk. His actions caused her death. He is responsible for killing the woman he loves. Even if the story ended with Indy's eyes wide open, the scenes between him and Marion would provide enough emotional content for us to care about the character and *feel something* rather than just watch the movie.

角色弧光只是情感冲突的一种形式，并非剧本的必要元素。但通常来说，你需要某种情感冲突来塑造主角的人性。虽然《夺宝奇兵》中印第安纳·琼斯确实有一个微妙的角色弧光（他是世界上最好奇的人，把宝藏看得比人命更重要，还计划骗取玛丽昂的头饰……但最终他会闭上双眼保护玛丽昂——将人命置于宝藏之上），但剧本中的大部分情感冲突都集中在他与玛丽昂之间坎坷的关系上。她是他的前女友，两人之间存在着巨大的未解之谜。但他被迫与她合作，并努力克服这个难题。故事中最令人动容的场景是印第安纳·琼斯以为自己杀死了玛丽昂，于是借酒浇愁。他的行为导致了她的死亡。他要为自己所爱之人的死亡负责。即使故事以印第安纳·琼斯睁大双眼结束，他和玛丽昂之间的场景也足以提供足够的情感内容，让我们关心这个角色，并*有所感触*，而不仅仅是观看电影。


Although this is counter intuitive, a hero with a flaw they are struggling with is more interesting and involving than a “perfect” hero. Peter Parker in “Spider-Man” is responsible for the death of his Uncle Ben, and that guilt is what makes him easy to identify with. We have all done things we regret, we all have made terrible mistakes, none of us are perfect – and those flaws help us identify with a character. But even these flaws and issues need to be connected to the physical conflict in some way, not just tacked on to make your hero more interesting.

虽然这听起来有悖常理，但一个有自身缺陷、正在努力克服的英雄，比一个“完美”的英雄更有趣、更引人入胜。《蜘蛛侠》中的彼得·帕克要为本叔叔的死负责，正是这份愧疚感让他更容易引起观众的共鸣。我们都做过让自己后悔的事，都犯过严重的错误，没有人是完美的——而正是这些缺陷让我们能够与角色产生共鸣。但即便如此，这些缺陷和问题也需要与故事中的冲突有所关联，而不仅仅是为了让英雄更有趣而生硬地添加上去的。


Never forget that movies (even action movies) are *emotion pictures* - designed to make us feel something. If people are shooting at the hero, we need to care whether he or she lives or dies or the scene doesn't matter. An emotional conflict humanizes the character and makes them into more than just cannon fodder.

永远不要忘记，电影（即使是动作片）也是情感电影——旨在唤起我们的情感。如果有人向英雄开枪，我们就需要关心他或她的生死，否则这场戏就毫无意义。情感冲突使角色人性化，不再只是炮灰。


#↩

THEME AND NEXUS

主题与联系


Your big action conflict and your emotional conflict will be connected, and so will everything else. Stories are not random incidents. My “Thematic” theory connects all of the pieces of your story – from Character Arc to Act Two scenes to Actions and Visual Motifs to Specific Words and Phrases used in dialogue. I call the connection between all of these elements the Nexus... where theme touches everything.

你故事中的主要动作冲突和情感冲突是相互关联的，其他一切也都是如此。故事并非随机事件。我的“主题”理论将故事的所有元素联系起来——从人物弧线到第二幕场景，再到动作和视觉主题，以及对话中使用的特定词语和短语。我称所有这些元素之间的联系为“枢纽”……主题贯穿始终。


“Minority Report” is the ultimate Nexus film - thematic words and phrases pop up in much of the dialogue and are often part of the action. The screenplay by Scott Frank and Jon Cohen is based on a Philip K. Dick story where in the future, psychics can see crimes before they are committed, and the police arrest them. But when the psychics see the city's top cop, John Anderton, committing a future murder, he starts to wonder if the precog's vision is 20/20... while he runs for his life. So we have our man on the run and psychics who can see the future - and our theme is going to explore this idea of destiny and seeing the future.

《少数派报告》堪称Nexus电影的典范——主题词句频繁出现在对话中，并常常融入剧情。斯科特·弗兰克和乔恩·科恩的剧本改编自菲利普·K·迪克的小说，讲述了未来世界中，通灵者能够预见犯罪，并由警方逮捕他们。然而，当通灵者预见到城市最高警官约翰·安德顿将在未来犯下谋杀罪时，他开始怀疑这些预言家的视力是否真的准确……与此同时，他正亡命奔逃。于是，我们看到了亡命之徒和能够预知未来的通灵者——而我们的主题正是探讨命运和预知未来这一概念。


#↩

THE EYES HAVE IT

眼睛会说话


The film starts out with the precogs seeing a murder that has yet to be committed. One of the first lines of dialogue is future killer Howard Marks saying "You know how blind I am without my glasses."

影片开头，先知们预见了一起尚未发生的谋杀案。其中一句台词是未来的杀手霍华德·马克斯说的：“你知道我没戴眼镜的时候有多瞎吗？”


One of the first images we see is Marks' son cutting the eyes out of an Abe Lincoln mask - scissors poking through the eyes!

我们看到的第一个画面是马克的儿子正在剪掉亚伯拉罕·林肯面具的眼睛——剪刀从眼睛里戳了出来！


It's explained that "Precogs can see a murder four days out."

文中解释说，“先知可以提前四天看到谋杀案。”


The reason why Howard Marks is going to kill his wife and lover? He forgets his glasses, goes back home for them, and discovers his wife in bed with another man.

霍华德·马克斯为什么要杀死他的妻子和情人？他忘了拿眼镜，回家去拿，结果发现妻子和另一个男人睡在一起。


People in the future are identified by iris scans - called "Eye-Dents".

未来人们将通过虹膜扫描（称为“眼部识别”）来识别身份。


Not only do the police use iris scans, but they are used by advertisers to personalize video billboards and used to collect tolls on the subway.

不仅警方使用虹膜扫描，广告商也使用虹膜扫描来个性化视频广告牌，地铁也使用虹膜扫描来收取通行费。


Anderton may be the top cop in the city, but he's also a drug user. A drug dealer who recognizes him as the Police Chief pulls off his glasses to expose empty eye sockets and says "In the land of the blind, the one eyed man is king."

安德顿或许是这座城市最高级别的警官，但他同时也是个瘾君子。一个认出他是警察局长的毒贩摘下他的眼镜，露出空洞的眼窝，说道：“在盲人的国度里，独眼人称王。”


Danny Witwer is an *observer* from the Justice Department. That's a great one, because he could have been just an Agent with the Justice Department, but they found a way to put the eyes in there.

丹尼·维特沃是司法部的一名*观察员*。这个设定很棒，因为他原本可能只是司法部的一名普通特工，但他们想办法给他安排了观察员的角色。


"We see what they (the Precogs) see."

“我们看到了他们（先知们）所看到的一切。”


Witwer claims he has a warrant, "Show it to me."

维特沃声称他有搜查令，“拿出来给我看看。”


One of the Precogs, Agatha, grabs Anderton's arm and says: "Can you see?"

其中一位先知阿加莎抓住安德顿的手臂说：“你能看见吗？”


By the way, the three precogs are named after famous mystery writers – a Scott Frank touch, I'm sure. Anderton's mentor, Lamar, tells him to watch out for Witwer because: "The eyes of the nation are on us right now."

顺便一提，这三位预言家的名字都取自著名推理小说家——我敢肯定这是斯科特·弗兰克的安排。安德顿的导师拉马尔告诉他要提防维特沃，因为：“现在全国的目光都集中在我们身上。”


Once Anderton is accused of a future murder, he begins to question the very idea that precogs can see the future. The story itself was designed to explore the theme.

安德顿被指控犯下未来谋杀案后，他开始质疑预言家能够预知未来的说法。故事本身正是为了探讨这一主题而设计的。


On the run, Anderton plays hide and seek in a Lexus car factory with Witwer.

逃亡途中，安德顿和维特沃在一家雷克萨斯汽车工厂里玩起了捉迷藏。


Anderton goes to Dr. Hineman, who helped create the precogs. After hopping her fence, he's stung by some plants. The name of the plants? "Doll's Eyes". Again, they could have been called anything, but Scott Frank went for the thematic name.

安德顿去找了海尼曼博士，她曾参与创造预知者。他翻过海尼曼博士的栅栏后，被一些植物蜇伤了。这些植物叫什么名字？“娃娃眼”。其实它们可以叫任何名字，但斯科特·弗兰克选择了这个更贴切的名字。


Hineman tells him the precogs are basically crack babies who "Closed their eyes and dreamed only of murders."

希内曼告诉他，这些先知基本上都是吸毒过量而“闭上眼睛，梦里只有谋杀”的婴儿。


Her advice to Anderton? "Sometimes in order to see the light you have to risk the dark."

她给安德顿的建议是？“有时候，为了看到光明，你必须冒险进入黑暗。”


Anderton realizes that no matter where he goes, they will find him – thanks to the Eye-Dent system. The solution? Get an eye transplant!

安德顿意识到，无论他走到哪里，他们都会找到他——这都要“归功于”眼部追踪系统。解决办法是什么？去做眼角膜移植手术！


The crazy eye transplant doctor tells him that the nurse "Only has eyes for you."

那个疯狂的眼部移植医生告诉他，护士“眼里只有你”。


Anderton's ex-wife is a photographer who has "A good eye" according to Witwer.

据维特沃称，安德顿的前妻是一位摄影师，她“眼光很好”。


She tells him, "I left him because every time I looked at him I saw my son." She could have said "He reminded me on my son" but there's no looking and seeing in that sentence.

她告诉他：“我离开他，是因为每次看到他，我都会想起我的儿子。”她本可以说“他让我想起了我的儿子”，但这句话里并没有“看到”和“想起”这两个字。


Anderton's son is kidnapped at a public pool, and he screams "Have you seen my little boy?"

安德顿的儿子在公共游泳池被绑架了，他大声喊道：“你们看到我的小男孩了吗？”


The police have these little mechanical spiders that scan your eyes, and there's a great scene where Anderton tries to evade them.

警察有一种小型机械蜘蛛，可以扫描你的眼睛，安德顿试图躲避它们的场景非常精彩。


In order to break into the police station and kidnap the precog Agatha, he uses his old eyes at the retina scanners. Nice plan if it works, but Anderton drops his old eyes and they go rolling down a hallway toward a drainage grate! He has to chase his runaway eyes - another thriller scene that uses eyes!

为了闯入警察局绑架先知阿加莎，他用老眼在视网膜扫描仪上扫描。如果计划成功，那当然很棒，但安德顿却不小心把老眼掉了，它们顺着走廊滚向排水沟！他不得不追赶逃跑的眼球——又一个用眼睛制造悬念的惊悚场景！


You can make your own joke about rolling his eyes... But I kind of rolled my eyes when the retina scan still worked in this film. Even at McDonalds they take your employee ID out of the system after they fire you so that you won't have access to the cash drawer. This was the *police station* and a *murderer*.

你可以自己发挥想象，拿他翻白眼这件事开玩笑……不过，这部电影里视网膜扫描还能用的时候，我也确实翻了个白眼。就连麦当劳，解雇员工后都会把你的员工证从系统里注销，这样你就没法接触收银机了。这里可是*警察局*，而且是个*杀人犯*。


Now we get a funny "new eye gag" that's all about how seeing maybe shouldn't be believing - Anderton walks into the Gap and is identified as "Mr. Yakamoto" due to his new eyes. He holds up some clothes to a woman about Agatha's size - eyeballing the fit.

现在我们看到一个有趣的“新眼睛笑料”，它讲的是眼见不一定为实——安德顿走进盖普商店，因为他换了新眼睛，所以被认作“山本先生”。他拿起几件衣服给一位身材和阿加莎差不多的女士看，凭感觉判断合不合身。


The reason why he kidnaps the precog? "Agatha, I need to see... to see what is going to happen to me."

他绑架预言家的原因是什么？“阿加莎，我需要看看……看看我未来会怎么样。”


When they're trying to evade the police at a shopping mall, Agatha talks Anderton through it. "Can you see that umbrella? Take it!" She could have just said "Take the umbrella".

当他们试图在购物中心躲避警察时，阿加莎指导安德顿。“你看到那把伞了吗？拿着它！”她其实可以直接说“拿着伞”。


"You see a woman in a brown dress, she knows your face."

“你看到一个穿棕色连衣裙的女人，她认得你。”


When the police finally spot Anderton and Agatha, they don't say "I've got them" they say "We've got eyes on him."

当警察最终发现安德顿和阿加莎时，他们没有说“我抓到他们了”，而是说“我们已经盯上他了”。


The story also deals with perception in many scenes. Balloons obscure the Anderton and Agatha at the mall. The umbrella they grab comes in handy when it starts raining and *everyone* has an umbrella... making everyone look alike. In the precog vision of the crime there's a third man looking through the window... and that guy turns out to be a picture on a billboard across the street. Often what is seen in the story isn't really what is happening - the same way the precog's vision of Anderton committing murder isn't exactly what happens in the story.

故事中许多场景都探讨了感知问题。在商场里，气球遮住了安德顿和阿加莎的视线。他们抓起的伞在下雨时派上了用场，因为*每个人*都撑着伞……让大家看起来都一样。在预言家对犯罪的预知中，有一个人正透过窗户往里看……而这个人后来发现只是街对面广告牌上的照片。故事中呈现的景象往往与实际发生的事情并不完全一致——就像预言家预知安德顿杀人的场景与故事中实际发生的情况并不完全相同一样。


When they drive in the countryside, Agatha looks out the car window and says, "Can you see it, it's beautiful."

当她们开车行驶在乡间时，阿加莎望着车窗外说：“你看，真美啊。”


After Anderton is captured, the prison warden, Gideon, describes what happens when you're put in the stasis prison: "They say you have visions. Your life flashes before your eyes and all of your dreams come true."

安德顿被俘后，监狱长吉迪恩描述了被关进休眠监狱后会发生什么：“他们说你会看到幻象。你的一生会在你眼前闪过，你所有的梦想都会成真。”


Okay, some of you are probably wondering if screenwriters actually go to all of the trouble of making sure they use the word “Observer” instead of “Agent” because it’s thematic. I can’t speak for everyone... but *I* do it. Every single word in my screenplay is important, and I give every individual word a certain amount of thought. If there is a better word, that’s the word I want to use. I will make a list of thematic words and phrases and find a way to naturally fit them into the dialogue (if possible). Obviously, Scott Frank also does this - we get words and phrases and actions and situations about sight in “Minority Report” so that the theme is in every scene... but invisible and unobtrusive.

好吧，你们中有些人可能在想，编剧们是不是真的会费尽心思用“观察者”（Observer）而不是“代理人”（Agent）这个词，仅仅因为这样更符合主题。我不能代表所有人……但*我*会这么做。我剧本里的每一个字都很重要，我会仔细斟酌每一个词。如果有更好的词，我就会用那个词。我会列出一些主题相关的词语和短语，并想办法把它们自然地融入到对话中（如果可能的话）。显然，斯科特·弗兰克也这么做——在《少数派报告》中，我们看到了许多关于“视觉”的词语、短语、动作和情境，使得这个主题贯穿始终……却又巧妙地隐藏起来。


#↩

USING YOUR NEXUS

使用您的 Nexus


In my script, "The Last Stand", an accountant for an Oakland, CA criminal organization turns state's evidence. After testifying, he goes into Witness Relocation, and begins a new life with his wife and son in suburbia. Three years later, the mob finds him, and asks him to go back to Oakland for a "mob trial". If he doesn't go peaceably, they'll use force.

在我的剧本《最后的抵抗》中，一名为加州奥克兰犯罪集团工作的会计转为污点证人。作证后，他进入证人安置计划，与妻子和儿子在郊区开始了新生活。三年后，黑帮找到了他，要求他回到奥克兰接受“黑帮审判”。如果他不配合，他们将使用武力。


The accountant must turn against one *family* (the mob) to protect another *family* (his wife and son). Throughout the script are various scenes and examples of "Protecting The Family". All of the characters are defined by their families. The mob is a family. The police are a family. The FBI is a family. Each family tries to protect its members.
