1) Combine two existing action gags to create a third. How about a foot chase of the roofs of cars stopped at a red light... then the light turns green and you have “car surfing”? I've combined fist fights and shoot outs to create really frightening close quarters shoot outs where pistols are used as clubs between gunshots. How about a car chase where the driver and passenger have to switch places? I have a scene in “Sleeper Agent” that begins as a car chased by motorcycles – exchanging gunfire – then one of the bad guys jumps off their motorcycle and climbs through the sun room inside the car with his machine gun – and we have a *very* close quarters gun fight in the middle of a car chase! Or how about combining a car chase and a safe cracking scene from a heist movie? “Fast Five” has that great opening scene where the cars are chasing the train, pull up along side it... and “peel” open the door on an armored security container to rob the contents – while the train is still speeding down the tracks! Take two ideas, twist them together, and you end up with something fresh and exciting.

1）将两个现有的动作桥段结合起来，创造出第三个。比如，在红灯前，一群人沿着停着的汽车车顶追逐……然后绿灯亮了，就变成了“车顶冲浪”？我曾经把拳击和枪战结合起来，创造出非常惊险的近距离枪战，在枪声间隙，手枪被当成棍棒使用。或者，来一场汽车追逐，让司机和乘客交换位置怎么样？我在《沉睡特工》里有一个场景，开头是一辆汽车被摩托车追逐——双方交火——然后其中一个坏蛋跳下摩托车，带着他的机枪爬进车里的阳光房——于是，我们在汽车追逐中上演了一场*非常*近距离的枪战！或者，把汽车追逐和劫匪电影里的保险箱破解场景结合起来怎么样？ 《速度与激情5》的开场戏精彩绝伦：几辆汽车追逐着火车，与火车并排而行……然后“撬开”一个装甲保险箱的门，趁火车还在轨道上飞驰时，抢走了里面的东西！将两个创意巧妙融合，最终呈现出如此新鲜刺激的场面。


2) Take the gag past the limit. Knock it up a level. In "The French Connection"s car chase, pedestrians jump out of the way of the moving vehicles; "The Corruptor" takes it well past the limit by hitting a bunch of innocent people on the sidewalk. You never want to pull your punches in an action scene – you want to take things to the limit... and then maybe over the line. The reason why we remember gags like Ah-nuld using the bad guy as a human shield – and the bad guy getting *riddled with bullets* - is that it's over the line. You just don't do those things in movies! There's a great gag in the beginning of “Terminator 2” where Ah-nuld throws a biker across the room – through the window into the bar's kitchen - and the biker lands on top of the stove – his face right on the hot grill! The problem with this method is that bigger isn't usually better, and eventually we'll run out of violence frontiers... everything will end up a Michael Bay “bigger explosions” movie. But if you can find the *clever* way to take things past the limit, go for it!

2）把笑料发挥到极致，更上一层楼。在《法国贩毒网》的追车戏中，行人纷纷躲避疾驰的车辆；而《腐败分子》则更进一步，直接撞倒了人行道上的一群无辜行人。动作戏永远不能手下留情——你要把事情做到极致……甚至越过底线。我们之所以记得像阿诺·施瓦辛格把反派当人肉盾牌，以及反派被打得“弹无虚发”这样的桥段，正是因为它们太过火了。电影里根本不会拍这种戏！《终结者2》开头有个很棒的笑料：阿诺把一个骑摩托车的家伙扔过房间——穿过窗户，落到酒吧的厨房里——那家伙正好摔在炉子上，脸直接贴在滚烫的烤架上！这种方法的弊端在于，越大通常并非越好，最终我们会发现暴力元素的极限……所有电影都会变成迈克尔·贝式的“爆炸越大越好”。但如果你能找到*巧妙*的方法突破极限，那就放手去做吧！


3) Mixing genres . Taking an action gag usually associated with one genre and using it in a different genre. Using horse stunts with motorcycles. "Raiders Of The Lost Ark" transfers some of Yakima Canutt's great stunts from "Stagecoach" (1939) to a motorcycle / truck chase. You can do horse chases and stunts on motorcycles, and flip that like they did in the remake of “3:10 To Yuma” and use modern day car chase gags with horses and wagons. In the *script* to “Night Hunter” I have a vampire hunter hero with a shotgun that shoots wooden stakes. Don't let genre limit you – if you see a great *dance move* in a musical, you might use that in as a great fight scene gag. Donald O'Connor ran up a wall and flipped over onto his feet in “Singing In The Rain” - and I've seen that gag used in a martial arts film. I've seen sword fights with gun barrels – knocking the gun barrel so that it misses the hero. Hey, Jean-Claude Van Damme has used *ballet moves* in films like Mark Verheiden's “Time Cop” to avoid being killed. You've seen that Western scene where the horse has to jump across the ravine from one cliff to another? Okay, in “True Lies” we get that scene with the bad guy on a motorcycle and Ah-nuld on a horse. I've used the western gag of gunfighters facing off for a quick draw contest many times, and in many unusual locations.

3）类型混搭。将通常与一种类型相关的动作笑料运用到另一种类型中。比如，将马匹特技与摩托车结合。《夺宝奇兵》就借鉴了雅基马·卡努特在1939年电影《驿马车》中的一些精彩特技，并将其运用到摩托车/卡车追逐戏中。你可以用马匹追逐和摩托车特技，然后像《决战犹马镇》的翻拍版那样，将现代汽车追逐的笑料与马匹和马车结合起来。在《夜行猎手》的剧本中，我设计了一个吸血鬼猎人英雄，他使用的霰弹枪可以发射木桩。不要让类型限制你的创作——如果你在一部歌舞片中看到一个精彩的舞蹈动作，你可以把它用作打斗场景中的一个绝妙笑料。唐纳德·奥康纳在《雨中曲》中跑上一堵墙，然后翻身站稳——我曾在一部武术电影中看到过类似的桥段。我见过用枪管进行剑术对决——击打枪管让子弹避开主角。嘿，尚格·云顿在马克·维海登的《时空特警》之类的电影里就用过*芭蕾舞步*来躲避攻击。你看过西部片里马要从一处悬崖跳到另一处悬崖的场景吗？好吧，在《真实的谎言》里，我们也看到了类似的场景，坏人骑着摩托车，阿诺·施瓦辛格骑马。我多次在各种意想不到的地方使用西部片里枪手对决拔枪的桥段。


4) Unusual locations. We're used to seeing those quick draw contests on dusty western streets... so let's stage them someplace else! In "Show Of Force" my Top Gun hero was engaged in an air battle with the villain. These sequences usually end with the hero shooting down the villain's plane, but that's the cliche I wanted to avoid. So I had them play chicken (from 1950s juvenile delinquent movies) and fire missiles at each other (the airplane version of the "high noon" shoot out). In those 1950s juvenile delinquent movies, there was always some guy who rolled out of the car only seconds before impact. So I had my hero eject before the planes slammed into each other... but the villain ejects, too! The hero and villain pop their parachutes about a hundred yards away from each other... and engage in a "high noon" shoot out in the sky! A "para-shoot out"! From the dusty western streets to the sky thousands of feet above the ground!

4）不同寻常的地点。我们习惯了在尘土飞扬的西部街道上看到那些快速拔枪比赛……所以，让我们换个地方来演吧！在《武力展示》中，我的《壮志凌云》英雄与反派展开了一场空战。这类场景通常以英雄击落反派的飞机而告终，但这正是我想要避免的俗套。所以我让他们玩起了胆小鬼游戏（借鉴了20世纪50年代青少年犯罪电影的套路），互相发射导弹（飞机版的“正午决斗”）。在那些20世纪50年代的青少年犯罪电影里，总会有人在撞击前几秒从车里跳出来。所以我让我的英雄在飞机相撞前弹射……但反派也弹射了！英雄和反派在相距约一百码的地方打开降落伞……然后在空中展开了一场“正午决斗”！一场“降落伞枪战”！从尘土飞扬的西部街道到万米高空！


5) Role reversals. Sometimes a cliche action gag can be made fresh and exciting just by swapping the hero and villain. We are used to seeing heroes following certain patterns and villains following other patterns... and that makes for a predictable scene. I've written some action scenes, then did a cut-and-paste to swap hero and villain names and see what I end up with. Often it's a more interesting scene. A scene in “Night Hunter” was inspired by the Tech Noir Bar shootout in “The Terminator” - I wondered what would happen if it was the *hero* blasting away in a crowded night club and the villain trying to get away? Another great role reversal is hero and love interest – and the example I use when I teach my 2 day class is “Romancing The Stone” where rough-tough action guy Michael Douglas is trying to scale a wall to save writer Kathleen Turner from the evil villain Zolo... except he can't get up the damned wall, so *she* has to save herself. She becomes the bad-ass fighter in the scene. Again, there are certain patterns that love interests and sidekicks and heroes follow – and mixing them up can result in unexpected elements in a scene. I've created some interesting action scenes just by writing the scene then swapping the characters.

5）角色互换。有时候，只要把英雄和反派互换一下，就能让老套的动作桥段变得新鲜刺激。我们习惯了英雄遵循某种模式，反派遵循另一种模式……这会让剧情变得可预测。我写过一些动作场景，然后把英雄和反派的名字互换一下，看看会得到什么。通常情况下，这样会更有趣。《夜行猎手》中的一个场景灵感就来自《终结者》里的科技酒吧枪战——我当时就在想，如果*英雄*在拥挤的夜总会里大开杀戒，而反派则试图逃跑，会发生什么？另一个很棒的角色互换是英雄和爱情对象——我在为期两天的课程中经常举《绿宝石》的例子，片中硬汉动作明星迈克尔·道格拉斯试图爬墙去救被邪恶反派佐罗绑架的作家凯瑟琳·特纳……结果他爬不上去，所以*她*只能自救了。她成了这场戏里的狠角色。再说一遍，爱情对象、跟班和英雄都有一些固定的模式——把他们混在一起，就能给场景带来意想不到的元素。我曾经通过写好场景，然后交换角色，创作出一些精彩的动作戏。


6) Props. Watch any Jackie Chan movie for an example. Chan loves to use whatever is available as a lethal weapon. In "Rumble In The Bronx" there's a fight in a grocery store that uses shopping carts, refrigerated cases, canned foods, and everything else you might find in the location as a weapon. Think about the location where your action scene takes place - what would you find there? How could you use it in a fight? I wrote an article for Script Magazine called “Hitchcock's Chocolates” about an Alfred Hitchcock theory that you use the elements of the locations and characters in your story. His film “Secret Agent” took place in Switzerland, so there was skiing and mountain climbing and a big scene in a chocolate factory... and the bad guy spies smuggled messages out in coded candy bar wrappers! So if you have a fight in a garden shed, using a rake or hoe as a weapon makes sense. This is not just a clever way to spice up a fight scene, it's *organic* - if you have a fight scene in a Starbucks Coffee shop, what are the weapons? If someone pulls out a meat cleaver, the audience will wonder where that came from. Using the weapons that are organic to the location or the character just makes sense... and combining this with unusual locations for an action scene results in all kinds of great props to use as fight scene gags.

6）道具。看看成龙的任何一部电影就知道了。成龙喜欢利用一切可以利用的东西作为致命武器。在《红番区》中，有一场发生在超市里的打斗，购物车、冷藏柜、罐头食品以及你在现场能找到的任何东西都被用作了武器。想想你的动作场景发生的地点——你会在那里找到什么？你如何将它们运用到打斗中？我曾为《剧本杂志》写过一篇题为《希区柯克的巧克力》的文章，探讨了阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克的一个理论：在故事中运用场景和人物的元素。他的电影《特工》的故事发生在瑞士，所以有滑雪、登山的场景，还有在巧克力工厂的大场面……而坏人间谍竟然用编码的巧克力包装纸传递信息！所以，如果你要在花园小屋里安排一场打斗，用耙子或锄头作为武器就合情合理了。这不仅仅是为打斗场面增添趣味的巧妙方法，它本身就非常“自然”——如果你的打斗场面发生在星巴克咖啡店，那么武器会是什么？如果有人掏出一把肉刀，观众肯定会好奇这刀是从哪儿来的。使用与场景或角色本身相符的武器才是明智之举……而将这一点与一些不寻常的动作场景相结合，就能创造出各种各样绝妙的道具，用来制造打斗场面的笑料。


7) Flipping the cliche. Just take what the audience expects to see and flip it just when they think they know what's coming next. In my "Dead Run" script I decided to play with cliches in my action scenes. I decided to end my car chase on a draw bridge. You've seen it a million times before: the hero's car jumps the gap in the bridge but the villain's car can't make it. Not in my script! The hero's car loses speed as it drives up the bridge, doesn't quite make the jump... gets wedged between both halves of the bridge. Stuck! The villain's car stops his car behind the hero's car, grabs his gun and starts shooting! The hero is a sitting duck! Only one way out - he opens the door and dives into the river below. Now he's a duck in the water - nothing to hide behind as the villain fires down at him! The only cover the hero can find - his car on the draw bridge. The villain has trouble shooting around it. Safety? Nope! As the draw bridge opens, the car gets unstuck... and falls down onto the hero! I twisted around the old "car jumps the draw bridge" cliche so that the expected doesn't happen.

7）颠覆陈规。打破观众的预期，在他们以为已经猜到接下来会发生什么的时候，来个出其不意的反转。在我的《亡命狂飙》剧本中，我决定在动作戏中玩转陈规。我决定把追车戏的结尾安排在吊桥上。你肯定看过无数遍这样的桥段：英雄的车飞跃桥面，反派的车却过不去。但我的剧本可不一样！英雄的车在桥上行驶时速度减慢，没能成功跃过……卡在了桥的两半之间。动弹不得！反派的车停在英雄的车后，拔枪扫射！英雄成了活靶子！唯一的出路——他打开车门，跳进下面的河里。现在他就像一只落水的鸭子——没有任何掩体，反派正朝他开火！英雄唯一能找到的掩体——吊桥上的车。反派很难绕过车子射击。安全吗？不！吊桥打开后，汽车脱困……然后掉下来砸在了主人公身上！我颠覆了“汽车飞跃吊桥”这个老套的桥段，让意料之外的事情发生了。


8) Upside down action. A cousin to flipping the cliche, this method uses the exact opposite of the scene we've seen before. Instead of a high speed car chase, we do the slowest car chase in history (stuck in rush hour traffic, moving at five miles per hour). A great example of this is when Goldfinger has James Bond strapped to the table and the laser beam is inching up towards his crotch and Bond says, “Do you expect me to talk?” and that is exactly what scenes like this are about. The villain tortures the hero for information or vice-versa. We've seen it in a million movies. But Goldfinger responds, “No, I expect you to die,” and *walks away*! I have a scene in a script where a car is trying to run over the hero... so the hero turn and runs straight at the car! If a scene works one way, do the opposite to find an original scene.

8）反转剧情。这种方法类似于颠覆陈规，它使用的场景与我们之前见过的完全相反。我们不用高速飙车，而是来一场史上最慢的飙车（堵在高峰期的车流中，时速只有五英里）。一个很好的例子是，当金手指把詹姆斯·邦德绑在桌子上，激光束缓缓向上照射到他的裆部时，邦德问道：“你指望我开口吗？” 这正是这类场景的精髓所在。反派拷问英雄以获取情报，或者反过来。我们在无数电影里都见过这种桥段。但金手指却回答说：“不，我希望你死。”然后转身离开！我剧本里有个场景，一辆车试图撞向英雄……结果英雄转身就朝车跑去！如果一个场景用某种方式拍出来效果很好，那就反其道而行之，创造一个全新的场景。


9) Personalize it or make it realistic. Find the detail that makes it different. We are so used to seeing Hollywood shoot outs that we forget what happens in real shoot outs. An automatic weapon not only sprays bullets, it sprays hot brass shell casings. You don't want to get hit by these. Have you ever seen a movie where the hero and villain are wrestling with a machine gun, and the hero pulls the trigger so that the hot brass hits the villain in the face? Did you know that a gun barrel becomes hot after firing and will burn your hand if you grab it? When you punch someone in the head, there's a good chance you'll break a knuckle or two. These details make great action gags, and can take your action sequence in a fresh new direction. After you've broken your hand, do you hit the guy again? Or start kicking him?

9) 个性化或使其更真实。找到让它与众不同的细节。我们太习惯看好莱坞式的枪战，以至于忘记了真实枪战中会发生什么。自动武器不仅会喷射子弹，还会喷射滚烫的弹壳。你肯定不想被这些弹壳击中。你有没有看过这样的电影：英雄和反派争夺机枪，英雄扣动扳机，滚烫的弹壳击中反派的脸？你知道枪管在射击后会变得很烫，如果你抓住它，就会烫伤你的手吗？当你打人头部时，很有可能会弄断一两个指关节。这些细节可以成为绝佳的动作笑料，并能让你的动作场面焕然一新。手骨折后，你会继续打人吗？还是开始踢他？


10) Gee whiz! Let your imagination run wild and come up with something weird. We've probably covered this with “Wanted”s car driving into a train and the whole bend it like Beckham shooting *around* people, but using your imagination to create an amazing action scene is a great way to get your scripts noticed... and have one of those scenes people talk about long after they've seen the movie. "The Matrix" has some wild action gags - like Carrie-Anne Moss jumping off a roof, through a small window in the building across the street, rolling down a flight of stairs and popping up with her guns ready for action. Outrageous! Hey, and that's not even mentioning the whole “bullet time” shoot out. Challenge yourself to come up with the most amazing action gags you can think of. The wilder the better! We want them to skim the dialogue because they can't wait to get to your next action sequence.

10）哇哦！尽情发挥你的想象力，想出一些奇奇怪怪的点子吧。我们可能已经用《通缉令》里汽车撞火车和贝克汉姆式绕着人群射门的桥段来举例过了，但用你的想象力创作一个精彩的动作场景，绝对是让你的剧本脱颖而出的好方法……而且还能让观众在看完电影很久之后仍然津津乐道。《黑客帝国》里就有很多疯狂的动作桥段——比如凯瑞-安·莫斯从屋顶跳下来，穿过街对面楼房的小窗户，滚下楼梯，然后突然出现，手里拿着枪，准备开火。真是太疯狂了！嘿，这还没提到“子弹时间”枪战呢。挑战一下自己，想出你能想到的最精彩的动作桥段吧。越疯狂越好！我们希望观众们会略过对话，因为他们迫不及待地想看你的下一个动作场面。


11) Another exciting method for creating action gags is to MacGyverize your props. In my “Last Stand” screenplay I have a fight in a kitchen that uses all kinds of weaponized household items you would find in your kitchen cupboards. Spray oven cleaner and a match makes a great blow torch. Mix cooking oil and dish soap and you get napalm. Ammonia and bleach makes poison gas. Hey, and we haven't even opened the knife drawer, yet! Actually, I think in that scene when the hero *does* open the knife drawer, he reaches in and grabs... the potato masher! Not the best weapon in a fight. But that's part of the fun of found weapons – they don't only include the things that would make great weapons, there's also the things that are mostly useless in a fight. Mostly. If you get stuck with the potato masher – how do you use it as a weapon? One of the two scenes that sold my “Night Hunter” script had the hero lose all of his weapons and have to dumpster dive for new weapons. He created shuriken fighting stars from food can lids and a bo from a broken broom handle. Though this was a cool scene, writing it required that I pick through garbage to see what might make a good weapon... kind of messy and smelly research. In Joe Carnahan's “The Grey” Liam Neeson uses broken airline miniature bottles to make a pair of deadly brass knuckles. If your hero is trapped in a class room with a box of paperclips, a rubber band, and a ruler – how would he defend himself?

11）另一个制造动作笑料的绝妙方法是改造道具。在我的剧本《最后的抵抗》中，有一场厨房打斗戏，用到了各种你能在厨房橱柜里找到的家用物品。烤箱清洁剂和火柴就能做成一个简易的喷灯。食用油和洗洁精混合就能制成凝固汽油弹。氨水和漂白剂混合就能制成毒气。嘿，我们还没打开刀具抽屉呢！实际上，我觉得在那个场景里，当主角打开刀具抽屉时，他伸手进去抓的是……土豆捣碎器！这可不是打斗中最好的武器。但这正是“捡来的武器”的乐趣所在——它们不仅包括那些能成为强力武器的东西，还包括那些在打斗中几乎毫无用处的东西。当然，只是“几乎”没用。如果你手里只有土豆捣碎器——你该怎么把它当武器用呢？我的《夜行猎手》剧本之所以能成功售出，其中一个场景是：主人公失去了所有武器，不得不去垃圾堆里翻找。他用食品罐头盖制作了手里剑，用断掉的扫帚柄制作了棍子。虽然这个场景很酷，但为了写好它，我不得不翻遍垃圾堆，看看哪些东西能做成好武器……这可真是个又脏又臭的研究过程。在乔·卡纳汉的《人狼大战》中，利亚姆·尼森用碎的航空小瓶子制作了一副致命的指虎。如果你的主人公被困在教室里，只有一盒回形针、一根橡皮筋和一把尺子——他会如何自卫呢？


12) Unusual uses. A cousin to MacGyverizing – some items have a boring common use, but with some imagination can be used for evil! My friend Bob Stone bought a ceramic frog for his garden that croaked whenever anyone passed in front of it. Kind of a joke thing... but I came up with a slightly different use for it, and in my “Baker Touch” script I have a spooky scene where an FBI Agent is creeping through a bank robbery gang's house, knowing that there are four armed men hiding somewhere inside. But the robbers have set up a dozen of these ceramic frogs as alarms. Every time she triggers a frog's croaking, she spins – ready to fire... And the hidden bank robbers know her position! The frogs make great gags throughout the scene – creating jump moments and suspense. Now whenever I see something innocent that can be used for a potentially evil purpose in an action scene I write it down. You know those Birthday cards that allow you to record your own greeting? Imagine recording “Here I am!” on a dozen of them and setting each to trigger when someone opens a door? In “Rear Window” Jimmy Stewart uses his camera's flash to blind the man trying to attack him. I think with things like this, the more “innocent” an item is, the more fun it is to use it as a weapon. If you can find a way to use a Teddy Bear as a weapon, I guarantee people will be talking about that after the movie.

12）非同寻常的用途。这有点像“麦克盖式改造”——有些东西用途平淡无奇，但只要发挥一点想象力，就能用于邪恶的目的！我的朋友鲍勃·斯通买了一只陶瓷青蛙放在花园里，只要有人从它前面经过，它就会呱呱叫。这本来只是个玩笑……但我想到了一个略有不同的用途。在我的剧本《贝克之触》里，我设计了一个惊悚的场景：一名联邦调查局特工潜入一个银行劫匪团伙的房子，她知道里面藏着四个持枪歹徒。但劫匪们设置了十几个这样的陶瓷青蛙作为警报器。每次特工触发青蛙的叫声，她就会转身——准备开枪……而藏在里面的劫匪们也因此知道了她的位置！这些青蛙在整个场景中制造了许多笑料——营造出惊险刺激的氛围和悬念。现在，每当我看到一些看似无害的东西，却有可能在动作场景中被用于邪恶的目的时，我都会把它记下来。你知道那种可以录制自己祝福语的生日贺卡吗？想象一下录制“我来了！”把十几个都设置成有人开门时触发？在《后窗》里，吉米·斯图尔特就用相机闪光灯晃瞎了试图袭击他的人的眼睛。我觉得像这样的东西，越是“无辜”的物品，用作武器就越有趣。如果你能找到用泰迪熊当武器的方法，我保证电影结束后人们会津津乐道。


I always jot down props and action gag ideas and action scene ideas. You never know when you'll be writing an action scene and need a great gag, flip through the note cards and find the perfect thing to make my scene work. Keep your eyes open for the details in life – that's where you'll spot the cool action gags. That ladder on the back of the SUV stuck in traffic next to you?

我总是会记下道具、动作笑料和动作场景的灵感。你永远不知道什么时候会需要写一个动作场景，需要一个绝妙的笑料，这时翻翻这些笔记卡片，就能找到让场景成立的完美道具。时刻留意生活中的细节——你会发现那些酷炫的动作笑料。比如，你旁边堵车时，SUV 后备箱上的梯子？



#↩

REVERSALS AND RUGPULLS

逆转与拉格普尔斯


Now that we have our original action scenes and some great action gags, how do we keep those scenes exciting? Shane ("Lethal Weapon") Black says: "The key to a good action scene is reversals. The "Star Wars" movies work because they are FULL of reversals."

既然我们已经有了原创的动作场面和一些精彩的动作笑料，那么如何才能让这些场面保持刺激呢？《致命武器》的导演肖恩·布莱克说：“精彩动作场面的关键在于反转。《星球大战》系列电影之所以成功，正是因为它们充满了反转。”


What's a reversal, you ask? Let Shane explain: "It's like a good news, bad news joke. The bad news is, you get thrown out of an airplane. The good news is, you're wearing a parachute. The bad news is, your rip cord breaks. The good news is, you have a back up 'chute. The bad news is, you can't reach the cord. Back and forth, just like that, until the character reaches the ground. He's gonna die... no, he's not... Reversal, reversal, reversal."

你问什么是反转？让肖恩来解释：“这就像一个有好消息也有坏消息的笑话。坏消息是你被扔出了飞机。好消息是你穿着降落伞。坏消息是你的降落伞拉绳断了。好消息是你还有备用伞。坏消息是你够不到拉绳。就这样来回折腾，直到角色落地。他要死了……不，他不会……反转，反转，反转。”


There are two types of reversals – Story Reversals and Scene Reversals. Story Reversals are when a character has a plan or the audience has an expectation and it runs into a dead end, so that the character must figure out a new plan. The romantic lead finally works up the nerve to ask person of their dreams out on a date... except they are with their new beau. Reversal. Now the story must go in a different direction. Story Reversals are like rocks and mountains in the way of a river – the river will still flow to its destination (the sea), but it will have to work its way around the obstacles. Shane was talking about Scene Reversals, which are the cornerstone of any great action scene. These are little things that come in the way of moment-by-moment plans. The hero reaches out to grab a fallen gun and the villain kicks it away. But filling your action scenes with Scene Reversals you keep them exciting and involving and unpredictable. It's not just two people fighting – which can get boring after a sentence or two – it's a battle where advantage changes with every line.

反转有两种类型——故事反转和场景反转。故事反转是指角色原本的计划或观众的预期落空，导致计划无法实现，角色不得不另寻新方案。比如，浪漫的主角终于鼓起勇气约梦中情人出去……结果发现对方已经有了新欢。反转！故事必须朝着另一个方向发展。故事反转就像河流上的巨石和山脉——河流最终仍会奔向终点（大海），但必须绕过这些障碍。肖恩刚才谈到的是场景反转，它是任何精彩动作场景的基石。这些看似不起眼的小细节，却会打破原有的计划。比如，英雄伸手去捡掉落的枪，反派却一脚踢开。在动作场景中穿插场景反转，能让它们保持刺激、引人入胜且充满悬念。这不仅仅是两个人之间的争斗——这种争斗一两句话后就会变得无聊——这是一场优势随着每一句话而变化的战斗。


#↩

JUST WHEN YOU THOUGHT IT WAS SAFE

正当你以为一切都安全的时候


Reversals make your action scenes unpredictable and exciting. It's one cliffhanger after another, and the audience stays on the edge of their seats wondering what will happen next.

剧情反转让动作场面更加难以预测，也更加刺激。一个接一个的悬念让观众始终紧张不已，迫不及待地想知道接下来会发生什么。


In "The Fugitive" Harrison Ford as Richard Kimble is being chased down the stairs by Agent Gerard. Kimble reaches the lobby, but Gerard is right behind him. Kimble breaks through a crowd of people, and sees the automatic exit door only a few feet away. But the doors are whooshing closed. Gerard is right behind him. Kimble squeezes through the doors... but his foot gets stuck! Gerard draws his gun, and gets ready to shoot. Kimble tries to wiggle his foot out. Gerard takes aim. Kimble squeezes his foot out of the door. Gerard fires! Kimble hits the dirt. Gerard re-aims. Kimble stumbles to his feet. Gerard has a PERFECT shot and squeezes the trigger. BANG! The glass scars... it's bullet proof. Kimble gets away.

在电影《亡命天涯》中，哈里森·福特饰演的理查德·金布尔被探员杰拉德追赶着下了楼梯。金布尔跑到大厅，但杰拉德紧随其后。金布尔挤过人群，看到自动出口就在几英尺外。但门嗖地一声关上了。杰拉德就在他身后。金布尔挤过门……但他的脚卡住了！杰拉德拔出枪，准备射击。金布尔试图把脚挣脱出来。杰拉德瞄准。金布尔终于把脚从门里挤出来了。杰拉德开枪了！金布尔应声倒地。杰拉德重新瞄准。金布尔踉跄着站了起来。杰拉德瞄准得非常准，扣动了扳机。砰！玻璃裂开了……原来是防弹的。金布尔逃脱了。


The great thing about reversals is that they are no cost excitement – you could spend millions of a big car chase, but a great reversal costs nothing. I interviewed Robert Rodriguez for Script Magazine, and the budget for his first film "El Mariachi" was only $7,000.00 - so there was no money for special effects, stars, or locations. The only thing Robert had was the script, and he filled it with reversals.

反转的妙处在于它能带来零成本的刺激——你可以花几百万美元拍一场大型追车戏，但一个精彩的反转却无需任何成本。我曾为《剧本杂志》采访过罗伯特·罗德里格兹，他的第一部电影《杀手悲歌》的预算只有7000美元——这意味着没有钱用于特效、明星或外景拍摄。罗伯特唯一拥有的就是剧本，而他用反转填满了整个剧本。


My favorite example from the film is the scene where our hero is being chased down the street by armed killers and comes to an intersection. The light is against him. The killers are gaining. Our hero grabs the tailgate of a passing pick up truck and flips inside the bed. The killers get to the intersection and see the pick up truck zooming away. Our hero breathes a sigh of relief... he's safe! The villain gets on his walkie talkie and tells his henchman that the hero has escaped in a truck, can the henchman head him off? In the pick up truck bed, our hero ducks down so that no one can see him. The henchman tells the villain: "I don't need to head him off. He jumped in the back of MY pick up truck. Want me to bring him around?" The hero panics as the pick up truck swings around and takes him back to the villain!

电影里我最喜欢的例子是，我们的英雄被一群持枪杀手追赶，来到一个十字路口。红灯对他不利，杀手们步步逼近。英雄抓住一辆疾驰而过的皮卡车的后挡板，翻身钻进了车厢。杀手们赶到路口，看到皮卡车飞驰而去。英雄长舒一口气……他安全了！反派拿起对讲机，告诉他的手下英雄已经乘车逃跑了，问手下能不能拦住他。在皮卡车厢里，英雄赶紧蹲下，不让任何人看到他。手下对反派说：“我不用拦他了。他跳进了我的皮卡车后车厢。要我把他带回来吗？”英雄惊慌失措，皮卡车猛地掉头，把他带回了反派面前！


The cantina shoot out in the sequel/remake “Desperado” is wall-to-wall reversals... my favorite is when the Mariachi and the Assassin slide down the bar top and put their guns to each other's heads and pull the triggers: click! Click! Now they are grabbing fallen guns from the hands of dead bad guys trying to find one with ammunition!

续集/重制版《亡命之徒》中的酒馆枪战充满了反转……我最喜欢的是，当墨西哥流浪乐队成员和刺客从吧台上滑下来，用枪指着对方的脑袋扣动扳机时：咔哒！咔哒！现在他们却在从死去的坏蛋手中捡枪，试图找到一把有子弹的枪！


#↩

REVERSALS IN ACTION

行动中的逆转


When I was a guest speaker at the Sacramento Film Festival a few years ago, I used a scene from “Road Warrior” to show how reversals work... but for the new edition of the book I thought it would be fun to use a scene from “Raiders Of The Lost Ark”, so here is the “Flying Wing Scene. The set up: Indiana Jones and Marion have been captured by the Nazis... who also have Ark. They escape – but are deep in Nazi controlled territory and must find a way out. That's when Indy spots the Flying Wing and tells Marion that they will *fly* out of here. He tells her to remove the wheel blocks so that they can take off while he deals with the pilot. Indy climbs the wing to deal with the Pilot in the cockpit...

几年前我在萨克拉门托电影节做客座演讲时，曾用《疯狂的麦克斯2：公路战士》中的一个场景来解释反转的原理……但为了新版书籍，我觉得用《夺宝奇兵》中的一个场景会更有趣，所以就有了“飞翼”场景。故事背景：印第安纳·琼斯和玛丽昂被纳粹俘虏……他们还得到了约柜。他们成功逃脱，但身处纳粹控制区深处，必须找到出路。这时，印第安纳发现了飞翼，告诉玛丽昂他们可以乘飞机离开这里。他让玛丽昂移开轮挡，以便他们起飞，而他则去对付飞行员。印第安纳爬上机翼，准备在驾驶舱里解决飞行员……


BAD NEWS: When Indy gets partway up the wing, a Soldier comes up behind him with a huge monkeywrench.

坏消息：当印第安纳·琼斯爬到机翼一半高度时，一名士兵拿着一个巨大的扳手从他身后出现。


GOOD NEWS: Indy slides down the wing to fight him. This is good news, because they are in the middle of a Nazi camp, and if the Soldier had called for help there would be hundreds of soldiers to deal with.

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯从机翼滑下来与他交战。这是个好消息，因为他们身处纳粹集中营，如果那个士兵呼叫支援，他们就得面对数百名士兵。


BAD NEWS: The Soldier swings the monkeywrench at Indy's head.

坏消息：士兵挥舞着扳手砸向印第安纳·琼斯的头部。


GOOD NEWS: Indy catches his arm and pushes him back until the monkeywrench hits one of the plane's two whirring propellers – kicking the wrench out of his hands. Now the fight is more even, and Indy K.O.s the Soldier.

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯抓住他的胳膊，把他往后推，直到扳手撞到飞机两个旋转的螺旋桨之一——扳手被踢飞了。现在双方势均力敌，印第安纳·琼斯击倒了士兵。


BAD NEWS: The biggest, baddest, baldest Nazi soldier in the world sees Indy knock down knock down the other soldier and wants to get into this fight... but he's going to take off his shirt to expose his amazing build first.

坏消息：世界上最高大、最凶狠、最秃顶的纳粹士兵看到印第安纳·琼斯击倒了另一名士兵，也想加入战斗……但他要先脱掉上衣，露出他惊人的身材。


GOOD NEWS: Marion grabs the first set of wheel blocks from the plane. One set down, one to go!

好消息：玛丽昂从飞机上取下了第一组轮块。一组搞定，还剩一组！


BAD NEWS: The Big Nazi just slams Indy in the face, knocking him down. The Big Nazi then *picks Indy up* to throw him...

坏消息：纳粹大佬一拳打在印第安纳·琼斯脸上，把他打倒在地。然后，纳粹大佬又把琼斯拎起来，准备把他扔出去……


GOOD NEWS: Indy bites the Big Nazi's arm to get him to let go.

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯咬了纳粹大佬的胳膊，让他放手。


BAD NEWS: The Big Nazi still throws Indy – just probably not as far as if he hadn't been bitten. Hey, maybe that's good news?

坏消息：纳粹大魔王仍然会把印第安纳·琼斯扔出去——只是可能不会像没被咬过那样扔得那么远。嘿，也许这是个好消息？


GOOD NEWS: Indy runs around the plane – away from the Big Nazi!

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯绕着飞机跑——躲开了那个大纳粹！


BAD NEWS: Right into the Pilot's pistol sights! The Pilot carefully aims at Indy's head! The Pilot fires – but misses because the plane is slowly moving. Re-aims!

坏消息：正中飞行员的瞄准镜！飞行员小心翼翼地瞄准印第安纳·琼斯的头部！飞行员开枪——但因为飞机缓慢移动，所以没打中。重新瞄准！


GOOD NEWS: Indy sees the Pilot and runs away... back to the Big Nazi! Okay, that's not entirely good news.

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯看到了飞行员，然后逃走了……回到了纳粹大佬身边！好吧，这也不完全是好消息。


BAD NEWS: The Big Nazi *knocks* Indy back to the front of the plane!

坏消息：纳粹大佬把印第安纳·琼斯打回了飞机前部！


WORSE NEWS: Right into the Pilot's pistol sights again! The Pilot gets ready to fire!

更糟糕的消息：又一次正中飞行员的瞄准镜！飞行员准备开火！


GOOD NEWS: The Big Nazi steps in the Pilot's way and begins beating the crap out of Indy. Again – This is good news? The Big Nazi knocks Indy to the ground... and prepares to stomp him. I guess that is better than being shot in the head.

好消息：纳粹大佬挡住了飞行员的路，开始暴揍印第安纳·琼斯。再说一遍——这算是好消息？纳粹大佬把印第安纳·琼斯打倒在地……准备狠狠踩他。我猜这总比被爆头强吧。


BAD NEWS: Indy throws dirt in the Big Nazi's eyes, blinding him. Okay, you might think that sounds like Good News, except when the Big Nazi staggers away – the Pilot has a clear shot at Indy's *head* and prepares to pull the trigger!

坏消息：印第安纳·琼斯朝纳粹大佬的眼睛里扔了土，把他弄瞎了。好吧，你可能觉得这听起来像个好消息，但当纳粹大佬踉跄着走开时——飞行员正好瞄准了印第安纳·琼斯的脑袋，准备扣动扳机！


GOOD NEWS: Marion *slams* the wheel blocks into the Pilot's head, and he goes down in the cockpit – firing the gun... and landing on the throttle!

好消息：马里恩用轮块猛击飞行员的头部，飞行员掉进了驾驶舱——开枪……然后落在了油门上！


WEIRD NEWS: Because Marion has only pulled the wheel blocks from one side of the plane, once the Pilot falls onto the controls it begins a slow pirouette. Spinning in a circle with the blocked wheels at the center. It's like ballet – with propellers.

奇闻：由于玛丽昂只移开了飞机一侧的轮挡，当飞行员扑到操纵杆上时，飞机开始缓慢旋转。被卡住的轮子在中心打转。这就像芭蕾——只不过是用螺旋桨表演。


BAD NEWS: The Big Nazi is just wailing on Indy.

坏消息：纳粹分子正在猛攻印第安纳波利斯。


GOOD NEWS: Marion gets into the cockpit to try and stop the plane from moving, but...

好消息：玛丽昂进入驾驶舱试图阻止飞机移动，但是……


BAD NEWS: Can't get the pilot off the controls – dude is heavy – and...

坏消息：没办法让飞行员离开驾驶舱——这家伙太重了——而且……


WORSE NEWS: The cockpit canopy slams down – trapping her inside the plane with the unconscious Pilot. She can not get out – the canopy is locked somehow.

更糟糕的消息：驾驶舱盖猛然落下——她和昏迷的飞行员被困在飞机里。她出不来——舱盖不知何故锁住了。


MORE BAD NEWS: The Big Nazi continues to pound on Indy.

更多坏消息：纳粹分子继续猛攻印第安纳波利斯。


MORE WORSE NEWS: Marion sees a troop truck filled with Nazi Soldiers drive by... stop when they see the spinning plane... and head right towards them!

更糟糕的消息：玛丽昂看到一辆满载纳粹士兵的军车驶过……当他们看到旋转的飞机时停了下来……然后径直朝飞机驶去！


GOOD NEWS: Marion scrambles into the plane's “tail gun” compartment, aims at the truckload of soldiers, and opens fire. Killing all but one, who scrambles for cover.

好消息：玛丽昂迅速爬进飞机的“尾炮”舱，瞄准卡车上的士兵，开火射击。除了一个士兵外，其余全部被击毙，那个士兵慌忙寻找掩体。


BAD NEWS: Because the plane is doing that slow pirouette – Marion can no longer fire at the one last soldier – he's behind her now. Grabbing his gun. Getting ready to fire.

坏消息：由于飞机正在缓慢旋转，玛丽昂无法再向最后一个士兵开火——他现在在她身后，正抓起枪，准备射击。


WORSE NEWS: The plane's wing slices into a fuel tanker truck nearby – spraying gallons of gasoline all over!

更糟糕的消息：飞机机翼切入附近一辆油罐车——大量汽油喷溅而出！


GOOD NEWS: The plane finally comes around and Marion gets the last soldier moments before he can fire and get her.

好消息：飞机终于绕了过来，玛丽昂在最后一名士兵开枪射杀她之前抓住了他。


BAD NEWS: Indy has been knocked to the ground by the Big Nazi... right in the path of the moving plane wheels!

坏消息：印第安纳·琼斯被纳粹大佬打倒在地……正好落在了飞机轮子的行进路线上！


GOOD NEWS: Indy dives *behind* the plane wheels – so that the wheels are between him and the Big Nazi. Better news – he sees the pilot's fallen pistol! He reaches for it...

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯跳到飞机轮子后面——这样轮子就挡在他和纳粹大佬之间了。更好的消息——他看到了飞行员掉落的手枪！他伸手去拿……


BAD NEWS: The plane's wheels run over the gun... and the wheels are no longer between him and the Big Nazi, who lunges for him!

坏消息：飞机的轮子碾过了大炮……轮子不再挡在他和那个大纳粹之间，大纳粹向他扑了过来！


WORSE NEWS: Remember that tanker truck spilling gasoline? Well a river of gasoline has reaches the troop truck... which EXPLODES! This is worse news because just over the hill where there are hundreds of Nazi soldiers? They see that explosion and the commander orders some soldiers to stay with the Ark while others go to investigate. Indy and Marion will soon be massively outnumbered and captured again!

更糟糕的消息：还记得那辆漏油的油罐车吗？现在，汽油像河流一样流到了运兵车上……爆炸了！更糟糕的是，就在山那边，数百名纳粹士兵正守着那里。他们目睹了爆炸，指挥官命令一些士兵留在方舟旁，其他人前去调查。印第安纳·琼斯和玛丽昂很快就会寡不敌众，再次被俘！


EVEN WORSE NEWS: Another river of gasoline is flowing to the plane – and the burning exploded troop truck's gasoline river of *burning* gas is now headed to the plane where Marion is trapped!

更糟糕的消息：又有一股汽油流向飞机——燃烧爆炸的军用卡车流出的燃烧汽油现在正流向玛丽昂被困的飞机！


GOOD NEWS: Indy gets away from the Big Nazi long enough to climb the wing to try and free Marion... but the canopy is stuck!

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯摆脱了纳粹大魔头，爬上机翼试图解救玛丽昂……但是座舱盖卡住了！


BAD NEWS: The Big Nazi climbs up the wing and knocks Indy off!

坏消息：纳粹大佬爬上机翼，把印第安纳·琼斯撞了下来！


WORSE NEWS: That river of burning gas is getting closer... closer... closer!

更糟糕的消息：那条燃烧的气体河流越来越近……越来越近……越来越近了！


GOOD NEWS: Indy gets some sort of adrenaline rush and POUNCES on the Big Nazi – slamming him in the face again and again and again!

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯肾上腺素飙升，猛扑向纳粹大佬——一下又一下地猛击他的脸！


BAD NEWS: It's like he's hitting a brick wall. The Big Nazi just takes the slams to the face without even blinking! Then SLAMS Indy so hard he bounces onto the ground... unable to move. Indy has given it his best shot – and failed. He is going to die.

坏消息：他就像撞上了一堵砖墙。那个纳粹大佬竟然连眼皮都不眨一下就硬生生地挨了几拳！然后狠狠地把印第安纳·琼斯摔在地上……动弹不得。印第安纳·琼斯已经竭尽全力——但还是失败了。他死定了。


WORSE NEWS: The Big Nazi moves up to STOMP on Indy – and kill him.

更糟糕的消息：纳粹大佬正准备对印第安纳·琼斯痛下杀手——甚至要杀了他。


GOOD NEWS: Indy looks up, preparing to die... then covers his face... As the propeller hits the Big Nazi and cuts him to ribbons. Yech! There's a cool shot where the Big Nazi's blood spray over the red & white swastika on the tail of the plane – turning it mostly red.

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯抬头望去，准备赴死……然后捂住了脸……螺旋桨击中了那个纳粹大佬，把他撕成了碎片。真恶心！有个很酷的镜头，纳粹大佬的血喷溅到飞机尾翼上的红白相间的纳粹标志上——把它染成了鲜红色。


BAD NEWS: That burning river of gasoline? Almost to the plane. Marion is pounding on the cockpit canopy and can not get it open. She is about to be burned alive.

坏消息：那条燃烧的汽油河？快要烧到飞机上了。玛丽昂正在猛烈敲打驾驶舱盖，但打不开。她即将被活活烧死。


GOOD NEWS: Indy finds the Pilot's fallen gun, grabs it, scrambles up the wing...

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯找到了飞行员掉落的枪，抓起枪，爬上了机翼……


BAD NEWS: The burning river of gasoline is only inches away.

坏消息：燃烧的汽油河就在几英寸之外。


GOOD NEWS: Indy blasts the canopy locks off with the pistol, pulls Marion out of the plane and they run away as the plane and everything else blows sky high! A MASSIVE EXPLOSION!

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯用手枪打掉了座舱盖锁，把玛丽昂拉出飞机，两人趁着飞机和周围的一切爆炸升空之际逃走了！发生了巨大的爆炸！


BAD NEWS: A bunch of Nazi soldiers arrive at the burning wreckage – so Indy and Marion have to hide... and they have no way to escape anymore now that the plane is a burning wreck, and the Nazi's have the Ark, and will probably win the war...

坏消息：一群纳粹士兵抵达了燃烧的飞机残骸——印第安纳·琼斯和玛丽昂不得不躲藏起来……现在飞机已经化为焦土，纳粹分子又得到了约柜，很可能会赢得战争，他们已经无路可逃了……


GOOD NEWS: Indy's Arab pal Sallah finds them before all of those Nazi soldiers and tells him: If you want the Ark, they are loading it onto a truck for Cairo!

好消息：印第安纳·琼斯的阿拉伯朋友萨拉在纳粹士兵之前找到了他们，并告诉他：如果你想要约柜，他们正在把它装上卡车运往开罗！


See how the Good News/Bad News aspect of reversals works? Scene Reversals ask a question: will Indy be able to survive the Big Nazi stomping him to death? Then giving you an answer that creates a brand new question: the Big Nazi gets shredded by the propeller, but now how will Indy be able to get Marion out of the cockpit before the river of fire blows them both to smithereens? Each solution creates a brand new problem. A reader can't put the script down - there's always an unanswered question, an unsolved problem. Before the reader knows what's happening they have been drawn into the protagonist's problems. They are hooked! Emotionally involved in the scene. That is the reason why we remember this scene from a 1981 movie over thirty years later! Reversals *work*!

明白“好消息/坏消息”这种反转手法的精髓了吗？场景反转会抛出一个问题：印第安纳·琼斯能否在被纳粹大佬踩死之前幸存下来？然后给出的答案又会引出一个全新的问题：纳粹大佬被螺旋桨撕成了碎片，但现在印第安纳·琼斯该如何才能在火海将他们炸成碎片之前把玛丽昂救出驾驶舱？每一个解决方案都会带来一个全新的问题。读者根本停不下来——总会有一个未解之谜，一个悬而未决的问题。在读者还没弄明白发生了什么之前，他们就已经被卷入了主人公的困境之中。他们被牢牢吸引住了！他们完全沉浸在剧情之中。这就是为什么三十多年后，我们仍然记得这部1981年电影中的这个场景！反转手法真的有效！

The best way to create a reversal is to look for the road less traveled. In any scene, there are at least three choices. Pick the one you've never (or seldom) seen. Then think "good news, bad news". What if the villain has a 13 shot Browning and the hero has a 5 shot Smith and Wesson? You're setting up a reversal, by having the hero run out of bullets (at a critical moment, of course). When the hero finally gets the villain in his sights and pulls the trigger... Click! Bad news. Then, let's say, the villain raises his gun. Worse news. But the hero Throws his empty gun at the villain, hitting him in the face. Good news! The villain shakes it off (he's really macho) and re-aims. Bad news! Now keep it going for an entire action scene, and you'll create a page turner that no reader can skim.

制造反转的最佳方法是另辟蹊径。任何场景中至少都有三种选择。选择你从未见过（或很少见过）的那一种。然后想想“好消息，坏消息”。如果反派有一把13发子弹的勃朗宁左轮手枪，而英雄只有一把5发子弹的史密斯威森左轮手枪呢？你通过让英雄在关键时刻子弹耗尽来制造反转。当英雄终于瞄准反派并扣动扳机时……咔哒！坏消息。然后，假设反派举起了枪。更糟糕的消息。但英雄把空枪扔向反派，正中他的脸。好消息！反派抖了抖身子（他真是个男子汉），重新瞄准。坏消息！现在，把这种手法运用到整个动作场景中，你就能创作出一部引人入胜、让人无法略读的佳作。


#↩

PLOT TWISTS

剧情反转


There was a time before “The Sixth Sense” when a plot twist didn't have to be something that came at the end and changed the whole meaning of the story. When a Plot Twist could happen in the middle of the script, and just change the course of the story. Let's go back to that time for this chapter... and our action screenplays. Just as a Scene Reversal is a dead end or element that changes the actions within a scene, a Story Reversal is the same thing on a story level. A Plot Twist is when it's more than just a dead end or a change – it's a completely unexpected change that twists the story in a different direction. More on the level of “Luke, I am your father” than the endings of “The Sixth Sense” or the original “Planet Of The Apes” (where the ending changed the whole story we've just seen). A plot twist can be something physical like when they finally get into the safe in “Tower Heist”... and it's empty! Or it can be something emotional like the scene in “From Paris With Love” where the geeky CIA hero discovers that the assassin he has been stalking... is his fiance. My favorite twist is from Alfred Hitchcock's early film “The 39 Steps” when our man-on-the-run-hero Richard Hannay goes to the local authorities – Professor Jordan, kind of the village mayor – and tells him that there is a ring of spies operating in his area, lead by a man who is missing the top section of his little finger... and Jordan raises his hand and says: “Like this?” Twist! Now the man he thought was the solution to his problems ends up *being* his problems. What I love about this twist is the way it is casually revealed that Jordan is the villain.

在《第六感》之前，剧情反转并不一定非得出现在结尾，彻底改变故事的意义。它也可以发生在剧本的中间，仅仅改变故事的走向。让我们回到那个时代，在本章中探讨动作片剧本。正如场景反转是指场景中出现死胡同或改变剧情走向的元素一样，故事反转在故事层面也是如此。而剧情反转则不仅仅是死胡同或改变——它是一种完全出乎意料的改变，将故事引向另一个方向。它更像是“卢克，我是你父亲”那样的反转，而不是《第六感》或原版《人猿星球》（它们的结局彻底改变了我们刚刚看到的整个故事）的结局。剧情反转可以是实实在在的，比如在《高楼大劫案》中，他们终于打开了保险箱……却发现里面空空如也！或者，它也可以像《巴黎谍影》里那样充满情感冲击：那个书呆子气的CIA特工发现自己一直跟踪的刺客……竟然是自己的未婚妻。我最喜欢的反转来自阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克早期的电影《三十九级台阶》。亡命天涯的主人公理查德·汉内去找当地官员——乔丹教授，相当于村长——告诉他，他所在的地区有一个间谍组织，头目小指尖缺失一截……乔丹举起手，问道：“像这样吗？” 反转！他原本以为能解决他所有问题的人，最终却成了他的问题本身。我喜欢这个反转的地方在于，它以一种不经意的方式揭示了乔丹才是真正的反派。


One of the most common problems with new scripts is that they're often too predictable. The reader *knows* what's going to happen next, so why read on? Already we're up against the conventions of the genre - we know the hero will usually win and the villain will be vanquished. So our job as action writers is to make sure the story doesn't take a direct path from beginning to end, but corkscrews a little. Zigs when you think it's going to zag. The great thing about twists is that they not only make the story unpredictable, they also give the story a conflict boost and sometimes make us doubt the hero actually will be triumphant.

新剧本最常见的问题之一就是情节过于可预测。读者*知道*接下来会发生什么，那为什么还要继续读下去呢？我们已经要面对类型片的固有套路——我们知道英雄通常会获胜，反派会被打败。所以，作为动作片编剧，我们的任务是确保故事不会从头到尾一帆风顺，而是要出人意料地曲折发展。在你以为它会往左的时候，它却会往右转。反转的妙处在于，它不仅能让故事变得难以预测，还能增强故事的冲突性，有时甚至会让我们怀疑英雄是否真的能够最终获胜。


In William Goldman's "Marathon Man", Babe's spy brother dies in his arms after being murdered by the villain, Zell. His brother's partner Janey asks if his brother said anything before he died. Any important information? Babe says "No". Later in the film, Babe has been kidnapped by Zell, who asks the same question... Only Zell is using a dentist's drill to jog Babe's memory. It's the signature scene in the film – and the one that had audiences screaming in the cinema. Zell, who was a Nazi dentist during World War Two and extracted many gold teeth from Jews in concentration camps knows how to use a drill on someone's teeth to create the most pain possible... and because we have all been to the dentist, we feel Babe's pain. “Is it safe?” Suddenly, Janey breaks into Zell's secret hide-out and rescues Babe. As they speed away, Janey asks Babe what he told Zell. "You've got to tell me." After Babe answers, Janey turns the car around and takes him *back* to Zell's hide-out! Twist! Janey is a bad guy!

在威廉·戈德曼的《马拉松人》中，贝比的间谍哥哥被反派泽尔杀害后死在了他的怀里。哥哥的搭档珍妮问他哥哥临死前有没有说过什么，有没有什么重要的信息？贝比回答“没有”。影片后半段，贝比被泽尔绑架，泽尔又问了同样的问题……只不过这次泽尔是用牙钻来唤醒贝比的记忆。这是影片的标志性场景，也是让观众在影院里尖叫的场景。泽尔在二战期间曾是纳粹牙医，在集中营里从犹太人身上拔掉了许多金牙，他深谙如何用牙钻折磨人，制造出最大的痛苦……因为我们都看过牙医，所以我们能感同身受贝比的痛苦。“安全吗？”突然，珍妮闯入了泽尔的秘密藏身处，救出了贝比。他们飞速逃离时，珍妮问贝比他跟泽尔说了什么。“你必须告诉我。”贝贝回答后，珍妮调转车头，把他带回了泽尔的藏身处！剧情反转！珍妮竟然是个坏人！


When we look back on this twist, it makes perfect sense. From the very beginning, Janey was trying to find out what Babe's brother told him. The "rescue" only makes sense if Janey is a bad guy. How else would he have known the location of Zell's secret hide-out?

回过头来看这个转折，一切都说得通了。从一开始，简尼就一直在试图弄清楚贝贝的哥哥告诉了他什么。“营救”行动只有在简尼是坏人的情况下才说得通。否则，他怎么会知道泽尔的秘密藏身之处呢？


That's the most important rule about twists: They have to be logical upon reflection - it has to make sense and be set up. In this BluRay age the audience can zip back and look for the clues. If Janey was a bad guy in the rescue scene, he was a bad guy in the scenes before, right? He didn't just turn bad on the spot. This goes back to Lajos Egri's “No honest man will becomes a thief overnight; no thief will become an honest man in the same period of time." He points out that good drama requires a character to go from one state to another (to grow, to change), but the change must be gradual... or the character may have always secretly been a bad guy. But if the character has always secretly been a villain, they must be consistent. In “Marathon Man”, once we know that Janey is working for Zell we can zip back and see that he was *always* working for Zell – he has always wanted to know if Babe's brother told him anything before he died. Janey is consistent. The twist isn't contrived by the writer at the last minute – the twist just revealed something that was there all along.

关于剧情反转，最重要的原则就是：它们必须经得起推敲——必须合情合理，并且早有铺垫。在蓝光时代，观众可以随时回看之前的剧情寻找线索。如果Janey在营救场景中是坏人，那么他在之前的场景中也是坏人，对吧？他不可能突然变坏。这可以追溯到Lajos Egri的名言：“没有哪个诚实的人会在一夜之间变成小偷；也没有哪个小偷会在短时间内变成诚实的人。”他指出，好的戏剧需要一个角色从一种状态转变为另一种状态（成长，改变），但这种转变必须是渐进的……否则这个角色可能一直都是个隐藏的坏人。但如果一个角色一直都是个隐藏的反派，那么他必须前后一致。在《马拉松人》中，一旦我们知道Janey为Zell工作，我们就可以回看之前的剧情，发现他*一直*都在为Zell工作——他一直想知道Babe的哥哥在死前有没有告诉他什么。珍妮的逻辑始终如一。这个转折并非编剧临时拼凑的——它只是揭示了一直存在的东西。


#↩

FORESHADOWING

铺垫


A plot twist may change the story for the hero and the audience, but it doesn't *actually* change anything – it just reveals what has always been true. If the hero's best friend is revealed as a villain on page 73, he was also a villain on page 37... and needs to act like it. Just because *we* don't know the best friend is a villain doesn't mean the *best friend* doesn't know it – of course he knows who he is and what his motives are!

剧情反转或许会改变主人公和读者对故事的理解，但实际上并没有改变什么——它只是揭示了一直以来的真相。如果主人公最好的朋友在第73页被揭露是反派，那么他在第37页就已经是反派了……而且他需要表现得像个反派。仅仅因为我们不知道这位好朋友是反派，并不意味着他自己不知道——他当然知道自己是谁，也知道自己的动机是什么！


The clues to the twist are called "Foreshadowing", and they are required for every twist. We need to be able to watch the film a second time and see all of those clues we missed the first time around. The best example of this is “The Sixth Sense”, because everyone has seen it... and few saw that big twist at the end coming. (Spoilers for those who have not seen the film!) When we come to the end and it is revealed that Bruce Willis is *dead*, it's a huge shock. An amazing twist! But when we watch the film for the second time, we wonder why we didn't see that twist coming – it's so obvious! The kid sees dead people... like Bruce Willis! There's that great scene where Bruce Willis has an anniversary dinner with his wife... and she's so cold and distant. When he talks, she completely ignores him as if he isn't there... because he isn't there – he's dead! That scene was a big emotional moment the first time I saw it, because I thought it was just a marriage on the rocks scene. And everything about that scene can be taken in two ways – as their relationship coming to an end the first time you see it... and that he's dead and doesn't know it the second time you see it. His character never opens a door, is never shown driving (he takes the bus), and the only person he really interacts with is the kid... the kid who sees dead people. That is how all twists should work – once the secret truth has been revealed you should be able to go back and spot all of the places the writer foreshadowed that twist... and if *you* are the writer? Part of the *fun* is writing those scenes because you know that twist is coming.

剧情反转的线索被称为“伏笔”，每个反转都需要伏笔。我们需要能够二刷电影，发现第一次观看时错过的所有线索。最好的例子就是《第六感》，因为几乎每个人都看过这部电影……但很少有人预料到结尾的那个惊天反转。（以下内容涉及剧透，请未观看者谨慎阅读！）当影片结尾揭示布鲁斯·威利斯*已死*时，我们震惊不已。这是一个惊人的反转！但当我们二刷时，我们会疑惑为什么第一次没有预料到这个反转——它明明如此显而易见！那个孩子能看到死人……比如布鲁斯·威利斯！影片中有一个精彩的场景：布鲁斯·威利斯和妻子共进周年纪念晚餐……她却冷漠疏离。当他说话时，她完全无视他，仿佛他根本不存在……因为他确实不存在——他已经死了！第一次看到那场戏时，我被深深触动了，因为我当时以为那只是一段濒临破裂的婚姻。那场戏的一切都可以有两种解读——第一次看的时候，是他们的关系走向终结……第二次看的时候，是他已经死了，但他自己却毫不知情。他的角色从未开过门，也从未开车（他一直坐公交车），他唯一真正互动的人就是那个孩子……那个能看到死人的孩子。所有反转都应该如此——一旦真相揭晓，你应该能够回过头去，发现编剧埋下的所有伏笔……而如果你就是编剧呢？创作这些场景的乐趣之一就在于你知道反转即将到来。


There's a good twist in Ernest Lehman's "North By Northwest". Cary Grant is chasing a man named George Kaplan, who is (in turn) chasing James Mason (the villain). Grant hops on board a train bound for Grand Rapids, Michigan (Kaplan's destination). In the train he meets Eva Marie Saint, who is also bound for Grand Rapids. They have an affair. When the train reaches Grand Rapids, Eva Marie Saint lures him into a trap! She's James Mason's mistress! One of the villains! It's a great twist, that holds up to logical examination. We know that the hero and the villain have the same destination. The train travels to that destination. We are given a clue: We *know* that the villain is on the train. The only thing we *don't* know, is that the villain and Eva Marie Saint are in cahoots. Once that is revealed, it all makes sense. Even the affair on the train was designed to control him so that he didn't discover the villain was on the train.

欧内斯特·雷曼执导的《西北偏北》中有一个精彩的反转。加里·格兰特饰演的角色正在追捕乔治·卡普兰，而卡普兰又在追捕詹姆斯·梅森（反派）。格兰特跳上一列开往密歇根州大急流城（卡普兰的目的地）的火车。在火车上，他遇到了同样前往大急流城的伊娃·玛丽·圣。两人发生了婚外情。当火车抵达大急流城时，伊娃·玛丽·圣设下陷阱，引诱格兰特落入圈套！原来她是詹姆斯·梅森的情妇！是反派之一！这是一个绝妙的反转，经得起逻辑推敲。我们知道英雄和反派的目的地相同，火车也开往同一个目的地。我们得到了一条线索：我们*知道*反派就在火车上。我们*不知道*的是，反派和伊娃·玛丽·圣是一伙的。一旦真相揭晓，一切就都说得通了。甚至连火车上的那件事也是为了控制他，让他不发现坏人就在火车上。


Be careful when foreshadowing your twist that you don't "Telegraph" it. You want the audience to find the clues *after* the twist, not *before* it (or it isn't really a twist). This is a balancing act which takes some practice before you'll perfect it. One method is to plant the clue to your twist as early as possible, to give the audience lots of time to forget it. That way, after the twist occurs, they'll remember the foreshadowing and say to themselves: "I should have seen it coming!" If you think about “The Sixth Sense” Bruce Willis gets shot in the first few minutes of the film, so when we see him after the fade out and time has passed, we just assume he got out of the hospital and has gone back to work. And by the time the twist is revealed we have completely forgotten that he was shot in the first few minutes.

在埋下剧情转折的伏笔时，务必小心，不要“剧透”。你希望观众在转折发生*之后*发现线索，而不是*之前*（否则就称不上是转折了）。这需要一些练习才能掌握，需要一定的技巧。一种方法是尽早埋下转折的线索，给观众足够的时间去忘记它。这样，在转折发生之后，他们会想起之前的伏笔，然后自言自语：“我早该想到的！”想想《第六感》，布鲁斯·威利斯在影片开头几分钟就中枪了，所以当镜头淡出，时间过去之后，我们看到他时，我们理所当然地认为他已经出院并重返工作岗位。等到转折揭晓时，我们早已完全忘记了他在影片开头几分钟中枪的事。


#↩

DO YOU BELIEVE IN MAGIC?

你相信魔法吗？


The best way to “hide” a twist is through magic. A magician uses *Diversion* and *Anticipation* to trick the audience. When a magician shows you that there's nothing up his sleeve, he is secretly pulling a card from the secret pocket in the back of his coat and sliding it under a glass of water on the table. You have focused your attention on his sleeve... and it's a diversion. His wand is a diversion. Those flourishes are diversions. For the remainder of the trick, you anticipate that the card will appear in the hand at the end of that sleeve, and are completely surprised when the card turns up under a glass of water on the table.

隐藏魔术反转的最佳方法是运用魔术技巧。魔术师会利用“转移注意力”和“预判”来迷惑观众。当魔术师向你展示袖子里什么也没有时，他其实正悄悄地从外套背后的暗袋里抽出一张牌，然后把它滑到桌上的一杯水下面。你的注意力被他的袖子吸引住了……而这正是转移注意力的手段。他的魔杖也是一种转移注意力的方式。那些花哨的魔术动作也都是转移注意力的手段。在接下来的表演中，你会一直期待着那张牌会出现在他袖子末端的手里，而当牌出现在桌上的一杯水下面时，你却感到无比惊讶。


“The Sixth Sense” is also a good example of the use of a diversion. Before we know that twist end, we believe that it is the story of a child psychologist who failed with one very disturbed patient and now has a new patient – a young boy – who seems even more troubled. Will he be able to save this patient? Or will the boy kill himself like his other patient? We are so focused on Willis trying to break through to the kid that we don't notice all of those clues that he's really dead. And when Willis finally breaks through and the kid explains what's troubling him – that he sees dead people – about halfway through the film, instead of thinking that Willis is dead, we worry that the kid is more disturbed than we originally thought. And we also worry that rational child psychologist Willis will not believe the kid... and the kill will become worse due to Willis screwing up... as he did before with that other patient who killed himself. While we are worried about Willis making the same fatal mistake twice, we don't even notice even more foreshadowing. And when we begin seeing the dead people – the hanging students, the murdered little girl – we are scared and fear that Willis will not believe the kid really can see dead people. We don't think: Hey, the kid can see Willis, right? The kid diversion keeps “expanding” and occupying our thoughts so that we don't see the obvious until it is revealed to us at the end. It's a great diversion.

《第六感》也是运用转移视线的好例子。在得知结局反转之前，我们以为这是一个儿童心理学家失败后接手一个新病人——一个看起来更加痛苦的小男孩——的故事。他能救活这个病人吗？还是这个男孩会像他之前的病人一样自杀？我们全神贯注于威利斯试图与孩子沟通，以至于忽略了所有暗示他其实已经死亡的线索。当威利斯终于突破防线，孩子向他解释了困扰他的事情——他能看到死人——大约在影片中段，我们并没有想到威利斯已经死了，而是担心这个孩子比我们最初想象的还要痛苦。我们也担心理性的儿童心理学家威利斯不会相信孩子的话……担心威利斯会因为自己的失误而导致悲剧发生……就像他之前对那个自杀的病人那样。当我们担心威利斯会犯同样的致命错误两次时，我们甚至没有注意到更多的伏笔。当我们开始看到死者——上吊的学生、被谋杀的小女孩——我们感到恐惧，担心威利斯不会相信那个孩子真的能看到死人。我们不会想：嘿，那个孩子能看到威利斯，对吧？孩子的这个线索不断“扩展”，占据了我们的思绪，以至于我们直到最后才看到显而易见的真相。这是一个绝妙的转移视线之术。


When crafting your twist, the best way to keep from “telegraphing” it is with a strong diversion – just like a magician doing a magic trick. While the audience is worried about the troubled boy they never notice the dead protagonist.

在构思剧情反转时，避免“泄露”真相的最佳方法是设置一个强有力的干扰——就像魔术师表演魔术一样。当观众担心那个身处困境的男孩时，他们根本不会注意到主角已经死去。


#↩

A TWISTED EXAMPLE

一个扭曲的例子


There's an old Hitchcock Presents episode about a guy who gets pulled over by the police on his way home from work. The guy says "I know I was speeding, but can you give me a break? It's my birthday, and my wife's making a special dinner." The cops put him in handcuffs. "We aren't arresting you for speeding... we're arresting you for *murder*."

有一集老版的《希区柯克剧场》，讲的是一个男人下班回家途中被警察拦下。他说：“我知道我超速了，但能不能饶了我？今天是我的生日，我老婆正在准备一顿丰盛的晚餐。” 警察给他戴上手铐。“我们不是因为你超速逮捕你……我们是因为你犯了谋杀罪逮捕你。”


Our hero says there must be a mix up, he's innocent. "They're all innocent." The hero *pleads*. It's his birthday. His wife is waiting at home. "You've got the wrong man." One of the policemen shows him a sketch of the killer... and it's our hero!

我们的主人公说一定是搞错了，他是无辜的。“他们都是无辜的。”主人公恳求道。今天是他的生日。他的妻子在家等着他。“你们抓错人了。”一名警察给他看了一张凶手的素描……那人竟然是我们的主人公！


Now our hero begins to panic. It's his birthday. Things like this aren't supposed to happen on your birthday. Our hero again pleads innocence. The mean policeman says, "That's it. We were going to take you to the station-house, but now we're going to take you to an old warehouse and beat a confession out of you."

我们的主人公开始惊慌失措。今天是他的生日。生日这天不应该发生这种事。主人公再次辩解自己是无辜的。那个凶狠的警察说：“就这样吧。我们本来要把你带回警局，但现在我们要把你带到一个废弃的仓库，把你打到认罪为止。”


Our hero really panics when the police car turns into an industrial section and pulls up in front of an old warehouse. He pleads, "I'm innocent. Don't beat me!" The policemen drag him into the dark warehouse and flip on the lights. "Surprise!" It's a surprise birthday party thrown by his wife and friends!

当警车驶入工业区，停在一座旧仓库前时，我们的主人公彻底慌了。他哀求道：“我是无辜的，别打我！” 警察把他拖进黑暗的仓库，打开了灯。“惊喜！”原来是他的妻子和朋友们为他准备的惊喜生日派对！


When you look back on this episode, you realize that the surprise party is the logical thing to happen on our hero's birthday... getting arrested for murder isn't. The arrest was the *diversion* from the surprise party. When the policemen take him into the warehouse, we *anticipate* it's because they want to beat a confession out of him. Boy, are we surprised! This twist works because the logical course of events (the surprise birthday party) is the twist. By leading the audience to believe it's one thing, then revealing that it's almost the opposite – we have a great twist.

回看这一集，你会发现，在主人公的生日当天举办惊喜派对才是合乎逻辑的选择……而因谋杀罪被捕则完全不合情理。逮捕行动是为了转移人们对惊喜派对的注意力。当警察把他带进仓库时，我们理所当然地认为他们想逼他认罪。结果却出乎意料！这个反转之所以成功，是因为合乎逻辑的事件发展（惊喜生日派对）本身就是反转。通过引导观众相信一件事，然后揭示几乎截然相反的事实——我们成功地制造了一个精彩的反转。


When we hold the diversion up to the light, we see just how flimsy it is: What are the odds that someone who looks just like you committed a murder? What are the odds that the cops would spot you driving around and arrest you for the murder? And don't these cops seem a little hasty to beat a confession out of a guy who cooperates with them? The entire arrest scenario isn't logical... but we believe it because the writer focused our attention away from the real story. He tricked us, just like a magician.

当我们仔细审视这个转移视线的伎俩时，就会发现它有多么站不住脚：一个长得跟你一模一样的人犯下谋杀案的概率有多大？警察发现你开车四处巡逻并逮捕你的概率有多大？而且，这些警察是不是太急于逼迫一个配合他们的人认罪了？整个逮捕过程根本不合逻辑……但我们却信以为真，因为作者成功地转移了我们的注意力，让我们忽略了真正的故事。他就像一个魔术师，欺骗了我们。


That's the way to create a good twist: Focus the audience away from the logical progression of the plot through diversion and anticipation... then, when the logical events occur, it's unexpected! As writers, we are magicians and our screenplays are the magic trick. *We* know the Policemen are taking him to a surprise birthday party – but in order for the twist to work we need to convince the audience that our hero is really under arrest for murder and these two policemen are really going to take him to an old warehouse and beat him. As writers we can see both layers of the story – the lie on the surface and the truth underneath. For the twist to work we need to control both layers – to write those scenes like the “Sixth Sense” anniversary dinner which works for both layers. A magician knows they are performing a trick – they know the rabbit doesn't appear in their hat due to a miracle or sorcery. They have to use diversion and anticipation to keep the audience focused away from the hat while they secretly work its false bottom so that the rabbits can “appear”. No different for writers – except we seldom work in tuxedos and top hats.

这就是制造精彩反转的秘诀：通过转移观众注意力、制造悬念，让他们忽略剧情的逻辑发展……然后，当合乎逻辑的事件发生时，就会出人意料！作为编剧，我们就像魔术师，剧本就是魔术道具。我们都知道警察要带他去参加一个惊喜生日派对——但为了让反转奏效，我们需要让观众相信，我们的主人公真的因为谋杀被捕了，而这两个警察真的要把他带到一个旧仓库里殴打。作为编剧，我们能看到故事的两层含义——表面上的谎言和隐藏在背后的真相。为了让反转成功，我们需要掌控这两层含义——就像《第六感》里的周年纪念晚宴那样，巧妙地将两层含义融合在一起。魔术师知道自己在表演魔术——他们知道兔子不会因为奇迹或魔法而从帽子里出现。他们必须利用转移观众注意力、制造悬念，让他们的注意力远离帽子，同时暗中操作帽子的暗门，让兔子“出现”。作家也一样——只不过我们很少穿着燕尾服和高顶礼帽工作。


#↩

SOAP OPERA TWISTS

肥皂剧剧情反转


A plot twist changes the director of the story. When Richard Hannay goes to the one person who he thinks can help him in “The 39 Steps” and that person ends up being *twist* the villain, he is in worse trouble than before, and now must escape both the police *and* the villain... and how do you convince the police that the man in charge, Professor Jordan, is an enemy spy? If a twist *does not* change the direction of the story we have what I call a Soap Opera Twist, like Frau Blucher in “Young Frankenstein” who finally reveals that Baron Frankenstein was her boyfriend. Um, so?

剧情反转改变了故事的走向。在《三十九级台阶》中，当理查德·汉内去找他认为唯一能帮他的人，结果这个人竟然是反派时，他陷入了比之前更糟糕的境地，现在他不仅要躲避警察，还要躲避反派……而且，你该如何说服警察，让他们相信负责人乔丹教授是敌方间谍呢？如果剧情反转没有改变故事的走向，那我们就称之为“肥皂剧式反转”，就像《年轻的弗兰肯斯坦》中的布吕歇尔夫人最终揭露弗兰肯斯坦男爵是她的男朋友一样。嗯，所以呢？


A Soap Opera Twist reveals information that may be shocking, but doesn't really change anything. Imagine if in “Star Wars” Luke and Leia's kiss was a lot more passionate... hey, imagine that they ended up in bed together if you want. Or in a warm Taun Taun. Now, Luke and Leia break up – still friends – and she hooks up with Han Solo in “Empire Strikes Back” and she says “I love you” and Han says that great line, “I know”... and then in “Return Of The Jedi” Leia and Han are a couple, and then Luke discovers that he has a sister... and it's Leia. Yikes! He kissed her (or slept with her in a warm Taun Taun if you prefer). Shocking! But does it change the course of the story in any way? Nope. By the time Luke finds out she is his sister, they've blown up Death Star 2 and saved the worlds. Weird and kinky that he slept with her, and it will probably make family reunions a little awkward, but it doesn't change the story. That's a Soap Opera Twist.

肥皂剧式的剧情反转揭示了一些可能令人震惊的信息，但实际上并不会改变任何事情。想象一下，如果《星球大战》中卢克和莱娅的吻更加激情……嘿，如果你愿意，甚至可以想象他们最终上了床。或者在温暖的塔恩塔恩兽里。现在，卢克和莱娅分手了——但仍然是朋友——在《帝国反击战》中，她和汉·索罗在一起了，她说了“我爱你”，汉说了那句经典台词“我知道”……然后在《绝地归来》中，莱娅和汉成了一对，之后卢克发现自己有个妹妹……而且是莱娅。天哪！他吻了她（或者如果你愿意，也可以说在温暖的塔恩塔恩兽里和她睡了）。真是令人震惊！但这会以任何方式改变故事走向吗？不会。当卢克发现她是他的妹妹时，他们已经摧毁了死星二号，拯救了世界。他跟她睡了，这事儿既怪异又变态，可能会让家庭聚会变得有点尴尬，但这改变不了故事的走向。这就是肥皂剧的剧情反转。


Watch out for Soap Opera Twists – they are really false twists.

小心肥皂剧式的剧情反转——它们其实都是假的。


#↩

HOLD YOUR TWISTS

保持你的发型


The longer you "hold" a plot twist, the more powerful it becomes. The audience gets used to whatever your “anticipation” and “diversions” are and the twist is even more surprising. If Bruce Willis is shot by his patient in the first few minutes of “The Sixth Sense”, then a dozen minutes after that you reveal that he's dead – not much of a twist. We haven't had time to get so used to his being alive that we forget that he was shot. But hold that twist until the end of the movie and it has real impact on the audience. You want to hold your twists for as long as possible, to give them maximum impact,

剧情反转“保留”的时间越长，其冲击力就越强。观众会逐渐习惯你之前设置的各种“悬念”和“干扰”，这时反转就显得更加出人意料。如果《第六感》开头几分钟，布鲁斯·威利斯就被他的病人枪击，十几分钟后你才揭示他已经死了——这算不上什么反转。我们还没来得及习惯他还活着，以至于忘记他曾经中枪。但如果把这个反转留到电影结尾，它就能真正打动观众。你应该尽可能地保留你的反转，以达到最大的冲击力。


In my script "Unreasonable Force" a pair of Detectives are ambushed by a gang. One Detective is shot in the chest and goes down, the other barely escapes with his life. The gang torches the police car and the corpse inside. The survivor feels guilty. He should have helped his fallen partner instead of run.

在我的剧本《不合理武力》中，两名侦探遭到一伙歹徒伏击。一名侦探胸部中弹倒地，另一名侦探侥幸逃生。歹徒焚毁了警车和车内的尸体。幸存者感到内疚，他本应该救助倒下的搭档，而不是逃跑。


What if his partner had still been alive at the time?

如果他的搭档当时还活着呢？


The surviving detective has to tell his partner's child that Mommy isn't coming home... she was killed in the line of duty.

幸存的侦探不得不告诉他搭档的孩子，妈妈再也回不来了……她因公殉职了。


The surviving partner sinks into depression...

幸存的伴侣陷入了抑郁……


Not knowing that his partner is alive! She was wearing her bullet proof vest. The body burned beyond recognition in the police car is a female gang member shot in the cross fire.

他并不知道他的同伙还活着！她当时穿着防弹背心。警车里那具被烧得面目全非的尸体是一名在交火中被击中的女性帮派成员。


The longer you give the audience to accept that the partner is dead, the greater the impact of the twist when they find out she's alive. They get used to her being dead. They come to accept it as a fact... *then* spring your twist!

你让观众接受搭档已死的时间越长，当他们发现她还活着时，剧情反转带来的冲击力就越大。他们逐渐习惯了她已死的事实，并接受了它……*然后*突然抛出你的反转！


One of the worst notes I've ever gotten from a producer was on my cheesy creature feature “Gatorbaby” about a group of 20-somethings spending a week on their wealthy great-grandfather's private island for his 104 th birthday. When they get there, he has already gone to bed, but leaves a note to make themselves at home. His mansion is filled with old pictures of him as a young man – no photo shows him older than late 30s or early 40s. The next morning there is food prepared for them, but gramps is not around – heck, he's about to turn 104, how often does he even get out of bed? The 20-somethings figure that he is close to death, probably making out his will, and they are in competition to inherit his fortune. And they begin turning against each other and trying to undermine the others so that they can inherit. They have a conversation with him through his bedroom door, there's a scene where he's silhouetted in a doorway and talks to them... but he really hasn't been revealed yet. Well, he's an old man! Finally he comes out of his room... and he may be 104 years old but he looks no older than 40! He's found a method to stay forever young, and has no intention of *ever* dying. By holding the twist that he doesn't look his age, that reveal becomes a shock. But the crazy development executive wanted me to have him greet them when they arrived – giving away the twist! And when I tried to explain it, he just did not understand. That's what made this a terrible note – that the development exec couldn't understand the basic concept of holding a twist once it had been explained to him. Yikes!

我收到过的最糟糕的制片人意见之一，是关于我那部俗套的怪兽电影《鳄鱼宝贝》。这部电影讲的是一群二十多岁的年轻人为了庆祝他们富有的曾祖父104岁生日，在他位于私人岛屿上的住所待了一周。他们到达时，曾祖父已经入睡，但留下了一张便条，让他们随意。他的豪宅里挂满了年轻时的老照片——没有一张照片显示他超过30岁末或40岁初。第二天早上，有人为他们准备了饭菜，但爷爷不在——哎，他都快104岁了，还能起床几次呢？这群二十多岁的年轻人猜测他快要去世了，可能正在立遗嘱，他们开始争夺继承权。于是，他们开始互相倾轧，试图陷害其他人，以便自己能够继承遗产。他们隔着卧室门和他交谈，有一个场景是他站在门口，身影隐约可见，和他们说话……但他的真实身份还没真正揭晓。好吧，他是个老头！最后他终于从房间里出来了……他可能已经104岁了，但看起来却只有40岁！他找到了永葆青春的方法，而且根本不打算死。正是因为他看起来不像他的实际年龄，所以这个揭晓才如此令人震惊。但那个疯狂的制片主管却想让我安排他在他们到达时迎接他们——这样就把悬念泄露了！当我试图解释时，他根本听不懂。这就是这个剧本最糟糕的地方——制片主管竟然无法理解如何设置悬念这个基本概念，即使我已经向他解释过了。真是糟糕！


The longer you hold a twist, the bigger the twist becomes.

扭转的时间越长，扭转的幅度就越大。


#↩

RUGPULLS

拉格普尔斯


A rugpull is like a twist to the 100th power. A rugpull is a *major* twist which shocks the audience and takes the plot in an entirely unexpected direction. A good example is the "Psycho" shower scene. What's shocking about that scene isn't the nudity or the graphic violence, it's that the *lead character* is killed. The audience doesn't know what to do after that. They've never been presented with a problem like this in a movie before. The hero isn't supposed to get killed one third of the way through the film. You can't do that in a movie!

“反转”就像是剧情反转的百倍。所谓“反转”，指的是那种令人震惊的重大转折，它会彻底颠覆观众的认知，让剧情朝着完全出乎意料的方向发展。电影《惊魂记》中的淋浴场景就是一个很好的例子。这个场景令人震惊的并非裸露或暴力画面，而是主角被杀。观众在那一刻完全不知所措。他们从未在任何电影中遇到过这样的问题。英雄不应该在电影进行到三分之一的时候就死去。这在电影里是绝对不允许的！


In “Night Hunter” film I introduced the female lead, a reporter for a tabloid newspaper like the Weekly World News, set her up as sarcastic and funny and the perfect foil for our male lead - who is the last of the vampire hunters. The lead is on the run from the police who had falsely accused him of being a serial killer; and when he hijacks her car during a police chase, we all know what happens next. We've seen Hitchcock movies and all of the knock offs, we've seen “Three Days Of The Condor”, we've seen enough movies to know she will think he's guilty for a while and then see evidence that he's innocent and reluctantly help him and they will fall in love and by the end of the film he will be proven innocent and no longer be on the run, and they will walk off together holding hands. Except at the end of the car chase (the beginning of Act 2) the police shoot kill her. She is *dead*. Wait, you can't do that in a movie!

在电影《夜行猎手》中，我塑造了女主角，一位类似《世界新闻周刊》的小报记者，将她设定为一个讽刺幽默、与男主角——最后的吸血鬼猎人——形成完美对比的角色。男主角被警方诬陷为连环杀手而亡命天涯；在一次警匪追逐中，他劫持了她的车，接下来的剧情我们都知道了。我们看过希区柯克的电影以及所有模仿之作，看过《秃鹰七十二小时》，看过足够多的电影，知道她会先怀疑他有罪，然后看到他清白的证据，勉强帮助他，两人坠入爱河，影片结尾他被证明无罪，不再逃亡，两人手牵手离开。然而，在追车戏的结尾（第二幕开始），警察开枪打死了她。她*死了*。等等，电影里怎么能这么拍呢！


A rugpull is *drastic*. Although I wouldn't recommend killing your lead character, killing the sidekick, the love interest, or the lead's mom unexpectedly is a good rugpull.

“突然反转”指的是剧情走向*非常极端*。虽然我不建议杀死主角，但出人意料地杀死配角、恋人或主角的母亲，都是不错的“突然反转”手法。


Neil Jordan's "The Crying Game" has a great rugpull. The film's famous secret takes the story into such a strange and unpredictable direction, that the audience doesn't know what will happen next. You might at first think that this is just a twist, but twists don't make the audience jump that high out of their seats, nor will a twist change the entire course of the story and characters. After that rugpull, nothing in "The Crying Game" is the same. Even when the IRA gunmen come back into the story, the plot has derailed onto such a different track that the outcome isn't what you thought it would be.

尼尔·乔丹的《哭泣的游戏》有一个精彩的反转。影片中著名的秘密将故事引向了一个如此怪诞且难以预料的方向，以至于观众完全无法预知接下来会发生什么。你或许会觉得这只是一个普通的剧情反转，但普通的反转并不会像《哭泣的游戏》那样让观众如此惊艳，也不会彻底改变故事和人物的走向。在这个反转之后，《哭泣的游戏》的一切都发生了改变。即使爱尔兰共和军的枪手再次出现，剧情也早已偏离了原先的轨道，最终的结局也出乎你的意料。


The great thing about the surprise hit “Taken” is that it is constantly doing things you can not do in a movie - and that element of shock and surprise is probably what made it connected with the audience. The ticket buyers are just like that studio reader - they get tired of watching the same completely predictable movie every Friday night, and want to see something that is the same, but different. Something that fits in a popular genre, but does unexpected things within that genre.

《飓风营救》这部意外爆款电影最棒的地方在于，它不断尝试一些电影里不可能做到的事情——而正是这种令人震惊和意想不到的元素，或许正是它能引起观众共鸣的原因。购票观众就像电影公司的读者一样——他们厌倦了每个周五晚上都看同样毫无新意的电影，他们想要看一些既熟悉又不同的作品。一部既符合热门类型，又能在这个类型中做出意想不到的创新之作。


Liam Neeson plays a divorced dad who seldom saw his daughter (Maggie Grace) while she was growing up, and now that she's almost an adult, he plans on spending the summer with her. They get the divorced dad thing right - it's messy, with all kinds of unresolved issues. There is no happy ending - family gets back together feel in this film - this is a family torn apart and it's going to stay that way. But that summer Neeson was going to spend getting closer to his daughter? She's going to be in Paris with her friend. This film constantly sets up a situation where we think we know what will happen, then completely trashes that situation unexpectedly.

利亚姆·尼森饰演一位离异父亲，女儿（玛姬·格蕾斯饰）从小就很少见到他。如今女儿即将成年，他计划和她一起度过这个夏天。影片对离异父亲的刻画很到位——关系混乱，各种问题悬而未决。影片没有皆大欢喜的结局，没有那种一家人最终团聚的感觉——这是一个支离破碎的家庭，而且注定无法重归于好。然而，尼森原本打算利用这个夏天和女儿增进感情，结果女儿却要和朋友去巴黎。这部电影不断地营造出一种我们以为自己能猜到接下来剧情发展的氛围，然后又出人意料地彻底颠覆这种局面。


When Grace and her friend get to Paris, they split a cab with a cute guy... and Grace discovers that the relatives of her friend they were supposed to be staying with are on vacation for the summer - so it's just two boy-crazy girls in a Paris apartment. While she's on the phone to Neeson, admitting that there is no adult supervision - some guys break into the flat and grab her friend. It's sudden and unexpected and the struggle knocks over half the furnishings. Neeson tells her to find a bedroom and hide under the bed, then talks her through what will probably happen.

格蕾丝和朋友到了巴黎后，和一位帅哥拼车……格蕾丝这才发现，她们原本要借宿的朋友的亲戚暑假都去度假了——所以现在只有两个花痴女孩待在巴黎的公寓里。她正和连姆·尼森通电话，坦白说没有大人看管时，几个男人闯进了公寓，抓住了她的朋友。事情发生得猝不及防，扭打中把一半的家具都弄翻了。尼森让她找个卧室躲到床底下，然后跟她解释了接下来可能发生的事情。


We are sure that ex-spy dad will be able to save her by phone - because we've seen that he's a badass, and this is his cute underage daughter.

我们确信这位前间谍老爸一定能通过电话救她——因为我们已经见识过他有多厉害，而这可是他可爱的未成年女儿。


But instead, he says: "You will be taken".

但他却说：“你会被带走。”


Hey, we though ex-spy dad would have some sort of plan to prevent that from happening! Nope. It's inevitable. The guys come into the bedroom, do a search, and leave without finding her... we are sure she's safe! Then - YANK - someone grabs her feet and pulls her from under the bed. That's not what's supposed to happen in a movie! In a movie, the bad guys don't win!

嘿，我们还以为身为前间谍的老爸会想出什么办法阻止这种事发生呢！结果呢？没办法，这事儿是不可避免的。那帮家伙进了卧室，搜了一番，然后没找到她就走了……我们确信她安全了！然后——猛地一拽——有人抓住她的脚，把她从床底下拽了出来。电影里可不是这么演的！电影里，坏人是不会赢的！


She screams, one of the badguys finds the phone, Neeson makes his threat... and the phone is *smashed*.

她尖叫起来，一个坏人找到了手机，尼森发出威胁……然后手机就被砸碎了。


There's also a great bit of unexpected plotting here - two *wealthy* American girls are kidnapped. So, when the girls are kidnapped, we immediately think there will be a call to Grace's wealthy stepfather (Xander Berkeley) with a ransom demand. But there is no call. After being lead to believe this will be about ransom, it's not. It's a "white slave" ring - kidnapping tourist girls, getting them hooked on drugs, forcing them to work as prostitutes. Not what we expected. After setting up how rich Berkeley is for the first third of the film, the story does something else - whenever you thought you knew what would happen next, the story does something you'd never expect.

影片中还有一段出人意料的剧情——两个家境富裕的美国女孩被绑架了。所以，当女孩们被绑架时，我们立刻想到格蕾丝的富裕继父（赞德·伯克利饰）会接到赎金索要电话。但并没有。在被引导相信这起案件与赎金有关之后，真相却并非如此。这是一个“人口贩卖”团伙——他们绑架旅游女孩，让她们染上毒瘾，强迫她们卖淫。这完全出乎我们的意料。影片前三分之一都在铺垫伯克利的财富，之后剧情却来了个出人意料的反转——每当你以为自己猜到接下来会发生什么时，故事总会做出你意想不到的事情。


The best *you can't do that in a movie* scene is when Neeson is cornered with another character - a completely innocent character. Someone on Neeson's side, helping him to find his daughter. And, to escape the predicament, Neeson pulls a gun and shoots this innocent person! Kind of a variation on that advice on what to do if you and a friend are being chased by a Grizzly Bear - trip your friend. Shooting this completely innocent person creates a diversion which allows Neeson to get away. He doesn't shoot to kill - he just wounds them. You can't just shoot another good guy to get away, can you? Well, not in a movie! Completely unexpected and brutal.

电影里最精彩的“绝对不可能”的桥段是：尼森被另一个角色——一个完全无辜的人——逼到了墙角。这个人是尼森的同路人，帮他寻找女儿。为了摆脱困境，尼森竟然拔枪射杀了这个无辜的人！这有点像“如果你和朋友被灰熊追赶该怎么办——绊倒你的朋友”的反面教材。射杀这个无辜的人制造了混乱，让尼森得以脱身。他并非想要杀死对方，只是击伤了对方。你不可能为了逃脱就射杀另一个好人，对吧？至少在电影里不行！这完全出乎意料，而且非常残酷。


When this book first came out there was a storyboard sketch on the cover from my “Double Action” screenplay that managed to crash and burn on its way to the screen when post-Soviet Russia went from welcoming films with open arms, to the Russian Mafia wanting significantly greased palms. The screenplay opens with a tough modern day Texas Sheriff and his comic relief side-kick deputy and establishes their relationship. The deputy is kind of a screw up, but the Sheriff takes care of him like an older brother – and is organized and intelligent enough for the both of them. We meet the Sheriff's wife and kid, to see that he's not just a man of action, he's a family man, too – the perfect hero for an action movie. Then the Sheriff and Deputy go to serve a warrant, which turns into a shoot out, and in the shoot out the Sheriff saves the Deputy's life a couple of times... and then, when you think the shoot out is over – the Sheriff is shot dead by the last escaping bad guy. I killed the hero. I thought that would completely shock the studio reader and later the audience – you can't do that in a movie! Major rug pull, but the great thing about doing this is that now the comic-relief side-kick (the role who usually has a short life expectancy) must become the hero. Because he's been established as a screw up, we still are not sure he will survive the whole movie... and that makes the story unpredictable. I don't know what sold the script, but my guess is that killing the hero in the first 15 pages woke up a sleepy studio reader and kept him from skimming the rest of the screenplay.

这本书刚出版时，封面上印着我那部名为《双重行动》的剧本的故事板草图。这部剧本在搬上银幕的路上遭遇了滑铁卢，因为后苏联时代的俄罗斯从对电影的热情拥抱，变成了俄罗斯黑手党想要从中捞取大量好处。剧本以一位强悍的现代德克萨斯州警长和他负责搞笑的副手搭档开篇，并交代了他们之间的关系。副手有点儿不靠谱，但警长像兄长一样照顾他——而且警长足够有条理、足够聪明，可以应付他们俩。我们见到了警长的妻子和孩子，发现他不仅是个行动派，也是个顾家的男人——简直是动作片里的完美英雄。之后，警长和副手去执行搜查令，结果演变成一场枪战。在枪战中，警长几次救了副手的命……然后，正当你以为枪战结束了的时候——警长被最后一个逃跑的坏蛋击毙了。我把英雄写死了。我当时觉得这肯定会让制片厂的审稿人和后来的观众大吃一惊——电影里可不能这么做！这简直是惊天大反转，但这么做的妙处在于，原本负责搞笑的配角（通常戏份不多）现在必须成为英雄。因为他之前被塑造成一个笨蛋，所以我们仍然不确定他能否活到电影结束……这让剧情充满了悬念。我不知道是什么让剧本最终被采纳，但我猜想，在前15页就让英雄领便当，肯定让昏昏欲睡的审稿人清醒过来，不再匆匆略读剩下的剧本了。


In Hitchcock's “Sabotage” (1936) the deep cover terrorist gives his step-son a box to deliver by a specific time. Inside the box is a ticking bomb, but the kid doesn't know that. The kid gets distracted by some street performers and some other things in the big city and ends up wasting time as kids will do... the whole while suspense builds. We know the bomb is in the box, and we know why it must be delivered by a certain time - that's when it will go off. But, we also know that you can't kill a cute little kid on screen, right? Wrong! Hitchcock believed this so shocked the audience when the film came out that they disliked it. But we are still talking about it today because it's a great rug-pull.

在希区柯克1936年的电影《破坏》（Sabotage）中，一名卧底恐怖分子交给他的继子一个盒子，让他在指定时间前送达。盒子里装着一枚定时炸弹，但孩子并不知道。他被街头艺人和大城市里的其他事物分散了注意力，像所有孩子一样浪费时间……整个过程悬念迭起。我们知道盒子里有炸弹，也知道为什么必须在特定时间送达——因为炸弹会在那个时间爆炸。但是，我们也知道你不能在银幕上杀死一个可爱的小孩，对吧？错！希区柯克坚信这一点，这让影片上映时观众大吃一惊，以至于他们不喜欢这部电影。但时至今日，我们仍然在讨论它，因为它是一个精彩的反转。


In “The Big Heat” (1953) written by Sydney Boehm from a book by William P. McGivern, Glenn Ford is an incorruptible cop investigating the suicide of a fellow cop, who begins to believe it was murder ordered by mob boss Mike Lagana. The chief wants him to drop the case – the cop may have been dirty and they don't want that getting in the papers... and the mob wants him to just take some money and go away. Ford is married, living on a cop's salary, and could sure use the money... but he turns down the bribe. His wife thinks it's the right thing, goes out to the car to drive to the store and... BLAM! The car blows his wife to pieces in his front yard. Up, you can't do that in a movie!

在悉尼·博姆根据威廉·P·麦吉弗恩的小说改编的电影《大热》（1953）中，格伦·福特饰演一位正直的警察，他正在调查一位同事的自杀案。福特逐渐怀疑这是一起黑帮老大迈克·拉加纳指使的谋杀。局长想让他放弃调查——因为那位同事可能不干净，他们不想让这件事见诸报端……而黑帮则想让他拿点钱就走人。福特已婚，靠警察的微薄薪水生活，他当然很需要这笔钱……但他拒绝了贿赂。他的妻子认为他做得对，于是走到车旁准备开车去商店……砰！汽车在他家前院爆炸，把他的妻子炸成了碎片。哎，电影里可不能这么拍！


After a rugpull, *anything* is possible. The audience has been hit by something so unexpected that they don't know what will happen next. You could kill the hero. The victim might still be alive. The villain might even win!

剧情反转之后，一切皆有可能。观众被突如其来的变故震惊，完全无法预料接下来会发生什么。英雄可能会死，受害者可能还活着，甚至反派也可能获胜！


A word of caution: Rugpulls are like nuclear weapons. You can't use them indiscriminately. If you start killing lead characters after a while your script is going to be about some bystander who has nothing to do with the story... plus the audience will come to *expect* the unexpected... making your script predictable again. “Oh, that's his mother? Probably killed in a kitchen explosion in the next scene.” You can't use rugpulls in every script – they are special tools. But sometimes, you just have to do the unthinkable... something that completely changes the trajectory of the story and turns a cop investigates the mob story into an ultra-violent “Death Wish” like revenge flick. The audience thought the story was going to be one thing, but the rugpull turns it into something completely different. Shockingly different.

友情提示：剧情反转就像核武器，不能随意使用。如果你经常让主角领便当，你的剧本就会变成一个与故事毫无关联的旁观者……而且观众会开始期待意料之外的事情发生……这会让你的剧本再次变得可预测。“哦，那是他妈妈？估计下一幕就会在厨房爆炸中丧命。” 你不能在每个剧本里都用剧情反转——它们是特殊的工具。但有时候，你必须做一些意想不到的事情……彻底改变故事走向，把一个警察调查黑帮的故事变成一部像《猛龙怪客》那样的超暴力复仇片。观众原本以为故事会是那样，但剧情反转却把它变成了完全不同的东西。令人震惊的改变。


Twists, Reversals, And Rugpulls keep the pages turning on your script, and keep the audience interest in what happens next. A good twist will have the audience jumping out of their seats and screaming. But to keep the audience on the EDGE of their seats, we fill our scripts with suspense.

剧情反转、出人意料的转折和出人意料的反转，让你的剧本引人入胜，让观众对接下来的发展充满兴趣。一个好的反转会让观众吓得跳起来尖叫。但为了让观众始终保持高度紧张，我们会在剧本中营造悬念。



#↩

SUSPENSE

悬念


Keeping the audience on the edge of their seat is the function of *suspense*. Suspense is not the same as action, nor is it the same as surprise. Suspense is the *anticipation* of action. The longer you draw out the anticipation, the greater the suspense. Once the action happens, the suspense is over... but that's okay, because then we have the action, and we're writing action screenplays.

让观众屏息凝神是悬念的作用。悬念不同于动作，也不同于惊喜。悬念是对动作的期待。期待的时间越长，悬念就越强。一旦动作发生，悬念也就结束了……但这没关系，因为接下来就是动作戏了，而我们写的正是动作剧本。


Hitchcock explained suspense in a number of interviews; "Two men are having an innocent little chat. Let us suppose that there is a bomb underneath the table between them. Nothing happens, then all of the sudden, BOOM! There is an explosion. The audience is surprised, but prior to this surprise, it has been an absolutely ordinary scene, of no special consequence.

希区柯克在多次采访中解释悬念的产生：“两个男人正在进行一场普通的闲聊。假设他们之间的桌子底下有一颗炸弹。什么也没发生，突然，轰！爆炸了。观众会感到惊讶，但在这次惊讶之前，这只是一个极其普通的场景，没有任何特别之处。”


"Now let us take a SUSPENSE situation. The bomb is underneath the table, but the audience knows it... Probably because they have seen the villain place it there. The audience is aware that the bomb is going to explode at one o'clock, and there is a clock in the decor. It is a quarter to one. In this situation, the same innocuous conversation becomes fascinating, because the audience is longing to warn the characters on the screen: 'There's a bomb beneath you, and it's about to explode!'

现在我们来看一个悬念情境。炸弹在桌子底下，但观众知道……可能是因为他们亲眼看到反派把它放在那里。观众知道炸弹会在一点钟爆炸，而场景布置里正好有个钟。现在是差一刻一点。在这种情况下，原本看似无关紧要的对话变得引人入胜，因为观众很想警告屏幕上的角色：“你们脚下有炸弹，马上就要爆炸了！”


"In the first case, we have given the audience fifteen seconds of SURPRISE at the moment of the explosion. In the second case, we have provided them with fifteen MINUTES of SUSPENSE."

“在第一种情况下，我们在爆炸发生的那一刻给了观众十五秒钟的惊喜。在第二种情况下，我们给了他们十五分钟的悬念。”


There are two basic kinds of suspense: the "ticking clock" (or time lock) and "cross cutting". The Hitchcock example above is a ticking clock. We are given an event which will occur at a certain time, and our suspense builds as we get closer and closer to the time of the event.

悬念主要有两种类型：“滴答作响的时钟”（或时间锁定）和“交叉剪辑”。上面提到的希区柯克例子就属于滴答作响的时钟。影片告诉我们某个事件将在某个特定时间发生，随着事件发生时间的临近，悬念也随之增强。


You can further divide 'ticking clocks' into two categories: Big Clocks and Scene Clocks.

你还可以将“滴答作响的钟”进一步分为两类：大钟和场景钟。


#↩

THE BIG CLOCK

大钟


The big clock is a ticking clock which covers the *entire* film. A major event in the film will occur at a certain time, and the hero is usually racing to stop it... but time is running out. In “Minority Report” thanks to the pregogs, Tom Cruise knows that he will murder Leo Crow in 36 hours. The problem is - he has no idea who Leo Crow is, where he is, or why he would ever want to murder him. Because he's the head of the Pre-Crimes Division - a policeman who believes in the precogs ability to predict murders with 100% accuracy, he knows that he has 36 hours to stop himself from killing Crow. He sets his watch to count down from 36 hours, and throughout the rest of the film he keeps consulting his watch. How much time does he have left?

影片中贯穿始终的大钟是一个滴答作响的时钟。影片中的重要事件会在特定时间发生，而英雄通常会争分夺秒地阻止它……但时间紧迫。在《少数派报告》中，多亏了先知，汤姆·克鲁斯知道自己会在36小时后杀死利奥·克劳。问题是——他根本不知道利奥·克劳是谁，在哪里，也不知道他为什么要杀他。因为他是“犯罪预警部门”的负责人——一位相信先知能够百分之百准确预测谋杀案的警察——他知道自己有36小时的时间来阻止自己杀死克劳。他把手表调到36小时倒计时，在接下来的剧情中，他不断地看表。他还剩下多少时间？


At one point he looks at his watch and has only 51 minutes until he will murder Leo Crow. Since the Pre-Crimes Cops all have the same information that he has, he knows they will be there to capture him *before* he murders Crow. The clock keeps ticking/ He looks at his watch - how much time does he have left?

他看了看表，发现距离他谋杀利奥·克劳只剩下51分钟了。由于所有“犯罪侦查警察”都掌握着和他一样的信息，他知道他们会在他动手之前就抓住他。时间一分一秒地过去。他看了看表——他还剩下多少时间？


The next time he looks at his watch he has 12 minutes left. Time is running out!

他下次看表时，还剩12分钟。时间不多了！


The next time he looks at his watch he has just under 5 minutes... and he's in Crow's hotel room. Time is really running out!

他下次看表时，只剩下不到5分钟了……而他已经在克劳的酒店房间里了。时间真的不多了！
