We get to see Cruise's watch as it counts down the seconds - 10 - 9 - 8 - 7 - 6 - 5 - 4 - 3... suspense building with every second that passes! As time ticks away, he becomes more desperate... and the audience becomes more involved.

我们可以看到克鲁斯的手表在倒计时——10、9、8、7、6、5、4、3……每一秒过去，悬念都在增加！随着时间的流逝，他变得越来越绝望……观众也越来越投入。


In Stephen DeSouza's classic 80's action flick "Commando”, John Matrix has twelve hours until the plane he was supposed to be on lands and the villains realize that he has escaped. That's twelve hours to find and rescue his kidnapped daughter... or the bad guys will kill her. Matrix sets his 1980s digital watch to count down the hours, and he frequently glances at his watch to find out how much time he has left. As the film goes on, time ticks away until we're down to *seconds* before they kill his daughter. The Big Clock is what separated this film from the dozens of other throw away action films, and ended up making Arnold a star. “These guys eat too much red meat!” Check out the Russian version “Den' D” - same exact story with different locations.

在斯蒂芬·德索萨执导的80年代经典动作片《突击队》中，约翰·马特里克斯只有12个小时的时间，他原本应该乘坐的飞机即将降落，而反派们会发现他已经逃脱。他必须在这12个小时内找到并救出被绑架的女儿……否则坏人就会杀了她。马特里克斯设置了他那块80年代的电子表来倒计时，他时不时地瞥一眼手表，看看还剩下多少时间。随着剧情的推进，时间一分一秒地流逝，直到距离女儿被杀只剩几秒。正是这“大时钟”让这部电影从众多平庸的动作片中脱颖而出，并最终成就了阿诺·施瓦辛格的巨星地位。“这些人吃太多红肉了！”不妨看看俄罗斯版的《Den' D》——故事完全一样，只是地点不同。


Sometimes a Big Clock can be cut into pieces, like in “Source Code” where a commuter train has blown up... and the mad bomber plans on blowing up the whole city of Chicago next. So they send our Iraq war hero Colter Stevens (Jake Gyllenhaal) back in time for 8 minutes to find the terrorist on the commuter train before it explodes... and that is one Big Clock. But there is a “Bigger Clock” - the bomb that *hasn't* exploded and will level Chicago if Colter can't find the bomber and stop him. But he fails – the train explodes and kills everyone on it, and he has to keep going back until he finds the guy. So each of the time travel segments is a Big Clock, plus the whole story has an additional Big Clock. This reminded me of one of my favorite films, “The Satan Bug” (1965), which we will discuss in a minute. The concept of a Big Clock movie made up of Big Clock scenes makes for an edge of your seat film.

有时，一个“大时钟”会被分割成许多片段，就像电影《源代码》里那样，一列通勤列车爆炸了……而疯狂的炸弹客计划接下来炸毁整个芝加哥。于是，他们派伊拉克战争英雄科尔特·史蒂文斯（杰克·吉伦哈尔饰）回到过去8分钟，在列车爆炸前找到恐怖分子……这本身就是一个“大时钟”。但还有一个“更大的时钟”——那枚尚未爆炸的炸弹，如果科尔特找不到炸弹客并阻止他，芝加哥就会被夷为平地。但他失败了——列车爆炸，车上所有人丧生，他不得不一次又一次地回到过去，直到找到那个人。所以，每一次时间旅行都是一个“大时钟”，而整个故事本身也包含着一个额外的“大时钟”。这让我想起了我最喜欢的电影之一《撒旦虫》（1965），我们稍后会讨论这部电影。由无数个“大时钟”场景组成的“大时钟”电影，本身就充满了扣人心弦的紧张感。


Another good example of The Big Clock is "High Noon". We know the bad guys are arriving at noon, and suspense builds as every minute ticks away. In "High Noon" that grandfather clock becomes the focus of the film, and we keep returning to it. As every minute ticks away, Will Kane comes closer to the big shoot out. Kane tries everything to get help, and as time ticks away, he becomes more desperate... and the audience becomes more involved.

《正午》是“大时钟”的另一个绝佳例子。我们知道坏人会在正午时分出现，随着时间一分一秒地流逝，悬念也随之加剧。在《正午》中，那座老式座钟成为了影片的焦点，我们不断地被它吸引。随着时间的流逝，威尔·凯恩离最终的枪战越来越近。凯恩想尽一切办法寻求帮助，随着时间的流逝，他变得越来越绝望……观众也越来越投入其中。


Another classic western uses a big clock in the exact opposite way. The original version of "3:10 To Yuma" (based on a story by Elmore Leonard), our hero is a regular guy, a farmer, picking up some spare change guarding an evil desperado in a hotel until the 3:10 prison train comes to take him away. In "High Noon" the clock is ticking away until the confrontation begins, in "3:10 To Yuma" the clock ticks away until the confrontation is over. If our hero can hold off the desperado's henchmen until 3:10, he'll survive. But the henchmen's plans escalate as time passes. Becoming more and more violent. After a while, we begin to wonder if our farmer-hero can survive the attacks by these evil gunslingers. If he can hold on just another ten minutes....

另一部经典西部片则以截然相反的方式运用了时钟。在原版《决战犹马镇》（改编自埃尔莫·伦纳德的小说）中，我们的主人公是一位普通的农民，为了赚取一些零钱，他不得不在一家旅馆里看守一个邪恶的亡命之徒，直到3点10分的囚车来接他。在《正午》中，时钟滴答作响，直到冲突开始；而在《决战犹马镇》中，时钟滴答作响，直到冲突结束。如果我们的主人公能够抵挡住亡命之徒的手下直到3点10分，他就能活下来。但随着时间的推移，手下的计划不断升级，变得越来越暴力。过了一段时间，我们开始怀疑这位农民英雄是否能够抵挡住这些邪恶枪手的攻击。他还能再坚持十分钟吗……


That's suspense.

真是悬念迭起。


The remake pulls much of the action *out of the room* which opens up the story, yet oddly dissipates the suspense. It *does* give us a great horse chase, though... and great roles for both Russell Crowe and Christian Bale. But some things that seem innovative and interesting kind of undermine the story - at the end the desperado decides to do the right thing and give himself up... which kind of negates the whole film we have just seen. Though this is a great ending on paper, I think it runs into that “villain's death karma” thing we looked at back in the Hero Chapter – if the villain has made the hero's life hell for the past 110 minutes, the villain needs to get 110 minutes worth of hell all at once in the end. When the villain decides to reform, it seems like they are cheating karma. Check out both versions – each has something to offer.

翻拍版将大部分动作戏都搬到了房间之外，这虽然拓展了故事的格局，却也奇怪地削弱了悬念。不过，它确实呈现了一场精彩的骑马追逐戏……而且罗素·克劳和克里斯蒂安·贝尔的表演都非常出色。但一些看似创新有趣的地方却在某种程度上削弱了故事——比如，在结尾，亡命之徒决定改邪归正，自首……这似乎否定了我们之前看到的整部电影。虽然从理论上讲，这是一个很棒的结局，但我认为它触及了我们在“英雄篇”中讨论过的“反派的死亡因果报应”——如果反派在过去的110分钟里让英雄的生活如同地狱，那么反派最终也应该承受同样的痛苦。当反派决定改邪归正时，感觉就像是在欺骗因果报应。不妨看看这两个版本——它们各有千秋。


Another film that uses a Big Clock in the exact opposite way is Don Siegel's “Hell Is For Heroes”, where a handful of soldiers are left at a remote outpost during World War 2... only to discover that an entire division of Nazis are headed their way! They know that if they can survive the night an American division will come to relieve them in the morning... but it's a handful of guys against *the German army*. Can they hold out until morning? As every minute ticks away, they are closer to salvation... but the Nazis are closer to a full scale attack! If they can hold on just another ten minutes....

另一部以截然相反的方式运用大钟的电影是唐·西格尔的《英雄的地狱》。影片讲述了二战期间，几名士兵被留在偏远哨所，却发现一个纳粹师正朝他们逼近！他们知道，如果能熬过一夜，第二天早上就会有美军师前来接替他们……但面对的是德军，他们只是几个人而已。他们能坚持到天亮吗？随着时间一分一秒地过去，他们离获救越来越近……但纳粹的全面进攻也越来越近！如果他们能再坚持十分钟……


That's suspense.

真是悬念迭起。


#↩

SCENE CLOCKS

场景时钟


If there's a *macro* there must be a *micro”, and “Scene Clocks” can also be used to create suspense. A Scene Clock is like the Hitchcock bomb. A small ticking clock used in a scene or a series of scenes to keep the movie hopping.

既然有宏观层面，就必然有微观层面，“场景时钟”也可以用来营造悬念。场景时钟就像希区柯克的炸弹，是一种在某个或一系列场景中使用的小型滴答时钟，用来推动剧情发展。


A good example of the Scene Clock is the opening scene of “Minority Report”. The precogs predict a murder - a business man will return home from work unexpectedly, discover his wife in the arms of another man, and stab them both to death with a pair of scissors... unless Tom Cruise and his team can stop them.

《少数派报告》的开场就是一个很好的“场景时钟”例子。先知们预言了一起谋杀案——一名商人会意外下班回家，发现妻子与另一名男子在一起，然后用剪刀将两人刺死……除非汤姆·克鲁斯和他的团队能够阻止他们。


They look up the future killer's address - but it doesn't match the neighborhood in the precog images. Did he move? The clock is ticking - they have to figure out his new address just from looking at the images. Tom sees a kid on an old push merry-go-round, that narrows it down to one neighborhood. With the clock ticking - closer and closer to the time of the murder - Tom and his Team jet to the future crime scene. They get there and... all of the houses look exactly the same. The clock is ticking - only minutes until the murder!

他们查到了未来凶手的地址——但与预知图像中的街区不符。他搬家了吗？时间紧迫——他们必须仅凭图像找出他的新地址。汤姆看到一个孩子在玩老式旋转木马，这缩小了范围，确定了一个街区。随着时间一分一秒地流逝——距离谋杀案发生的时间越来越近——汤姆和他的团队迅速赶往未来的犯罪现场。他们到达那里后发现……所有的房子看起来都一模一样。时间紧迫——距离谋杀案发生只剩几分钟了！


Tick. Tick. Tick.

滴答。滴答。滴答。

Minutes left to seconds left.

剩余时间从几分钟到几秒。


Tom has to figure out which one of the houses will be the crime scene. When he figures out the clues, they rush into the house with only seconds to spare... and stop the murder from happening.

汤姆必须找出哪栋房子是犯罪现场。当他找到线索后，他们争分夺秒地冲进房子……阻止了谋杀的发生。


There's another scene clock a few scenes later when the precogs predict that Tom will murder Leo Crow. The only other person who saw the precog's images was the nerdy guy who takes care of them. "I like you boss, you've always been good to me... so I'll give you 2 minutes before I hit the alarm." Now Cruise has 2 minutes to get out of the building... and he ends up trapped in an elevator with his arch-enemy Witworth...

几个场景之后，又出现了一个场景时钟，预言家们预测汤姆会谋杀利奥·克劳。唯一一个看到预言画面的人是负责照看预言家们的那个书呆子。“我喜欢你，老板，你一直对我很好……所以我给你两分钟时间，不然我就拉响警报了。”现在克鲁斯只有两分钟时间逃出大楼……结果他却被困在电梯里，和他的死对头维特沃斯在一起……


Tick. Tick. Tick.

滴答。滴答。滴答。


Another good example of the Scene Clock is the nuclear bomb used at the end of "Goldfinger". Goldfinger activates the bomb, then handcuffs James Bond to it. Toss in Odd Job as a diversion and you've upped the suspense through cross cutting (which we'll get to later). After Bond fries Odd Job, he races to the nuclear bomb, with time ticking away. He tries to disarm the bomb, but what does he know of nuclear weapons?

另一个运用场景时钟的好例子是《金手指》结尾的核弹。金手指启动了炸弹，然后把詹姆斯·邦德铐在了炸弹上。再加上奥德·乔布的干扰，通过交叉剪辑（我们稍后会详细介绍）就提升了悬念。邦德干掉奥德·乔布后，争分夺秒地赶往核弹。他试图拆除炸弹，但他对核武器又了解多少呢？


Tick. Tick. Tick.

滴答。滴答。滴答。

Minutes left to seconds left.

剩余时间从几分钟到几秒。


Then the nuclear expert arrives and begins the disarming procedure. But is there enough time left?

随后，核专家赶到并开始解除核武库的程序。但时间还够吗？


Tick. Tick. Tick.

滴答。滴答。滴答。

The seconds run out.

时间到了。


We *see* the timer clock, as it goes from double digits to single digits.

我们*看到*计时器时钟，它从两位数变为个位数。


Tick. Tick. Tick.

滴答。滴答。滴答。


The bomb is finally disarmed with only *seconds* to spare. (Trivia question: How many seconds?)

炸弹终于在最后几秒钟被拆除了。（小知识：到底是几秒？）


#↩

DEADLINES

截止日期


Whether it's a Scene Clock or a Big Clock it's based on a *deadline*. A certain exact time when something is going to take place. Usually the more exact the time, the better the suspense. If your villain says "I'll be back at nightfall to kill you", it's not as effective as if he says "I'll be back at seven fifteen to kill you". We can look at a clock and *see* how many minutes are left until seven fifteen, but looking at the sky and trying to figure out when nightfall starts is open to interpretation. Without a deadline and consequences in a rom-com, Hugh Grant wouldn't have to race anywhere at the end of the movie... so even if you are not writing an action or thriller film, these techniques are important.

无论是场景时钟还是大时钟，它们都基于一个*截止日期*。也就是某个特定时间点，某件事将会发生。通常来说，时间越精确，悬念就越强。如果你的反派说“我会在天黑时回来杀了你”，这远不如他说“我会在七点十五分回来杀了你”来得有效。我们可以看钟表*知道*距离七点十五分还有多少分钟，但仰望天空试图判断夜幕何时降临则有很多种解读。在浪漫喜剧中，如果没有截止日期和后果，休·格兰特在电影结尾就不用赶路了……所以，即使你写的不是动作片或惊悚片，这些技巧也很重要。


The sooner the audience knows that deadline, the sooner the suspense begins. And the more often we *see* the ticking clock (some physical manifestation of time passing) the better the suspense. Have the hero look at his watch, have him run into a store with a clock...

观众越早知道截止日期，悬念就越早开始。而且，我们越频繁地看到滴答作响的时钟（某种时间流逝的具象表现），悬念就越强烈。让主人公看表，让他跑进一家有钟表的商店……


We have to know how close the deadline is, or it is not effective.

我们必须知道截止日期有多近，否则就无法有效执行。


The remake of “The Taking Of Pelham 123” has a rapidly approaching deadline where the audience is made aware of exactly how much time is left on the clock throughout the film. A mysterious guy named Ryder (John Travolta) and his crew have hijacked the Pelham subway train in New York City. Though he can't take the hijacked subway train to Cuba, he can take it to an isolated piece of track where his crew can defend the train, and make a list of demands. He radios the dispatcher, Garber (Denzel Washington) tells him the City of New York has exactly one hour to get him $10 million. That gives us our big ticking clock for the entire movie - 60 minutes and counting down to 0. But what are the consequences?

翻拍版《骑劫地下铁》中，时间紧迫，影片始终让观众意识到时间的流逝。一个名叫莱德（约翰·特拉沃尔塔饰）的神秘男子和他的同伙劫持了纽约地铁的佩勒姆线列车。虽然他无法将劫持的列车开往古巴，但他可以将其带到一段偏僻的轨道上，让他的同伙守卫列车，并列出一份要求清单。他通过无线电联系调度员加伯（丹泽尔·华盛顿饰），加伯告诉他，纽约市政府必须在一个小时内支付他1000万美元。这就是贯穿整部电影的倒计时——60分钟倒计时结束。但后果又是什么呢？


Ryder tells Garber that if he does not have the $10 million in one hour, he will kill one hostage every minute until he gets the money. Which gives us consequences and an additional series of deadlines. Once the 60 minutes are up, we have a series of 60 second deadlines... with someone being killed as consequences for *each* 60 second deadline. Plus, almost everything else in the film is given some sort of Scene Clock. We now have some hard deadlines that our protagonist must meet, or there are hard consequences. That presses the protagonist in to action - they can't just wait until Ryder gets hungry and gives up, they must do something *now* to prevent the loss of innocent lives.

莱德告诉加伯，如果他一个小时内筹不到1000万美元，他就会每分钟杀害一名人质，直到筹到钱为止。这带来了后果，也带来了一系列新的期限。60分钟结束后，接下来是一系列60秒的期限……每个60秒期限都会导致一人死亡。此外，影片中几乎所有其他事件都设定了某种“场景时钟”。现在，主角必须遵守一些紧迫的期限，否则将面临严重的后果。这迫使主角采取行动——他们不能坐等莱德饿死放弃，他们必须立即采取行动，阻止无辜生命的逝去。


Our protagonist Garber is just a dispatcher, not a hostage negotiator. So when the best NYPD hostage negotiator Camonetti (John Turturro) shows up, they send Garber home and Camonetti takes over... but Ryder refuses to talk to Camonetti! He gives them 60 seconds to get Garber back on the radio or he will kill the Motorman. Now, as Ryder counts down from 60, they race through the building looking for Garber, and finally find him outside the building on his way home! They grab him and rush him back to the radio... with Ryder counting down... and are not fast enough. Ryder kills the Motorman! Deadlines and consequences and a great Scene Clock.

我们的主人公加伯只是个调度员，并非人质谈判专家。所以当纽约警局最优秀的谈判专家卡莫内蒂（约翰·特托罗饰）赶到时，他们让加伯回家，卡莫内蒂接手了谈判……但莱德拒绝与卡莫内蒂交谈！他给了他们60秒时间让加伯回到无线电旁，否则他就要杀了那个“电工”。莱德开始倒计时，他们冲进大楼寻找加伯，最终在楼外找到了他，当时他正要回家！他们抓住他，把他送回无线电旁……莱德继续倒计时……但他们还是不够快。莱德杀死了“电工”！时间紧迫，后果严重，剧情节奏把握得非常出色。


While we have this 60 minute big clock countdown going on, there are several more small deadlines spread out throughout the screenplay. Once the $10 million in cash is assembled, they have to drive cross-town against the clock to deliver it to Ryder. Another deadline of sorts - this one is all about *distance*. Can they get the money across town in time? The film is a great example of using deadlines to create suspense and tension.

虽然影片中有一个60分钟的大倒计时，但剧本里还穿插着几个小的截止日期。一旦筹集到1000万美元现金，他们就必须争分夺秒地开车横穿整个城市，把钱交给莱德。这又是一个类似截止日期的挑战——这次的重点在于“距离”。他们能及时把钱送到目的地吗？这部电影巧妙地运用了各种截止日期来营造悬念和紧张感，堪称典范。


#↩

DOES ANYBODY KNOW

WHAT TIME IT IS?

有人知道现在几点了吗？


But you can also use the *lack* of a physical clock to build suspense. Have you ever been on your way to work and got caught in a traffic jam? No watch and your car clock doesn't work? You *know* you're late for work, but you don't know *how* late. So you keep searching for a clock. Maybe the bank has one? No. Maybe you can see the clock in the 7-11 store. It's too far away, you can't read it. I've had this happen to me, and become so desperate to know what time it is that I've looked through the windows of cars to try and read other driver's watches.

但你也可以利用缺少实体时钟这一点来营造悬念。你有没有过这样的经历：上班路上堵车，没带手表，车里的时钟又坏了？你知道自己上班要迟到了，但不知道到底迟到了多久。于是你开始到处找时钟。也许银行有？没有。也许你能在7-11便利店看到时钟。但太远了，看不清。我也遇到过这种情况，当时我急得不行，甚至会透过车窗去看其他司机的手表。


In Alfred Hitchcock's “Notorious” there's a great "soft clock" - during a huge party at Nazi Sebastian's house, Cary Grant and Sebastian's wife Ingrid Bergman - who is really a deep cover CIA Agent - plan on searching his wine cellar. Bergman has managed to get keys to everyplace else in the house and do a quiet search, but there's only one wine cellar key and that's on Sebastian's key rings. So she swipes it just before the party while he's getting dressed and plans on returning it before he notices that it's missing.

在阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克的电影《美人计》中，有一个非常巧妙的“暗号”——在纳粹分子塞巴斯蒂安的家中举办的一场盛大派对上，凯瑞·格兰特和塞巴斯蒂安的妻子英格丽·褒曼（实际上她是一名秘密的中央情报局特工）计划搜查他的酒窖。褒曼设法弄到了房子里其他所有地方的钥匙，可以悄悄地进行搜查，但酒窖的钥匙只有一把，而且就在塞巴斯蒂安的钥匙串上。于是，在派对开始前，趁着塞巴斯蒂安正在穿衣服的时候，她偷偷拿走了钥匙，并打算在他发现钥匙不见之前还给他。


Grant and Bergman sneak into the wine cellar and begin searching...

格兰特和伯格曼偷偷溜进酒窖，开始搜寻……


Unaware that the party is so successful that they're running out of champagne. We see the tub filled with champagne bottles as the waiters pull them out and pop the corks one-by-one. Fewer bottles - fewer bottles - fewer bottleS. The bottles are like our ticking clock. Eventually there will be so few bottles that a waiter will ask Sebastian to go down to the wine cellar to get some more... but when exactly is that? When there are ten bottles left? Five bottles left? Because we aren't exactly sure, the next bottle they pull from the tub might spell death for Grant and Bergman.

他们浑然不知派对如此成功，香槟都快喝光了。我们看到侍者们从装满香槟酒瓶的桶里一瓶接一瓶地取出，拔开瓶塞。瓶数越来越少——越来越少——越来越少。这些酒瓶就像我们倒计时的时钟。最终，酒瓶会少到侍者不得不请塞巴斯蒂安去酒窖再取一些……但究竟是什么时候呢？只剩十瓶的时候？五瓶的时候？因为我们无法确定，所以他们从桶里取出的下一瓶，或许就意味着格兰特和伯格曼的末日。


I decided to use this idea in a recent script called "Hard Return" after hearing my friend Roger Ebert constantly complain about how overused those red LED bomb timers are in films. The world as we know it will be destroyed in ten hours. A big red LED "countdown clock" on the wall of Mission Control begins counting back - 00:59:59 - 00:59:58 - 00:59:57 - Counting the seconds until we are all dead.

我最近在一部名为《硬返航》（Hard Return）的剧本中采用了这个想法，起因是我听朋友罗杰·艾伯特（Roger Ebert）不断抱怨电影里红色LED炸弹计时器用得太多了。我们所知的世界将在十小时后毁灭。任务控制中心墙上一个巨大的红色LED“倒计时钟”开始倒计时——00:59:59——00:59:58——00:59:57——倒计时着我们所有人死亡的最后几秒。


Then the power goes out.

然后就停电了。


Instant panic.

瞬间恐慌。


"Does anybody have a watch?"

“有人有手表吗？”


Someone has an old fashioned watch, but has it been set for the right time? Is the sweep second hand accurate? Wait, is that minute hand on the seven or the eight? What if it's two minutes off, and the world ends before we complete the mission?

有人有一块老式手表，但时间调准了吗？秒针准吗？等等，分针是在7还是8？万一慢了两分钟，世界在我们完成任务之前就毁灭了怎么办？


I took the cliche red LED timer and turned it!

我拿起那个俗套的红色LED计时器，把它转了过来！


One of my favorite “soft clocks” is in Richard Matheson's novel “I Am Legend” where a vampire plague has turned everyone except our hero Robert Neville into blood suckers who only come out after sunset. But on cloudy days it's difficult to tell exactly when the sun sets – and sometimes he gets trapped miles from the safety of his home-fortress. The lack of a hard deadline is used to build dread – which is a sister to suspense. On some days Neville never knows when he has run out of time, and this keeps you constantly worried that he will make the mistake of *not* looking at his watch and get in trouble. This is a brilliant novel which has now been filmed three times... and oddly enough the very first version made on the cheap with Vincent Price is still the best.

我最喜欢的“软时钟”之一出自理查德·马西森的小说《我是传奇》。小说中，一场吸血鬼瘟疫将除主人公罗伯特·内维尔以外的所有人都变成了吸血鬼，他们只在日落后出没。但在阴天，很难准确判断日落时间——有时他会被困在离家数英里之外的地方。这种缺乏明确时间限制的设定营造了恐惧感——这与悬念如出一辙。有些时候，内维尔根本不知道时间何时耗尽，这让你时刻担心他会犯错，比如没看表，从而惹上麻烦。这是一部精彩的小说，已被改编成三部电影……奇怪的是，由文森特·普莱斯主演的最初版本虽然成本低廉，却仍然是最好的版本。


Creating an ambiguous ticking clock is a little dangerous. You have to make sure the audience understands that there is a deadline or the suspense won't work.

营造一种模棱两可的倒计时效果有点危险。你必须确保观众明白存在一个截止日期，否则悬念就无法成立。


#↩

WHEN TIME RAN OUT

当时间耗尽时


No matter how you use the clock, time *must* be running out. The less time left on the clock, the higher the suspense. Obviously, if the villain's bomb is set to explode in an hour, it's more exciting than if it's set to explode a week from next Tuesday.

无论你如何运用时间，时间*必须*在流逝。剩余时间越少，悬念就越高。显然，如果反派的炸弹将在1小时后爆炸，那肯定比炸弹将在下周二爆炸要刺激得多。


Ticking clocks are almost always stopped in time... but they don't have to be. The thriller “Out Of Time” is filled with beat-the-clock suspense... where the protagonist often *doesn't* solve the problem in time, which leads to even bigger problems!

滴答作响的时钟几乎总是停止运转……但它们并非必须如此。惊悚片《超时空》充满了与时间赛跑的悬念……主人公往往无法及时解决问题，这反而导致了更大的麻烦！


Denzel Washington is a small town cop in Florida who is having an affair with the wife of the town's big celebrity, ex-pro football star Dean Cain. When Cain and his wife are murdered, a team of big city detectives are brought in to solve the crime. Now Denzel must race against the detectives to find the real killer before they uncover all of the evidence that points to him.

丹泽尔·华盛顿饰演佛罗里达州一个小镇的警察，他与镇上名人、前职业橄榄球明星迪恩·凯恩的妻子有染。凯恩夫妇惨遭谋杀后，大城市的侦探团队被调来侦破此案。如今，丹泽尔必须与侦探们争分夺秒，在他们发现所有指向他的证据之前，找出真正的凶手。


A good example of typical beat-the-clock suspense is when the detectives have the wife's phone records FAXed to the police station. Denzel *knows* there will be dozens of calls to his cell phone - evidence of his affair that might turn him into the number one suspect. So he has to intercept the FAX, scan it into his computer, delete his name and phone number from the list, then re-FAX it to the police department FAX machine. Problem is, after he intercepts the FAX, the detectives call the phone company and ask why it's taking so long... and the phone company resends the FAX! Now Denzel must scan and delete against the clock! Will he get his FAX sent before the phone company can resend theirs?

一个典型的争分夺秒的悬疑故事是这样的：侦探们把妻子的通话记录传真到了警察局。丹泽尔*知道*他的手机上会有几十个来电记录——这些记录很可能成为他出轨的证据，让他成为头号嫌疑人。所以他必须截获传真，扫描到电脑里，从列表中删除自己的姓名和电话号码，然后再重新传真到警察局。问题是，在他截获传真后，侦探们打电话给电话公司，询问为什么这么久还没处理完……结果电话公司又重新发送了一遍！现在丹泽尔必须争分夺秒地扫描和删除！他能在电话公司重新发送之前把传真发出去吗？


Later in the film, Denzel *fails* to beat the clock, which creates a big, juicy, conflict. Because he knew the victims, he has an inside track the big city detectives don't have. He uncovers a suspect - a friend of Cain's with a serious criminal record - and races to capture the suspect at his hotel room and recover any evidence that implicates Denzel. When Denzel leaves the police station, the detectives have found the suspect's name and are searching for his current location. Can Denzel get to the hotel, capture the suspect, destroy or remove any evidence that might implicate him in the murder; *before* the detectives get there?

影片后半段，丹泽尔没能赶在时间耗尽前完成任务，这引发了一场扣人心弦的冲突。由于他认识受害者，所以掌握了大城市侦探们所不具备的内部线索。他发现了一名嫌疑人——凯恩的一个有严重犯罪记录的朋友——并争分夺秒地赶到嫌疑人下榻的酒店房间将其抓获，同时还要收集任何可能牵连到丹泽尔的证据。当丹泽尔离开警局时，侦探们已经查明了嫌疑人的名字，正在搜寻他的下落。丹泽尔能否在侦探们到达之前，赶到酒店，抓获嫌疑人，并销毁或清除任何可能与谋杀案有关的线索呢？


Denzel gets to the hotel, finds a bunch of evidence that implicates him (the plan was to frame him for the murders) and also finds the suspect... with a gun! The two fight, Denzel *kills* the suspect, grabs the evidence, flees the hotel room... but the detectives have arrived at the hotel! They seal off all of the exits! Now he is trapped in the hotel with evidence implicating him in the murders and the suspect dead upstairs! How do you get past the detectives? Because Denzel *fails* to beat the clock, fails to make his deadline, an intense situation is created - how the heck can he escape?

丹泽尔到达酒店，发现了一堆对他不利的证据（原本的计划是陷害他谋杀），还发现了嫌疑人……而且嫌疑人手里拿着枪！两人搏斗，丹泽尔*杀死*了嫌疑人，抢走了证据，逃出了酒店房间……但侦探们已经抵达酒店！他们封锁了所有出口！现在他被困在酒店里，证据指向他，而嫌疑人却死在了楼上！他该如何逃脱侦探的追捕？由于丹泽尔*没能*在最后期限前完成任务，陷入了困境——他究竟该如何脱身？


Because the hero usually beats the clock in movies, when he or she fails it's unexpected and interesting. It creates another layer of suspense and adds conflict from those consequences.

因为电影里的英雄通常都能在时间限制内完成任务，所以当他/她失败时，就会显得出人意料，引人入胜。这会增添一层悬念，并因失败的后果而增加冲突。


#↩

MULTIPLE CLOCKS

多个时钟


Don't stop with one clock. Use multiples. A Big Clock and a few Scene Clocks. You can't have too much suspense.

不要只用一个钟，要用多个。一个大钟，再加几个场景钟。悬念越多越好。


In “The Satan Bug” a villain has stolen germ warfare material from a top secret government lab. The Big Clock has our hero trying to figure out who the villain is and where he has the germs stashed before the villain escapes. There are a half dozen Scene Clocks, ending with the hero capturing the villain and the villain explaining that he's planted a germ bomb in Los Angeles set to go off at noon.

在《撒旦虫》这一集中，一个反派从一个绝密政府实验室窃取了细菌战材料。在“大时钟”环节中，我们的英雄必须找出反派的身份以及他藏匿细菌的地点，以免反派逃脱。本集共有六个场景时钟，最终以英雄抓获反派、反派承认他在洛杉矶安放了一枚细菌炸弹，将于中午引爆而告终。


That final Scene Clock keeps the last twenty minutes of the film hopping as the good guys try to find, then disarm, the bomb before it explodes and infects everyone in L.A. with a killer disease. “The Satan Bug “ is a suspense textbook, using both Scene Clocks and a Big Clock to keep us on the edge of our seat for the entire running time of the film. Using a clock of some sort based on a fixed deadline and consequences is the most common way to create suspense in a film. Remember that suspense is the anticipation of an action – so as soon as the action occurs, that suspense is over. But what about suspense in an action scene? Is that possible?

影片最后二十分钟的紧张气氛始终萦绕在观众心头，正义一方必须找到并拆除炸弹，才能阻止它爆炸，避免致命病毒感染洛杉矶所有人。“撒旦病毒”堪称悬念教科书，它巧妙地运用了场景时钟和大型时钟，让观众在整部影片中都提心吊胆。在电影中，利用某种基于固定期限和后果的时钟来营造悬念是最常见的手法。记住，悬念是对即将发生的动作的期待——一旦动作发生，悬念也就消失了。但是，动作场景中如何营造悬念呢？这有可能吗？


#↩

CROSSCUTTING

横切


The other way to create suspense is through crosscutting. Crosscutting began as an editing technique in the silent era, designed to heighten suspense (usually credited to Eisenstein). There are two types of cross cutting, 'Action' and 'Suspense'.

另一种营造悬念的方法是交叉剪辑。交叉剪辑起源于默片时代，是一种旨在增强悬念的剪辑技巧（通常认为是爱森斯坦首创）。交叉剪辑分为两种类型：“动作”和“悬念”。


For an example of 'Suspense' cross cutting we go back to Hitchcock: "A curious person breaks into someone else's room and begins to search through the drawers. Now, you show the person who lives in the room coming up the stairs. Then you cut back to the person who is searching, and the audience feels like warning him: 'Be careful, someone's coming up the stairs!' You cut back and forth between the searcher and the flat owner. The closer the flat owner gets, the more exciting the suspense. Soon the audience is yelling, 'Get out! Get out!'"

举个“悬念”交叉剪辑的例子，我们可以回顾希区柯克的作品：“一个好奇的人闯入别人的房间，开始翻找抽屉。这时，镜头切换到房间的主人上楼。然后切回正在翻找的人，观众会忍不住想提醒他：‘小心，有人上楼了！’镜头在翻找者和房主之间来回切换。房主越靠近，悬念就越强烈。很快，观众就会大喊：‘快出去！快出去！’”


My erotic thriller, "Riptides", is about a husband who strays while his wife is away. The husband is in bed with his girlfriend when the wife returns early from her business trip.

我的情色惊悚小说《激流》讲述的是一个丈夫趁妻子不在家时出轨的故事。妻子提前结束出差回家时，丈夫正和情人躺在床上。

Suspense crosscutting moves back and forth between two subjects, with suspense building as the two subjects become closer to each other. Whether this is a man searching a house while the homeowner gets closer, or a killer stalking a victim hidden in the closet of an old dark house, or two trains on the same track racing towards each other; cross cutting takes two people or objects we *don't* want to see in the same scene and puts them on a collision course.

悬念交叉剪辑在两个主体之间来回切换，随着两人距离的拉近，悬念也随之增强。无论是男子在屋内搜寻而屋主悄悄靠近，还是杀手在阴暗老宅的壁橱里跟踪藏匿的受害者，亦或是两列火车在同一轨道上疾驰而去；交叉剪辑将我们*不想*看到的两个人物或物体置于同一场景，并让他们朝着碰撞的方向发展。


Suspense cross cutting can be used in a scene, or stretched over an entire script; as in “Bourne Identity” where we are constantly cutting back and forth between Chris Cooper and his team at Treadstone who are searching for Bourne, and Bourne trying to figure out who he is and why people are trying to kill him. As the film progresses, the two continue on a collision course... getting closer and closer!

悬念交叉剪辑既可以用于单个场景，也可以贯穿整个剧本；例如在《谍影重重》中，我们不断地在克里斯·库珀和他的“绊脚石”团队搜寻伯恩的场景，以及伯恩试图弄清自己是谁以及为何有人要杀他的场景之间来回切换。随着电影的推进，两人之间的冲突愈演愈烈……越来越近！


#↩

ACTION CROSSCUTTING

动作交叉


Action crosscutting takes two *separate* actions and divides the audience's loyalties between them. The idea is to create a pair of different actions, and just as one scene gets exciting, jump to the other. When that scene becomes exciting, jump back to the first scene.

动作交叉剪辑将两个*独立*的动作场景并置，从而分散观众的注意力。其理念是创造两个不同的动作场景，当其中一个场景开始精彩时，切换到另一个场景。当第二个场景也精彩起来时，再切回第一个场景。


Suspense is created through *cliffhangers* at the end of each segment.

每段结尾都设置了*悬念*，以此制造悬念。


The Villain aims his gun at the Hero and gets ready to pull the trigger...

反派举枪瞄准英雄，准备扣动扳机……


Cut to the Sidekick fighting with the Henchman on the roof of a building.

镜头切换到跟班在楼顶与喽啰搏斗的场景。

The Sidekick gets in a few punches, then the Henchman knocks the Sidekick off the roof!

小跟班打了几拳，然后喽啰就把小跟班从屋顶上打了下去！

The Sidekick grabs the edge of the roof with his fingertips.

小跟班用指尖抓住屋顶边缘。

The Henchman steps on his hand...

喽啰踩到了他的手……


Cut to, the Hero drops to the floor just as the Villain fires.

镜头一转，英雄倒在地上，反派随即开火。

The Hero rolls across the carpet and knocks the Villain down.

英雄滚过地毯，将恶棍撞倒在地。

The gun goes skittering.

枪脱手飞走了。

The Hero scrambles for the gun.

英雄慌忙去抢枪。

The Villain grabs a table and swings it at the Hero's head.

反派抓起一张桌子，朝英雄的头猛砸去。

The Hero aims the gun at the Villain and pulls the trigger.

英雄将枪对准反派，扣动了扳机。

Click.

点击。

Out of bullets...

子弹用完了……


Cut to, the Sidekick...

镜头切换到跟班……


The audience wants to find out how the Hero gets out of his problem *and* find out how the Sidekick gets out of HIS problem. By cutting between the two, you can draw out the action, and draw out the suspense, for quite a few minutes.

观众想知道英雄如何摆脱困境，也想知道配角如何摆脱困境。通过在两人之间切换镜头，你可以延长剧情发展，并将悬念持续数分钟之久。


Action Crosscutting works great in Act Three, where you may have to fill 20 pages with exciting action sequences. It allows variety and suspense, and keeps the reader turning the pages to find out how the hero gets out of this one. But the reader can't skim, or she'll never find out how the Sidekick survives. A great example is the end of “Mission Impossible: Ghost Protocol” where Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) is engaged in an epic fight with the villain over a briefcase filled with launch codes in an automated car park, which is cross-cut with comic relief Benji (Simon Pegg) is trying to rewire a computer without tools and keeps pricked his fingers into a bloody mess, which is cross-cut with sidekick Brandt (Jeremy Renner) who is battling the henchman in order to get get the power back on. We cut between all three battles – each being a different part of the solution which will stop a nuclear missile from taking out San Francisco (oddly – the city where I saw the film). By cutting from one character to another and creating a cliffhanger, the sequence continued to be exciting during all three battles. Cross cutting for suspense is a great Act Three tool, and can turn a longish action sequence into a page turner.

动作交叉剪辑在第三幕中效果极佳，因为你可能需要用精彩的动作场面填满二十页。它既能带来多样性，又能制造悬念，让读者迫不及待地翻页，想知道主角是如何脱险的。但读者也不能略读，否则就永远不会知道搭档是如何幸存的。一个很好的例子是《碟中谍4：幽灵协议》的结尾：伊森·亨特（汤姆·克鲁斯饰）在自动化停车场与反派展开了一场争夺装有发射密码的公文包的史诗级大战，与此同时，负责搞笑的本吉（西蒙·佩吉饰）正在尝试在没有工具的情况下重新连接电脑，结果手指被扎得血肉模糊；而他的搭档布兰特（杰瑞米·雷纳饰）则正在与喽啰搏斗，试图恢复电力供应。我们在这三场战斗之间来回切换——每一场战斗都是阻止核导弹袭击旧金山（巧合的是，我看这部电影的城市）解决方案的不同部分。通过在不同角色间切换镜头并制造悬念，三场战斗的节奏都保持了紧张刺激。交叉剪辑是第三幕中营造悬念的绝佳技巧，可以将冗长的动作场面变成引人入胜的精彩片段。


#↩

FOCUS OBJECTS

焦点对象


Suspense scenes are based on a "focus object" which the suspense revolves around.

悬疑场景通常围绕一个“焦点对象”展开，悬念就发生在这个对象周围。


The bomb under the table, a fraying rope on a rope bridge our hero is racing across, the bloody back seat of the car the protagonist transported the body in. In Hitchcock's “Saboteur” the only man who can prove the hero is innocent has fallen from the Statue Of Liberty's torch... the hero hangs on to the sleeve of his coat. The man dangles hundreds of feet above the ground. Hanging by a thread. The thread that connects his sleeve to his coat. The thread begins to unravel! The entire scene is focused on that thread! Will it hold long enough for the hero to haul him up? That's suspense!

桌子底下的炸弹，主人公飞奔而过的绳桥上摇摇欲坠的绳索，以及主人公运送尸体时所乘坐的那辆汽车血迹斑斑的后座。在希区柯克的《破坏者》中，唯一能证明主人公清白的人从自由女神像的火炬上掉了下来……主人公紧紧抓住他的衣袖。那人悬在数百英尺的高空，命悬一线。那根连接着他衣袖和外套的线开始断裂！整个场景的焦点都集中在那根线上！它能撑到主人公把他拉上来吗？这就是悬念！


In my cable film “Hard Evidence” there is a scene where our businessman hero and his drug running girl friend have to cross a border with $4 million in cash and heroin in a suitcase. Now, this case is specially designed to pass through an ex-ray machine, but the minute a Customs Agent opens it, my hero is in jail for the rest of his life.

在我拍摄的电视电影《铁证如山》中，有一个场景是这样的：我们的商人主人公和他的毒贩女友必须带着装有400万美元现金和海洛因的行李箱过境。这个箱子是特制的，可以通过X光机安检，但海关人员一旦打开它，我的主人公就得终身监禁。


In the script, they fly into LA and go through the customs line at the airport. As they wait their turn, suspense builds. Someone in front of them has their luggage searched. Their bag gets closer and closer to the Customs Agent. Tension.

剧本中，他们飞抵洛杉矶，在机场排队过海关。等待的过程中，气氛逐渐紧张起来。前面有人被检查了行李，他们的行李也越来越靠近海关人员。紧张感不断升级。


Their turn. The Customs Agent examines the suitcase exterior and asks them questions. His fingers move to the latches... will he open it? The girlfriend makes a joke, the Customs Agent smiles, and passes them through without opening their luggage.

轮到他们了。海关人员检查了行李箱的外观，并询问了一些问题。他的手指移向了锁扣……他会打开吗？女友开了个玩笑，海关人员笑了笑，没有打开他们的行李就放他们过去了。


In a story conference, one of the producers wanted to change the location from the airport to a drive through check point.... they had a beautiful one they could get for the film. I argued: The focus of the scene needs to be the suitcase filled with drugs and money. If we drive a car through the checkpoint, the focus becomes the *car*. The Customs Agent will want to search the trunk, check to see if anything is hidden in the spare tire, and feel the seats for suspicious lumps. Sure, he might search the suitcase, but it's one of *several* items in his search, not the *focus* of his search.

在一次故事讨论会上，一位制片人想把拍摄地点从机场改成汽车安检站……他们正好有一个条件很好的安检站可以租。我反驳说：这场戏的重点应该是装满毒品和现金的行李箱。如果我们开车通过安检站，焦点就变成了*车*本身。海关人员会想搜查后备箱，检查备胎里有没有藏东西，还会摸摸座椅有没有可疑的凸起。当然，他可能会搜查行李箱，但那只是他要搜查的*几个*物品之一，而不是*重点*。


The producer ended up agreeing with me that the airport scenario was better than the check point, even if the location wasn't as exciting. The scene as written was focused and suspenseful.

制片人最终也同意我的看法，认为机场的场景比安检站的场景更好，即使地点不如安检站那么刺激。剧本里的那场戏节奏紧凑，悬念迭起。


“Transporter 3” has a big high concept focus object swiped from some other movie... one that starred Rutger Hauer, coincidentally! Our tough guy driver Frank (Jason Statham) and the girl he's transporting each have an explosive bracelet around their wrists - if they get 25 feet away from the car, the bomb is activated, 50 feet away from the car and the bomb is set to go off... and 75 feet away from the car? Blam! Frank is blown to a zillion pieces in a massive fireball and explosion. So, it's best not to leave the car. This leads to some great scenes - one where the car is stolen and Frank has to keep up with it and get it back, using a bicycle and anything else he can grab.

《玩命速递3》有一个非常吸引眼球的核心概念，它显然是从另一部电影里偷来的……巧合的是，那部电影的主演正是鲁特格尔·豪尔！我们的硬汉司机弗兰克（杰森·斯坦森饰）和他运送的女孩手腕上都戴着一个爆炸手环——如果他们离开汽车25英尺，炸弹就会启动；离开汽车50英尺，炸弹就会爆炸……而离开汽车75英尺？砰！弗兰克会被炸成碎片，在巨大的火球和爆炸中化为乌有。所以，最好不要离开汽车。这引出了一些精彩的场景——其中一场戏是汽车被偷了，弗兰克必须骑着自行车，利用一切可以找到的东西追回汽车。


But the director never shows us the danged bracelet in this chase - green you're okay, yellow at 25 feet, orange at 50 feet, red at 75 feet before you blow up. I want to know how much trouble Frank is in from minute to minute! They come up with this great suspense "focus object" and then never focus on it! No shots of it! Now, those "shots" may have been on the page or they may not have been - but *our* job is to make sure they *are* there. The action on the page includes milking that focus object for everything it's worth and making the scene a nail-biter of a read. We want to show that bracelet changing from green to yellow... and then changing from yellow to orange... then have Frank get close enough to the car that it goes back to yellow again. And keep that happening again and again throughout the scene. Once you create that focus object, it's your job to create the suspense that goes with it. If it ain't on the page, it ain't gonna be on the screen.

但导演在这场追逐戏里始终没给我们展示那该死的腕带——绿色表示安全，25英尺处变成黄色，50英尺处变成橙色，75英尺处变成红色，然后就会爆炸。我想知道弗兰克每分钟到底有多危险！他们想出了这么一个绝妙的悬念“焦点”，却从来不给它任何镜头！一个镜头都没有！当然，这些“镜头”可能出现在剧本里，也可能没有——但我们的任务是确保它们出现。剧本里的动作描写包括充分利用这个焦点，让整个场景扣人心弦。我们要展现腕带从绿色变成黄色……然后从黄色变成橙色……然后让弗兰克靠近汽车，腕带又变回黄色。让这个过程在整个场景中反复出现。一旦你创造了这个焦点，你的任务就是创造与之相符的悬念。如果剧本里没有，屏幕上也不会出现。


A great example of the focus object in a suspense scene is the wine cellar key in that famous scene from “Notorious”. Alicia (Ingrid Bergman) is a party girl who has been drafted by CIA Agent Devlin (Cary Grant) during World War 2 to spy on Nazi Alex Sebastian in Rio. Alicia and Devlin fall in love... and then they get their orders – Alicia is to *sleep with* Sebastian. This throws a monkey wrench into their relationship. Alicia ends up marrying Sebastian and as Mrs. Sebastian she has access to the keys to every room... except the wine cellar. Since one of the Nazis freaked at a wine bottle, Devlin is sure that is the key to whatever these Nazis are up to... and orders Alicia to steal the key. And this begins a sequence that is *all about that key*. She steals the key from Sebastian’s key ring while he is dressing for the party only a few feet away. She has the key in her hand - when Sebastian approaches her, grabs both of her hands! He tells her how much he loves her and lifts one of her hands, opens it... (the empty one, close call) and kisses her palm. Then goes to kiss the other hand... but Alicia pulls him into her arms so that he’ll forget about the hand with the key in it. Distracts him with some loving so he won’t find the stolen key. That scene comes before the party, where the key is the focus as Alicia palms it off to Devlin and eventually Sebastian realizes the key is missing from his ring when he and the butler go down to get some more champagne. That key is the center of focus for about 15 minutes of the film!

悬疑场景中焦点物的一个绝佳例子是电影《美人计》中著名的酒窖钥匙场景。艾丽西亚（英格丽·褒曼饰）是一位派对女王，二战期间被中央情报局特工德夫林（加里·格兰特饰）招募到里约热内卢监视纳粹分子亚历克斯·塞巴斯蒂安。艾丽西亚和德夫林坠入爱河……然后他们接到命令——艾丽西亚要和塞巴斯蒂安上床。这给他们的关系带来了巨大的冲击。艾丽西亚最终嫁给了塞巴斯蒂安，作为塞巴斯蒂安夫人，她可以拿到所有房间的钥匙……除了酒窖。由于一名纳粹分子对一个酒瓶反应过度，德夫林确信这把钥匙是揭开纳粹阴谋的关键……于是命令艾丽西亚偷走这把钥匙。接下来的剧情就完全围绕着这把钥匙展开。就在几步之遥，塞巴斯蒂安正在为派对盛装打扮时，艾丽西亚从他的钥匙串上偷走了钥匙。她手里拿着钥匙——塞巴斯蒂安走近她时，一把抓住她的双手！他告诉她自己有多爱她，然后抬起她的一只手，掰开……（那只手空着，好险），吻了吻她的手掌。接着他想吻另一只手……但艾丽西亚一把将他拉入怀中，让他忘记了手里拿着钥匙的那只手。她用温柔的爱抚分散他的注意力，让他找不到那把被偷走的钥匙。这一幕发生在派对之前，派对上，钥匙成了焦点。艾丽西亚把钥匙交给德夫林，最终塞巴斯蒂安和管家下楼去拿香槟时，才发现戒指上的钥匙不见了。这把钥匙在影片中占据了大约15分钟的篇幅！


Suspense is the backbone of any script, no matter what genre. Comedies, romances, science fiction, westerns, and of course Action Films. By using ticking clocks and cross cutting, you can keep those pages turning, and keep the audience glued to the edge of their seats between your action scenes.

无论什么类型，悬念都是剧本的灵魂。喜剧、爱情片、科幻片、西部片，当然还有动作片，都离不开它。通过运用时间紧迫感和交叉剪辑，你可以让读者欲罢不能，在动作戏的间隙，也能让观众屏息凝神，紧张不已。



#↩

SECRET SUCCESS

秘密成功


"It's a film with a secret." How often have we heard those words? When we hear them, don't we want to run right out to the theater, plunk down our $11, and find out what that secret is?

“这是一部藏着秘密的电影。”我们听过这句话多少次了？每当听到这句话，我们难道不想立刻冲到电影院，掏出11美元，看看这个秘密到底是什么吗？


When it comes to writing successful action screenplays, I've got a secret. Do you want to know what it is? Of course you do. Everyone loves finding out a secret. It makes us feel naughty and superior at the same time. You still want to know my secret? What if I *don't* tell you? Wouldn't you get angry?

说到写出成功的动作剧本，我有个秘诀。你想知道是什么吗？当然想知道。谁不喜欢发现秘密呢？这让我们既感到一丝刺激，又觉得自己高人一等。你还想知道我的秘诀吗？如果我*不*告诉你呢？你不会生气吗？


No need to worry. My secret is.... Secrets! I use them in my action scripts, and you can, too. From Batman to Bourne, all kinds of action screenplays use secrets. Secrets can be divided into Big Secrets, Little Secrets, and Character Secrets.

别担心。我的秘诀就是……秘密！我在动作剧本里运用秘密，你也可以。从蝙蝠侠到谍影重重，各种动作剧本都运用了秘密。秘密可以分为大秘密、小秘密和角色秘密。


#↩

BIG SECRETS

重大秘密


Big secrets are usually found in mystery films, but have been put to good use in such dramas as "Suddenly, Last Summer" and can be the “machine that drives the story” in an action film. The audience either knows about the secret, and is on the edge of their seat hoping no one will discover it; or are trying to discover what the secret is, given various hints and clues throughout the story.

悬疑片中通常会出现重大秘密，但《夏日惊魂》等剧情片也巧妙地运用了这些秘密，而秘密在动作片中更能成为推动剧情发展的关键。观众要么早已洞悉秘密，紧张地等待着它被揭开；要么在剧情中根据各种线索和暗示，努力寻找秘密的真相。


My favorite Big Secret is from Robert Towne's "Chinatown". Evelyn Mulwray is protecting her husband's alleged mistress. Why? There is some connection between the two women, and we spend much of the film wondering what it could be. Usually wives and mistresses don't much care for each other (with the exception of the two in "Diabolique"). The curiosity gets the best of detective Jake Gittes, and he forces Mrs. Mulwray into a confrontation.

我最喜欢的“大秘密”出自罗伯特·汤恩的《唐人街》。伊芙琳·穆尔雷包庇着她丈夫的所谓情妇。为什么？这两个女人之间似乎存在某种联系，而影片的大部分时间都在探讨这究竟是什么。通常来说，妻子和情妇之间并没有什么交集（除了《恶魔》中的那对）。好奇心驱使着侦探杰克·吉特斯，他迫使穆尔雷夫人与情妇对峙。


By this point, the audience is more than just curious. We know this is some huge deep dark dirty secret. We've been waiting the entire film to hear this. We know she is about to reveal the one thing she has never revealed to anyone. And we get to eavesdrop!

到了这个时候，观众的好奇心已经远远超过了单纯的好奇。我们知道这其中隐藏着一个惊天秘密，一个不可告人的秘密。整部电影里，我们都在等待着听到这个秘密。我们知道她即将揭露她从未向任何人透露过的秘密。而我们，竟然有机会偷听！


Evelyn admits that the mistress is her sister... And her daughter. That her father molested her and she had a child by him. This is a secret so shocking, audiences were talking about it months later. To be in on a secret this big is delicious!

伊芙琳承认情妇是她的妹妹……也是她的女儿。她承认自己曾被父亲性侵，并怀上了他的孩子。这个秘密如此惊人，几个月后观众们还在热议。能知道这么大的秘密真是太刺激了！


The reveal of this secret becomes the crescendo of the film.

这个秘密的揭晓成为了影片的高潮。


It becomes apparent on a second viewing, that the Big Secret is what has been driving this film almost from the beginning. The moment the mistress is introduced, the question on every character's mind is: Who is she? The quest for her identity becomes the focus of the script. With every scene, our curiosity grows more intense, until the final reveal.

二刷之后，你会发现，贯穿整部电影的“惊天秘密”几乎从一开始就在推动剧情发展。情妇一出场，每个角色心中就只有一个疑问：她是谁？寻找她的身份成了剧本的核心。随着剧情的推进，我们的好奇心也愈发强烈，直到最终揭晓。


A variation on the "Chinatown" Big Secret was used in Carl Franklin's "Devil In A Blue Dress". But the secret was not given enough power in this script. The film should have focused on the question: Why would a beautiful white society woman enjoy hanging out in the all-Black South Central Los Angeles? Then when that big reveal comes in act three, it would have the same impact as the reveal in "Chinatown".

卡尔·富兰克林的《蓝衣魔鬼》借鉴了《唐人街》的“大秘密”，但剧本并未充分展现这个秘密的震撼力。影片本应着重探讨这样一个问题：为什么一位美丽的白人上流社会女性会喜欢在全是黑人的洛杉矶南中心区闲逛？如此一来，当第三幕揭晓真相时，才能达到与《唐人街》中同样的震撼效果。


The secret of using Secrets is to come very close to revealing the secret (without doing so) several times within your script. To bring up the secret constantly. To ask the question "Why would a wife protect her husband's mistress?" or "Why would a white society woman hang out in a Black neighborhood?" Since you can't actually ask the question more than twice in your script, your character's *actions* must lead the audience to ask the question themselves.

运用“秘密”这个主题的秘诀在于，在剧本中多次巧妙地接近真相（但始终保持克制），不断地暗示这个秘密的存在。比如，提出诸如“妻子为何要包庇丈夫的情妇？”或“白人上流社会女性为何会出现在黑人社区？”之类的问题。由于剧本中你只能提出两次这样的问题，因此，角色的*行为*必须引导观众自行思考这些问题。


Evelyn Mulwray isn't curious about her husband's mistress, and actually pays Jake to forget about her. Later she hides the mistress. Most of Evelyn's *actions* in the film are aimed at keeping her relationship with the mistress a secret. Every time he lies to Jake about the mistress, we ask ourselves: "What does she have to hide?" The more you can get your audience to ask that question, the more impact the reveal will have upon them.

伊芙琳·穆尔雷对丈夫的情妇并不好奇，反而付钱让杰克忘记她。后来她还藏匿了情妇。影片中伊芙琳的大部分行为都是为了保守她与情妇关系的秘密。每当杰克对她隐瞒情妇的存在时，我们都会不禁自问：“她究竟有什么不可告人的秘密？” 你越能让观众产生这样的疑问，真相揭晓时带来的冲击力就越大。


Big Secrets may also be found in all of Tennessee Williams' Southern Gothic plays, like the aforementioned "Suddenly, Last Summer" which has a big secret which includes homosexuality, cannibalism, and private beaches. Though we may not have anything that extreme in an action screenplay, Big Secrets figure into everything from “The Dark Knight” to all of the “Bourne” movies.

在田纳西·威廉姆斯的所有南方哥特式戏剧中，都隐藏着巨大的秘密，例如前文提到的《夏日惊魂》，其中就包含着同性恋、食人以及私人海滩等惊天秘密。虽然动作片剧本中可能不会出现如此极端的情节，但从《黑暗骑士》到所有《谍影重重》系列电影，巨大的秘密几乎无处不在。


Superheroes like Batman and Spider-Man and Superman all have secret identities which play a role in the stories. One of the major plot threads in the overly-plotty “Dark Knight” has Batman's secret identity discovered by Wayne Enterprises accountant Coleman Reese. If this information gets into the hands of The Joker, he can bring down Batman and take over Gotham City. Except the Joker is all about chaos, so he puts a price on Reese's head and *everyone* in Gotham is gunning for the man. Now for Batman to protect his secret identity he must save the life of the man trying to reveal it... which creates a couple of big action scenes.

像蝙蝠侠、蜘蛛侠和超人这样的超级英雄都有秘密身份，这些身份在故事中扮演着重要角色。在剧情略显繁复的《黑暗骑士》中，一条重要的情节线索是韦恩企业的会计科尔曼·里斯发现了蝙蝠侠的秘密身份。如果这个信息落入小丑手中，他就能扳倒蝙蝠侠，统治哥谭市。然而，小丑生性混乱，他悬赏捉拿里斯，哥谭市的每个人都想置他于死地。为了保护自己的秘密身份，蝙蝠侠必须救下试图揭露真相的里斯……由此引发了几场精彩的动作戏。


One of several problems I had with “Spider-Man 2” was that, after spending the first film doing everything possible to protect his secret identity in order to protect the woman he loves from danger, in the second film he seems not to care at all about his secret identity – allowing pretty much the whole city to know who he is under the mask. That negates the whole reason for the funny costume in the first place and makes you wonder if he *wants* Mary Jane to be in danger! What's up with that?

我对《蜘蛛侠2》的诸多不满之一在于，第一部里他为了保护心爱的女人，竭尽全力地隐藏自己的真实身份，而到了第二部，他似乎完全不在乎了——几乎全城的人都知道面具下的人是谁。这完全否定了他当初穿那身滑稽服装的意义，也让人不禁怀疑他是不是*想*让玛丽·简身处险境！这到底是怎么回事？


But you don't have to wear tights to have a secret identity – in the opening of “The Bourne Supremacy” our amnesiac spy Jason Bourne and his girlfriend Marie are living in a quiet village in India as far away from the rest of the world as possible. They have a “secret identity” as just regular people, and have done almost everything to keep their true identity secret... when they are discovered by Russian Agent Kirill... who tries to kill both of them. Which leads to a big action scene and tragedy... and Bourne coming out of retirement to get revenge. Which means having his secret identity exposed is what gets him involved in the story. And like all of the Bourne movies, the story is also about a buried secret... which Bourne is now trying to uncover. The secret of his first assassination mission – which was so top secret it's not even recorded in any of the CIA or Treadstone's files. Whatever that first mission was is what drives the whole story – with both Bourne and Pamela Landy at the CIA trying to figure it out. Spy movies are usually *filled* with secrets, and often secrets are what drive the stories of *secret agents*.

但你不必穿紧身衣才能拥有秘密身份——在《谍影重重2》的开头，失忆的特工杰森·伯恩和他的女友玛丽隐居在印度一个与世隔绝的宁静村庄。他们伪装成普通人，竭尽全力保守真实身份的秘密……直到他们被俄罗斯特工基里尔发现……基里尔试图杀死他们。这引发了一场激烈的动作戏和悲剧……伯恩也因此重出江湖，展开复仇。这意味着，正是他秘密身份的暴露，让他卷入了这场故事。和所有伯恩系列电影一样，故事也围绕着一个被埋藏的秘密展开……而伯恩现在正试图揭开这个秘密。这个秘密与他第一次执行的暗杀任务有关——这项任务极其机密，甚至没有被记录在中央情报局或“绊脚石”行动的任何档案中。无论第一个任务是什么，它都推动着整个故事的发展——伯恩和中央情报局的帕梅拉·兰迪都在努力查明真相。间谍电影通常充满了秘密，而秘密往往是推动特工故事发展的关键。


Secrets are also part of the other characters in “Bourne Supremacy” - both Pamela Landy (Joan Allen) and Ward Abbott (Brian Cox) aren't the lead characters, they're both CIA Agents, but each is completely different. Landy is a digger - she'll do anything to uncover the secrets behind the Treadstone operations (even if it puts her career in peril). Ward wants to cover everything up - bury the past (and Treadstone) and get on with CIA business. These are two very different approaches to the same job... and they are also the two choices facing Jason Bourne. These two supporting characters are there to support the story - and are different aspects of the big decision Bourne must make in the story. Bourne can either hide from the secrets in his past or dig into his past and discover some more frightening secrets about who he was... maybe even who he is. So just as Bourne's character is all about secrets, so are Landy and Ward's characters. All are different aspects of how people deal with secrets. And all three are dealing with the one Big Secret that is driving the entire story.

秘密也是《谍影重重2》中其他角色的共同点——帕梅拉·兰迪（琼·艾伦饰）和沃德·阿博特（布莱恩·考克斯饰）虽然并非主角，但两人都是中情局特工，只是性格迥异。兰迪是个刨根问底的人，她会不惜一切代价揭开“绊脚石”行动背后的秘密（即便这会危及她的职业生涯）。沃德则想掩盖一切，埋葬过去（以及“绊脚石”行动），继续执行中情局的任务。这是两种截然不同的行事方式……也是杰森·伯恩面临的两种选择。这两个配角的存在是为了推动剧情发展，他们代表了伯恩必须做出的重大抉择的不同方面。伯恩可以选择逃避过去的秘密，也可以选择深入挖掘，发现更多关于他过去……甚至现在的可怕秘密。因此，正如伯恩这个角色本身就与秘密息息相关一样，兰迪和沃德这两个角色也同样如此。这三者都从不同角度展现了人们处理秘密的方式。而这三者都围绕着同一个推动整个故事发展的“大秘密”展开。


#↩

LITTLE SECRETS

小秘密


Little Secrets can take a bland scene and turn it into an intense, nail biting, edge of the seat experience. Where Big Secrets drive a story, Little Secrets drive a scene. A Little Secret is something, which if discovered, will place our protagonist in hot water. The audience is usually let in on the secret at the beginning of the scene, then we sit on the edge of our seats hoping that no discovers it.

小秘密能让平淡无奇的场景瞬间变得紧张刺激、扣人心弦。如果说大秘密推动剧情发展，那么小秘密则驱动场景推进。小秘密指的是一旦被发现，就会让主角陷入困境的事情。观众通常会在场景开始时得知这个秘密，然后便会屏息凝神，祈祷它永远不会被揭穿。


A great example of a Little Secret appears in Steven de Souza and Jeb Stuart's screenplay "Die Hard". John McClane is battling terrorists (lead by Hans Gruber) who have taken his wife Holly, sleazy businessman Ellis (and others) hostage in a high rise office building. If the terrorists learn the relationship between McClane and Holly, they will hurt her to get at McClane.

史蒂文·德·索萨和杰布·斯图尔特的剧本《虎胆龙威》中就有一个绝佳的“小秘密”例子。约翰·麦克莱恩正在与恐怖分子（由汉斯·格鲁伯领导）作战，恐怖分子将他的妻子霍莉、卑鄙的商人埃利斯（以及其他人）劫持在一栋高层办公楼里。如果恐怖分子得知麦克莱恩和霍莉的关系，他们就会伤害霍莉来对付麦克莱恩。


* * *


A VOICE comes over McClane's radio.

麦克莱恩的收音机里传来一个声音。


HANS VOICE

汉斯的声音

I have someone who wants to talk to you. A

有人想跟你谈谈。

Very Special Friend who was at the party

一位非常特别的朋友也参加了派对

with you tonight.

今晚和你在一起。


McClane's face falls. Oh, God. Eyes closed, he waits for the

麦克莱恩脸色沉了下来。哦，天哪。他闭上眼睛，等待着……

voice that tells him it's all over.

一个声音告诉他，一切都结束了。


VOICE

嗓音

Hello, Johnny Boy?

你好，约翰尼男孩？


McClane's eyes open, showing equal parts shock and hope.

麦克莱恩睁开双眼，脸上既有震惊又有希望。


IN THE OFFICE

在办公室

Camera adjusts to show ELLIS as Hans gives him the CB.

镜头调整，显示汉斯将CB交给埃利斯。


McCLANE

麦克莱恩

Ellis?

埃利斯？


Ellis has a cigarette, and a Terrorist brings him a diet coke.

埃利斯手里拿着一支烟，一名恐怖分子给他拿来一罐健怡可乐。


ELLIS

埃利斯

John, they're giving me a few minutes to

约翰，他们给我几分钟时间

try and talk some sense into you...

我试着跟你讲讲道理……


McCLANE

麦克莱恩

(carefully)

（小心）

Ellis, what have you told them?

埃利斯，你都跟他们说了些什么？


ELLIS

埃利斯

I told them that we're old friends and you

我告诉他们我们是老朋友，而你

were my guest at the party.

他们是我的派对客人。


McClane sighs, partially relieved.

麦克莱恩叹了口气，略感宽慰。

HANS, meanwhile, narrows his eyes.

与此同时，汉斯眯起了眼睛。


McCLANE

麦克莱恩

Ellis... you shouldn't be doing this...

埃利斯……你不应该这样做……


* * *


This scene builds suspense around the secret of John McClane's identity. The audience knows he is Holly's husband. That is his point of vulnerability. This secret must be hidden at all costs. See, even “Die Hard” is a movie about a guy with a secret identity!

这一幕围绕着约翰·麦克莱恩的真实身份营造了悬念。观众知道他是霍莉的丈夫，而这正是他的弱点。这个秘密必须不惜一切代价保守。瞧，就连《虎胆龙威》也是一部讲述一个拥有秘密身份的男人的电影！


When the scene begins, McClane and the audience think that Hans has discovered the secret. Then when Ellis speaks, we think Ellis may have told the secret. When we find that he hasn't told the secret, we begin to worry that the terrorists will *force* Ellis to tell the secret.

场景开始时，麦克莱恩和观众都以为汉斯发现了秘密。然后埃利斯开口说话，我们又觉得他可能已经泄露了秘密。但当我们发现他并没有泄露秘密时，我们开始担心恐怖分子会*强迫*埃利斯说出秘密。

Knowing that a secret exists is a partial reveal. Even if the terrorists completely believe Ellis (they don't) they will want to learn details about McClane. Each detail is a stumbling block, which may reveal the secret. Every word Ellis speaks is another step closer to Hans discovering that McClane is Holly's husband. Another step closer to Holly's torture or death.

知道秘密的存在本身就是一种部分揭露。即使恐怖分子完全相信埃利斯（他们不会），他们也会想要了解麦克莱恩的更多细节。每一个细节都是绊脚石，都可能最终揭开秘密。埃利斯说的每一句话都让汉斯离发现麦克莱恩是霍莉的丈夫更近一步，也让霍莉离遭受酷刑或死亡更近一步。


I used a Little Secret in my Made For Cable movie "Hard Evidence". A businessman is framed for murder, and realizes the only way out is to plant the murder gun and other evidence on the real killer.

我在为有线电视制作的电影《铁证如山》中使用了“小秘密”这个桥段。一个商人被陷害谋杀，他意识到唯一的出路就是把凶器和其他证据栽赃到真凶身上。


The murder evidence (and three quarters of a million dollars in blackmail money) are in a briefcase. As the businessman gets ready to meet the real killer (and plant the evidence) there's a knock at his door. The police Detective investigating the crime!

谋杀证据（以及75万美元的勒索款）都装在一个公文包里。正当商人准备与真凶见面（并栽赃陷害）时，有人敲门。是负责调查此案的警探！


Then a very tense scene occurs where the businessman is questioned by the Detective with the briefcase full of evidence sitting on a table between them. The Detective places his hands on the case several times in the scene. Once he even plays with the latches. Each time, you think he might discover the evidence and arrest the businessman.

接下来是一场气氛紧张的戏：侦探盘问商人，桌上放着装满证据的公文包。侦探在审问过程中多次将手放在公文包上，甚至有一次还摆弄了一下包扣。每一次，你都担心他会发现证据，逮捕商人。


What could have been a typical "Detective questions suspect" scene becomes an edge of the seat nail biter because of the inclusion of a secret. The audience wants to scream "Don't let him find that!" at the screen. This scene would have worked *without* the briefcase full of evidence, but adding that secret added suspense.

原本可能只是典型的“侦探审问嫌疑人”的场景，因为加入了一个秘密而变得扣人心弦。观众恨不得对着屏幕大喊“别让他发现那个！”。即使没有装满证据的公文包，这个场景也足够精彩，但正是这个秘密的加入，才让悬念更加浓烈。


In my Thriller Class on audio I talk about the film “Bedroom Window” where the police come to question our hero – who claims to have been alone when he witnessed a murder... but was actually sleeping with his boss's wife at the time, and *she* witnessed the murder. That's the secret he's trying to hide, the Big Secret that drives the story. But his apartment is littered with “little secrets” - all kinds of evidence that his boss's wife was there that night, from her cigarettes to various personal items that he can't explain if the police find them. The great thing about little secrets like this is that they can build a great deal of suspense... but cost the production nothing.

在我的音频惊悚课上，我谈到了电影《卧室之窗》。故事讲述的是，警察前来询问我们的主人公——他声称目睹谋杀案时独自一人……但实际上，案发时他正和老板的妻子睡觉，而她目睹了谋杀案。这就是他试图隐藏的秘密，也是推动剧情发展的关键所在。然而，他的公寓里却散落着许多“小秘密”——各种各样的证据都表明他老板的妻子当晚在场，从她的香烟到各种私人物品，如果被警察发现，他根本无法解释。这类小秘密的妙处在于，它们能够营造出极强的悬念……而且对制作成本几乎为零。


Little Secrets can also be used for comic effect. Watch any episode of "I Love Lucy" for an example. In every scene, Lucy is trying to hide a secret from Ricky, and comedy grows from the exaggerated lengths to which she goes in order to protect her secret. How many chocolates can you hide in your mouth?

小秘密也可以用来制造喜剧效果。看看《我爱露西》的任何一集就知道了。每一幕里，露西都试图对瑞奇隐瞒一个秘密，而她为了保守秘密所做的种种夸张举动，也正是喜剧效果的来源。你能把多少块巧克力藏在嘴里呢？


Including a Little Secret in almost every scene will create tension, suspense, (or comedy), and identification with the protagonist in your audience. The secret becomes the sub focus of the scene. A counter point to the dialogue, and a way to expose character.

几乎在每个场景中都加入一个小秘密，就能营造紧张、悬念（或喜剧效果），并让观众与主角产生共鸣。这个秘密会成为场景的次要焦点，与对话形成对比，并以此展现人物性格。


#↩

CHARACTER SECRETS

角色秘密


Character Secrets are the stuff Southern Gothics are made of. Dark, personal, family secrets which must remain hidden at all costs, only to be unleashed in a volcanic explosion of drama at the end. Though Character Secrets fuel the works of Tennessee Williams and Lillian Hellman, they need not be the stuff of explosive drama. Because what separates Character Secrets from Big Secrets is: Character Secrets need not be revealed in the script. They can remain secrets.

人物秘密是南方哥特式小说的精髓所在。这些黑暗的、个人的、家族的秘密必须不惜一切代价地隐藏起来，最终在结尾以火山爆发般的戏剧性方式被揭露。虽然人物秘密是田纳西·威廉姆斯和莉莲·海尔曼作品的驱动力，但它们并非一定要引发爆炸性的戏剧冲突。因为人物秘密与重大秘密的区别在于：人物秘密无需在剧本中揭示。它们可以永远保持秘密。


I am positive some are now asking, "What is the use of having a secret if it is not revealed? How will the audience ever know of its existence?"

我确信现在有些人会问：“如果秘密不被揭露，那拥有秘密有什么用？观众又怎么会知道它的存在呢？”

A secret helps define a character and create a sub-text for his or her actions. What we feel we have to hide from others tells us a lot about ourselves. Maintaining that secret will influence every choice we make. Every choice our characters make.

秘密有助于塑造人物形象，并为人物的行为赋予更深层次的含义。我们觉得必须对他人隐瞒的事情，其实反映了我们自身的很多特质。保守这个秘密会影响我们做出的每一个选择，也会影响我们笔下人物做出的每一个选择。


Let's say we have a businessman who inflates his resume in order to land a job. Now this businessman lives in fear that the lie on his resume will be exposed. He may lose his job. He also begins to see himself as a fraud.

假设有一位商人为了找到工作而夸大了自己的简历。现在，这位商人一直担心简历上的谎言会被揭穿，从而失去工作。他甚至开始觉得自己是个骗子。


Do others in his firm wonder why he seems to have less experience than his resume boasts? Do they begin to think of him as second rate? Will our businessman compensate for this by being overly punctual and bureaucratic? Or will he work extra hours in hopes that if his secret is discovered, his job performance will outshine it? Or does he become a delegator: Giving tasks which may expose his weakness/ secret to others? He may become the office paranoid, living in constant fear that others are trying for his title.

公司里的其他人是否会疑惑，为什么他的经验似乎不如简历上写的那样丰富？他们是否会开始认为他能力平庸？这位商人会不会通过过度守时和官僚主义来弥补这一点？或者他会加班加点，希望即使秘密被揭穿，也能用出色的工作表现来掩盖？又或者他会变成一个善于委派任务的人，把一些可能暴露自己弱点/秘密的任务交给别人？他可能会变得疑神疑鬼，时刻担心别人会觊觎他的职位。


Quite a lot of characterization choices from one fudged resume, eh? This secret shades what might have been a standard businessman, turning him into someone three dimensional and different. Someone with a secondary motivation in every scene. Hide the secret. Make sure no one discovers it.

一份造假的简历竟然能塑造出这么多人物形象，是吧？这个秘密让原本可能只是个普通商人的角色变得立体而独特。他每场戏里都有着更深层次的动机。务必保守这个秘密，确保无人知晓。


Before writing a script, I usually write a biography for each of my characters. Included are such mundane things as education, first love, worst job, pet words and phrases, and anything else which I may need to refer to while writing the script. But I also include the character's "dark secret", which may be anything from an inflated resume to something larger and more gothic like incest or murder. I usually don't reveal the dark secret in the script, but it tints the dialogue and actions of every scene that character plays in.

在写剧本之前，我通常会为每个角色写一份人物传记。传记里会包含一些琐碎的信息，比如教育背景、初恋、最糟糕的工作、常用语等等，以及任何我在写作过程中可能需要参考的内容。但我也会在传记里加入角色的“黑暗秘密”，这可能包括夸大的简历，也可能包括更骇人听闻的事件，比如乱伦或谋杀。我通常不会在剧本里直接揭露这个黑暗秘密，但它会影响到该角色出现的每一个场景的对话和行为。


Character Secrets don't have to be dark – look at Harry's secret in “True Lies” - he's a dashing, James Bond-like spy... who tells his wife he's a boring computer salesman.

角色的秘密不一定要很黑暗——看看《真实的谎言》中哈利的秘密——他是一个英俊潇洒、像詹姆斯·邦德一样的间谍……却告诉妻子他是一个无聊的电脑推销员。


#↩

SECRET SUSPENSE

秘密悬疑


Secrets are like little ticking time bombs, waiting to go off. Waiting to twist your tale into a new direction or fuel your characters to make dangerous decisions. Secrets are part of your life, and they should become an integral part of your character's lives. As was noted in Stephen Sondheim and Anthony Perkin's brilliant screenplay "The Last Of Sheila": "The harder you try to keep a secret in, the more it wants to get out."

秘密就像一颗颗定时炸弹，随时可能引爆。它们会扭转你的故事走向，或者驱使你的角色做出危险的决定。秘密是你生活的一部分，也应该成为你笔下人物生活中不可或缺的一部分。正如斯蒂芬·桑德海姆和安东尼·珀金斯在他们精彩的剧本《希拉之死》中所说：“你越是努力保守秘密，它就越想逃出来。”


If you have a secret, everybody wants to know what it is. If your script has a secret, the Producer will keep turning pages, hoping to discover it. Now it's a shared secret between you and the Producer. And the harder the Producer tries to keep the secret, the more he wants to spill it to the world. On screen. In Technicolor. So using secrets in your action script may be your secret weapon for success.

如果你有个秘密，人人都想知道是什么。如果你的剧本里藏着秘密，制片人会不停地翻页，希望能发现它。现在，这成了你和制片人之间的秘密。制片人越是努力保守秘密，就越想把它公之于众。在大银幕上，以绚丽的色彩呈现。所以，在你的动作剧本里巧妙地运用秘密，或许就是你成功的秘密武器。


I've got a secret...

我有个秘密……



#↩

SOMETHING EXTRA

额外的东西


The difference between a good action script and a great one is in the details. Think about your favorite action films – what made them special? A great action sequence? An amazing character? A great story idea? But what about all of the “secondary cool stuff” that elevates the film from standard action to memorable. I like to think of these “secondary cool things” as that something extra you give the audience – a *bonus* that they were not expecting.

优秀动作剧本和卓越动作剧本的区别就在于细节。想想你最喜欢的动作片——是什么让它们如此特别？精彩的动作场面？令人印象深刻的角色？绝妙的故事构思？但那些让影片从普通动作片升华到令人难忘的“幕后亮点”呢？我喜欢把这些“幕后亮点”看作是你给予观众的额外惊喜——一份他们意想不到的*额外福利*。


#↩

COOL DEVICES

酷设备


Here's a scene we have seen a million times before: The cops are outside the badguy's house, ready to break down the door. Guns ready, wearing bullet proof vests or riot gear. The cops always wonder what's behind that door. When they break it down, will they find an army of bad guys waiting to shoot them down? Will they find a mother and her child, and realize their informant has given them the wrong address? Or will they find their suspect alone and unarmed?

我们已经看过无数次这样的场景：警察在坏人家门外，准备破门而入。他们全副武装，身穿防弹背心或防暴装备。警察总是好奇门后究竟是什么。破门而入后，他们会发现一群坏人正等着把他们射杀吗？他们会发现一位母亲和她的孩子，然后意识到线人给了他们错误的地址吗？还是他们会发现嫌疑人独自一人，手无寸铁？


The question for the screenwriter is, How do we make this scene different that the thousands of other scenes exactly like it? This was answered in "Patriot Games" by giving the cops (and the audience) a little something extra. A neat device that amazed the audience. The police take a fiber optic strand and slide it under the door of the bad guy's flat. They twist the strand around until they have thoroughly reconnoitered the room. They know where every bad guy is, if he's armed, and what he's armed with. Once they have all of this knowledge, they crash open the door.

编剧面临的问题是：如何让这场戏与成千上万个类似的场景区分开来？《爱国者游戏》的答案是：给警察（以及观众）一些额外的惊喜。一个令观众惊叹的巧妙装置。警察拿出一根光纤，从坏人的公寓门缝下塞进去。他们转动光纤，彻底侦察了房间。他们知道每个坏人的位置、是否携带武器以及携带的武器种类。掌握了所有这些信息后，他们破门而入。


A neat idea. Something extra which makes this scene in "Patriot Games" different than all of the others. I don't know if this idea originated with Tom Clancy or the screenwriters, but I'm sure its genesis was in news reports about Doctors using fiber optic strands to recon the interior of the human body without major surgery. To transplant a device used in medicine to police work is genius at work.

真是个绝妙的主意。正是这一点让《爱国者游戏》中的这一幕与其他场景截然不同。我不知道这个想法是出自汤姆·克兰西之手还是编剧之手，但我确信它的灵感来源于新闻报道，报道中提到医生们利用光纤在无需大型手术的情况下探测人体内部。将医学领域的设备移植到警务工作中，真是天才之举。


In my HBO film “Crash Dive” I read Tom Clancy's research notes for “Hunt For Red October” published as “Submarine” before I wrote the screenplay, and was *looking* for interesting things on the submarine that I might use for another purpose. The two great finds – neither made it into the movie – were an emergency buoy that could be programmed to transmit a radio message and an infra-red viewing device for rescuing sailors in the event a smoky fire broke out in the submarine. The buoy was used by my hero Carter to get a message to Admiral Pendleton (Frederick Forest) after the terrorists had destroyed his short burst transmitter and were in control of the submarine's radios. The infra-red firefighting tool was used by the hero to see the position of the terrorists in another section of the submarine before he attacked – giving him an advantage. That cool bit was scrapped in favor of a cliché network of air ducts the hero could crawl through on the submarine. Um, no room for air ducts on a submarine. This is what happens when you tell director that it's “Die Hard on a submarine” - and they think that requires the hero in air ducts. But some of the cool things actually made it into the film by some miracle.

在我的HBO电影《潜水艇》（Crash Dive）中，我先阅读了汤姆·克兰西为《猎杀红色十月》（Hunt For Red October）所作的研究笔记，该笔记后来以《潜艇》（Submarine）为名出版。在创作剧本之前，我一直在寻找潜艇上一些有趣的东西，希望能找到可以用于其他用途的素材。其中两项重要的发现——可惜最终都没出现在电影里——分别是可编程发送无线电信号的紧急浮标，以及用于在潜艇发生烟雾火灾时营救水兵的红外探测设备。我的主人公卡特正是利用这个浮标，在恐怖分子摧毁了彭德尔顿海军上将（弗雷德里克·福雷斯特饰）的短脉冲发射器并控制了潜艇的无线电通讯后，向他发出了求救信号。而红外灭火设备则被主人公用来在发起攻击前，观察潜艇另一区域恐怖分子的位置，从而占据了先机。然而，这个精彩的桥段最终被舍弃了，取而代之的是潜艇上一个老套的通风管道网络，主人公可以爬进去探索。呃，潜艇上哪有地方装通风管道。这就是你跟导演说“这是潜艇版的《虎胆龙威》”的后果——他们居然觉得主角得躲在通风管道里。不过，有些很酷的镜头居然奇迹般地出现在了电影里。


One of the things I loved about “Face/Off” was the magnetic prison. Whenever there's a disturbance the guards just press a button and all of the prisoner's boots stick to the floor. Not a big thing, just a cool little thing in a scene. Come up with enough of those and you have a script that impresses the reader and eventually the viewer.

我最喜欢《变脸》的一点就是那个磁力监狱。每当发生骚乱，狱警只需按下一个按钮，所有囚犯的靴子就会吸附在地板上。这虽然不是什么大事，但却是场景中一个很酷的小细节。如果能多运用一些这样的小技巧，就能写出一个让读者印象深刻，最终也能打动观众的剧本。


Another cool thing in that movie is something to think about with both your heroes and you villains: character specific weapons. In an early scene with Castor Troy (Nicolas Cage) his brother has a cigar box that contains all of Troy's personal needs – from Chicklets gum to a pair of matched automatic pistols with gold and ivory grips. No one else in the history of film has guns like this!

这部电影里还有个很酷的地方，值得我们思考，无论是英雄还是反派：角色专属武器。在影片早期卡斯特·特洛伊（尼古拉斯·凯奇饰）的一个场景中，他的兄弟有一个雪茄盒，里面装着特洛伊的所有个人用品——从口香糖到一对配有金象牙握把的配套自动手枪。电影史上可没有其他人拥有过这样的枪！


One of the hot holiday gifts for 2011 is a new Mattel Hot Wheels car that comes with a built in digital camera that can film 12 minutes of video – and even has a video screen underneath to watch the footage and a USB cable so you can watch it on your laptop. If this is a *toy* you can buy for your kid, imagine the kind of gadgets the CIA has? But even if your Hero isn't a spy, he can hit Toys R Us on the way to the Villain's lair and pick up a portable spy camera that can zoom under a door and into a room to grab intelligence before being pulled back to safety with a piece of monofilament fishing line. How cool is that?

2011年最热门的节日礼物之一是一款美泰Hot Wheels玩具车，它内置数码相机，可以拍摄12分钟的视频——车底甚至还有一个屏幕，方便观看录像，还配有USB连接线，可以连接到笔记本电脑上播放。如果这都算是玩具，想想看，CIA（中央情报局）都用些什么高科技装备？就算你的小英雄不是间谍，他也可以顺路去玩具反斗城，买一个便携式间谍相机，可以钻到门缝下，伸进房间拍摄情报，然后用一根单丝鱼线把它拉回来。是不是很酷？


In my script “Down For The Count” my bodyguard hero has a pool table that flips over to expose an arsenal. I had a scene where he went to get a gun, and he could have just opened a drawer or a closet – but I wanted to give the audience a little something extra and came up with the pool table. We expect Bruce Wayne to have a secret stash of weapons because he's a superhero – but a regular guy?

在我的剧本《倒地不起》中，我的保镖英雄有一张可以翻转的台球桌，里面藏着一个军火库。我写了一个他去拿枪的场景，他本来可以直接打开抽屉或衣柜——但我想要给观众一些额外的惊喜，所以就想到了用台球桌。我们觉得布鲁斯·韦恩作为超级英雄，藏有秘密武器是理所当然的——但一个普通人呢？


One of the cool things about “Batman Begins” was how all of those corny Batman tools from the past became really cool Wayne Industries military equipment re-purposed. The “tumbler” Batmobile, the body armor that becomes the Batsuit, the paratrooper glider rig that allows him to “fly” and even looks like bat wings. A major part of why I liked “Batman Begins” was that they tool the silly things from Batman and found serious and logical ways they could exist... and when the Batmobile crashes in “The Dark Knight” and the Batcycle pops out moments before it self destructs? Something cool and extra!

《蝙蝠侠：侠影之谜》最酷的地方之一，就是它把过去那些老套的蝙蝠侠道具都改造成了威恩工业的炫酷军用装备。比如“翻斗车”蝙蝠车、变成蝙蝠战衣的盔甲、让他“飞行”的伞兵滑翔翼（外形甚至像蝙蝠翅膀）。我喜欢《蝙蝠侠：侠影之谜》的一个重要原因，就是他们把蝙蝠侠那些看似滑稽的道具，用严肃而合乎逻辑的方式赋予了它们存在的意义……还有《蝙蝠侠：黑暗骑士》里蝙蝠车坠毁，蝙蝠摩托在它自毁前一刻弹出的那段？真是既酷炫又精彩！


#↩

COOL ACTIONS

酷炫动作


Another neat idea popped up in Alan Sharp's "Rob Roy". Rob Roy has been captured by the army, under the command of his nemesis Archie. Hands tied, he is tethered to the back of a horse by about fifty feet of rope. No way to escape. He can only run fifty feet, before he reaches the end of his rope. We have seen "escape from the bad guys" scenes in a million films, but Alan Sharp treats us to something extra. When the Army stops at a bridge over a raging river, and Archie dismounts, Rob Roy quickly runs up to him, twists the tether line around his neck, then jumps off the bridge. The rope strangles Archie (forcing the army to rescue him) and breaks Rob Roy's fall into the river (dangling him a few feet from the surface). The only way the Army can save Archie from strangulation is to cut the rope... and free Rob Roy!

艾伦·夏普的《罗布·罗伊》中又出现了一个绝妙的创意。罗布·罗伊被他的死对头阿奇率领的军队俘虏了。他双手被绑，被一根大约五十英尺长的绳子拴在马背上。他根本无处可逃。他只能跑五十英尺，绳子就到头了。我们在无数电影里都见过“逃离坏人”的场景，但艾伦·夏普却给我们带来了一些惊喜。当军队在一条湍急的河流上的桥边停下，阿奇下马后，罗布·罗伊迅速跑到他跟前，把绳子缠在他的脖子上，然后纵身跳下桥。绳子勒住了阿奇的脖子（迫使军队去救他），也缓冲了罗布·罗伊落入河中的冲击力（让他悬在离水面几英尺的地方）。军队要想救阿奇，唯一的办法就是割断绳子……然后救出罗布·罗伊！


Of all the possible ways for Rob Roy to escape, this method gives us the most for our money. It was such a neat idea, that the audience I saw it with cheered. How clever! I wish that I had come up with that idea for one of my scripts.

罗布·罗伊逃脱的所有方法中，这种方法最物超所值。这真是个绝妙的主意，我看的那场戏里，观众都欢呼起来。太聪明了！真希望我当初也能想到这个点子，用在我的剧本里。


Though it couldn't save the film, one of the things I liked about the new version of “Conan The Barbarian” was when young Conan was allowed to participate in the “Warrior Test” with the older boys. He's about ten years old and the other boys are in their teens – young men – and Conan's father (the great Ron Perlman) gives each of them a bird's egg and has them run a mountain obstacle course. Those who return with their eggs unbroken can train to be warriors. The older boys take their eggs and run as Conan watches... then his father hands him an egg and asks “What are you waiting for?” Conan takes the egg and tries to catch up with the older boys. Part of the obstacle course ends up being the other boys – they do everything they can to smash their competition's eggs. But when they come across a group of enemy warriors preparing to attack the village, all of the other boys turn and run back home. Little Conan attacks. These enemy warriors roar like jungle beasts (cool idea) and fight little Conan. Later Conan returns to the village covered in blood... carrying the *heads* of the enemy warriors! He drops the heads on the ground before his father... then spits out the unbroken egg. That unbroken egg was fantastic! If only the rest of the film had been that clever!

虽然这没能挽救整部电影，但新版《野蛮人柯南》里我最喜欢的一点是，小柯南被允许和年纪稍大的男孩们一起参加“勇士试炼”。他当时大约十岁，而其他男孩都已是十几岁的少年——也就是年轻男子——柯南的父亲（由伟大的朗·普尔曼饰演）给他们每人一个鸟蛋，让他们跑一段山地障碍赛。那些带着完好无损的鸟蛋回来的人可以接受勇士训练。年纪稍大的男孩们拿着鸟蛋开始奔跑，柯南在一旁看着……然后他的父亲递给他一个鸟蛋，问：“你还在等什么？”柯南接过鸟蛋，试图追上年纪稍大的男孩们。障碍赛的一部分竟然是其他男孩——他们想尽一切办法砸碎对手的鸟蛋。但当他们遇到一群准备进攻村庄的敌军时，其他男孩都转身跑回了家。小柯南奋起反击。这些敌军像丛林野兽一样咆哮（这个设定很棒），与小柯南展开激战。后来，柯南浑身是血地回到了村子……手里还拿着敌军战士的头颅！他把头颅扔在父亲面前的地上……然后吐出了那枚完好无损的鸡蛋。那枚完好无损的鸡蛋真是太棒了！要是整部电影都能像这枚鸡蛋一样精彩就好了！


Always look for that something extra a character can do – especially if you have a scene that we have seen before.

永远要寻找角色可以做的额外事情——尤其是在你遇到我们以前见过的场景时。


#↩

COOL DIALOGUE

精彩对话


In Scott Rosenberg's "Things To Do In Denver When You're Dead", that little something extra is the bizarre slang the gangsters use. Instead of "Goodbye", they say "Boat Drinks". An old timer translates this for us: While in prison, convicts dream of drinking cocktails on a yacht when they get out. Hence "Boat Drinks", which is a variation on "Have a nice day". Weird slang peppers this script, from "Buckwheats" to "Give it a name", every line of dialogue giving the audience something extra.

在斯科特·罗森伯格的《死后在丹佛要做的事》中，最特别之处在于黑帮分子使用的那些古怪俚语。他们不说“再见”，而是说“游艇酒”。一位老家伙为我们解释道：囚犯在监狱里梦想着出狱后能在游艇上喝鸡尾酒。因此就有了“游艇酒”，这是“祝你今天愉快”的变体。从“荞麦”到“给它起个名字”，各种奇特的俚语贯穿整部剧本，每一句台词都给观众带来额外的惊喜。


Many writers are obsessed with using accurate slang, but slang evolves and changes. What's hip today may become passe. So why not invent your own slang? Why not create interesting phrases and contractions that are specific to the world your characters live in?

许多作家痴迷于使用准确的俚语，但俚语会不断发展变化。今天流行的俚语可能很快就会过时。那么，为什么不创造自己的俚语呢？为什么不创作一些有趣的短语和缩略语，让它们更贴合你笔下人物所处的世界呢？


What is the Lone Ranger's horse's name? What is the Green Hornet's car named? Another aspect of Cool Dialogue is to give things pet names – which gives them a personality. In the “Executioner “ novels by Don Pendleton the hero Mack Bolan carries a stainless steel 44 automatic named “Big Thunder” - isn't that more interesting than just carrying some generic gun? Nicknames – for people, cars, weapons, places, and everything else – can be a “something extra” in dialogue that can turn generics into cool specifics.

独行侠的马叫什么名字？青蜂侠的车叫什么名字？酷炫对话的另一个技巧是给事物起昵称——这能赋予它们个性。在唐·彭德尔顿的《刽子手》系列小说中，主人公麦克·博兰携带一把名为“大雷霆”的不锈钢.44口径自动手枪——这难道不比携带一把普通的枪更有趣吗？给人物、汽车、武器、地点以及其他一切事物起昵称，可以为对话增添“亮点”，将普通事物变成酷炫的特色。


#↩

COOL WORLDS

酷世界


Every script takes us into a world where the story takes place... where the audience will spend two hours of their lives. You can chose any world you want - the only limit is your imagination! So take us someplace cool! Take us behind the scenes someplace and show us how that world works. All of the cool stuff that makes the audience feel like insiders.

每个剧本都会带我们进入一个故事发生的奇幻世界……观众将在那里度过两个小时。你可以选择任何你想要的世界——唯一的限制就是你的想象力！所以，带我们去一个酷炫的地方吧！带我们去幕后探秘，看看那个世界是如何运作的。所有那些能让观众感觉自己身临其境的精彩内容。


At one point in my career I turned down adapting Dan Brown's “Angels & Demons” which takes us to places we have never been before - not only inside the Vatican and inside the Vatican politics of electing a new Pope, but also into the world of the Illuminati - that secret organization of rogue scientists what have been waging a top secret battle against the Catholic Church for hundreds of years. Even on Earth there are secret worlds where film has yet to take us - and Tom Hanks and his weird haircut was our tour guide for this one. We will not be going to any of the normal stops on the Vatican Tour, he's going to take us to all of the cool places that are strictly off limits - in fact, if you ask the Vatican these places don't even exist. But we're going to go there anyway – Cool!

在我职业生涯的某个阶段，我曾拒绝改编丹·布朗的《天使与魔鬼》。这部小说将带我们去往前从未涉足的地方——不仅包括梵蒂冈内部以及选举新教皇的政治运作，还包括光明会的世界——这个由叛逆科学家组成的秘密组织，数百年来一直在与天主教会进行着一场绝密的斗争。即使在地球上，也存在着电影尚未触及的秘密世界——而汤姆·汉克斯和他那奇特的发型，正是我们这次的向导。我们不会去梵蒂冈之旅的任何常规景点，他将带我们去所有那些绝对禁止入内的酷炫之地——事实上，如果你问梵蒂冈，他们会告诉你这些地方根本不存在。但我们还是要去——酷！


If your script is about armored truck guards, take us behind the scenes and show us the interesting details of their world. If your script is about Navy SEALS, show us how they live their lives and let us see the equipment they use and maybe takes us for drinks at McP's after the mission. If your story is about astronauts or professional killers or magicians or deep sea explorers – takes us into that world and let us live your character's lives vicartiously.

如果你的剧本是关于装甲车保安的，那就带我们走进幕后，展现他们世界中那些有趣的细节。如果你的剧本是关于海豹突击队的，那就展现他们的生活方式，让我们看看他们使用的装备，或许还可以安排他们在任务结束后去麦当劳喝一杯。如果你的故事是关于宇航员、职业杀手、魔术师或深海探险家——那就带我们进入他们的世界，让我们感同身受地体验他们的生活。


Though “Worlds” are usually the *Arena* for the story, they can also be locations like Rio de Janeiro. “Fast Five” did something interesting and avoided the tourist locations and luxury for the gritty slums. Though there have been films that took place in the favelas before, it is an interesting and unusual location... and part of what makes the film unique. “Winter's Bone” takes us into some backwoods version of hell populated by hillbilly gangsters who would rather kill you and dump you in the swamp than answer your questions. Both of these films give the audience a sort of travelogue of places you would probably not want to visit in real life... but in the safety of a cinema? Cool!

虽然“世界”通常是故事的“舞台”，但它们也可以指像里约热内卢这样的地点。《速度与激情5》做了一件很有意思的事，它避开了旅游景点和奢华场景，选择了破败的贫民窟。虽然之前也有电影以贫民窟为背景，但贫民窟仍然是一个有趣且不寻常的地点……这也是这部电影的独特之处。《冬天的骨头》则带我们进入了一个偏僻的“地狱”，那里居住着一群乡巴佬匪徒，他们宁愿杀了你，把你扔进沼泽，也不愿回答你的问题。这两部电影都为观众呈现了一幅你现实生活中可能并不想去的地方的“旅行画卷”……但在安全的电影院里？酷毙了！


Part of why we love movies is that we get to live other people's lives for two hours. I don't want to join the Navy, but I want to sit behind the stick of a F-14 fighter plane as a Top Gun pilot for a couple of hours and experience their world. The more details of that world you can show me, the more enjoyable my experience. In a strange way movies are a VR ride - the more detailed the world we create, the more the audience can immerse themselves in it. They more realistic the experience. So – what is the cool world your story takes place n?

我们喜欢电影的部分原因在于，我们可以体验别人的生活两个小时。我不想加入海军，但我很想坐在F-14战斗机的操纵杆后，像《壮志凌云》里的飞行员一样，体验几个小时，感受他们的世界。你展现的世界细节越多，我的体验就越精彩。从某种意义上说，电影就像虚拟现实体验——我们创造的世界越细致，观众就越能沉浸其中，体验也越真实。那么，你的故事发生在一个怎样的酷炫世界里呢？


#↩

CLEVER SOLUTIONS

巧妙的解决方案


There was a TV episode, I think from "Banacek" or “Mission Impossible”, where a ton of gold bullion is stolen from vault overnight. But how was it removed? Too heavy to lift, too bulky to get past the posted guards. Of all the various methods available, the screenwriter chose the one with something extra. The gold bricks were stacked against the back wall of the vault and painted brick red. They had never been removed from the vault, just disguised to look like the vault's back wall. Part of our job as writers is to amaze – just like a magician. If you can *reveal* something instead of just show it, that makes for a more interesting scene or solution. If we have a choice between the “normal” way to do something and the clever way – always go with the clever way! Use your creativity and imagination in every scene and situation.

我记得有一集电视剧，好像是《巴纳切克》或者《碟中谍》里的，讲的是一吨金条一夜之间从金库里被盗。但金条是怎么被搬走的呢？太重搬不动，体积太大也过不了守卫的关卡。编剧想了各种各样的办法，最后选了一个更有“惊喜”的。他把金砖堆在金库的后墙上，涂成了砖红色。这些金砖其实从未被搬出过金库，只是伪装成了金库的后墙。我们作为编剧，工作之一就是要让观众感到惊喜——就像魔术师一样。如果你能*揭示*一些东西，而不是仅仅展示它，那会让场景或解决方案更加精彩。如果要在“常规”方法和巧妙方法之间做出选择——永远选择巧妙的方法！在每一个场景和情境中，都要充分发挥你的创造力和想象力。


One of the best ways to separate your script from the thundering herd is to fill it with cool ideas, give every scene something extra. Go over your script scene by scene, and try to infuse each with something extra, either a neat device or a neat method. Whichever, it should be something we haven't seen before. Something which will have the audience talking about it long after the final credits have rolled. Now all we have to do is introduce our hero, and we're off to the shoot outs!

让你的剧本从众多平庸之作中脱颖而出的最佳方法之一，就是在剧本中注入酷炫的创意，让每个场景都别具一格。逐场审视你的剧本，尝试为每一场戏都注入一些新意，无论是巧妙的装置还是新颖的方法。无论是什么，都应该是前所未见的，是能让观众在片尾字幕结束后仍津津乐道的。现在，我们只需要介绍一下主角，就可以开始精彩的枪战了！



#↩

HERO INTRODUCTION

英雄介绍


In your screenplay, you don't just want your protagonist to walk into a room – you want to give them an introduction. One amazing scene where you introduce your lead character before they become involved in the plot full time. But the *better* method is to find a way to introduce the lead character as part of the story. The idea is to develop a great signature scene which sets the character up for the rest of the film.

在你的剧本里，你不想只是让主角走进房间——你需要给他一个正式的介绍。你可以设计一个精彩的场景，在主角正式加入剧情之前就介绍他/她。但更好的方法是，将主角融入到故事中。关键在于打造一个令人印象深刻的标志性场景，为角色在整部电影中的发展奠定基础。


In "The Ipcress File" (1965) we first see Harry Palmer as he wakes up in the morning and prepares for work. It is a simple scene which tells us *everything* we need to know about this character. He has to find his glasses before he can see the alarm clock. He grinds his own gourmet coffee beans, and uses a complicated coffee maker. He looks out his flat window while drinking his coffee. Later, he finds a woman's ear ring in his bed... while searching for his misplaced gun. And he leaves his apartment late for work.

在《伊普克雷斯档案》（1965）中，我们第一次看到哈里·帕尔默是在清晨醒来准备上班的场景。这是一个简单的场景，却向我们展现了关于这个角色的一切。他得先找到眼镜才能看到闹钟。他自己研磨精品咖啡豆，并使用一台复杂的咖啡机。他一边喝咖啡，一边望着窗外。后来，他在床上发现了一枚女士耳环……当时他正在寻找自己丢失的枪。最后，他上班迟到了。


All of the important elements of character we need to know about Harry Palmer is established in this scene... From here, the film whisks us away on an adventure. Though we don't need to know every single detail of the character after their introduction scene, we need to know enough about them to understand how they will react to the basic events of the story and what we might expect from them. If a character is introduced as a mild mannered computer programmer like Neo in “The Matrix”, we won't expect them to be a bad-ass martial arts expert in the very next scene. Even when a character is introduced out of their element as John McClane is in “Die Hard” there are some pretty strong hints that he's a bad-ass: they allow him to carry a gun on a plane! This isn't your normal nervous flier with an armload of stuffed animals for his kids. When the fishermen pull Jason Bourne out of the ocean, he has been shot several times and has a high tech gadget implanted in his body. Not just some tourist who fell off a cruise ship.
