Each team member should have a special talent or knowledge of some sort, to make them valuable to the team and more than just an extra set of hands. Each team member should have a special weapon of some sort – no two should have the same fighting skills. Each team member should speak differently, so that if you were to cover the character headings in dialogue, you could easily tell them apart just by speech patterns and pet words and phrases. Each team member must have a different look, so that you can tell them apart at a glance... we don't want to confuse two team members in the middle of that big Act Three shoot out!

听起来很难？更难的还在后面。每个队员都应该有自己的角色弧线或情感冲突——这些问题可能会在电影结尾得到解决（也可能不会）。每个队员都应该拥有某种特殊才能或知识，使他们对团队更有价值，而不仅仅是多了一双手。每个队员都应该拥有某种特殊武器——没有两个人的战斗技能是相同的。每个队员的说话方式都应该不同，这样即使你用对话遮住角色标题，也能仅凭说话模式和常用语轻松区分他们。每个队员的外貌也必须不同，这样你才能一眼认出他们……我们可不想在第三幕的大枪战中把两个队员搞混！


Doc Savage was a character in a series of a zillion pulp novels from the 1930s, about a team of adventurers who saved the world from a maniacal villain every month (mostly written by Lester Dent). He was the model for Superman (The Man Of Steel) and even had a Fortress Of Solitude and dozens of other things that ended up in the Superman comic books. Doc Savage, the "Man Of Bronze" was the team leader. Tall, muscular, good looking. Indiana Jones meets Ah-nuld with a little James Bond thrown in for good measure. They made a cheesy film in the 70s starring Ron Ely (who played Tarzan on TV) and at one point in time Frank Darabont was going to make a movie with Ah-nuld before he decided to run for Governator of California... I have the script somewhere.

“铁血博士”是上世纪30年代一系列通俗小说中的人物，讲述了一群冒险家每月拯救世界于一个疯狂反派之手的故事（大部分由莱斯特·丹特创作）。他是超人（钢铁之躯）的原型，甚至拥有一座“孤独堡垒”以及其他许多后来出现在超人漫画中的元素。“铁血博士”是这支队伍的领袖，身材高大，肌肉发达，英俊潇洒。他就像印第安纳·琼斯遇上阿诺·施瓦辛格，还带点詹姆斯·邦德的影子。70年代，他们拍了一部很烂的电影，由罗恩·伊利（电视剧《泰山》中的泰山扮演者）主演。弗兰克·达拉邦特一度打算和阿诺·施瓦辛格合作拍摄一部电影，但后来他决定竞选加州州长……我记得我好像还留着那份剧本。


Doc's five man team of "associates" were:

Doc的五人“助手”团队分别是：


Colonel John “Renny” Renwick: The world's top engineer. Over six feet tall. An ex-boxer with massive ham-sized fists who is always depressed and sees a cloud in every silver lining.

约翰·“雷尼”·伦威克上校：世界顶级工程师。身高超过六英尺。曾是拳击手，拥有像火腿一样粗壮的拳头，总是闷闷不乐，凡事都看不到一丝希望。


Major Thomas “Long Tom” Roberts: Electrical expert. The “physical weakling” of the group, but a fast draw with a gun... and an expert with canons.

托马斯·“长汤姆”·罗伯茨少校：电气专家。他是团队中“体格最弱的”，但拔枪速度极快……而且精通火炮。


Brigadier General Theodore Marley “Ham” Brooks: Harvard lawyer. Slender, handsome, quick moving. He never goes anywhere with out his razor sharp wit and razor tipped sword-cane. Urbane, witty – kind of a William Powell type.

准将西奥多·马利·“哈姆”·布鲁克斯：哈佛律师。身材修长，相貌英俊，行动敏捷。他总是带着他那犀利的智慧和一把尖锐的剑杖。举止文雅，风趣幽默——有点像威廉·鲍威尔那种类型。


Lieutenant Colonel Andrew Blodgett “Monk” Mayfair: Short, bald, hairy chested chemist and demolition expert. Lowbrow humor and earthy dialogue – the opposite of “Ham”, so they always end up paired together on missions. Remember, it's all about contrast!

安德鲁·布洛杰特·“蒙克”·梅菲尔中校：身材矮小，秃顶，胸毛浓密，是一位化学家兼爆破专家。他幽默低俗，对话粗犷——与“哈姆”截然相反，所以他们总是被安排在同一个任务组。记住，对比至关重要！


William Harper “Johnny” Littlejohn: Expert in geology and archeology. Wears a monocle and uses ten syllable words. Very thin. As a kid, this character sent me to the dictionary to decipher his dialogue on a regular basis. Remember, it's about distinctive dialogue!

威廉·哈珀·“约翰尼”·利特尔约翰：地质学和考古学专家。戴着单片眼镜，说话总是用十音节词。非常瘦。小时候，这个角色经常让我查字典才能听懂他的台词。记住，关键在于独特的对话！


Each one of these guys had his own special weapon, his own style of dialogue and his own special talent. Whenever they needed to get past an alarm system, Long Tom was there. Whenever they needed to MacGyver up an explosive device, Monk was there. When they came upon lost civilizations (they always did) Johnny was there. When they got hauled into court, or into a sword fight, Ham was there. If their plane crashed in the Arctic, you knew Renny could rebuild it and get them out of there before the polar bears attacked (they always did). This team worked out of the 86 th floor of the Empire State Building in New York and often under the cover of the “Hildago Trading Company”, and managed to fight a different super villain in a different exotic local in 181 novel-length stories published in Doc Savage Magazine between 1933-1949. I read them in their 70s Bantam paperback editions as a kid – and on the back of every book was a break down of the team and their special skills and unique weapons. The joy of reading them really was the characters – lots of jokes and banter and romantic rivalries.

他们每个人都有自己的特殊武器、独特的对话风格和独特的才能。每当他们需要突破警报系统时，长汤姆总会挺身而出。每当他们需要像麦克盖弗那样改造爆炸装置时，蒙克总会出手。每当他们遇到失落的文明（他们总是会遇到），约翰尼总会在场。每当他们被带上法庭或卷入剑斗时，哈姆总会挺身而出。如果他们的飞机在北极坠毁，你肯定知道雷尼能把它修好，并在北极熊袭击之前（北极熊总是会袭击）把他们救出来。这支队伍以纽约帝国大厦86层为据点，经常以“伊达尔戈贸易公司”的名义进行掩护，并在1933年至1949年间发表于《野蛮博士》杂志的181部小说篇幅的故事中，在不同的异域风情之地与不同的超级反派展开了战斗。我小时候读的是70年代Bantam出版社的平装版——每本书的封底都详细介绍了团队成员、他们的特殊技能和独特武器。读这些书的乐趣其实在于人物塑造——大量的笑话、斗嘴和浪漫的竞争关系。


And that's one of the important lessons about teams – it's all about the characters.

这就是关于团队的重要教训之一——一切都取决于团队成员的性格。


If you look at the team from my favorite of the new Team Effort flicks, “The Losers”, they also have distinctive personalities and dialogue and attitude and each has their own specific weapon and military specialty:

如果你看看我最喜欢的新团队合作电影《失败者联盟》，你会发现他们也都有鲜明的个性、对话和态度，而且每个人都有自己特定的武器和军事专长：

Clay played by Jeffrey Dean Morgan is the leader and planner – “Operational Control”.

杰弗里·迪恩·摩根饰演的克莱是领导者和策划者——“运营控制”。


Pooch played by Columbus Short is in charge of Transport and Heavy Weapons – the married guy whose wife is about to give birth when they get called on their mission.

由哥伦布·肖特饰演的普奇负责运输和重型武器——他已婚，妻子即将分娩，这时他们接到了执行任务的召唤。


Cougar played by Oscar Jaenada is an expert sniper (Long-Range Eliminations) and a man who few words who is never seen without his beat up cowboy hat.

奥斯卡·贾恩那达饰演的库格是一名技术精湛的狙击手（远程歼灭），他寡言少语，总是戴着他那顶破旧的牛仔帽。


Jensen played by Chris Evans in the Communications and Technical expert – and a hella fast runner. He's not the least bit brave, and usually ends up bantering with...

詹森由克里斯·埃文斯饰演，是一位通讯和技术专家，而且跑得飞快。他一点也不勇敢，经常和别人斗嘴……


Roque played by Idris Elba is Demolitions and Tactical expert... and as in many Team Efforts, he's the guy who switches sides. More on that coming up!

伊德里斯·艾尔巴饰演的罗克是爆破和战术专家……而且就像很多团队合作一样，他是个会倒戈的人。更多详情敬请期待！


Aisha played by Zoe Saldana who is kind of a femme fatale who ends up joining the team by the end, where she proves herself handy with a rocket launcher. Like with any good Team movie, she has an agenda that brings her into conflict with the team... but also has her falling into bed with Clay.

佐伊·索尔达娜饰演的艾莎是个有点蛇蝎美人的女子，最终加入了团队，并展现了她使用火箭筒的精湛技艺。就像所有优秀的团队电影一样，她也有自己的计划，这让她与团队产生了冲突……但也让她和克莱发生了关系。


Again, each character is a complete individual with different vocabularies and speech patterns and attitudes and looks and weapons and skills and everything else. One of the reasons why I liked this film more than “A Team” or “Basterds” is the distinctive characters. Because each was different than they other they could put them in a series of combinations, working together in pairs, and it was a different kind of fun. In my Dialogue Secrets Blue Book I look at ensemble comedies and how each of the Marx Brothers has a completely different type of comedy, so that there's something funny no matter what kind of sense of humor you have... and I think the same thing is the key to a great Team Effort script. You want different types of characters so that not only is each interesting individually, every time you pair two of them you get a different dynamic that is fun.

再次强调，每个角色都是一个完整的个体，拥有不同的词汇、说话方式、态度、外貌、武器、技能等等。我喜欢这部电影胜过《天龙特攻队》或《无耻混蛋》的原因之一就是它鲜明的角色。正因为每个角色都与众不同，所以可以让他们以各种组合方式进行搭档合作，从而产生一种别样的乐趣。在我的《对话秘籍蓝皮书》中，我探讨了群戏喜剧，以及马克斯兄弟各自截然不同的喜剧风格，这样无论你的幽默感如何，都能找到笑点……我认为，这正是优秀团队合作剧本的关键所在。你需要不同类型的角色，这样不仅每个角色本身都很有趣，而且每次两个角色搭档合作时，都会产生不同的互动，带来意想不到的乐趣。


#↩

INTRODUCTIONS

引言


In "The Professionals" (1966) Lee Marvin doesn't say, "we need another guy", he says: "What we really need is an equalizer. A dynamiter. A man with a delicate touch: to blow out a candle without putting a dent in the candle holder. And I know just the guy. He's not far from here...In jail." Burt Lancaster's character is introduced by his specific talent and weapon. Later we find out he's a well dressed romeo who can con his way into *any* woman's bed, and that he's had a few brushes with the law... he's currently shackled with a dozen other prisoners waiting to be taken to Yuma Prison for most of the rest of his life.

在1966年的电影《职业杀手》中，李·马文并没有说“我们需要另一个人”，而是说：“我们真正需要的是一个平衡者，一个炸弹，一个手法轻柔的人：吹灭蜡烛时不会在烛台上留下任何痕迹。我知道有这么一个人。他就在附近……在监狱里。”伯特·兰卡斯特饰演的角色以其独特的才能和武器出场。后来我们发现，他是一个衣着考究的情圣，能用花言巧语哄骗任何女人上床，而且他还有过几次违法记录……目前他和其他十几名囚犯一起被铐着，等待着被送往尤马监狱，在那里度过余生的大部分时光。


“The Professionals” introduces one character at a time, each in their own element. This method has been used in films like “The Andromeda Strain” where the scientists are shown in every day life when the crisis hits and each is scooped up by the military to work on the problem. This method allows us a moment of the character in their “natural habitat” before the action kicks in. A version of this was done in the heist movie “Tower Heist” - with each character introduced in their element before the story kicks in.

《职业特工队》采用逐一介绍角色的方式，让每个角色都置身于各自的生活环境中。这种手法也曾用于《安德洛墨达病毒》等影片中，影片展现了科学家们在危机爆发前的日常生活，随后他们被军方召集起来解决问题。这种手法让我们在剧情展开之前，得以一窥角色在其“自然栖息地”中的生活状态。类似的手法也出现在犯罪电影《高楼大劫案》中——每个角色都在故事正式开始前，以各自的方式被介绍出场。


Another method of introducing your team is what usually ends up the very next scene in those films, that big briefing room scene where the team ends up meeting each other. Movies like “Guns Of Navarone” and “Where Eagles Dare” use this method. The challenge in the briefing room is to find some small thing that each can do in the room to give us a hint at their skills... like catching a falling coffee cup in “Ronin”. These small things give us a hint at the big things that will come later.

另一种介绍团队成员的方法通常是电影中紧接着的场景——大型简报室场景，团队成员在此互相认识。像《纳瓦隆大炮》和《鹰狼突击队》这样的电影就采用了这种方法。简报室里的挑战在于找到一些每个人都能在房间里完成的小事，以此来暗示他们的技能……就像《浪人》里接住掉落的咖啡杯一样。这些小事预示着之后将会发生的大事。


I had a challenge in my HBO film "Crash Dive!" - I had to introduce some key members of the submarine crew who would become part of the hero's "team" later in the film. A US 688 submarine gets hijacked on the high seas and they think they can get one man onto the sub – so they pick retired Naval engineer and brainiac James Allen Carter. Once on the submarine he has crew members as a potential team, and there's a scene (not in the film) where Carter and Lisa Stark go over the profiles of every member of the submarine crew and come up with an onboard team – each with special skills and different weapons disciplines. These are Navy guys – so they are already trained for battle. One of the questions at this point in the script is: are the guys they select still alive? One key guy ends up dead by the time he gets on the sub (again, I'm not sure that made it all the way to the screen). But I wanted to give the audience a feel for their personalities and backgrounds - a way to like them – before they become those black & white photos on the dossiers spread on on Carter's kitchen table.

我在为HBO拍摄电影《冲锋陷阵！》时遇到了一个挑战——我必须介绍一些潜艇上的关键成员，他们会在影片后期成为主角的“团队”成员。一艘美国688号潜艇在公海上被劫持，劫持者认为可以找到一个人登上潜艇——于是他们选中了退休海军工程师兼天才詹姆斯·艾伦·卡特。卡特登上潜艇后，他可以挑选一些潜在的团队成员。剧本中有一个场景（电影里没有）是卡特和丽莎·斯塔克仔细研究了每位潜艇成员的资料，并组建了一支艇上团队——每个人都拥有特殊技能和不同的武器专长。这些人都是海军出身——所以他们已经接受过战斗训练。剧本此时的一个问题是：他们挑选的这些人还活着吗？其中一位关键人物在登上潜艇之前就已经牺牲了（我不确定这个情节最终是否出现在了电影里）。但我希望在他们变成卡特厨房桌子上摊开的档案中的黑白照片之前，让观众对他们的个性和背景有所了解——让他们喜欢上他们。


The problem was, I only had a page and a half to introduce the team before the sub hijacking began. How can you introduce six characters in a page and a half, and give the audience enough of their backstory to know them, be funny so that the audience likes them, yet not sound like exposition? I came up with this answer:

问题是，在潜艇劫持事件开始之前，我只有一页半的时间来介绍团队成员。如何在短短一页半的篇幅内介绍六个角色，既要让读者充分了解他们的背景故事，又要足够有趣让读者喜欢他们，同时还要避免显得像是在进行枯燥的解释？我想到了以下方法：


***

潜艇在水下巡航。

***


The sea shanty allowed each character to talk about themselves without sounding expositional. We know that Robison is a ladies man, that Murphy has self depreciating humor (he jokes about how ugly he is in his verse), that Collins is a "Hillbilly driver" which conjures up images of running moonshine, that Dent is religious, that Wager is willing to gamble, and shows us Block trying to escape the music. Since each gets his verse, the actor will get to use physical actions as well. Because the song had a punchline, the audience will laugh, and like these guys... I hoped.

这首海员小调让每个角色都能讲述自己的故事，而不会显得生硬突兀。我们知道罗宾逊是个风流成性的花花公子，墨菲有自嘲的幽默感（他在歌词里拿自己的丑陋开玩笑），柯林斯是个“乡巴佬司机”，这让人联想到私酿酒的运输，丹特是个虔诚的信徒，韦格喜欢赌博，而布洛克则试图逃离音乐的魔爪。由于每个人都有自己的歌词，演员们还可以运用肢体动作。因为这首歌有个笑点，观众会笑，就像这些家伙一样……我希望如此。


On the set, the film's director decided a song is a song... So he removed the sea shanty scene and substituted a rap number performed by extras who would not really be in the film again (except as crew members with numbers) and which did nothing to illuminate their characters. The critical members of the submarine's crew were *never introduced*. Hey, then they cut out the scene where Carter and Lisa talked about them while “assembling the team” from dossiers! We know nothing about them when the submarine is hijacked, and have trouble telling them apart. This was further complicated by bad casting choices which de-ethnicized the crew. Three of the actors cast look almost identical in crew cuts and uniform. How confusing!

在片场，导演觉得歌曲就是歌曲……于是他删掉了海员号子那段，换成了一段由群众演员表演的说唱，这些群众演员之后几乎不会再出现在电影里（除了作为带编号的船员），而且这段说唱对他们的角色塑造毫无帮助。潜艇上的关键船员*从未被介绍过*。更糟糕的是，他们还删掉了卡特和丽莎在根据档案“组建团队”时谈论这些船员的那段戏！潜艇被劫持时，我们对他们一无所知，甚至很难分辨他们。糟糕的选角更是雪上加霜，让船员们失去了民族特色。三个演员剪了寸头，穿着制服，看起来几乎一模一样。真是太让人困惑了！


Just as there are good guy teams, there are badguy teams – in “The Losers” and “The Expendables” and most of the others – and the same things hold true for them as well. Each of the terrorists in "Crash Dive!" was given their own weapon and their own point of view. My bad guy team. The female, Bolanne, wore a form fitting black suit with a bandoleer of throwing knives. One villain had a garrotte, another used a matched pair of pistols, a brutish ex-goatherd used a club and saw everything as "flock management". Each villain had a distinctive weapon, look, personality, attitude and world view. None of that made it into the film either! On film each of the terrorist is just a terrorist, and they all use the same kind of guns and speak the same and look the same and act the same. More confusion!

就像有正义的团队一样，也有邪恶的团队——比如《失败者联盟》和《敢死队》等等——同样的道理也适用于他们。《坠落！》中的每个恐怖分子都有自己的武器和独特的视角。我心目中的反派团队是这样的：女反派博兰妮身穿黑色紧身衣，腰间挎着一串飞刀；一个反派拿着绞索；另一个使用一对手枪；一个粗暴的前牧羊人挥舞着棍棒，把一切都看作是“羊群管理”。每个反派都有自己独特的武器、外貌、性格、态度和世界观。然而，这些在电影里统统都没有体现！在电影里，每个恐怖分子都只是恐怖分子，他们用的枪、说的话、长相、行为举止都一模一样。真是让人更加困惑！


#↩

ACCESSORIZING YOU TEAM

为您的团队提供配件


When you create your team members accentuate the differences between each team member. Is one a cowboy in western garb and another a flashy dresser in a $5,000 Italian suit? The cowboy will have different speech patterns than the clothes horse. The cowboy will listen to different music, have different points of reference, and use a different approach to problem solving than our man in Armani. Look at the guys in “The Losers” - all have distinctive looks and clothes and attitudes and everything else!

在创建团队成员时，要突出每个成员之间的差异。比如，一个是身着西部牛仔装束的牛仔，另一个是穿着价值 5000 美元意大利西装的时尚达人？牛仔的说话方式和时尚达人截然不同。牛仔听的音乐不同，看待事物的角度也不同，解决问题的方法也和穿着阿玛尼的时尚达人不一样。看看电影《失败者联盟》里的那些家伙——他们每个人都有着鲜明的个性、独特的穿着、独特的态度，以及其他各方面的特点！


On my HBO World Premiere "Steel Sharks" I had to create a Navy SEAL team which Admiral Billy Dee Williams would send deep into enemy territory via Gary Busey's submarine. The problem here: the entire team would be dressed in identical uniforms, and then put on camouflage face paint... How can we ever tell them apart?

在我的HBO全球首播剧集《钢铁鲨鱼》中，我需要设计一支海军海豹突击队，由比利·迪·威廉姆斯海军上将驾驶加里·布塞的潜艇深入敌后。问题是：所有队员都要穿一样的制服，脸上还要涂上迷彩油彩……我们怎么才能区分他们呢？


By "Accessorizing".

通过“配饰”。


Whenever you have five soldiers, five bank robbers, or five doctors who all will be dressed the same, it's important to give each one a little something to tell them apart. An accessory.

当你有五个士兵、五个银行劫匪或五个医生，他们都穿着同样的服装时，重要的是要给每个人一些区别开来的东西。比如配饰。


Let's take five bank robbers dressed in identical blue suits and ski masks. Which is which? Give one a boutonniere, another a gold crucifix, a third gets a stop watch on a lanyard around her neck, a fourth wears dark glasses *over* the ski mask, the fifth wears a red cowboy bandanna around her neck. Now the audience can tell them apart at a glance.

假设有五个银行劫匪，都穿着同样的蓝色西装，戴着滑雪面罩。你能分辨出谁是谁吗？给其中一个戴上胸花，另一个戴上金十字架，第三个脖子上挂着一条挂着秒表的绳子，第四个在滑雪面罩外面戴了一副墨镜，第五个脖子上系着一条红色牛仔头巾。现在观众一眼就能认出他们了。


Each "accessory" is also a way to show character. In "Steel Sharks" I had a deeply religious character who always wore a crucifix, touching it sometimes during the mission. It was his touchstone, a great way to show his character, and was a physical way to tell him from the other guys when they were all dressed alike. The tough, stern SEAL who would become the hero's mentor and surrogate father as the script progressed, wore a necklace of every bullet that ever hit him. This was a great symbol of the character's hardness, his invulnerability, and a way to instantly identify him. I had one of these "accessories" for each team member. A way to tell them apart and tell us about their character. The director didn't get it, and didn't use them. Try to tell these guys apart in the shoot outs now!

每件“配饰”也都是展现人物性格的一种方式。在《钢铁鲨鱼》中，我设计了一个虔诚的信徒，他总是佩戴着十字架，有时甚至在任务中触摸它。十字架是他的精神支柱，也是展现他性格的绝佳方式，同时还能在所有人都穿着统一服装时，让他与其他队员区分开来。随着剧情发展，那位强悍严厉的海豹突击队员将成为男主角的导师和代理父亲，他佩戴着一条项链，上面串着他曾经被击中的每一颗子弹。这象征着他坚韧不拔、刀枪不入，也让他一眼就能被认出来。我为每个队员都设计了这样一件“配饰”，既能区分他们，又能展现他们的性格。可惜导演没理解我的意思，也没有采用这些设计。现在，你试试看能在枪战中分辨出这些人！


The more alike the characters look or dress, the stronger the accessory must be. Our five bank robbers in ski masks require “big” interesting accessories. The SEAL team in uniform and camouflage make up require big accessories. When we don't have the instant visual reference point of clothing style or the face of the actor or anything else to tell characters apart, we need that something extra. Since you are giving each character that extra accessory, make sure it reveals character as well. And points for fun stuff like sun glasses over the ski mask.

角色外貌或穿着越相似，配饰就必须越醒目。我们五个戴着滑雪面罩的银行劫匪需要“醒目”的配饰。身着制服、化着迷彩妆的海豹突击队员也需要醒目的配饰。当我们无法通过服装风格、演员面容或其他任何视觉参照物来区分角色时，就需要一些额外的元素。既然你为每个角色都搭配了配饰，那就确保它也能展现角色的个性。像在滑雪面罩上戴太阳镜这样的趣味配饰也能加分。


#↩

CONTRAST DIFFERENCES

对比差异


Can not street this enough. All of your team members need to be different. They must have different strengths and weaknesses. Different 'looks'. Different personalities and ways of handling problems. Different "voices" and speech rhythms. The audience must be able to instantly tell one from another.

这一点我怎么强调都不为过。你的团队成员必须各不相同。他们必须拥有不同的优势和劣势，不同的外貌，不同的性格和解决问题的方式，不同的声音和语速。听众必须能够立即区分他们。


All of these things probably need to be planned out before you begin writing because if one of your characters is a Grand Prix racer, it'll probably change the outcome of your car chase if he's driving. Or create an interesting scene if he ends up in the backseat, and your fussy art expert is driving. A change in the outcome of the car chase is going to change *every* scene which comes after it. So plan ahead! Make up a list of character traits for each team member. Contrast each Team Member with the Hero, and make sure there's plenty of contrast between each Team Member and the other members of the team, too. The more similar they are, the more different they must be!

所有这些细节都需要在动笔之前规划好，因为如果你的角色中有一位一级方程式赛车手，那么由他来驾驶追车戏的结局很可能就会改变。或者，如果他最终坐在后座，而由你那位挑剔的艺术专家来驾驶，那也会创造出一个有趣的场景。追车戏结局的改变会影响到之后*每一个*场景。所以，一定要提前计划！为每个团队成员列出性格特征。将每个团队成员与主角进行对比，并确保每个团队成员之间也存在足够的差异。他们越相似，就越需要有差异！


The best way to bring out the different characters of your Team members is to pair them with the member who is *least* like them. In James Cameron's amazing “Aliens”, emotionally damaged survivor Ripley (Sigorney Weaver) is paired with steely calm Marine Hicks (Michael Biehn) which helps expose both characters. Ripley is the civilian, Hicks is the ultimate Marine - lots on contrast between the two. Ripley is scared, Hicks is always cool. We would never know that Hicks has a sense of humor if it weren't for his relationship with Ripley. Initially Hicks objects to taking Ripley along on the mission, but as the conflict intensifies, their relationship grows. A key moment is when Hicks shows her how to use the pulse rifle - Ripley has gone from baggage Hicks thought he'd have to carry to an equal. That's a *moment*!

展现团队成员不同性格的最佳方法是让他们与性格最不相符的成员搭档。在詹姆斯·卡梅隆的杰作《异形》中，情感受创的幸存者雷普利（西格妮·韦弗饰）与冷静沉着的陆战队员希克斯（迈克尔·比恩饰）搭档，这有助于展现两人的性格特点。雷普利是平民，希克斯是终极陆战队员——两人形成了鲜明的对比。雷普利胆怯，希克斯总是冷静沉着。如果不是通过他和雷普利的关系，我们永远不会知道希克斯也有幽默感。起初，希克斯反对带雷普利一起执行任务，但随着冲突的加剧，他们的关系也逐渐发展。一个关键时刻是希克斯教她如何使用脉冲步枪——雷普利从希克斯原本以为他必须背负的包袱，变成了与他并肩作战的伙伴。这真是一个令人难忘的时刻！


Hicks and Hudson are also paired in some scenes to show character. When they're introduced both are in uniform and almost impossible to tell apart ("Yes, Hicks?" "Hudson, sir. He's Hicks.") but when the conflict erupts we can see that these two are very different characters. Hicks is always cool and quiet, Hudson develops a motor-mouth when he's scared.

希克斯和哈德森在一些场景中被安排在一起，以展现他们的性格。两人初次登场时都身着制服，几乎难以区分（“是希克斯吗？”“是哈德森，长官。他就是希克斯。”），但当冲突爆发时，我们便能看出这两人截然不同的性格。希克斯总是冷静沉着，而哈德森在恐惧时则会变得滔滔不绝。


HUDSON

哈德逊

Well that's great! That's just

那太好了！真是太棒了！

fucking great, man. Now what the

太棒了，伙计。现在怎么办？

fuck are we supposed to do, man?

我们他妈的该怎么办？

We're in some pretty real shit now!

我们现在真的遇到大麻烦了！


HICKS

希克斯

Are you finished?

你做完了吗？


We can see how calm Hicks is by comparing him to how panicked Hudson is. They bring out the character in each other whenever they are together... so Cameron keeps throwing them together in scene after scene. We may not know anything about Hudson's life back on Earth, but his behavior creates a fully fleshed out character. We really know him. When he's screaming "Game over man! Game over!" we laugh - but we also feel his panic. We care about him. Both Hudson and Hicks are real people because we've learned about them as their relationship has developed over the course of the script.

我们可以通过对比希克斯的冷静和哈德森的惊慌失措来看出这一点。他们俩在一起时，彼此都能激发对方的性格……所以卡梅隆不断地让他们同框出现。我们或许对哈德森在地球上的生活一无所知，但他的行为塑造了一个血肉丰满的角色。我们真的了解他。当他大喊“游戏结束了！游戏结束了！”时，我们会笑——但我们也能感受到他的恐慌。我们关心他。哈德森和希克斯都是真实存在的人物，因为随着剧情的推进，他们的关系不断发展，我们也逐渐了解了他们。


But do we need to like the characters to care about them? The two most unlikable characters in “Aliens” are tough female Marine Vasquez and wimpy new Lieutenant Gorman ("How many drops is this for you, Lieutenant?" "Thirty-eight... simulated."). She's completely antagonistic, he's so pathetic it's hard to care about him. So Cameron sticks them together. They are opposites, and the contrast between the two brings their characters to the surface. Their relationship evolves throughout the script - hitting highs and lows. Nothing could be lower than when Gorman crashes the Armored Personnel Carrier - trapping them on the alien planet.

但我们真的需要喜欢这些角色才能关心他们吗？《异形》中最令人讨厌的两个角色分别是强悍的女海军陆战队员瓦斯奎兹和懦弱的新任中尉戈尔曼（“中尉，这要多少滴？”“三十八滴……模拟的。”）。她完全是反派，他则如此可怜，让人难以对他产生好感。于是卡梅隆把他们凑到了一起。他们是截然相反的两个人，正是这种对比将他们的性格刻画得淋漓尽致。他们的关系在剧本中不断发展，跌宕起伏。而最糟糕的莫过于戈尔曼驾驶装甲运兵车坠毁，将他们困在了外星星球上。


VASQUEZ

瓦斯奎兹

He's fucking dead!

他死透了！


She grabs Gorman by the collar, hauling him up roughly,

她揪住戈尔曼的衣领，粗暴地把他拽了起来。

ready to pulp him with her other fist.

她准备用另一只拳头把他打成肉泥。


VASQUEZ

瓦斯奎兹

Wake up pendejo! I'm gonna kill you,

醒醒吧，蠢货！我要杀了你！

you useless fuck!

你这个废物！


Hicks pushes her back. Right in her face.

希克斯一把将她推开，直接推到她脸上。


HICKS

希克斯

Hold it. Hold it. Back off right now.

等等，等等，立刻退后。


Vasquez releases Gorman. His head smacks the deck.

瓦斯奎兹放开了戈尔曼。戈尔曼的头重重地摔在了甲板上。


Vasquez is aggressive, Gorman is ineffective (mostly because he's unconscious in that scene). But the script keeps throwing the two together, and each brings out the character in the other. This pays off when Vasquez and Gorman are trapped in an air duct together as an army of alien warriors approaches. She gives him the "power greeting" she only shares with a chosen few to show her respect. Gorman returns the greeting and hands her two grenades, keeping two for himself. When the creatures descend upon them, the two who were once enemies die together... as friends. And we care about both of them - we've come to know them and even like them. All because these two *contrasting* team members were paired in scene after scene.

瓦斯奎兹性格强势，戈尔曼则显得有些无能（主要是因为那场戏里他昏迷不醒）。但剧本却不断地将两人安排在一起，而他们彼此激发出了对方的性格特质。当瓦斯奎兹和戈尔曼被困在通风管道里，面对即将到来的外星战士大军时，这种安排发挥了关键作用。她向他行了只对少数人才会行的“力量问候”，以示敬意。戈尔曼也回礼，并递给她两枚手榴弹，自己留了两枚。当那些生物向他们袭来时，这对曾经的敌人最终并肩而亡……以朋友的身份。我们关心着他们两人——我们了解了他们，甚至喜欢上了他们。这一切都源于这两个性格迥异的队友在一场又一场的戏中被安排在一起。


Once you've created your Team Members and made sure they have different personalities and different looks, make sure to pair up the most different members to bring their characters (and some great drama) to the surface.

创建好团队成员后，确保他们性格各异、外貌不同，务必将性格迥异的成员配对，以展现他们的个性（以及一些精彩的剧情）。


#↩

WEAPONS FOR WEIRDOS

怪人的武器


The very first movie I ever worked on was Paul Kyriazi's martial arts film "Weapons Of Death" (1982), which was made in my home town area while I was taking Film Appreciation courses in my local community college and dreaming of Hollywood. I think I was 18 years old.

我参与制作的第一部电影是保罗·基里亚齐执导的武术片《死亡武器》（1982年），这部电影是在我的家乡附近拍摄的。当时我正在当地的社区大学学习电影鉴赏课程，梦想着去好莱坞发展。我想我当时18岁。


Each team member in the film is given a specific weapon and a specific character arc. The story concerns the daughter of a wealthy family from San Francisco's Chinatown who is kidnapped by the Tongs. The girl's brother, played by Eric Lee, assembles a team to rescue her from among his karate class friends: David, the bow and arrow expert, has trouble shooting at live targets. Eric, the swordsman, was stomped by the lead hench in Act One. Josh, the lance expert, is opposed to killing. Paul, the gunslinger, is engaged to the girl the badguys have kidnapped. And Curt, who uses a Conan-sized broadsword is the girl's father... or maybe he isn't. Each team member has a moment of truth in the film, where they must confront their personal demons to survive.

影片中，每个队员都拥有专属武器和独特的角色弧光。故事讲述的是旧金山唐人街一位富裕家庭的女儿被帮派绑架。女孩的哥哥（由李铭顺饰演）从他的空手道课同学中组建了一支队伍去营救她：弓箭高手大卫，却连实弹都射不准；剑术高手埃里克在第一幕就被帮派头目踩在脚下；长矛高手乔什反对杀戮；枪手保罗与被绑架的女孩订婚；而使用一把堪比柯南的巨型阔剑的科特，则是女孩的父亲……或许并非如此。影片中，每个队员都将面临考验，他们必须直面内心的恐惧才能生存下去。


"Weapons Of Death" also uses a *Bad Guy Team*. A group of henchmen sent by the Villain to get the good guy team. Each member of the Bad Guy Team also has a special weapon and a special talent. This film is the most fun when it pairs off a Good Guy Team member with a lance against a Bad Guy Team member with a broadsword. There are dozens of fight styles and combinations you go through until the end of the film when each Good Guy Team member faces off against his Bad Guy Team counterpart: Two guys fighting with broadswords, or two guys in a high noon style pistol shootout. The different weapons – and combinations of weapons when one good guy fights one bad guy – is what makes this film fun.

《死亡武器》也运用了“反派小队”的概念。这是一群反派派来对付正义一方的喽啰。反派小队的每位成员都拥有特殊的武器和技能。这部电影最精彩的部分莫过于正义一方成员使用长矛对抗反派成员使用阔剑的对决。影片中展现了数十种不同的战斗风格和组合，直到结尾，正义一方的每一位成员都与自己的反派对手展开最终决战：两人挥舞阔剑，或者两人上演一场如同《正午》般的枪战。正是这些不同的武器——以及正反双方对决时武器的组合运用——让这部电影如此引人入胜。


Though the plot is a complete mess, this a fun film that has never been released on DVD expect in poor quality bootlegs of cut down TV versions. The original was beautifully shot anamorphic scope Panavision (ultra wide screen) on 35mm and deserves an actual video release. The head villain played by Gerald Okamura has co-starred in movies like “The Octagon” and “Big Trouble In Little China” and “G.I. Joe: Rise Of The Cobra” and is not only an expert fighting with weapons, he *creates* weapons for films and collectors and other martial arts masters. One of the great things in “Weapons Of Death” is his duffel bag of unusual weapons...

尽管剧情一团糟，但这部电影趣味十足，却从未发行过DVD，只有一些画质低劣的电视剪辑版盗版。原版采用35毫米胶片拍摄，画面精美，堪称变形宽银幕（Panavision），理应发行正规的录像带。片中由杰拉德·冈村饰演的大反派曾出演过《八角笼》、《妖魔大闹唐人街》和《特种部队：眼镜蛇的崛起》等影片，他不仅是一位武器格斗专家，还为电影、收藏家和其他武术大师打造武器。《死亡武器》的一大亮点就是他那装满奇特武器的旅行包……


So let's think about how we are going to arm our Team Members. We want each to specialize in a different weapons than the others, and have that weapon be some glimpse of their personality it possible. Like any prop, we want it to reflect character. Just for the heck of it, let's look at the team from “The Expendables” and see what sort of weapons each uses...

那么，我们来想想该如何为团队成员配备武器。我们希望每个人都能专精于不同的武器，并且如果可能的话，武器还能体现他们的个性。就像任何道具一样，我们希望它能反映人物性格。不妨参考一下《敢死队》中的团队成员，看看他们都使用什么样的武器……


Leader Barney Ross (Sylvester Stallone) has a pair of matching pistols.

巴尼·罗斯（西尔维斯特·史泰龙饰）首领有一对相同的双枪。

Lee Christmas (Jason Statham) is a blades specialist, knife thrower.

李·克里斯马斯（杰森·斯坦森饰）是一位刀术专家，擅长飞刀。

Yin Yang (Jet Li) is a martial arts expert (duh).

阴阳（李连杰）是一位武术专家（废话）。

Gunnar Jensen (Dolph Lundgren) is an ultra long range sniper.

冈纳·詹森（杜夫·龙格尔饰）是一名超远程狙击手。

Hale Caesar (Terry Crews) is an expert in heavy weapons.

黑尔·凯撒（特里·克鲁斯饰）是重型武器专家。

Toll Road (Randy Couture) is their demolition expert.

Toll Road（Randy Couture）是他们的拆除专家。


See how each specializes in a different weapon? Find the weapon that fits each character, and there are always extra points for unusual weapons and disciplines. I recently jokes that I want to see a character who *juggles* in one of these films. But just as Castor Troy has that matching set of gold and pearl handled automatics in “Face/Off”, you want to find one of a kind weapons for your characters if possible. If you can come up with a cool weapon for every member of both your good guy team and your bad guy team, every time they get into an action scene will be fun... before the fighting even begins!

看看每个角色都擅长哪些武器？找到适合每个角色的武器，而且不常见的武器和技能组合总能加分。我最近开玩笑说，我想在这些电影里看到一个会杂耍的角色。就像《变脸》里的卡斯特·特洛伊拥有那套金柄珍珠柄的自动手枪一样，你也应该尽可能为你的角色找到独一无二的武器。如果你能为正反两派的每个成员都设计出酷炫的武器，那么每次他们进入动作场景时，即使战斗还没开始，也会充满乐趣！


#↩

DETAILS, DETAILS

细节，细节


Another device which pops up in team efforts is the conflict within a team, which is part of the contrast we discussed earlier. Alastair MacLean novels (and the films made from them like "The Guns Of Navarone" and "Where Eagles Dare") always have tension and dissension within the team. From basic personality conflicts, to "one of us is a Nazi informer" subplots, conflict within a team keeps the scenes between car chases and shoot outs exciting, and adds another level of tension to the action scenes. Will Joe save Hal's life during the shoot out; when, in the preceding scene, Hal admitted that he'd slept with Joe's girl?

团队合作中另一个常见的元素是团队内部冲突，这也是我们之前讨论过的对比之一。阿拉斯泰尔·麦克林的小说（以及根据这些小说改编的电影，例如《纳瓦隆大炮》和《鹰狼突击队》）总是展现团队内部的紧张和分歧。从基本的性格冲突，到“我们之中有人是纳粹线人”之类的支线剧情，团队内部冲突让飙车和枪战之间的场景始终保持刺激，并为动作场面增添了另一层紧张感。在枪战中，乔会救哈尔的命吗？要知道，在前一场戏里，哈尔可是承认自己睡了乔的女友。


In "The Split" (1968) based on one of the Richard Stark novels by Don Westlake, a team of professional robbers are going to hit the LA Coliseum during a Rams playoff game. Tension in the team begins when a racist member played by Donald Sutherland locks horns with team leader Jim Brown (playing a version of Parker). Each team member, Gene Hackman, Julie Harris, Ernest Borgnine, and Warren Oates, must choose sides in this racial debate.

根据唐·韦斯特莱克的小说《分裂》（1968）改编的电影讲述了一伙职业劫匪计划在洛杉矶公羊队季后赛期间抢劫洛杉矶纪念体育馆的故事。团队内部的紧张关系始于唐纳德·萨瑟兰饰演的种族主义成员与团队领袖吉姆·布朗（饰演帕克的某种化身）之间的冲突。吉恩·哈克曼、朱莉·哈里斯、欧内斯特·博格宁和沃伦·奥茨等团队成员都必须在这场种族辩论中选择立场。


A better team heist film with racial undertones is Nelson Gidding's "Odds Against Tomorrow". Racist Robert Ryan gets teamed with Harry Belafonte for a heist and can't seem to set aside his prejudices long enough to pull the job. When the robbery falls apart, they are forced to work together to survive. "Odds Against Tomorrow" is a good example of how to incorporate a social message in a film which is also non-stop action. Just because we are blowing things up real good doesn't mean we can't also make a point at the same time. This is a great film with a fantastic jazz score, based on a novel by William P. McGivern who wrote a bunch of great action and thriller novels – many that have been turned into classic films.

尼尔森·吉丁执导的《明日之战》是一部更胜一筹的团队劫案电影，它带有种族隐喻。种族主义者罗伯特·瑞恩与哈里·贝拉方特搭档执行一项劫案，但他似乎始终无法放下偏见，最终导致行动失败。当抢劫计划失败后，他们被迫合作以求生存。《明日之战》很好地诠释了如何在一部动作场面精彩纷呈的电影中融入社会信息。即使影片充斥着爆炸场面，也不妨碍我们表达一些深刻的观点。这部电影配乐精彩绝伦，爵士乐也十分动听。它改编自威廉·P·麦吉弗恩的小说，麦吉弗恩创作了许多优秀的动作和惊悚小说，其中许多都被改编成了经典电影。

#↩

GOOD BAD GUYS, BAD GOOD GUYS

好坏人，坏好人

An extension of Team Conflicts is the *Good Bad Guy* and *Bad Good Guy* characters also found in MacLean films and books. In "Where Eagles Dare" we know that one of the good guys team is really a Nazi informer... But who? As the film plays out, we are given clues to the bad good guy's identity, but when it's finally revealed... it's still a good twist.

团队冲突的延伸体现在麦克莱恩的电影和小说中常见的“正邪双方”角色上。在《鹰狼突击队》中，我们知道正义一方的队员中有人是纳粹线人……但究竟是谁呢？随着剧情发展，我们逐渐获得线索，最终揭晓了这位“正邪双方”的身份，但即便如此，这仍然是一个精彩的反转。


For a textbook example of how to use good bad guys and bad good guys, read Robert Rostand's "The Killer Elite" – no relation to the recent Jason Statham movie. In this kick ass action book, three bodyguards are protecting an African Dignitary from three top assassins sent to kill him. But one of the assassins is providing anonymous tips to the good guys. And one of the three good guys is tipping off the bad guys. The resulting novel is filled with twists, turns, and thrill a minute action as our hero, Locken, tries to figure out which assassin he shouldn't kill, and which one of his two trusted sidekicks he should kill. This is one of my favorite action books, made into a film by Sam Peckinpah in the 70s... but got so mangled on the way to the screen that the film has as much to do with the book as that Jason Statham flick that swiped the title. Someone *really* needs to remake this and do a version that is 100% faithful to the book. Um, I would be interested in scripting. By the way – because everything is connected, the guy who made all of the cool weapons for the Peckinpah movie was... Gerald Okamura! He's also in the film with my friend Eric (“Little King Of Kata”) Lee!

想要学习如何巧妙运用亦正亦邪的角色，不妨读读罗伯特·罗斯丹的《杀手精英》（The Killer Elite）——与最近杰森·斯坦森主演的同名电影无关。在这部精彩刺激的动作小说中，三名保镖负责保护一位非洲政要，使其免遭三名顶级刺客的暗杀。然而，其中一名刺客却在匿名向保镖提供情报。而三名保镖中也有一人向刺客通风报信。小说情节跌宕起伏，扣人心弦，主人公洛肯必须设法弄清楚自己不该杀哪个刺客，以及应该杀掉自己两个得力助手中的哪一个。这部小说是我最喜欢的动作小说之一，萨姆·佩金帕在70年代将其改编成电影……但电影改编过程中被严重篡改，以至于它与原著的关联程度，几乎与那部盗用书名的杰森·斯坦森电影不相上下。真的*非常*需要有人重拍这部电影，拍一个百分百忠于原著的版本。嗯，我对编剧很感兴趣。顺便一提——因为一切都息息相关——为佩金帕电影制作所有炫酷武器的人是……杰拉德·冈村！他还和我朋友埃里克·李（《卡塔小国王》）一起出演了这部电影！


As I said at the beginning of this chapter, Teams fill the role of sidekicks... and that means someone is going to die! Either at the end of Act One or the end of Act Two (or both, if you have enough team members) one of the loyal, trusted, witty members of the team is probably going to get blown away. In “Guns Of Navarone” a team member is seriously injured in a mountain climbing accident – gets gangrene – and has to be left behind. In “Were Eagles Dare” one of the team dies when they parachute behind enemy lines... except he was shot! “The Expendables” did something interesting and had Dolph Lundgren's drug addiction take him out of the mission. But when you have a *team* you can usually afford to have a couple of them killed in combat, right?

正如我在本章开头所说，团队成员扮演的是配角的角色……这意味着总会有人牺牲！要么在第一幕结尾，要么在第二幕结尾（如果团队成员足够多，可能两者都有），团队中那些忠诚、值得信赖、机智幽默的成员很可能就会牺牲。在《纳瓦隆大炮》中，一名团队成员在登山事故中身负重伤——患上了坏疽——不得不被留下。在《鹰狼突击队》中，一名团队成员在空降敌后时牺牲……只不过他是被枪杀的！《敢死队》则做了一件有趣的事，让杜夫·龙格尔的毒瘾让他退出了任务。但是，当你拥有一个*团队*时，你通常可以承受几个成员在战斗中牺牲，对吧？


In "The Professionals" the team is forced to shoot their horses to avoid discovery by Raza's army. Robert Ryan is given the task, but can't harm the innocent animals... This leads to Burt Lancaster's capture and torture at the end of Act One. At the end of Act Two, Robert Ryan is wounded and the team must leave him behind to escape capture. Immediately after the team escapes, there is a silent "funeral" for Ryan... much like the one they held for Lancaster at the end of Act One.

在《职业特工队》中，为了避免被拉扎的军队发现，特工队被迫射杀他们的马匹。罗伯特·瑞恩被委派了这项任务，但他不忍心伤害这些无辜的动物……这导致伯特·兰卡斯特在第一幕结尾被捕并遭受酷刑。第二幕结尾，罗伯特·瑞恩受伤，特工队为了逃脱追捕不得不抛下他。特工队逃脱后，立即为瑞恩举行了一场无声的“葬礼”……就像他们在第一幕结尾为兰卡斯特举行的葬礼一样。


The funeral after a team member's death is a moment for the team to cast aside their differences and band together. It has the potential to be the most powerful moment of your film, the only time your macho action audience gets a little misty in the eyes. So milk it if you can! Make that funeral scene the most powerful scene in your script. Why? Because it's fun to see an audience of macho grown men cry. Team Efforts are difficult to write, but can be lots of fun when you get the banter going between the guys (or gals if you've seen the Hong Kong film “So Close”) and they seem to be popular with audiences as I write this. So maybe we will see Paul Thomas Anderson's “The Magnolia Team”?

团队成员去世后的葬礼，是他们放下分歧、团结一致的时刻。这有可能成为你电影中最感人至深的片段，也是你那些硬汉动作片观众唯一会眼眶湿润的时刻。所以，如果可以的话，一定要好好利用这个机会！让葬礼场景成为你剧本中最震撼人心的片段。为什么？因为看到一群硬汉落泪，真的很有意思。团队合作题材的电影很难写，但当你让男人们（或者如果你看过香港电影《如此接近》的话，也可以是女人们）之间展开精彩的对话时，就会变得非常有趣。而且，在我写这篇文章的时候，这类题材似乎很受观众欢迎。所以，我们或许会看到保罗·托马斯·安德森的《木兰花团队》？



#↩

PERSONAL INJURIES

人身伤害


Pop Quiz: Which hurts more: hitting your elbow on a door frame or getting blasted by a laser? The obvious answer is the laser blast, but it isn't the correct answer. If I were to show you a film clip where a man hit his elbow on a door frame, you'd go "ouch". You'd understand the pain and empathize with the man. But if I showed you a "Star Trek" clip where a laser dissolves a man, it wouldn't effect you. You've never been hit by a laser blast, you have no idea what it feels like.

小测验：肘部撞到门框更疼，还是被激光照射更疼？显而易见的答案是激光照射，但这并非正确答案。如果我给你看一段视频，一个男人肘部撞到门框，你会“哎哟”一声。你会体会到那种疼痛，并感同身受。但如果我给你看一段《星际迷航》的片段，激光把一个人溶解掉，你却不会有任何感觉。你从未被激光照射过，你根本不知道那是什么感觉。


We all know about the evils of abstracts. Mystery novelist and TV writer Joe Gores says in the Mystery Writer's Handbook, "Don't indulge in 'soft' writing. A street, means any street. A car, means any car. I want to see a specific street, a specific car. Hard detail is what makes a story believable." The same holds true for violence in our action scripts – the more specific, the more believable.

我们都知道抽象概念的弊端。悬疑小说家兼电视编剧乔·戈尔斯在《悬疑作家手册》中写道：“不要沉溺于‘软性’写作。一条街道，就是指任何一条街道。一辆车，就是指任何一辆车。我要看到的是一条具体的街道，一辆具体的车。具体的细节才能让故事可信。”同样的道理也适用于动作剧本中的暴力描写——越具体，就越可信。


You probably take special care when deciding whether your protagonist drives a sports car or a family sedan, if he wears tennis shoes or spats; but even specifics can be abstracts if the audience hasn't experienced them personally. The audience needs to feel the character's pain, and that means they need to be able to relate to it.

你或许会格外用心决定主角开的是跑车还是家用轿车，穿的是运动鞋还是绑腿鞋；但即便如此，如果观众没有亲身经历过，这些细节也会变得抽象。观众需要感受到角色的痛苦，这意味着他们需要能够感同身受。


Which takes us back to that laser gun. Even if you actually know how lasers work, create a brand name and specifications, fill in all the knobs and do-dads – create the *details*; the audience still won't understand the pain of your laser blastee. There are things we can relate to and things we can only imagine... and things that we have never experienced like a laser blast end up vague and ineffective.

这就引出了激光枪的话题。即便你真的了解激光的工作原理，设计了品牌名称和规格参数，把所有旋钮和小玩意儿都考虑周全——把*细节*都描述得淋漓尽致；观众仍然无法体会到被激光枪击中的痛苦。有些事我们能感同身受，有些事我们只能想象……而像激光枪击这种我们从未经历过的事情，最终只会显得模糊不清，毫无效果。


George Lucas figured out a way to by-pass this problem by creating 'light sabers', which are basically laser blades. They cut. We all know what it is like to get cut, don't we?

乔治·卢卡斯想出了一个绕过这个问题的办法，那就是创造“光剑”，它本质上就是激光刀刃。它们可以切割。我们都知道被割伤是什么感觉，不是吗？


#↩

VIOLENCE IS AS VIOLENCE DOES

暴力就是暴力的行为。


Using violence in your action script is meaningless unless your audience can feel it. Remember: film is communication. Your script must be designed to communicate with the audience (through the medium of the camera and the actors). The difference between effective violence and gratuitous violence is: Gratuitous violence isn't felt by the audience. It's just exploitation. Spurting blood and exploding heads. Who among us have had our heads explode? (If this *has* happened to you, please don't write me... I'd rather not know). When we see that guy's head explode in “Scanners” we don't go “Ouch”, we go “Cool” or “Gross” or some combination of both.

除非观众能感受到暴力，否则在动作剧本中使用暴力毫无意义。记住：电影是一种沟通方式。你的剧本必须旨在与观众沟通（通过镜头和演员）。有效暴力和无谓暴力的区别在于：无谓暴力无法让观众产生共鸣，它只是一种剥削。比如喷血和爆头。我们当中谁经历过爆头？（如果你经历过，请不要写信给我……我宁愿不知道。）当我们在《扫描者》中看到那个人的头爆开时，我们不会说“哎哟”，而是会说“酷”或“恶心”，或者两者兼而有之。


So violence needs to be personalized.

所以暴力行为需要个性化。


Here are three examples of action scenes which work because the audience understands the results of the violence:

以下三个动作场景之所以成功，是因为观众理解暴力行为的后果：


Steven deSouza and Jeb Stuart's "Die Hard" contains one of the most painful moments on film. John McClane is our barefoot hero, taking on a team of ruthless terrorists. Hans and Karl have cornered McClane in the Computer Room, and the three are involved in a shoot out

史蒂文·德索萨和杰布·斯图尔特的《虎胆龙威》包含了影史上最令人揪心的片段之一。约翰·麦克莱恩是我们的赤脚英雄，他要对抗一群冷酷无情的恐怖分子。汉斯和卡尔将麦克莱恩逼入了电脑室，三人随即展开枪战。


* * *


HANS

汉斯


looks at the glass all around him, gets and idea. He SHOUTS to

他环顾四周，看着周围的玻璃，突然想到一个主意。他大声喊道

Karl:

卡尔：


HANS

汉斯

The glass! Shoot the glass!

玻璃杯！射击玻璃杯！


And, saying this, he demonstrates. Karl follows suit.

说着，他做了个示范。卡尔也跟着做了。


McCLANE

麦克莱恩


As glass flies everywhere, McClane sees one option and takes it.

玻璃碎片四处飞溅，麦克莱恩看到一个选择，便毫不犹豫地选择了它。

BLASTING a burst to keep their heads down, he WHIRLS, JUMPS on

他猛地扫射，让他们低下头，然后转身，跳了上去。

top of a long counter and RUNS ACROSS THE ROOM. Their BULLETS

站在长柜台上，然后跑过房间。他们的子弹

follow him, six inches behind his moving form.

跟着他，跟在他移动的身后六英寸处。


McClane reaches the end of the counter, DIVES to the floor:

麦克莱恩跑到柜台尽头，纵身扑倒在地：


HIS FOOT

他的脚


goes right down on a jagged SHARD. He groans, keeps going.

他一头栽倒在一块锋利的碎片上。他呻吟着，继续往下走。


STAIRWELL DOOR

楼梯间门


He's out, gone, safe.

他已经出去了，安全了。


INT. BATHROOM - NIGHT

内景 浴室 - 夜晚


McClane all but crawls inside. His dragging foot leaving a trail

麦克莱恩几乎是爬进去的。他拖着的脚留下了一道痕迹。

of blood on the linoleum.

油毡地板上的血迹。


Wincing in pain, McClane washes his foot in a sink basin. He

麦克莱恩疼得龇牙咧嘴，在水槽里洗着脚。

washes a deep cut, but the pain doesn't relent.

清洗了一道很深的伤口，但疼痛并没有缓解。


* * *


When I was a kid, I was walking barefoot in my back yard and stepped on a nail. It went right through my foot. I'll bet, in your life, you once stepped on broken glass while barefoot or ,maybe broke a drinking glass and cut yourself picking up the pieces. It hurts. We know it hurts. When John McClane drags himself into the bathroom, we know *exactly* how he feels. The pain is real for us, more real than a shotgun blast. Strange isn't it?

小时候，我光着脚在后院走，一脚踩到钉子，钉子直接穿透了我的脚。我敢打赌，你这辈子肯定也光着脚踩过碎玻璃，或者打碎过玻璃杯，捡碎片的时候割伤过自己。很疼。我们都知道疼。当约翰·麦克莱恩拖着疲惫的身体走进浴室时，我们*完全*能体会到他的感受。这种疼痛对我们来说是真切的，比枪声还要真实。是不是很奇怪？


I already mentioned the scene in “Marathon Man” where the villain Szell tortures the hero with a dental drill – and that scene had the audience squirming in their seats because *we've been there* and we know what that feels like. Just revving up the dental drill puts us on edge.

我之前已经提到过《马拉松人》里反派塞尔用牙钻折磨英雄的那一幕——那一幕让观众坐立不安，因为我们都经历过类似的场景，我们知道那种感觉。光是听到牙钻启动的声音就足以让我们感到紧张。


My second example is from the classic Dean Riesner scripted "Play Misty For Me". Clint Eastwood is having a major ex- girlfriend problem: She is trying to kill him. With a knife. A very sharp knife. Do you know what “defense wounds” are?

我的第二个例子来自迪恩·里斯纳编剧的经典影片《迷雾追魂》。克林特·伊斯特伍德遇到了一个棘手的前女友问题：她想杀了他。用一把刀。一把非常锋利的刀。你知道什么是“防御性伤口”吗？


She attacks Clint with the knife, stabbing out at his face. Not wanting to get stabbed in the face, he catches the knife in his hand. Ouch! There's a close up shot of the blade slicing his fingers as he tries to hang onto it. Double ouch! Then she pulls the blade back, out of his hand, practically severing his fingers. Triple ouch!

她用刀袭击克林特，刀尖直指他的脸。克林特不想被刺中脸部，赶紧用手接住了刀。哎哟！镜头特写，刀刃划破了他的手指，他拼命想抓住刀。哎哟！接着她猛地抽回刀，刀刃从他手中滑落，几乎要将他的手指切断。哎哟！


How many of us have been chopping an onion or carrot and cut ourselves? Probably everyone. Again, we know *exactly* how being cut with a knife feels. When it happens on screen, part of the audience's brain flashes back to the time they were cut, and they instantly feel the pain.

我们当中有多少人切洋葱或胡萝卜时割伤过自己？可能每个人都有过这样的经历。我们都*非常清楚*被刀割伤是什么感觉。当这种场景出现在屏幕上时，观众的大脑会瞬间回想起自己被割伤的经历，并立刻感受到那种疼痛。


My last example is from a dark comedy film called "Swimming With Sharks" about a Personal Assistant who holds his mean spirited Boss hostage and metes out a strange revenge for on the job abuse. I've seen this film four times, and every time the audience jumps at one painful scene. Even though I know the scene is coming, it still affects me:

我最后一个例子来自一部名为《与鲨共泳》的黑色喜剧电影，讲述的是一位私人助理挟持了心肠歹毒的老板，并对他在工作中遭受的虐待进行了奇特的报复。我看过这部电影四遍，每次都会被某个令人揪心的场景吓一跳。即使我知道那个场景即将到来，它仍然会影响到我：


The Personal Assistant takes a crisp, clean, new piece of paper and slashes his Boss's face with paper cuts. Ouch! He also cuts his Boss's tongue with a sharp envelope flap. Ouch! This scene was worse for me than "Play Misty For Me". I work with paper and envelopes EVERY DAY. Paper cuts hurt worse than anything else on earth (including that nail in the foot). And a paper cut on your tongue? I've had one before. The pain stays for weeks! If you haven't seen "Swimming With Sharks", it's well worth a rent. Oh, and did I mention the Boss is a film producer?

私人助理拿起一张崭新干净的纸，用纸片划破了老板的脸。哎哟！他还用锋利的信封封口划破了老板的舌头。哎哟！这一幕比《迷雾追魂》还让我难受。我每天都要和纸张和信封打交道。纸片划破比世上任何东西都疼（包括脚上的钉子）。舌头被纸划破？我以前就被划过。那种疼痛会持续好几个星期！如果你还没看过《与鲨共泳》，强烈推荐租来看看。哦，对了，我有没有提到老板是个电影制片人？


The key to writing an effective action sequence is to make sure the violence is something the audience understands, and can empathize with. As B-Movie Maven Fred Olen Ray once asked me: "If a man is shot by a laser and falls down, is the laser on stun or kill? Is he hurt or dead?" We don't know, because we've never been shot by a laser.

写出精彩动作戏的关键在于确保暴力场面是观众能够理解并产生共鸣的。正如B级片大师弗雷德·奥伦·雷曾经问我的那样：“如果一个人被激光击中倒地，激光是造成眩晕还是致命？他是受伤还是死亡？”我们不得而知，因为我们从未被激光击中过。


#↩

PAIN IS IN THE DETAILS

痛苦藏在细节里。


Personalizing action/violence/pain means showing us the *details*. Details that we can understand. Say you have a plane crash survivor forced to search for help in a rocky terrain. He has been walking all day, and stops to take off his dress shoes. When he takes off his socks, we see the blisters on his feet. Big, painful blisters. Some have broken open, and when the air touches the nerve endings, our Survivor gasps in pain.

将行动/暴力/痛苦具象化意味着向我们展示*细节*。这些细节必须是我们能够理解的。假设你有一个飞机失事幸存者，被迫在崎岖的地形中寻找救援。他已经走了一整天，停下来脱掉皮鞋。当他脱掉袜子时，我们看到他脚上的水泡。又大又疼的水泡。有些水泡已经破裂，当空气接触到神经末梢时，我们的幸存者疼得倒吸一口凉气。


Anyone who has ever had new dress shoes knows how this feels. Because this is drama, we have *magnified* the injury and the pain. Taken it up a couple of notches. I already mentioned the back alley dentistry in “Marathon Man”, but the film has a few more painful moments we can all relate to – from drowning in a bathtub to a brilliant fight scene where an assassin with a garote tries to kill Roy Scheider – but he gets his hand up to stop the thin steel cord from cutting into his neck... except that means that it cuts into his *hand*. That's the beginning of a martial arts fight where every time Sheider throws a karate chop he rips his hand open more. Ouch! We have all cut out hands and know what it feels like.

凡是穿过新皮鞋的人都知道这种感觉。因为这是剧情片，所以我们把伤痛放大了好几倍，简直是雪上加霜。我之前已经提到过《马拉松人》里的黑诊所牙医，但这部电影里还有一些我们都能感同身受的痛苦瞬间——从溺死在浴缸里，到一场精彩的打斗戏：一个杀手用绞索试图杀死罗伊·施奈德，他抬起手挡住那根细钢丝，结果钢丝割破了他的手。接下来就是一场武打戏，施奈德每次使出空手道劈砍，都会让他的手伤得更重。哎哟！我们都割破过手，知道那种感觉。


Steven deSouza's "Commando" ends with an epic battle in the furnace room of a mansion. At one point, John Matrix's face is pressed against the furnace door. Sizzle! We know how that feels, from the time we lifted the pan without a pot holder. DeSouza has magnified the pain by making the furnace door red hot, and subject of the burn our hero's face. You know that's gotta hurt!

史蒂文·德索萨的《突击队员》以一场发生在豪宅锅炉房里的史诗级战斗结尾。其中有一幕，约翰·马特里克斯的脸被紧紧地贴在锅炉门上。嘶嘶！我们都知道那种感觉，就像我们自己没用隔热手套就直接拿起锅一样。德索萨把锅炉门烧得通红，让英雄的脸被烫伤，更加凸显了这种痛苦。你知道那肯定很疼！


“The Immortals” has a knife right through the foot... and then that foot gets stomped on! The knife goes straight through the hand in “Blood Simple”, pegging the evil private detective's hand to a window frame. Ouch! And then he has to pull out the knife to get away. Yech! In “Doomsday” our female version of Snake Plissken yanks on a chain connecting a nose ring to and ear ring in order to get some cooperation. If you like gladiator movies, you've seen films like “Spartacus” where sand is thrown into the eyes of an opponent. Have you ever had dust in your eyes? Or sand anywhere that it shouldn't have been? We can relate to these injuries because we've suffered something similar.

《诸神之战》里，一把刀直接刺穿了脚……然后那只脚还被踩了一脚！《血迷宫》里，刀子直接穿过手，把邪恶私家侦探的手钉在了窗框上。哎哟！然后他不得不拔出刀子才能逃脱。真恶心！《末日求生》里，女版的蛇蝎美人为了获得合作，拽着连接鼻环和耳环的链子。如果你喜欢角斗士电影，那你肯定看过像《斯巴达克斯》这样的电影，里面有向对手眼睛里撒沙子的场景。你有没有眼睛里进过灰尘？或者沙子进到不该进的地方？我们能感同身受这些伤痛，因为我们都经历过类似的事情。


When you are writing a fight scene, think of the detail. The personal injury which will make your audience gasp in identification. I like to have villains break my hero's fingers, either by crushing them or bending them backwards. We know that hurts. Did you know that a pistol barrel gets hot after firing? Hot enough to burn? When I have two characters struggling with a gun which keeps discharging, I like to add in the burn factor. Grab the barrel... sizzle... ouch! We may not have burned our hands on a gun barrel, but we've burned our hands on *something* hot before. We know exactly how it feels.

写打斗场面时，要注重细节。要描写那种能让观众感同身受、倒吸一口凉气的伤势。我喜欢让反派打断主角的手指，无论是直接捏碎还是掰弯。我们都知道那有多疼。你知道手枪枪管开火后会变得很烫吗？烫到能烫伤人？当两个角色争夺一把会走火的枪时，我喜欢加入烫伤的元素。抓住枪管……嘶嘶……哎哟！我们可能没被枪管烫伤过，但我们肯定被其他烫的东西烫过。我们完全明白那种感觉。


The shell casing from an automatic are also hot enough to burn, and I've had two men struggling over a gun with one purposely trying to spray his face with sizzling hot shells ejected from the gun. We know how it feels to have someone step on our foot really hard, to get something in our eye, to get a pavement scrape, to get salt in an open wound (never thought a salt shaker could be a torture device, did you?), to hit our thumb with a hammer, to hurt our knees and elbows and everything else that makes us scream in real life. These are the kinds of things to use in your action scenes to make them effective.

自动步枪的弹壳温度也高得足以灼伤人，我曾亲眼目睹两个人为了争夺一把枪扭打在一起，其中一个故意用滚烫的弹壳喷自己的脸。我们都知道被人狠狠踩一脚是什么感觉，眼睛里进了东西是什么感觉，被路面刮伤是什么感觉，伤口里撒盐是什么感觉（你肯定没想到盐瓶也能当刑具吧？），拇指被锤子砸到是什么感觉，膝盖和手肘受伤是什么感觉，以及其他所有在现实生活中让我们痛苦尖叫的事情。这些都是动作戏中可以用来增强效果的元素。


#↩

TOO MUCH VIOLENCE?

暴力场面太多了吗？


People often wonder how much violence is too much violence? And others don't wonder when they probably should... and then *you* wonder of they are psychos. The amount of violence in your screenplay and how graphic your descriptions are will rest on the tone of your screenplay. Comedians say it's not the joke, it's the delivery and Tone is the "delivery" of your script. The overall mood of the script. A comedy needs to be funny. But the tone of a script also influences what is acceptable in the story when it comes to violence.

人们常常纠结于暴力程度究竟该如何界定？有些人明明应该思考这个问题，却从未想过……然后你就会怀疑他们是不是心理变态。剧本中暴力的程度以及描写是否露骨，取决于剧本的整体基调。喜剧演员常说，重要的不是笑话本身，而是表演方式。而剧本的基调正是这种“表演方式”，它决定了剧本的整体氛围。喜剧需要搞笑，但剧本的基调也会影响故事中暴力场面的可接受程度。


Don Westlake wrote novels about professional thieves. The ones he wrote featuring Parker were violent crime novels (like “Point Blank”), the ones he wrote about Dortmunder were light comedies (like “The Hot Rock”). Both series have similar plots... in fact there's a strange cross-over novel (“Jimmy The Kid”) where the Dortmunder gang tries to replicate a Parker gang crime. The book alternates between chapters of Parker's violent version and Dortmunder's funny version of the exact same scene. We expect savage violence in the Parker novels, we don't expect to find scenes like that in the light-comedy Dortmunder stories. One series is dark and gritty and realistic, the other is fun and funny.

唐·韦斯特莱克创作了许多关于职业窃贼的小说。他笔下的帕克系列是暴力犯罪小说（例如《步步惊魂》），而多特蒙德系列则是轻松喜剧（例如《热石》）。这两个系列的情节颇为相似……事实上，还有一部奇特的跨界小说（《小子吉米》），讲述的是多特蒙德团伙试图模仿帕克团伙的犯罪行为。这本书的章节交替呈现，帕克的暴力版本和多特蒙德的滑稽版本讲述的是同一场景。我们期待在帕克系列小说中看到残酷的暴力，却不希望在轻松喜剧风格的多特蒙德故事中看到类似的场景。一个系列黑暗、残酷、写实，另一个系列则轻松有趣。


Both "The Wild Bunch" and "Butch Cassidy And The Sundance Kid" have the same plot, the same characters, the same end, many of the same scenes... but much different "tones". One is a very violent action story, the other is a buddy movie (light comedy). “The Wild Bunch” ends with the gang being shot to pieces in slow motion with blood spurting and guts spraying... “Butch Cassidy And The Sundance Kid” ends with the gang running out to face an army... and we freeze frame. Though they probably get shot to pieces as well, the tone of the film prohibits the story from showing it. “The Wild Bunch” has a gang member get his face shot off with a shotgun – and live! His face a bloody mess of meat. “Butch Cassidy” has a gang member get kicked in the groin and double over in pain... while the audience laughs. You could not transpose those scenes without alienating the audience.

《野战群》和《虎豹小霸王》情节相同，人物相同，结局相同，许多场景也相同……但“基调”却截然不同。一部是暴力动作片，另一部是轻松喜剧。《野战群》的结尾是帮派成员被慢镜头枪杀，鲜血四溅，内脏横飞……《虎豹小霸王》的结尾是帮派成员冲出去迎战军队……然后画面定格。虽然他们可能也被枪杀了，但影片的基调不允许展现这一幕。《野战群》中，一个帮派成员被霰弹枪打爆了脸——但他活了下来！他的脸血肉模糊。《虎豹小霸王》中，一个帮派成员被踢中腹股沟，痛苦地弯下腰……而观众却在大笑。如果把这两个场景互换，肯定会让观众感到不适。


Tone controls the level of reality in your screenplay, and that extends to the level of violence as well. So take tone into consideration when you are deciding if this scene is too violent or not violent enough... or just right.

剧本的基调决定了其真实程度，也包括暴力程度。因此，在决定某个场景是否过于暴力、不够暴力，或者恰到好处时，务必考虑基调因素。


Tone also give you a clue to what's expected on the page – how much detail you should go into when you are writing the violence. A gross and gory detailed description of a head exploding when a shotgun blast hit is will be out of place in “Butch Cassidy”, but might fit well in “The Wild Bunch”. Remember that usually less is more – and even if you are writing something with the savage tone of “The Wild Bunch”.

语气也能让你了解读者对文本的预期——比如在描写暴力时应该注重多少细节。在《虎豹小霸王》中，对霰弹枪击中头部后爆裂的血腥暴力描写会显得格格不入，但在《野战群》中可能就非常合适。记住，通常情况下，少即是多——即使你写的是像《野战群》那样充满野蛮气息的作品。


If *every* violent scene is super graphic and filled with lots of detailed descriptions of blood and guts and severed limbs and peeling flesh and... well, that may be a problem for two reasons: maybe you've got too much detail in your description and maybe some people will wonder if you like blood and guts so much that you might not be pleasant to work with. You know - maybe *you* are the psycho killer. You want evocative descriptions, but you don't want the reader to blow chunks all over your script. Plus, if every scene is really violent, it tends to lose its impact. The fingers getting blown off in “Taxi Driver” is a shocking violent moment because few scenes have been violent up to that point. If you want your violence to stand out, it can't be the norm.

如果*每一个*暴力场景都极其血腥，充斥着对鲜血、内脏、断肢、血肉撕裂等细节的描写……嗯，这可能会带来两个问题：一是你的描写过于细致，二是有些人可能会怀疑你是不是太喜欢血腥暴力，以至于难以相处。你知道吗——说不定*你*就是那个变态杀手。你想要生动的描写，但你也不想让读者对着你的剧本吐口水。此外，如果每个场景都过于暴力，就会削弱其冲击力。《出租车司机》中手指被炸断的场景之所以令人震惊，是因为在此之前几乎没有其他暴力场景。如果你想让你的暴力场面脱颖而出，就不能让它成为常态。


#↩

WHEN YOU WANT TO HURT THE WORLD

当你想要伤害世界的时候


Your villain has spent his entire life hurting people one by one, and now he's ready to move on to world destruction and/or domination. He wants to blow up Cleveland or wipe out his enemies' family lines. How do you make such massive destruction personal? There are two ways to make big action effective on screen.

你的反派一生都在残害他人，如今他准备将目标转向毁灭世界甚至统治世界。他想炸毁克利夫兰，或者彻底铲除敌人的家族血脉。如何才能让如此大规模的破坏显得更具个人色彩？有两种方法可以让大型动作场面在银幕上更具冲击力。


ONE: Make sure your protagonist has a stake in the outcome, and make sure the audience's identification with your protagonist is *very* strong. A good example is Donald Stewart and W. Peter Iliff's "Patriot Games". We are introduced to family man Harrison Ford, his wife and daughter. We learn to care about them as a family. When Ford steps in to thwart a terrorist bombing, not only do the terrorist come after him, they come after his family as well. Ford must stop the Terrorists, because he and his family are directly threatened.

第一：确保你的主角与结局息息相关，并确保观众对主角的认同感*非常*强烈。唐纳德·斯图尔特和W·彼得·伊利夫执导的《爱国者游戏》就是一个很好的例子。影片向我们介绍了哈里森·福特饰演的顾家男人，他的妻子和女儿。我们逐渐对他们一家人产生了感情。当福特挺身而出阻止恐怖袭击时，恐怖分子不仅追杀他，还盯上了他的家人。福特必须阻止恐怖分子，因为他和他的家人都受到了直接威胁。


“Taken” also fits the *personal stakes* scenario – they are taking his child. But usually when you are dealing with some world destruction scenario it's not a kidnapping, but a loved one who is in harm's way. Though the Villain in “Deep Impact” is a comet hurtling towards Earth, the Tea Leone character's father will be killed – and that's her stake in the conflict. If you can find a way to put your hero's loved ones in harm's way as a result of the Villain's Plan for world destruction, it gives the Hero even more reason to stop him.

《劫持》也符合“个人利害关系”的设定——他们要带走他的孩子。但通常情况下，当涉及到世界末日之类的场景时，并非是绑架，而是挚爱之人身处险境。虽然《天地大冲撞》中的反派是一颗冲向地球的彗星，但蒂娅·里昂饰演的角色的父亲将会丧命——这就是她在这场冲突中的利害关系。如果你能找到一种方法，让英雄的挚爱之人因为反派毁灭世界的计划而身处险境，就能让英雄更有理由阻止他。


If your villain is killing a bunch of people you don't know, or don't care about, it is meaningless violence. Giving a spear-carrier a scene where he is kind to small animals before he is killed just doesn't cut it. Audiences see it coming from a mile away. Is there anyone in the world who saw "Top Gun" and didn't *know* Goose was about to die after they suddenly introduce his wife and family halfway through the film?

如果你的反派杀害的是一群你不认识或不在乎的人，那这种暴力就毫无意义。让一个持矛兵在被杀前善待小动物，这种情节根本无法引起观众的共鸣。观众一眼就能看穿。世界上有谁看过《壮志凌云》后，在电影中途突然出现“鹅”的妻子和家人时，不知道他即将死去？


TWO: Have the Villain's Plan threaten the audience. We are sitting in the theater, minding our own business, when the Villain threatens to unleash a virus which will spread like wildfire. We see a map of the United States, and Donald Sutherland shows us how far the virus will spread in 24 hours... 48 hours... 96 hours (entire map is covered). Now the audience is affected by the villain's plan. If the hero doesn't stop him *we* will die.

第二：让反派的计划威胁到观众。我们坐在剧院里，原本平静无事，这时反派威胁要释放一种会像野火一样蔓延的病毒。我们看到一张美国地图，唐纳德·萨瑟兰向我们展示了病毒在24小时、48小时、96小时内会传播多远（整张地图都被覆盖了）。现在，观众也受到了反派计划的影响。如果英雄不阻止他，*我们*就会死。


This method works best in films where a nuclear incident will start a nuclear war which will probably destroy the world... or biological warfare will be unleashed. The audience itself is threatened by the villain's actions. We will become the victims. This is one of the factors in “X-Men: First Class” - with evil villain Sebastian Shaw (Kevin Bacon) engineering the Cuban Missile Crisis. If he succeeds, nuclear war will break out and we're all doomed.

这种方法在那些核事故可能引发核战争、最终毁灭世界，或者生物战爆发的电影中最为有效。观众自身也受到反派行为的威胁，我们仿佛成了受害者。这正是《X战警：第一战》的精髓所在——邪恶的反派塞巴斯蒂安·肖（凯文·贝肯饰）策划了古巴导弹危机。如果他得逞，核战争将爆发，我们都将万劫不复。


In my script "Crash Dive!", a group of terrorists have hijacked a 688 Attack Class nuclear submarine, and are threatening to nuke New York. Because I realized that might sound like a good idea to some audience members, I added the threat of firing at some random "small town" targets as well. Like the very city where the movie theater you're watching "Crash Dive!" is located in. Now you, the viewer, have a stake in the outcome... of course, it ended up as an HBO Movie, so whatever city you're watching it on TV may be that mystery target.

在我的剧本《冲锋陷阵！》中，一群恐怖分子劫持了一艘688型攻击级核潜艇，并威胁要用核弹袭击纽约。因为我意识到这听起来可能对某些观众来说是个好主意，所以我又加了一条威胁：他们还会袭击一些随机的“小镇”目标。比如，你现在正在观看《冲锋陷阵！》的电影院所在的那个城市。这样一来，作为观众的你，就与剧情走向息息相关了……当然，最终它被拍成了HBO电影，所以你正在电视上观看的那个城市，很可能就是那个神秘的目标。


The ultimate audience threat was in the William Castle film "The Tingler". At the end of the film, the Tingler escapes into a movie theater... the one *you're* sitting in! Vincent Price looks *right at you* and warns you "It's under your seat". Theaters were wired with buzzers under some of the seats to reproduce the feeling of the Tingler's attack. I'm sure a few people jumped. You want the villain's plan for world domination to either harm some character we have grown to love... or those of us in the audience watching the movie.

威廉·卡斯尔执导的电影《惊魂记》堪称终极观众威胁。影片结尾，惊魂怪逃进了电影院……就是你现在坐的那家！文森特·普莱斯直勾勾地盯着你，警告你“它就在你的座位底下”。为了营造惊魂怪袭击的氛围，影院在一些座位底下安装了蜂鸣器。我敢肯定，不少人都被吓了一跳。你肯定希望反派的统治世界计划要么伤害到我们喜爱的角色……要么伤害到我们这些正在观看电影的观众。


#↩

THIS WON'T HURT A BIT!

这一点也不疼！


The one thing you don't want to do when creating violence in an action scene is to make it ineffective and painless. If the audience doesn't feel anything when a character is killed or injured, that's akin to pornography. It's violence desensitized. We've all seen some film where the hero gets shot or stabbed or worse and wraps a handkerchief around the wound, and is as good as new. This very violent act was without pain, without feeling.

在动作场景中营造暴力时，最忌讳的就是让它变得毫无效果、毫无痛苦。如果观众在角色死亡或受伤时毫无感觉，那就跟色情片没什么两样了。那是对暴力麻木不仁的表现。我们都看过一些电影，英雄被枪击、刀刺，甚至更糟，却只是用手帕包扎一下伤口，就跟没事人一样了。这种极其暴力的行为，却让人感觉不到痛苦，毫无触动。


In real life pain hurts. Our job as screenwriters is to make an emotional connection with our audience. To *involve* them. To allow them to feel our characters' pain, and our characters' joys. To do that, we must personalize our stories and our action scenes and make the audience an active participant in our script. If the tone is light, the violence may not hurt as much... but there will also be less violence. The hero probably won't get shot in the face. If you are doing a *parody* or some story that is completely unreal – like the crazy “Gonzo Action” of films like “Crank” and “Shoot 'Em Up” then unreal violence is okay. But if your story takes place in some level of reality – pain should hurt. A character should just be able to shrug off a bullet wound. I think having realistic injuries makes a movie more exciting – when Jason Bourne injures his leg in “Bourne Supremacy” and spends much of the rest of the film limping (which puts him danger of being caught in the foot chase scene), it's realistic *and* adds to the thrills.

现实生活中，痛苦是会让人感到疼痛的。作为编剧，我们的职责是与观众建立情感联系，让他们*参与*剧情，让他们感同身受地体验角色的痛苦和喜悦。为了做到这一点，我们必须将故事和动作场面个性化，让观众成为剧本的积极参与者。如果影片基调轻松，暴力场面可能不会那么令人痛苦……但暴力程度也会降低。英雄可能不会被爆头。如果你创作的是*戏仿*作品，或者讲述的是完全虚构的故事——比如像《怒火攻心》和《枪火连天》这类疯狂的“冈佐动作片”，那么虚构的暴力是可以接受的。但如果你的故事发生在某种程度的现实中——痛苦就应该让人感到疼痛。一个角色应该能够毫发无损地承受枪伤。我认为逼真的伤势会让电影更精彩——比如在《谍影重重2》中，杰森·伯恩腿受伤，之后大部分时间都一瘸一拐地走（这让他在追逐戏中面临被抓住的危险），这既真实又增加了刺激感。


When you get ready to write the next draft of your action script, just remember: This time, it's personal... and emotional.

当你准备撰写下一稿动作剧本时，请记住：这一次，它是个人化的……而且充满情感。



#↩

EXPLODING THE CLICHES

打破陈规


One of the major problems with beginners scripts is that they are filled with scenes we've seen before, rather than scenes we'd like to see. Readers frequently note predictability, lack of plot twists, and overly simplistic elements as the reasons why scripts are rejected. I think much of this is due to screenwriters who reprocess old films into new scripts, thereby keeping cliches alive.

新手剧本的一大问题在于，它们充斥着我们早已见过的场景，而非我们想看到的场景。读者经常指出，剧本被拒的原因在于其情节过于可预测、缺乏转折以及过于简单。我认为这很大程度上是由于编剧们将老电影重新改编成新剧本，从而使陈词滥调得以延续。


My Websters defines a cliche as an oft repeated and tedious expression or idea. Boringly obvious and stale.

我的韦氏词典对陈词滥调的定义是：经常重复且令人厌烦的表达或观点。枯燥乏味，毫无新意。


So, now that we have met the enemy, how can we vanquish him?

既然我们已经遇到了敌人，我们该如何战胜他呢？


I believe the best method is to use his own weapons against him. Once you have isolated the cliche, turn it upside down and backwards upon itself, transforming it into a twist or reversal. Quentin Tarantino is famous for this.

我认为最好的办法就是以其人之道还治其人之身。一旦你找到了陈词滥调，就把它彻底颠覆，反转或反转剧情。昆汀·塔伦蒂诺就以这种手法闻名。


In "Reservoir Dogs" he gives us a group of macho, tough guy\ armed robbers. The tough guy cliche is: Once shot, they take it like a man. There are films where tough guys get shot, walk away, go home, and remove the bullet with a pocket knife and a pair of pliers, using whiskey (taken internally) as a pain killer. Mr. Tarantino turns this cliche upside down by having the gut shot Mr. Orange screaming in pain in the back of the getaway car. Flipping the cliche even more, Tarantino has Mr. Orange begging for his partner, Mr. White, to "just hold me". This is *not* cliché tough guy behavior. It is the exact *opposite* of how we expect tough guys to act.

在《落水狗》中，他塑造了一群肌肉发达、作风强悍的持械劫匪。硬汉的刻板印象是：中枪后，他们像个男人一样默默承受。有些电影里，硬汉中枪后，会径直离开，回家用小刀和钳子取出子弹，并用威士忌（内服）止痛。昆汀·塔伦蒂诺先生颠覆了这种刻板印象，让腹部中弹的橙先生在逃亡车后座上痛苦地尖叫。更进一步，塔伦蒂诺让橙先生哀求他的同伙白先生“抱紧我”。这并非刻板印象中的硬汉行为，而是与我们印象中硬汉的行事方式截然相反。


How does Mr. White react? Does he "put the wounded man out of his misery" like Pike does in "The Wild Bunch" by killing him like a lame horse?

怀特先生会作何反应？他会像《野战群》中的派克那样，为了“结束伤者的痛苦”而像杀死一匹跛马一样杀死他吗？


Nope. Mr. White holds his hand.

不，怀特先生握着他的手。


When was the last time you saw a film were tough guys held hands?

你上一次看到硬汉手牵手的电影是什么时候？


Tarantino, a movie junkie who knows every scene from every film ever made, is an expert at turning the oft repeated scenes on their heads to create something fresh and insightful. In every movie from “Dogs” to “Inglorious Basterds” (and probably “Django Unchained”) he takes the expected and flips it. He does this by setting up the cliche, and just when the audience says to themselves: "I know what's coming next", he gives them the exact opposite. Turning the cliche's weapons against itself.

昆汀·塔伦蒂诺是个影迷，对所有电影的每一个场景都了如指掌，他擅长将那些老套的桥段颠覆，创造出新鲜而深刻的作品。从《狗》到《无耻混蛋》（或许还有《被解救的姜戈》），他的每一部电影都打破常规，颠覆观众的预期。他先抛出一个老套的桥段，就在观众心想“我知道接下来会发生什么”的时候，他却给了他们截然相反的结局。他用老套的惯用手法反制了它。


The best way to deal with cliches is to: 1) Know Them, 2) Use Them, 3) Twist Them.

应对陈词滥调的最好方法是：1）了解它们，2）使用它们，3）改变它们。


Cliches are born every day, and part of our responsibility as screenwriters is to know what the new cliches are. This means you must be constantly studying films and reading new scripts. If five screenwriters avoid the same cliche by the same method, it becomes a *new* cliché! One of the best ways to avoid cliches is to *personalize* - instead of going for the obvious scene or the obvious storyline, look at *your* life and *your* interests and come up with the thing that only you could come up with. Something that follows your “voice” as a writer. Also, when dealing with characters look at the personal side of the character in the situation – what would they do or say that no other character in your script (or in film history) would say or do? Cliche's are lazy writing – going for the obvious instead of coming up with something that we *haven't* seen before.

陈词滥调每天都在诞生，而我们作为编剧的职责之一就是了解哪些是新的陈词滥调。这意味着你必须不断地研究电影，阅读新的剧本。如果五个编剧用同样的方法避免了同一个陈词滥调，那它就变成了一个新的陈词滥调！避免陈词滥调的最佳方法之一就是个性化——不要选择显而易见的场景或故事情节，而是审视你自己的生活和兴趣，创作出只有你才能想出来的东西。创作出符合你作为作家“声音”的作品。此外，在塑造角色时，要考虑角色在特定情境下的个人特质——他们会做出或说出哪些其他角色（无论是在你的剧本中还是在电影史上）都不会做出或说的事情？陈词滥调是懒惰的写作——选择显而易见的套路，而不是创作出我们以前从未见过的东西。


Cliched dialogue can either be a line we've hear too often, a line too "on the nose" for a scene, or a line which tell us what we see. No matter what, it is stale. I have a Blue Book on dialogue that contains all kinds of techniques for writing great dialogue – it's 200 pages, so I can't give you all of that information here... but I *can* share a few things that probably aren't in the Dialogue Blue Book.

陈词滥调的对话要么是我们听过太多遍的台词，要么是过于直白、不贴合场景的台词，要么是直接描述我们所看到的画面。无论如何，它都显得乏味。我有一本关于对话的蓝皮书，里面包含了各种撰写精彩对话的技巧——足足有200页，所以我不可能在这里把所有内容都告诉你……但我可以分享一些蓝皮书中可能没有提到的技巧。


Here are three good methods to deal with dialogue cliches:

以下是应对对话陈词滥调的三种好方法：


1) SAY THE OPPOSITE . Here is the seduction scene from Ernest Lehman's "North By Northwest". Roger Thornhill, wanted for murder, is hiding in Eve Kendall's sleeping car.

1）说反话。这是欧内斯特·莱曼的电影《西北偏北》中的一段诱惑场景。因谋杀罪被通缉的罗杰·索恩希尔藏身于伊芙·肯德尔的卧铺车厢里。

THORNHILL

索恩希尔

I can't let you get involved. Too dangerous.

我不能让你卷进来。太危险了。


EVE

前夕

I'm a big girl.

我是个大姑娘了。


THORNHILL

索恩希尔

In all the right places, too.

而且位置都选得恰到好处。


EVE

前夕

I mean, we've hardly met.

我的意思是，我们几乎没见过面。


THORNHILL

索恩希尔

That's right.

这是正确的。


EVE

前夕

How do I know you aren't a murderer?

我怎么知道你不是杀人犯？


THORNHILL

索恩希尔

You don't.

你没有。


EVE

前夕

Maybe you're planning to murder me, right here,

也许你正打算在这里杀了我。

tonight.

今晚。


THORNHILL

索恩希尔

Shall I?

我该怎么做？


EVE

前夕

Yes... Please do...

是的……请务必这样做……


This time, Eve's hands guide him, and it is a long kiss,

这一次，伊芙的手引导着他，这是一个绵长的吻。

indeed.

的确。


This dialogue takes places during a passionate embrace, and the exchange is broken by a number of serious kisses. It certainly doesn't *sound* like the typical seduction patter, does it? Eve gives very good reasons *not* to sleep with Thornhill. Not to even allow him in her room. And Thornhill does *nothing* to relieve any actual fears she may have that he really is a killer. Instead of talking about sex, they talk about violence. "Maybe you're planning to murder me"? The opposite of what they are feeling.

这段对话发生在两人热情拥抱之时，期间穿插着几个热烈的吻。这听起来可不像典型的诱惑话术，对吧？伊芙给出了充分的理由拒绝与索恩希尔发生关系，甚至不让他进自己的房间。而索恩希尔也丝毫没有消除她心中对他可能是个杀人犯的疑虑。他们没有谈论性，而是谈论暴力。“也许你打算杀了我？”这和他们内心的真实感受截然相反。


2) FIND THE DETAILS. Instead of having the character say what they feel, let them find a detail which illustrates their feelings. Have them talk about the detail, rather than the feelings. In "Terms Of Endearment" Debra Winger tells Shirley MacLane that she will miss her by saying "That is the first time I stopped hugging first." When Bo Hopkins is asked to surrender by the Pinkerton Detectives in "The Wild Bunch", he doesn't just say "no", he says: "You can kiss my sister's black cat's ass." Means the same thing, but is completely character specific. Surely the most memorable line in film history, and definitely too descriptive to be a cliche. The key is to *personalize* your dialogue with details from the character's life, which will not only get rid of the cliches, but offer insight and understanding of your character. Though, I think we learned more than we wanted to about Bo Hopkins' character.

2）寻找细节。与其让角色直接说出自己的感受，不如让他们找到一个能体现这种感受的细节。让他们谈论细节，而不是感受本身。在《母女情深》中，黛布拉·温格告诉雪莉·麦克莱恩她会想念她，她说：“这是我第一次不再主动拥抱别人。”在《野战群》中，当平克顿侦探要求博·霍普金斯投降时，他没有简单地说“不”，而是说：“你们可以去亲我妹妹的黑猫屁股。”意思相同，但完全是角色特有的。这无疑是电影史上最令人难忘的台词，而且绝对不是陈词滥调。关键在于用角色生活中的细节来*个性化*你的对话，这不仅可以摆脱陈词滥调，还能让你更深入地了解你的角色。不过，我觉得我们对博·霍普金斯这个角色的了解可能有点太多了。


3) EXPLODE THE CLICHE. This method requires that you find a cliche line and spin it to create witty variation in the tradition of Oscar Wilde and Dorothy Parker ("It was a divorce made in heaven", "If you laid all the girls from Vassar end to end, you won't have been the first"). "It's all over but the shouting" becomes "It's all over but the SHOOTING". "She's the ROAD apple of my eye." "I'm just going to play it by FEAR." "He's a man of a thousand faces, but a master of none." "She was at that SPENDER age." "They gave him the benefit of his CLOUT." "She never lets any grass grow under her BACK." Your character might complain of always being "a NEIGHBOR of love." Or know a liposuction expert who "Let the fat out of the hag." Yes, I admit these are all groaners, but these lines are no longer cliches.

3）打破陈规。这种方法要求你找到一句陈词滥调，然后加以巧妙改编，创造出类似奥斯卡·王尔德和多萝西·帕克式的诙谐妙语（比如“这是一场天作之合的离婚”，“就算你把瓦萨学院的女生首尾相连，你也不是第一个”）。“一切都结束了，只剩下争吵”可以改成“一切都结束了，只剩下枪击”。“她是我眼中的明珠。”“我只能靠恐惧行事。”“他千面人，却样样稀松。”“她正值挥霍无度的年纪。”“他们给了他影响力。”“她从不让任何事在她背后滋生。”你的角色可能会抱怨自己总是“爱的邻居”。或者认识一位抽脂专家，能“把老巫婆的脂肪抽出来”。没错，我承认这些话听起来很老套，但它们不再是陈词滥调了。


There are 200 pages of techniques in the Dialogue Blue Book that offer other solutions and some great tips on writing dialogue – if you need help with that aspect, check it out. No matter what method we may use, part of our duty as screenwriters is to keep our screenplays exciting and unusual, and the easiest way to do that is by avoiding cliches like the plague.

《对话蓝皮书》中有200页的技巧介绍，提供了其他解决方案和一些关于对话写作的实用建议——如果你在这方面需要帮助，不妨看看。无论我们采用什么方法，作为编剧，我们的职责之一就是让剧本保持精彩和新颖，而最简单的方法就是像躲避瘟疫一样躲避陈词滥调。



#↩

IT'S A SMALL WORLD

世界真小


The 1990s pitch by a well known writer-director went something like this: "World Heavyweight Champ Rocky Balboa is challenged by a boxer from Iraq, so he flies to the Middle East to take on Saddam's best fighter in an internationally televised match. The moment Rocky sees his opponent, he knows he's in trouble: This guy is HUGE. Big as a house. Trained from birth as a boxer. Rocky has little chance of winning.

上世纪90年代，一位知名编剧兼导演的构想大致如下：“世界重量级拳王洛奇·巴尔博亚接受一位伊拉克拳击手的挑战，于是他飞往中东，与萨达姆最强的拳手进行一场国际电视直播的比赛。洛奇一见到对手就知道自己麻烦大了：这家伙块头巨大，像座房子一样高，而且从小就接受拳击训练。洛奇几乎没有获胜的希望。”


"But he fights for America... and wins!

但他为美国而战……并且取得了胜利！


"Saddam gets mad, and has Rocky arrested and thrown into prison. The President Of The United States realizes the only way to be re-elected is to have Rocky Balboa rescued.... So he calls in the toughest commando ever to serve: John Rambo.

萨达姆勃然大怒，下令逮捕洛奇并将其投入监狱。美国总统意识到，要想连任，唯一的办法就是救出洛奇·巴尔博亚……于是，他召来了有史以来最强悍的突击队员：约翰·兰博。


"Rambo fights his way into Iraq, and breaks Rocky out of prison... Where the two men realize that they are identical twins separated at birth! After bonding, the two long lost brothers fight together to escape Iraq and destroy Saddam's regime!"

“兰博一路杀进伊拉克，救出了洛奇……两人这才发现他们竟然是出生即分离的同卵双胞胎！重归于好后，这对失散多年的兄弟并肩作战，逃离伊拉克，推翻萨达姆政权！”


Rocky and Rambo: Identical twins! What a small world!

洛奇和兰博：竟然是双胞胎！世界真小！


Motion pictures require us to suspend our disbelief. We know that Sylvester Stallone is not really Rocky Balboa, but an actor who used to get $20 million per picture and has a thing for tall, beautiful, fashion models. If Stallone takes a punch, we know he doesn't really get hurt. It's all make believe, and audiences are willing to buy a ticket and sit in the dark and pretend.

电影需要我们暂时放下怀疑。我们知道西尔维斯特·史泰龙并非真正的洛奇·巴尔博亚，而是一位曾经每部电影片酬高达2000万美元、并且对身材高挑、容貌姣好的模特情有独钟的演员。如果史泰龙挨了一拳，我们知道他并没有真的受伤。这一切都是虚构的，而观众们也愿意买票坐在黑暗中，沉浸在自己的幻想世界里。


But coincidence can lead to the death of suspension of disbelief. Wrenching the audience out of the "movie reality" and making them yell "Fake!" at the screen, or nudge their friends and say "Yeah, right" with epic sarcasm.

但巧合也会导致观众失去沉浸感，把观众从“电影现实”中拉出来，让他们对着屏幕大喊“假的！”，或者用极尽讽刺的语气碰碰朋友说“是吗，真的假的？”


Though film is not a realistic medium, relying more on the rhythms and wild logic of dreams, the viewing audience is (hopefully) wide awake. So your script should give the appearance of realism. We perceive reality to be mostly free of crazy coincidence. In fact, many coincidences which occur in real life would be considered unbelievable if transferred to the screen. Truth is often stranger than fiction, as they say. We want our scripts to *appear* realistic – and that means we will have to avoid crazy coincidences and set things up ahead of time.

虽然电影并非写实媒介，它更多地依赖于梦境般的节奏和天马行空的逻辑，但观众（希望如此）是完全清醒的。因此，你的剧本应该给人以真实感。我们认为现实生活中大多不会出现离奇的巧合。事实上，许多现实生活中发生的巧合，如果搬上银幕，反而会让人觉得难以置信。正如人们常说的，现实往往比小说更离奇。我们希望剧本看起来真实可信——这意味着我们必须避免离奇的巧合，并提前做好铺垫。


#↩

WANT TO GET LUCKY?

想走运吗？


The reason audiences reject coincidence is because they reek of luck. In "Fled" the hand-cuffed heroes on the run grab a hostage... who has handcuff keys in her purse! What are the odds? The pretty hostage decides to help them escape the police, and even falls in love with one of the prisoners! Amazing luck! Later in the film, the two heroes are being chased... and find a pair of motorcycles with the keys in the ignition! These two should have skipped the action plot and flown to Vegas!

观众之所以不相信巧合，是因为它充满了运气成分。《亡命天涯》里，两个被铐住的英雄在逃亡途中抓获了一名人质……而这人质的钱包里竟然有手铐钥匙！这概率也太低了吧？漂亮的人质决定帮助他们逃脱警察的追捕，甚至还爱上了其中一个囚犯！真是走了狗屎运！影片后半段，两个英雄被追捕……结果发现两辆摩托车的钥匙都插在点火器上！这两个家伙真应该放弃动作戏，直接飞去拉斯维加斯！


Coincidence is like cliché – usually a sign of lazy writing. Instead of setting up a way out of the problem ahead of time, or figuring out some reasonable way a couple of handcuffed guys could escape that makes sense, we get an amazing coincidence. The worst thing about coincidences like this in an action film is that they remove *conflict* - and *story is conflict* even if it's a rom-com... when you remove the conflict from an action movie we're back to those cops at the station sitting around eating donuts and waiting for the phone to ring. Wouldn't it be more exciting if the motorcycle didn't have the keys in the ignition? If the woman they kidnap didn't have *handcuff keys* in her purse?

巧合就像老套的情节——通常是编剧偷懒的标志。与其事先安排好解决问题的办法，或者想出一个合情合理的办法让两个被铐住的人逃脱，我们却看到一个匪夷所思的巧合。动作片里这种巧合最糟糕的地方在于，它会消除冲突——而故事的本质就是冲突，即使是爱情喜剧也一样……动作片一旦失去了冲突，就又回到了警察在警局里吃甜甜圈、等着电话响的场景。如果摩托车钥匙不在点火器上，或者被绑架的女人包里没有手铐钥匙，那岂不是更刺激？


#↩

CAUSALITY IS REALITY

因果关系即现实


Websters defines coincidence as "A seemingly planned sequence of accidentally occurring events".

韦氏词典将巧合定义为“看似有计划的一系列偶然发生的事件”。


In real life, things don't happen for any particular reason. Accidents happen. Film reality should mimic the accidental feel of real life. The causality. When the audience leaves the theater, they don't feel hand of God moving them like chess pieces... they have free will. They create their own destiny. They want the characters on screen to have the same freedom. Take choice away from the characters with "planned accidents" and you have destroyed reality. You have forced situations to occur instead of allowing them to proceed naturally. You are contriving the story instead of just letting it happen.

现实生活中，事情的发生并非出于任何特定原因。意外总是会发生。电影的现实感应该模仿现实生活中的偶然性，以及因果关系。当观众走出影院时，他们不会感觉自己像棋子一样被上帝之手操控……他们拥有自由意志，能够创造自己的命运。他们希望银幕上的角色也拥有同样的自由。如果用“人为制造的意外”剥夺角色的选择权，你就破坏了现实。你强行制造了事件，而不是让它们自然发展。你是在人为地编造故事，而不是顺其自然。


No matter how much planning and outlining has gone into your script, the audience should feel as if the events are occurring right before their eyes. In the theatre world they call this "The illusion of the first time". Even though the actors may have performed the play 300 times previously, when the Female Lead admits "I don't love you, I love your brother", the Male Lead should be shocked and heartbroken... as if this is the first time he's heard this, not the three hundred and first. The audience wants to believe every twist and reversal is happening right before their eyes... That they are *witness* to these events.

无论你的剧本经过多少精心策划和构思，观众都应该感觉剧情仿佛就发生在他们眼前。在戏剧界，这被称为“初次体验”。即使演员们之前已经演出过300遍，当女主角坦白“我不爱你，我爱你的哥哥”时，男主角也应该感到震惊和心碎……仿佛这是他第一次听到这句话，而不是第300一次。观众希望相信每一个转折和反转都发生在他们眼前……他们仿佛是这些事件的*见证者*。


As writers we may be secretly playing our characters like puppets, but we don t want the audience to ever see the strings. We don t want our scripts to seem forced, manipulative, contrived. In our scripts one event should logically lead to the next, carrying the character along with it. Natural and not contrived. That “Tennis Plotting” thing in micro as well as macro. Everything happens for a reason that the audience will believe.

作为编剧，我们或许暗地里像操控木偶一样操控着笔下的角色，但我们不希望观众察觉到丝毫的操控。我们不希望剧本显得牵强附会、矫揉造作。在我们的剧本中，一个事件应该合乎逻辑地引出下一个事件，并推动角色一同前行。一切都应该自然流畅，而非刻意为之。这种“网球式剧情安排”的理念，无论在微观层面还是宏观层面都适用。所有事件的发生都有其合理性，并且能够让观众信服。


#↩

HOW MANY COINCIDENCES ARE TOO MANY?

多少巧合才算太多？


Aren't you supposed to be allowed three coincidences in every script? I've heard three as the magic number from a bunch of new screenwriter and can only assume that some college professors decided to pick a random number for amount of permissible coincidences. Why they all chose three is a coincidence. If they were writing a script, that's the *only* one they could get away with.

难道剧本里不应该允许出现三个巧合吗？我听很多新手编剧都说“三个”是“神奇数字”，我只能猜测是某些大学教授随意选了个数字作为允许出现的巧合数量。他们偏偏都选了三个，这纯属巧合。如果他们在写剧本，那这大概是唯一能蒙混过关的数字了。


One coincidence. That's the limit in every genre but comedy. Here's the bad news: it's used up by a coincidence we usually aren't even aware of.

巧合一次。除了喜剧之外，其他所有类型的电影都只能做到这样。坏消息是：这种巧合往往被我们甚至意识不到的巧合所占据。


Coincidence is inherent in story. Real life is vague, problems aren't solved, there is no 'plot'. By organizing incidents into a beginning, middle, and end with a protagonist and antagonist; you're already using up your allotment of coincidence.
